Also, there can see motifs on the interior ceilings and walls of Faridkot Fort which show the rich Rajasthani traditions of craftsmanship. More sights in/around the town: Raj Mahal the Royal Palace of Maharaja Bikrama Singh on Area 61,000 m² - Darbar Ganj bungalow with a garden place, now been converted into Circuit House. Fairy Cottage (seven km on Chahal Road). This beautiful cottage is constructed by Maharaja Brijinder Singh in 1910–11. Check Tower (at the entrance of the Fairy cottage), Shaheed Bhagat Singh Park (in the city centre) in a beautiful scenery of the sunset in the evening. To do: Sheikh Farid Agman Purab festival (15-23 Sept); Bhatinda Virasat Mela and Heritage Festivals

name: Gurudwara Goindwal & Baoli Sahib
alt: Samadhi of Guru Angad Dev Ji
description: Located on western shore of Beas River, Northeast 30 km. It was the first centre of Sikhism, holds immense significance in reference to the Sikh pilgrimage sites. A popular pilgrimage destination for both Sikhs and Hindus. The entrance of place is well decorated with murals describing significant scenes of the Sikh history. The massive langar of the community kitchen provides food to a large number of visitors every day. Guru Amar Das Ji (the third Guru) established this place. There is a Baoli (well) with 84 steps leading down to it. The devout believe that by reciting Japji Sahib, the divine Word revealed to Guru Nanak Dev at each step after taking a bath in the Baoli.

name: Harike Bird Sanctuary
description: The second largest bird sanctuary in India. Also a National Wetland & Wildlife Sanctuary. Hari-ke-Pattan is one of India's leading in-land sweet water fish market and home of varied wild life.

name: Pul Kanjari village
description: Maharaja Ranjit Singh had been staying here in a Baradari as and when he passed by with his troops. It has been declared as a World Heritage Site by the UNESCO. It is said that once when a young dancer was going to Maharaja's Baradari for a dance performance, her shoe slipped into the water channel. A bridge (pul) was especially constructed to take her shoe out and hence this place got its name. Here is also a temple, a mosque and a Gurudwara. Popular shopping place for locals.

name: Ram Tirth
description: Consecrated by the appearance of Devi Sita, Ram Tirth was the birth place of the sons of King Rama. Making a special place in the holy scripts of ancient religions, the place was once the ashrama of saint Balmiki. The saint is believed to have scripted many of his sacred manuscripts at this place. A hut of Rishi Balmiki is still found at Ram Tirth where he once lived. After giving birth to Luv and Kush, Devi Sita used to stay at this place for a considerable period of time. The evidence of her stay still exists in the form a well which, it is believed, was dug by Hanuman. Devotees of King Rama and Devi Sita flock to this place every year to offer their prayers to the respected deities. As the locational position of the Ram Tirth is facilitated by easy accessibility, hence, the visitors conveniently reach this place of worship without any extra hassles.

name: Amritsar Heritage Walk
description: Despite visiting Amritsar and Golden temple several times, visitors find Heritage Walk experience extremely enjoyable and informative.

name: Old City Shopping
description: As you move through narrow path of old city and some other heritage buildings, you can see stalls selling everything from jootis to roasted sweet potatoes.

name: Mall of Amritsar
address: Main GT Road, MBM Farms, Sultan Wind Sub Urban
description: Shops of leading national, international and regional brands, five-screen cinema, hypermarket and one of Asia’s largest food courts. Services: customer relation desks, wheelchairs, children's play area, ambulance and first aid, Hi-tech security with CCTV, Gift wrapping at Hypercity hypermarket (Upper basement), Lost and found announcement services

name: Clock tower (since 1930)
address: new misri bazar, near golden temple

name: Golden Temple Community Kitchen
description: A dining hall (langar) serving free basic meals to all. Plates and spoons are handed out near the entrance, then follow the crowds inside and take the next vacant spot in one of the rows on the floor. Servers come by with large buckets of dal, chapatis and rice. Make sure to finish everything on your plate (wasting food isn't an option here) then take it outside to volunteers at the washing area. It's inside the complex which means no shoes and cover your head. At the ground floor of the building, they are serving chai. At the exit, there is a donation box for the free meals.

name: The Brothers or Bharavan the Dhaba
description: Serves traditional food or Chinese, continental at affordable prices. However, the food and service drops during peak times like weekends.

name: Bubby Dhaba
description: serves authentic Punjabi food at a very reasonable cost. Just metres from the main entrance of the Holy Golden Temple

name: Charming Chicken
description: Established in 1958. Very popular family restaurant, particularly for butter chicken with naan. No alcohol is permitted.

name: Kesar da Dhaba
description: It offers good Punjabi food made in pure ghee. Daal Makhni is worth trying. Don't forget to try a glass of Lassi after a heavy meal.

name: Moolchand Fish Shop
price: About ₹50 for a good-sized piece of fish, ₹70 for a serving of chicken
address: Off of GT Road near Tourist Guesthouse.
description: This tiny place is the definition of hole-in-the wall. If it looks like it has been there for 50 years, it's because it has! They'll weigh out your fish based on how much you want to pay, fry it, put some delicious spices on it, and serve it with spicy green chutney and raw onions. A little hard to find, but worth it.

name: My Kind of Place
description: Offers fast food such as pizza, burgers, and chips. It offers Chinese & Continental food also.

name: Neelam's
description: Offers pizza and other basics.

name: New Punjabi Rasoi
description: It's one of the most popular restaurants in town and serves up great Indian food including tasty masala dosas.

name: Bar One
address: Comfort Inn GSK Hotel Amritsar, 110, Albert Road

name: Empire Lounge
address: Welcom heritage Ranjits Svaasa, 47a, Mall Road Area

name: Golden Temple Dorm
price: Free, but donation expected (₹75-150 per night)
description: Offers free accommodation to pilgrims and tourists in very basic dorms or 3-bed rooms with AC and ventilation. It includes a shower, but toilets are outside with the other pilgrims. Maximum stay is 2-5 days, depending on utilization. You should remain quiet and respectful of the surroundings, keeping in mind that this is a holy place of pilgrimage more than a tourist attraction. Alcohol and smoking are strictly forbidden, not only within the temple complex but anywhere within sight of the temple complex. If you can handle that, then this is arguably the best place to stay—watching people go about their routine, talking to the pilgrims, and absorbing the gorgeous atmosphere. Put your donations in the donation box near the entrance to Ram Das Ji Niwas.

name: Tourist Guesthouse
description: A very nice place with a decent restaurant and friendly owners. About 25 minutes walking distance to the Golden Temple.

name: Country Inn & Suites by Radisson, Amritsar, Queens Road
description: A four-star hotel with rates starting ₹3000 for double rooms. Better rates online. Free Wireless and breakfast. 1.5 km to the Golden Temple and less than a km to the train station. Very clean and hospitable staff.

name: Green Acres Haveli
address: Green Acres lies right off the main airport (Ajnala) road, between the Amritsar city and its international airport
description: 5 minutes from the airport. Set amongst fruit orchards and lush greenery this diamond category farm stay lets guests experience rich Punjabi culture and heritage charm. It has been restored, and offers all modern conveniences and provides easy access to Amritsar attractions. Room packages range from ₹3000 to 6000 (inclusive of meals).

description: Four-star hotel.

price: Rooms starting at ₹2600 to ₹5000 for suites.
address: 101, District Shopping Centre, Ranjit Avenue, Amritsar-143001 (PB), India
description: Located in the most posh area, it has undoubtedly the best rooms and view in the town. Along with the most modern equipped suites, it is a great local favourite for dining for its hospitality and memorable stay. Don't forget to try out Golden Fried Chicken and continental cuisine.

name: Hotel Ritz Plaza
description: A more classy hotel with good rooms, service and a swimming pool.

description: A 3-star hotel.

address: Adjoining AlphaOne, MBM Farms, G. T. Road
description: 5 star hotel with a contemporary design, two restaurants, lounge and spa. 248 elegantly appointed guestrooms. Guest rooms: high-speed Internet - wired. Public areas: high-speed Internet - wireless.

address: District Shopping Centre, Ranjit Avenue, Amritsar-143001
description: Three-star hotel, four-star prices. Slightly out of town but a nicer more upmarket option with good service.

address: Ajnala Road (Airport Road), 8th Mile Stone, Amritsar, 143001, India
description: Five star-hotel with 186 rooms.

name: Ramada Amritsar
description: Four Star Hotel.Rooms : 149

name: Ranjit’s Svaasa
price: Rooms starting at around ₹6500 suites for 23000
description: It's opposite the Ebony Mall, down a little side street. The only boutique hotel in town, and a comparative oasis of calm in an otherwise hectic city. Ranjit's Svaasa is set in an old colonial house, and has been nicely refurbished with understated style. The place looks at its best at night. There is also a spa and small restaurant attached. Must be Amritsar's most expensive hotel

name: Hotel Golden Tower Amritsar
description: Panoramic point of view of the Golden Temple, multi-cuisine eatery with Indian, Chinese and Continental dishes. 24-hour in-room dining, Wi-Fi connectivity service, complimentary mineral water, tea- coffee maker, bathroom amenities with laundry assistance and, if required, doctor on call. Ample parking space. The hotel is multi-storey apart from the reception, there is a lounge where you can sit and drink tea.

name: Amritsar G.P.O.
address: Albert Rd and Court Rd corner
description: General Post Office. - Pincode: 143001

name: Uber
description: Book taxis through mobile apps for city and outstation travel.

name: inDrive
description: inDrive is a service that allows drivers and passengers to find each other and to independently agree on all the terms of each trip.

name: Ola Cabs
description: Cabs available through website and mobile app for local and outstation.

name: Mahajan Taxi Service
description: Outstation and local cabs available on website and app.

name: The Capitol Complex
description: Most of the capitol complex is fenced off due to tight security, the open hand is accessible and from there you can see the main buildings, albeit from a distance. If you want a closer look at the Capitol, you need to do a tour with the daily at 10AM, noon and 3PM—you need to be there 20 min before. Note the capitol and bureau are only open on M-F. This is one of 17 worldwide works by the architect Le Corbusier to be inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

name: Chandigarh Museum
description: This provides an interesting aspect on how Chandigarh was founded. It begins with the principles on which Chandigarh was built, selection of the Architects, the design for the people etc. The correspondence between the Punjabi officials overseeing the construction of the city, and the Federal Government in Delhi is fascinating, and well worth taking a few minutes to read. Close by is the Government Museum and Art Gallery as well as the Museum of Science and Natural History Museum.

name: Elante Mall
description: Elante Mall at Chandigarh is among the largest malls in North India, covering 20 acres. It is a mixed use development project which includes entertainment, hotels and business. Elante Mall has a retail space of over 1 million square feet. across "ground level and three upper levels". In the retail area, Elante Mall hosts various national and some huge internal brands like Heckett London,Apple ( eStore..Powered by Beyond Computers), Marks & Spencer, Brook Brothers, Rolex, Harley Davidson, Promod etc. Elante boasts of a great food court, a wonderful courtyard full of cafes, sports bars and has various clothing brands. In the entertainment section Elante Mall has PVR cinemas for entertaining large crowds.

name: The High Court
alt: Punjab and Haryana High Court also: Capitol High Court
description: The letter is fine for looking around the High Court; just show it to security at the entrance, around the back, but if you want to take photos you need to surrender your camera, and head in to fill out some more forms in the protocol office, and then take the forms back to security to get your camera back. It’s worth it as the building is amazing, and extremely photogenic. You can’t take any photos indoors.

name: The Japanese Garden
description: The Japanese Garden is a park in Sector 31 in union territory of Chandigarh. Built in 2014 in 13 acres of Land, by Indian Government, it was inaugurated by Shivraj Patil on 7th November 2014. It consists of water bodies, pagoda towers, water falls and golden bamboos. This is first ever garden in Chandigarh with Japanese touch and costs around ₹6 crore.

name: The Legislative Assembly
description: This is the Assembly for both Punjab and Haryana. It's easy to run out of time, so make sure you have a whole clear weekday to appreciate all the capitol buildings.

name: Museum and Art Gallery
description: The museum and the combined art gallery is an interesting place to go to. Artefacts range from Harappan period relics to paintings and coins from different areas and time periods. The Art Gallery has good collections of ancient and modern Indian art. Fossils of the local dinosaurs found in the region are on show in the adjacent natural history museum. The buildings that the Museums and Art Gallery are housed in are attractive.

name: Pinjore Gardens
description: Also called Yadavindra Gardens, these are 20 km (12 mi) from Chandigarh and 15 km (9 mi) from Panchkula, on the Chandigarh-Shimla road. Taxis and buses ply regularly between Pinjore and Chandigarh. Pinjore lies on the foothills of the lower Shivalik ranges. The fascinating gardens in the Mughal style are one of the most popular picnic spots in the region. A mini zoo, plant nursery, Japanese garden, historic palaces and picnic lawns await visitors.

name: Rock Garden of Chandigarh
description: In 1992, Nek Chand, a humble transport official, began to clear a little patch of jungle to make himself a small garden area. He set stones around the little clearing and before long had sculpted a few figures recycled from materials he found at hand. Gradually Nek Chand's creation developed and grew; before long it covered several acres and comprised hundreds of sculptures set in a series of interlinking courtyards. After his normal working day Chand worked at night, in total secrecy for fear of being discovered. When they did discover the garden, local government officials were thrown into turmoil. The creation was completely illegal, a development in a forbidden area. However, rather than demolishing the garden, they decided to give Nek Chand a salary so that he could concentrate full-time on his work, plus a workforce of fifty labourers.

name: Rose Garden
description: The city houses the largest rose garden in Asia. It also hosts an annual rose festival which is quite popular among the local population.

name: The Secretariat
description: You have to jump through some hoops to visit the Secretariat. First you need to find ‘Reception’, which is just a small building out the back, and show them your letter to get a visitor permit, then you need to see Security, who will let you in, then you need to see the main security officer inside, who will send you up to the Registrar, who will then send you back to the main security office. Thankfully you are escorted through most of this confusing, overly complex procedure, usually by a junior soldier with large machine gun. The whole process takes about 30 min to an hour. Once it’s all clear you can go up to the roof, check out the geranium gardens and take in an expansive view of all of Chandigarh. Then they will let you have a look out the front, which is more interesting.

name: Sukhna Lake
description: Sukhna Lake is an artificial reservoir. A popular place to hang out, one can expect to find residents of the city jogging or strolling along the banks. There is a walking path, a cafeteria, shops and a mini-amusement park and paddleboats. Shikaras are also available. The Sukhna Lake was created in 1958 by damming the Sukhna Choe, a seasonal stream that flows down from the Shivaliks. Storks and cranes make migratory stops at the lake. The lake, incidentally, has Asia's longest water channel for rowing and yachting. Visiting Sukhna Lake in the evening or early morning is a particularly pleasant experience.

name: International Dolls Museum
description: The museum has a collection of more than 250 dolls and puppets from over 25 countries, including India, Japan, Germany, Russia, and the United Kingdom. The dolls are made of a variety of materials such as wood, cloth, papier-mâché, and porcelain. The exhibits are arranged in various themes, such as fairy tales, Indian mythology and traditions, historical periods, and social causes.

name: National Gallery of Portraits
description: It was set up in 1977 in the heart of Chandigarh. The Museum has a vibrant and varied collection of portraits, busts, sculpture, images, prints of rare documents, photos and paintings based on India’s struggle for Independence. It has a big rectangular half comprising of 41 information panels describing details of movements and conspiracies during long freedom struggle of India from British Rule.

name: Pierre Jeanneret Museum
price: Rooms: ₹1,000 for Officers; ₹1,500 for Researchers, Scholars, Architect; ₹2,500 General Administration. Incl. breakfast
address: 57, Uttar Marg, Sukhna Lake, Sector 5, Chandigarh
description: The house of Chandigarh's first Chief Architect, Pierre Jeanneret has been converted into a museum. The Swiss-born architect Pierre Jeanneret, a cousin of Le Corbusier, was instrumental in the design and development of the capital city of Chandigarh. The three bedrooms on first floor have been opened up as guest rooms.

name: Le Corbusier Centre
hours: 10AM-5PM daily though hours may differ on public holidays
description: The old Architect's office is one of the earliest buildings constituted in Chandigarh. The museum was a workplace of Le Corbusier and his team therefore, building is of immense historic value to Chandigarh. The modest structure of building may well be considered as a seminal attempt at introducing concepts of sustainability and green architecture in the architectural annals of modern India.

name: War Memorial
description: The memorial is the largest post-Independence war memorial of the country with nearly 8459 names of deceased soldiers, since 1947 from the Army Air Force and Navy. The Place is designed to pay homage to the Jawans located in Bougainvillea garden. It was inaugurated by Late APJ Abdul Kalam in 2006. The walls of memorial are made from Pink Sandstone. It also has terrace like sitting area hence, makes a perfect place for Open Air theatre for conducting Light and Sound Show.

name: Bird Park
description: Opened in 2021, the Chandigarh Bird Park features enclosed aviaries containing aquatic and terrestrial birds, walking paths, and gardens. For an additional fee, you can have a parrot sit on your hand in one of the aviaries.

name: Maharaja Yadavindra Singh Stadium
description: This stadium, capacity 40,000, was completed in 2021. It hosts the Punjab cricket team and is expected to become the home of Punjab Kings in the IPL. It replaces Mohali stadium, which was bigger but hemmed in among housing.

name: Tandoori express
description: Don't miss this roadside outlet in sector 8. Providing specialised delicacies like kakoris and galoutis from Lucknow, amritsari fish and special waraqi wraps.

name: Tiffin Service in Chandigarh
description: Online tiffin and food delivery service in Chandigarh at very reasonable price. Open 7 days with breakfast, lunch and dinner food service. Make enquiries through call, sms, whatsapp, email, for more details visit website.

name: Barbeque Nation
description: buffet grill barbeque restaurant near you. Exciting Offers on lunch dinner with our trademark.

name: Chawla Chicken
description: There is a whole chain of Chawlas, the better ones being in Sector 8 and Sector 22.

name: Hot Millions
description: Very popular salad bar. Other locations Sector 35, Mohali, Panchkula.

address: Elante Mall bbmb Industrial Area Phase 1,
description: Afro-Portuguese chain restaurant serving flame-grilled chicken in spicy chilli sauce.

name: Nik Baker's
description: Also in Sector 9.

name: Oven Fresh
description: Also in Sector 35

name: Sagar Rathna
description: South Indian vegetarian chain.

name: Tehal Singh Chicken
description: One of the best places to try the famous butter chicken of Punjab.

name: Café 17
description: A very convenient (as well as very expensive) place to eat, chiefly on account of the fact that it is open round the clock. Multi-cuisine offerings such as "Fijian Mango and Walnut Salad" (₹500), "Naples Grilled Panini" (₹650), salmon pasta (₹600), "Barbados Prawns" (₹1,050). Frequent misspellings of the names of Italian dishes, unpardonable at these prices (e.g. "Penne Pomodoro Bassilico" for "penne al pomodoro e basilico", etc.). "Spaghetti con Fungi [sic]", apart from the misspelling, is translated in the menu as "Black fungus [sic] in pesto cream sauce", which may put some off (unnecessarily). The buffet breakfasts (7AM-10:30AM; ₹675), lunches (12:30-3PM; ₹1,100), and dinners (7:30-11:30PM; ₹1,300-1,400) here are mostly geared towards the Indian palate and best avoided (the atmosphere, somewhat sterile in the best of times, also changes for the worse during these communal feeding periods). The WiFi comes at a premium here (₹140 for 30 minutes).

description: for excellent Thai cuisine.

description: Experience trendy nightlife in Chandigarh.

description: The hotel offers 102 smart rooms, a multi-cuisine coffee shop called the Clever Fox Café, a Cyber Kiosk, a modern conference room, and a well equipped fitness centre.

name: Lemon Tree Hotel
address: Plot No. 3, MW Industrial Area Phase I
description: The hotel, with its 81 furnished rooms and suites, offers a wide array of accommodation options. Room categories include Superior Room; Executive Room; Studio Room and Executive Suite.

name: Hotel Taj Chandigarh
description: Still reasonably new, it is one of the best and easily one of the most expensive places to stay in Chandigarh, part of the Taj Hotels Resorts and Palaces group with properties in India and abroad (including Zambia, Maldives, and South Africa). Expansive lobby decorated with impressive original sculptural works contrasts starkly with the grubbiness of the neighbourhood outside (but this gives the place its raison d'être). Rooftop swimming pool and all the other usual five-star amenities. Good security; exclusive shopping arcade. Expect to pay for every breath of air you take.

address: 178 Industrial and Business Park, Phase I

address: Unit C516, Fifth Floor, 178-178A, Elante Business Park, Industrial Area Phase 1

name: Barua sagar
description: Baruasagar is around 24 km from Jhansi. It is a small town on the bank of Betwa river. It has a large lake which is called Barua sagar tal. Places to see here are the fort, Jarai-ka-Math, and the lake. It lies on Jhansi-Varanasi route and all the buses that go to Khajuraho pass through this town.

name: Chirgaon
description: Chirgaon is 30 km from Jhansi, It is on the banks of Betwa river. It is on National Highway 25. It is famous for National Poet Maithili Sharan Gupt who was from Chirgaon. Hindi authors generally describe this Triveni of poets from Chirgaon by comparing them with Triveni of Ganges.

name: Fort of Jhansi
description: The fort of Jhansi was built in 1613, by Raja Bir Singh Judao (1606-27) of Orchha. This fort is built on a rocky hill and the city of Jhansi is around this fort. During the earlier days, the wall of the fort was all around Jhansi city. This wall had ten gates. Some of these gates are still existing and some vanished with time. But places around these gates are still identified with name of gates. Some of the gates are Khandero Gate, Datia darwaza, Unnao gate, Jharna Gate, Laxmi Gate, Sagar Gate, Orchha Gate, Sainyar Gate and Chand gate. Timings: dawn to dusk daily.

name: Government Museum
description: The Government Museum is in a very picturesque location in the heart of the city. The surrounding area has some beautiful parks. At one side, is Deen Dayal Sabhagar (city auditorium). Nearby you can see Vrindavan Lal Verma park, Open-air theatre, Rani Lakshmi Bai Park, and a magnificent view of Jhansi fort. There is 1857 Mutiny Memorial on the way to the fort. It is a small park where 1857 mutiny has been depicted with statues that are made by metal scrap! The museum has a rich collection of sculptures, paintings, documents, etc. from different eras. A must see attraction during your visit to Jhansi, it will acquaint you with the history of the region.

name: Nag Mandir
description: This temple is in Jhansi cantonment. The beauty of this place is to visit it during sunrise. The spectacular view includes beautiful tree groves and beautiful aura of Jhansi. It shows the beauty is to be searched out in every thing.

name: Rani Mahal
description: Rani Mahal was built by Raghunath II of Newalkar family (1769-96). Rani Mahal is decorated with multicoloured paintings and art forms. Rani Mahal has been converted to museum with artefacts from 9th and 12th century AD. The best way to reach Rani Mahal is to take an auto from Elite crossing to the city..

name: St Jude's Shrine
description: This shrine of great imortance among Catholic Christians. St. Jude's bone is buried in the foundation of the cathedral. Devotees come from as far as Goa, on the St Jude's feast day on October 28, every year. Feast day is marked by a week long fair and a procession on the last day of the fair. This fair attracts people of all the faiths and religions.

name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
description: A massive church and school. Lot of celebrations take place around Christmas time and is packed.

name: Colvin Taluqdars' College
description: A must see place with great architecture. It was built in 1896 and named after British Indian colonial administrator Sir Auckland Colvin.

name: Firangi Mahal
description: The Oxford and Cambridge of India author/poet Shibli Naumani. For more details see the book Ul Farangi Mahal by Francis Robinson

name: Kukrail Reserve Forest
description: One of the three crocodilian breeding centres in India, including the freshwater gharials (Gavialis gangeticus), one of the 3 native species of crocodilians in India.

name: Marine Drive
description: Beautiful Gomti river-side and monumental structures view for fun with family and friends. Best time to visit is 4–6PM, during the sunset.

name: Shah Najaf Imambara
alt: शाह नजफ़ इमामबाड़ा Śah Najaf Imāmbāṛā

name: Dilkusha Kothi
description: The remains of an 18th-century house built in the English baroque style. The house was shelled during its involvement in the Siege of Lucknow in 1857, and only a few towers and external walls remain to this day, though the extensive garden is intact. The garden is packed by both local and foreign visitors during winter.

name: Bibiapur Kothi
description: A neoclassical building built by Nawab Asaf ud-Daula in the late 18th century. It was used as a country retreat, a place for the Nawab to escape the hustle of his royal court. After the dissolution of the Oudh State, the British used the building for military celebrations, and it became a part of the Lucknow Cantonment, although the building is open to the public.

name: Bara Imambara
description: A large and impressive tomb complex built in 1783. There is an interesting labyrinth inside, called Bhool Bhulaiya (भूल भुलैया Bhūl Bhulaiyā). You could easily spend half a day wandering around these beautiful but crumbling examples of Mughal architecture. If you hire a guide, do not expect him to know the way around; some are known to get lost in the labyrinth. The ticket also includes the Chhota Imambara, the Husainabad clock tower and picture gallery. Lone couples are not allowed to enter the labyrinth inside the complex without a guide. This prohibition is not brought to notice while buying the entry ticket. You will also have to pay a man ₹2 to mind your shoes while exploring the complex: shoes are not allowed inside.

name: Rumi Darwaza
description: An imposing gateway built by Nawab Asaf-Ud-Daula in 1784, modelled after a historical gate in Constantinople (present-day Istanbul). It used to be a gateway to the Nawab's palace, but unfortunately the palace was destroyed by the British in 1857.

name: Teele Wali Masjid
alt: टीले वाली मस्जिद Ṭīle Vālī Masjid
description: A mosque with a tomb of Shah Peer Mohammad.

name: Chota Imambara
description: An imposing mausoleum built by the third Nawab of Awadh in 1837.

name: Husainabad Clock Tower
description: A British landmark, set in a park with a somewhat poorly-curated picture gallery, and a lake. A great place for sunset.

name: Chatar Manzil
description: The palace of the Nawabs of Awadh, built by Nawab Ghazi Uddin Haider.

name: General Wali Kothi
alt: जनरल वाली कोठी Janral Vālī Koṭhī
description: An observatory commissioned in 1832 by Nawab Nasir ud-Din Haidar Shah, and became functional in 1841 when Colonel Richard Wilcox, a Royal Astronomer, was appointed. The building was in derelict condition after the death of Wilcox in 1847, and the instruments disappeared during the 1857 rebellion. It was said that once a brass pillar stood in central chamber through the roof. It was later occupied by the Imperial Bank of India (now State Bank of India) in 1923, and the building is since an SBI branch head office.

name: The Residency
description: The bloody history of the demise of this Raj-era compound is immortalised in the museum in the basement. This was the scene of the 1857 First Battle for Independence, referred to by the British as `The Indian Mutiny.´ Although you can still clearly see numerous cannon ball marks in the ruined buildings, thankfully it is a peaceful place today. So much so in fact, that you are likely to stumble across couples taking a little private time in the leafy shady groves. The Residency is clearly recognised by the locals and tourists alike as a breezy haven to escape from the bustle and dust of a busy Indian city. The Residency will try to sell you a photo pass for an additional ₹25. The guard will also ask you if you have a camera. However once you are inside, no one will say anything if you take photos.

name: Safed Baradari
description: A white-marbled building built by Nawab Wajid Ali Shah as a "palace of mourning". After the annexation of Oudh in 1856, the Baradari was used by the British to hold court for petitions and claims by the officers and nobles of the deposed monarch's reign and his relatives. Later, around 1923, it was handed over to the Taluqdars of Awadh for the British India Association of Oudh. The Baradari is owned by the association since then.

name: Tomb of Nawab Saadat Ali Khan
Ambedkar Memorial
description: A large, 107-acre development to honour Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar who was the architect of the Indian constitution. Impressive stone work, statues and fountains intermix with carefully sculpted gardens.

name: Manyawar Shri Kanshiram Ji Green Eco Park
National Botanical Research Institute
description: A botanical garden, and a good place for nature lovers. It features peacocks, a cactus museum, and research labs.

name: CIMAP (Central Institute of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants)
Haathi Park
description: A popular hangout place among the locals, the public park has two rows of large elephant statues as its main attraction.

name: Sahara Ganj Shopping Mall & PVR Cinemas
TORNOS
description: They offer some great heritage walks including a culinary walk.

name: Indira Gandhi Planetarium
address: 9, Nabi Ullah Rd, Suraj Kund Park
description: A building in the shape of Saturn.

name: Buddha Park
description: A small park on the side of a noisy congested road in Lucknow. A statue of the Buddha gives the park its name. The park features fun rides and boating facilities.

name: Nawab Wajid Ali Shah Prani Udyan
alt: नवाब वाजीद आली शाह प्राणी उद्यान Navāb Vājīd Alī Śah Prāṇī Udyān
description: The central zoo of Lucknow, established in 1921, and popularly known as Banarasi Bagh (बनारसी बाग़ Banārasī Bāġ) or Chidiya Ghar (चिड़ियाघर Ciṛiyāghar). The zoo is home to 463 mammals, 298 birds, and 72 reptiles representing 97 species, including tiger, lion, wolf, gibbon, black bear, rhino, blackbuck, swamp deer, barking deer, hog deer, elephant, giraffe, zebra, European otters, hill mynah, giant squirrel, great pied hornbill, golden pheasant, silver pheasant etc. It's one of the only two zoos in India to exhibit an orangutan. It has toy trains for children and a large number of animals in here. Fish aquariums also available. Available here is tasty Western-style food.

name: Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Park
description: A 76-acre park with courtyards, multiple jogging tracks, a fish pond and duck pond and a number of swings and benches for children.

name: Janeshwar Mishra Park
price: Entre is free, ₹100 per gondola boat ride
description: An urban park spread over 376 acres and partially modelled on London's Hyde Park. It has a human-made lake, cycling and jogging tracks, a sports centre and gymnasium and even gondolas.

name: Ekana Cricket Stadium
alt: Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium
description: Powerplay overs have been bowled in less time than it takes to say. Completed in 2017 and with a capacity of 50,000, it's on the ring road southeast edge of the city, and hosts the Uttar Pradesh team plus Lucknow Super Giants in IPL.

name: Hazaratganj
description: The city centre provides the food of the Mughals to Chinese and dosa of marksmen to the tastiest rabdis of moti mahal. The choice of cloth are the best for any occasion and the showrooms give every sort of thing you want. The celebrations of India's wins during world cups and solar powered lights make it a forever young market. The Hanuman temple is the place for you to express your devotion perfectly

name: Aminabad Market
description: Very old market, good for buying chikan (hand-embroidered clothes), leather shoes/bags and for chaat/sweets. There's a reasonably large book-market, consisting of an entire street. Gadbad-jhala is a market to get cheap bangles and fashion jewellery.

name: Chowk
description: Lively market. This is the place to find bargains, and check out the locals. Visit in the evening.

name: Hazratganj Market
description: Very trendy and upscale. All recognizable Western brands will be available here.

description: Movie multiplex and shopping mall

name: Nishatganj

description: Sells wide variety of crafts, including woven and hand embroidered garments, short tops, sarees, dupattas, home furnishings, artefacts, silver jewellery and accessories, organic honey, jams, preserves and herbs.

name: The Tornos Studio
description: They have great collection of book on Indian Mutiny. One can visit to read or watch a film on Lucknow. They will offer tea/coffee free of cost. But nothing is for sale - great place for evening. All this by appointment (call: 0522-2349472)

description: A rare cheaper place that accepts foreigners. Rooms are spacious and quiet, facilities are old, warm shower, wifi is very slow and unreliable, has cockroaches and mosquitos.

name: Lucknow Homestay
description: Has WiFi, home cooked meals and boasts of space. The hosts are friendly, and a mine of information.

name: New Sharma Hotel
description: There are two Sharma Hotels.

name: Sharma Hotel
description: Opposite charbagh railway station

address: Rani Laxmi Bai Marg, Kaiserbagh Officer's Colony

name: Hotel Mandakini Saket Regency
address: 92/3-A, Old R.T.O. Compound, Gautam Budh Marg (Latouche Road)
description: Reasonably friendly staff, just don't ask where to eat nearby, instead go a block or two back towards the station. The hotel doesn't have a restaurant but does offer room service. Rooms are reasonably clean but the air-con units are ancient and noisy. Large LCD TVs with cable. You may be able to negotiate a double room down to ₹1350 in the low season.

name: Clarks Avadh
description: One of the more centrally located hotels in Lucknow. Clean, well-kept and very smart. The restaurant named "Falaknuma" at the ninth floor has the right ambience to enjoy a Mughlai dinner with awesome views of the city. The Murg Malai Tikka is recommended. The service at the restaurant leaves much to be desired however, and the alcohol selections are in no way on par with what would be expected from an upscale hotel elsewhere. Wi-fi is available for a price.

name: Piccadily Hotel
address: Kanpur Rd, Sector B, Bara Birwa
description: A luxury hotel. 3 km from Lucknow Airport.

name: Fairfield by Marriott Lucknow
address: Gate No 2, Vibhuti Khand, Gomti Nagar

name: Golghar
description: Captain John Garstin built a Golghar for the storage of food for the British army with storing capacity of 140,000 tons in 1786.

name: Mahatma Gandhi Setu
description: The bridge over the river Ganges connecting Patna and Hajipur.

name: Kumhrar
description: Explore the ancient ruins of Pataliputra. Of the 80 pillars (Fa Hien, in 5th century CE, found the pillars shining as bright as glass) excavated at the site; only one remains.

name: Bihar Museum
description: Opened in 2015, the museum shows you the history of Bihar. It has several galleries, including the regional gallery, the contemporary gallery, the historical art galleries and the gallery on Bihari diaspora. The museum is open from 10:00 to 19:00 except Monday. However, the history part is closed after 17:00 hours and only the Children's Gallery is open from 17:00 to 19:00. Ticket costs for Indians are as follows: Adults - ₹100, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹50, Students - ₹50, while for foreigners is: Adults - ₹500, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹250, Camera - ₹100

name: Deep Narayan Singh Museum
description: Small local history museum, named after independence hero and first minister of Bihar, Deep Narayan Singh, who was born in Hajipur.

name: Gandhi Sangrahalaya
description: A public museum showcasing the life and principles of Mahatma Gandhi. It contains an exhibition containing photos, paintings, sculptures, manuscripts and quotations; all the major events in his life are told here. There is also a section containing photographs of his childhood through the various phases of Gandhi's life, including being taken to the crematorium. The building also houses a library which has a rich collection of books, magazine, literature and audio-video material related to Gandhi's life.

name: Indira Gandhi Planetarium
description: Among the largest and best planetariums in Asia, it attracts a large number of both domestic and foreign tourists. The planetarium has regular film shows on subjects related to astronomy and also holds exhibitions.

name: Patna Museum
price: Entry for foreigners ₹250, Indians, ₹10 additional ₹250 to see Holy Relic Casket.
description: It has more than 50,000 rare art objects, with many related to India in the ancient, middle ages and the British colonial era. Don't forget to see the Holy Relic Casket with the sacred ashes of Lord Buddha, and the beautiful statue Yakshani.

name: Shrikrishna Science Centre
price: ₹30 for general entry, tickets for particular shows cost extra
address: West Gandhi Maidan, Raja Ji Salai, Dujra Diara
description: The main science museum in the city with over 50 exhibits on physics and mathematics, with an emphasis towards optical illusions. Targeted towards kid aged 10 and over but adults will also have an enjoyable time the first time around.

name: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Science City
Rajendra Smriti Sangrahalaya
description: A museum dedicated to Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India.

name: Bharatiya Nritya Kala Mandir
description: A crafts museum and a multi-purpose cultural centre. The building contains dance and drama studios, a gallery space, and an art museum.

name: Kali Temple-Darbhanga House
description: One of the oldest temple of Goddess Kali.

name: Pathar ki Masjid
description: Built by Pervez, the elder brother of Shah Jahan and the first Mughal prince who made Bihar his residence.

name: Padri Ki Haveli
description: Oldest church in Bihar. When Roman Catholics first arrived in Bihar, they built a small church in 1713.

name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
description: The birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.

name: Maner-Sufi Saint Shrine
description: You can buy famous Maner Ka Ladoo(Sweets). Maner Sweets is one of the popular shops that specializes in these. However, avoid going there in the late evening or night.

name: Sonepur Cattle Fair
description: Largest cattle and animal fair in Asia. It is held in November in Sonepur which across the Ganges from Patna.

name: Buddha Smriti Park
description: A large park constructed in former jail ground is an oasis from noise and bustle of the city. Quiet meditative place and air conditioned libraries are the real relief even for a waiting time for the train. The large stupa is where ashes of Buddha originally from Vaishali are kept. There is a laser show in the evenings, which is related to the history of Bihar from the Ramayana to present.

name: Funtasia Water Park
description: Contains attractions like waterslides, wave pool, swimming pools, multi-cuisine restaurant, coffee shops, souvenir shops and a banquet hall.

name: Gandhi Maidan
description: Gandhi Maidan is the heart of this city today.

name: Sanjay Gandhi Jaivik Udyan
alt: Sanjay Gandhi Biological Park, Patna Zoo
description: One of the most popular picnic spots in Patna. It consists of a zoo and a botanical garden.

name: Shaheed Veer Kunwar Singh Azadi Park
Patna Golf Club
description: With some very tough holes, this well-maintained course situated downtown will prove interesting to amateur and pros alike. The Patna Golf Club is set in beautiful surroundings.

name: Bandhan Boutique
address: G-9, Pushpanjali Complex, Opp. S.K. Puri Check Post, Boring Road

name: Pind Balluchi
address: Revolving Floor, Biscomaun Bhawan, Gandhi Maidan
description: Pind Balluchi is a well-known chain of restaurants with franchises in various cities, now including Patna.

name: Hotel Patliputra Exotica
description: Surrounded by shopping and a 15-minute walk from Gandhi Maidan park, this modern hotel is 1.4 km from the nearest railway station and 2.3 km from the Bihar Museum. Elegant rooms feature wood floors, flat-screen TVs and sitting areas, as well as desks, washers, and balconies or terraces. Suites add dining tables and separate sitting areas. A 24-hour buffet restaurant serves international cuisine. There's also a stylish lounge with a bar and a snack menu, as well as a banquet hall and a fitness room.

name: Bharti Airtel
address: Bharti House, Nr. Income Tax Office, Ashram Road
description: Very good connectivity and service. Although the main office is at Ashram Road as listed, there are several shops where you can buy SIM.

name: Vodafone Idea
address: Vodafone West Limited, 6th floor, Sakar - II, Ellisbridge
description: Among the best networks in India.

name: Bharti Sanchar Nigam Limited
address: BSNL Central Exchange Office, Mirzapur, Shahpur, Ahmedabad
description: The state - owned cellular network.

name: Civil Hospital
description: It is Asia's largest hospital. One of the oldest and most modern hospitals in India.

name: Apollo Hospital (Main)
address: Plot No.1 A, Bhat GIDC Estate, Gandhinagar

name: Apollo Hospital City Center
address: 1, Tulsibaug Society, Opp. Doctor House, Nr. Parimal Garden, Ellisbridge

name: Shalby Hospital (Main)
address: Opp. Karnavati Club, S G Highway

name: Shalby Hospital (City Center Unit)
address: Vijay Cross Road, Nr. Fire Station, Navrangpura

name: Krishna Shalby Hospital
address: Siddhi Vinayak Complex, Balvatika - Maninagar Road, Kankaria, Maninagar

name: Care Institute Of Medical Sciences
address: CIMS Hospital, Nr. Shukan Mall, Off Science City Road, Sola
description: CIMS Hospital is accredited by various national bodies.

name: Sterling Hospital
address: Sterling Addlife India Limited, Sterling Hospital Road, Memnagar
description: Has a range of specialities.

name: Sanjivani Hospital
address: Sanjivani Super Speciality Hospitals Pvt. Ltd, 1, Uday Park Society, Nr. Sunrise Park, Vastrapur
description: A multi-speciality hospital founded in 1987.

name: Retina Foundation and Eye Research Centre
address: Retina Foundation and Eye Research Centre, AsoPalov Eye Hospital, Near the Underbridge, Old Raj Bhavan Road, Shahibaug
description: One of the most renowned eye care hospitals in India.

name: Radiance Hospitals
address: Shital Varsha Mall, Drive In Rd, Memnagar

name: Aurangabad Caves
description: This is a fine piece of architecture, is presented in the most unembellished manner. The caves lie just outside the city and are believed to have been excavated between the 2nd and the 6th century. They house the most stunningly intricate carvings. There are nine caves in all, most of them being the viharas. The 4th and the 7th cave are worth a dekko. The 4th cave stands well supported on 12 columns carved with scenes depicting the stories from the Jataka tales, whereas the 7th cave is embedded with carvings of women, adorned with jewels. The main attraction is the sculpture of a 'Bodhisatva' praying for deliverance.

name: Bibi ka Maqbara
description: A replica of the Taj Mahal, the Bibi-ka-Maqbara is the only example of the Mughal architecture of its kind in the Deccan plateau. It was built in 1679 by Aurangzeb’s son, in tribute to his mother, Begum Rabia Durani.

name: History Museum - Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University
description: It has on display a good number of ancient Indian paintings, coins, fabrics, arms, artifacts, etc. The museum collection is huge and has some fine sculptures from the excavation at Bhokardan, a nearby historic site.

name: Pan Chakki
description: This is a 17th-century water mill. The name has been derived from the mill that crushed grain for the pilgrims. There is a picturesque garden here that houses several beautiful fish tanks and it plays abode to the memorial of a Sufi Saint.

name: Shrimant Chatrapati Shivaji Raje Museum
description: As the name suggests, this museum is dedicated to the great warrior of Maharashtra - Chatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. A number of exhibits associated with Lord Shivaji are on display.

name: Soneri Mahal
description: an old historic monument now converted into museum houses a variety of ancient Indian pottery, dresses, remains of local palaces and antiques of daily use. A number of sculptures and reliefs from the local excavations are also on display.

name: Siddharth Garden
description: This is a beautiful landscaped garden, with good variety of trees and shrubs. There is a small aquarium inside the garden, however the biggest attraction is the Siddharth Garden Zoo, with a large variety of animals, viz. lions, tigers (white & Bengal), leopards, crocodiles, snakes (snake-house), civet cats, hyena, fox, porcupine, emu, deer and sprawling lawns to sit and have a great picnic.

name: Gayatri Chaat Bhandaar Road Side Eatery
description: Other unit at Kranti Chowk and are the oldest road side eateries in town. They serve excellent deep fried snacks like Kachoris, Samosas and Bhajjiyas hot and fresh prepared in front of you on a 'Chulha' (clay oven). However, it is not very hygienic.

name: Hotel Classic
price: Budget Sgl / Dbl ₹600/₹850, Std Sgl / Dbl ₹900/₹1180, Deluxe Sgl ₹1180

name: Hotel Girnar
address: Adalat Road, Pannalal Nagar, Maharashtra State Highway 30

name: Hotel Great Punjab
address: Bhanudas Sabhahgrah Railway Station Road, Bansilal Nagar

name: Hotel Heritage Palace
address: Maya Nagar, M G M (J N E C)

name: Hotel Manmandir
price: There is an Air-conditioned Dormitory for ₹300 per head. - 32 Rooms thoughtfully designed & furnished. Standard NA/C Sgl / Dbl / Extra Bed ₹1000/₹1250/₹300, Executive A/C, Sgl / Dbl / Extra Bed₹1300/₹1800/₹350, Ellora Executive A/C, Dbl ₹2400; Family Room A/C. 3 Bed/ Extra Bed ₹2100. all tax incl. (March 2015)
description: Locker is free.

name: MTDC Holiday Resort
description: Government Owned & Opetated

name: Sagar Plaza Hotel
description: One star hotel

name: Zostel Aurangabad
description: Beautiful and clean dorm beds for backpackers.

name: Hotel Kohinoor Plaza
price: Single Room Sgl 1200, Deluxe Room Sgl / Dbl / Extra Bed ₹1800/₹1900; Executive Suit / Executive Family / Kohinoor Club ₹2500/₹3100/₹4000 per room all tax incl. Extra Bed ₹430

name: Hotel Manor Aurangabad
description: Three star hotel

name: Hotel Sahyadri
price: Deluxe Sgl / Dbl ₹2100/₹2500, Executive Sgl / Dbl ₹2700/₹3100 tax incl. (2014)

name: Keys Hotel
description: Three star hotel

name: Quality inn Meadows
address: 6, Padegaon, Nashik Mumbai Highway, Village Mitmita

name: Aurangabad Gymkhana Club
description: Four star hotel.

name: Hotel Atithi Aurangabad
address: P-3, Jalna Road, Seven Hill Flyover

name: Hotel Rama International
address: Opp. New High Court, Jalna Road

name: Rudreshwar Ganapati Caves
description: One of the less-visited caves of Aurangabad district, and these are said to be from Buddhist era. Although there is a Shivalinga and a statue of Ganesha inside, these were latter-day additions by Hindus.

name: Ajanta Caves
price: ₹ 40 for Indians, SAARC and BIMSTEC visitors, ₹ 600 for others. Free for children 15 years and below
description: The Ajanta Caves depict the stories of Buddhism spanning the period from 200 BC and AD 650. These caves were re-discovered in the 19th century by some British officers who had been on a tiger hunt. These 29 caves were built by Buddhist monks using simple tools like hammers & chisels. These caves were the retreats of Buddhist monks who taught and performed rituals in the Chaityas and Viharas, the ancient seats of learning. The elaborate and exquisite sculptures and paintings depict stories from the Jataka tales. They also house images of nymphs and princesses. The Ajanta Caves and the treasures they house are a landmark in the overall development of Buddhism as such.

name: Ghatotkach Caves
description: Consists of three Buddhist caves of which one is a chaitya and two are viharas. The caves were excavated in the 6th century AD, and were influenced by Mahayana Buddhism. Specific preparations are needed to reach there as the access is difficult.

name: Antur Fort
description: It was built about the middle of the 15th century by a Maratha chief named Antur. It belonged to the Nizam Shahi of Ahmednagar between 16th and 17th centuries.

name: Gautala Autramghat Sanctuary
description: This is a dense forest reserve, with rare flora and fauna. Home to leopards, bears, wolves, hyenas, jackals, flying squirrels and 85 different species of colourful birds. Also try to visit the Pithalkhora Buddhist rock-cut caves (from the 2nd century BCE to 1st century CE), the Patnadevi Temple, the Mahadeva Temple and the Sita Khori waterfall.

name: Pitalkhora Caves
description: A . This lies peacefully nestled in the Satmala ranges of the Sahyadris. There are 13 cave sanctuaries embedded in this region. These monasteries date back from 2nd century BC to 5th century AD. Rich carvings with elaborate details can be seen in these monuments. WARNING: The side road to reach Pitalkhora from the main Aurangabad road is in an extremely bad shape. Don't go unless you have a SUV/Tata Sumo type of vehicle. The caves are reachable via a footbridge that is in a very bad shape. There is not much to see in the caves except for half-finished carvings.

name: Regional Tourist office
address: RTDC Hotel Ghoomar, High Court Road
description: Run by the Government of Rajasthan.

name: Mehrangarh Fort
description: Dominates the city and is the largest fort in all Rajasthan. Founded in 1458 as the site of Rao Jodha's new capital — hence the name, Jodhpur — the city has grown around it, and in the 500 years that have passed the fort has never been taken by force. It's easy to see why: it occupies the entire top of a 150-m hill with commanding views all around, with 3 km of massive ramparts built around the edges. An English-owned company 'Flying Fox' operate a zipline tour in the beautiful Chokelao Gardens within the fort.

name: Jaswant Thada
price: Entry ₹50 foreigners, ₹30 Indian. It is also free on the birthday of the Fort (about the 12th of May)
description: Royal cenotaphs built in marble, with a picturesque location next to a natural desert lake with lots of birds. Great view over the city and of the fort, as well as small well-kept gardens.

name: Mandore
description: The ancient capital of Marwar, before Jodhpur was built.

name: Umaid Bhawan Palace
description: Clearly visible to the south of the city and completed only in 1944, this is the last great palace built in India. The Maharaja of Jodhpur lives here to this day, but half the building has been converted to a 5-star hotel (see Sleep) and there is also a small museum on grounds (₹100 for foreigners, ₹30 for Indians, ₹10 for children 5 to 11 years, open 9AM-5PM). A few vintage cars are also on display in glass enclosures. You'll have to take a rickshaw to get here, and it's best to ask them to wait: around ₹100 for a round-trip with an hour's waiting time.

name: Ghanta Ghar
description: An architectural masterpiece built by Maharaja Sardar Singhji in 1910. It is illuminated with colorful lights at night.

name: Balsamand Lake
description: Now converted to a resort.

name: Gulab Sagar Lake
description: Gulab Sagar water storage was constructed by Gulab Rai in 1788.

name: Kailana Lake
description: A picnic spot and a main drinking water source for the city.

name: Ranisar Padamsar
description: Ranisar was made by Queen Jasmade Hadi, Rao Jodha's wife in 1459. Ranisar is near Fateh Pole in Mehrangarh.

name: Rajasthan International Folk Festival
description: International music festival held annually during October at Mehrangarh Fort.

name: Bishnoi Village Art
description: One of the better places to buy scarves, and share stories for a few hrs with the owner Papu over masala chai and pakora. Papu is very honest and will give you a fair price for his wide assortment of high quality materials.

name: Mohanlal Verhomal (MV) Spices
description: Manifacturer and exporter of all kinds of spices run by women. Tastings available.

name: Ganesh Handicrafts
description: The owner typically invites customers for a cup of masala tea and engages in friendly chats. The shop sells jewellery, textile, clothes (can be tailored-made), and furniture. Prices are fixed, so you don't need to bargain. Some scarves are as cheap as 200rps. They offer international shipping for bulky items.

name: Rajeev's - Grasim Exclusive Showroom
description: One of the higher end fashion lines (higher than Raymond). Buy custom-made men's clothing here at much more economical prices than in Delhi; for suits expect to pay ₹2,000 for labour, materials are extra with a series of different qualities (all prices negotiable). Suit construction takes 1-2 days after fitting.

name: Suncity Spices
description: One of the top spice/tea shops where the friendly and honest owner Mohammed will quietly offer you lower prices than on the list if you come in without a driver, i.e. no commission. ₹120 for each packet of spice/tea, and ₹100 per gramme of saffron. Wide selection of teas including flavours such as lemongrass & cucumber, lychee and guava

name: Via Bishnoi Village Craft
address: Jhalamand Circle, Near CTC Petrol Pump, Pali Road.
description: One of the better places to buy old and new handmade traditional and modern embroidered & patchwork textiles, shawls & scarves, clothing, fabrics, etc.

name: Gulab Jamun ki Sabji
description: Pokar sweets, very tasty sabji, made of raw gulab jamun (non sweet). Traditional Jodhpur style sweets.

name: Gulab Jamun
description: Chaturbhuj Ramesh Chandra sweets, very tasty. Every piece is around 50 g.

name: New Saheen Hotel (restaurant)
description: Nice restaurant busy with locals and not touristy. For about ₹60-80 you can try several different dishes. Selection includes fish, kababs, dal, paneer and fresh roti with ghee. On the second floor of a building, above a sign "qadri guesthouse", just outside of the old town, in an area full with pharmacies and clinics.

name: Shandar Sweet Home
description: Serves excellent Gulab Jamun Ki Sabzi, Kabuli & other Jodhpur specialties, popular with locals & quite economical.

name: Bal Samand
description: Outdoor dining as well as indoor dining in peaceful surroundings. Typical North Indian food. Alcoholic drinks also served. A perfect place for a quiet evening with family and friends.

name: Chilly and Garlic
description: A nice and cozy garden restaurant. It's a small place but good service and wonderful for family outing.

name: Mehran Terrace
description: Candlelit dining with an exquisite view of the city. Book ahead.

name: On the rocks
description: A nice place with outdoor dining. It has a separate bar and good ambiance. Great food but service is quite slow. They are more inclined towards serving foreigners and not so much to Indians.

name: Pukhraj Ji Ki Dhani
description: Typical Rajasthani food. Dal bati churma is only ₹150 for 1 person.

name: Pillars
description: In the courtyard of the palace, and the quality of the food is very high. ₹1,500 minimum for non-guests, and you can easily reach that with a main, an appetiser and a drink. Non-guests may be turned away if the hotel is full, so call ahead to avoid disappointment.

name: Amar Niwas Guest House
description: 527-year-old haveli run by a Brahmin family. The haveli maintains many of its original features such as stone lattice work balconies, gharokha, antique wooden ceiling and an open central courtyard. There is a plant-filled terrace with great views of the Mehrangarh fort and the oldest part of the blue city. 7 rooms decorated with Indian textiles and paintings. Hot and cold shower 24 hr. Roof-top restaurant with view of the fort, blue city & city wall.

name: Durag Niwas Guest House
description: Colourful and comfortable family-run guesthouse in a quiet area. The owners speak excellent English and are happy to assist travellers. Basic fan rooms from ₹350, free pickup from anywhere in town.

name: Ganpati Guest House
description: 9-room guest house with clean rooms. Get an auto-rickshaw to the clock tower and ask for directions. Rooftop restaurant with views of Mehrangarh Fort. Prices negotiable at check-in.

name: Heaven Guest House
description: Has 6 rooms of different sizes, all with attached bathrooms. Some have air conditioning and a television. Nice roof-top restaurant with great view.

name: Hill View Guest House
price: ₹300 for a fan room with a view
address: Near the Fort, Kille Khana, Fort Rd
description: This place is great value. The owners are nice, and the path up to the fort takes you to its doorstep.

name: Lake View Hotel & Resort
address: Akhey Raj Ka Talab, Kaylana Road, Jodhpur-Jaisalmer Highway

name: Hotel Sachdeva Excellency
address: Bank of Baroda Lane, Sojati Gate

name: The Kothi Heritage
price: Basic fan room from ₹2800 per person
address: Bachraj ji Ka Bagh 9th Chopasni Road,Sardarpura

name: Mandore Guest House
description: Traditionally designed bungalows/cottages, ethnically designed in round chalet style. A minute's walk from the main historic garden of Mandore.

name: Mehran View Guest House
description: Spacious, with heritage look, clean rooms, hot water facility for every room, Internet facility, veg and non-veg roof-top restaurant. Panoramic view of Mehrangarh Fort. Rooms with TV, air-conditioning.

name: Ratan Vilas
description: Still runs as an old Rajputana house, with excellent facilities and warm hosts. Courtyard meals. Large comfortable rooms that are clean and quiet. Not much in the nearby area. Beautiful pool.

name: Sadar Haveli Heritage Guesthouse
description: A restored 200-year-old haveli in a quiet part of the old town at the bottom of the hill under the fort. 4 rooms with large beds and 24 hr hot water. The rooms are arranged around a central courtyard garden as is the usual haveli style and the family that runs it make you feel very welcome. Great views of fort and city from the many roof terraces. In-house dining available with mains between ₹150 and ₹200. Room prices vary depending on season, ₹400-1,000.

name: Sarvar Guest House
description: 28 suites and double rooms. Furnished with traditional fixtures and old family portraits. Some of the rooms retain the original furniture as found when the Haveli restored. Roof-top restaurant with a view of the Meharangh Fort.

name: Shivam Paying Guest House
description: Nice rooms, some doubles have their own separate large beds with mirrors on the ceiling. Most importantly, they don't give commission to rickshaw drivers, so you'll have to be a bit persistent to get there (ask to get off by the clock-tower and then walk - rickshaw drivers will take you to commission places that will tell you they are Shivam, or else have someone wait outside the door who will pretend to be the owner and tell you that they are full. Get in the door to the front desk before asking about availability). If nobody around inside front door head upstairs to cafe/restaurant.

name: Singhvi's Haveli
address: navchokiya, ram dev ji ka chowk
description: This is more than 500-yr-old haveli.Clean and quiet rooms with aircon & hot water. Restaurant in the hotel. Continental breakfast . Beautiful view of the Fort & blue city from the roof top.

name: Tanu Guest House
address: Mehron Ka Chowk, Naya Bas Manak Chowk
description: Home stay run by the Mehra family. Rooms are clean and spacious. Rooftop restaurant gives view of the Fort, Blue city and Ghanta Ghar.

name: Veggi Guest House
description: Quiet and spacious, with clean rooms, hot water facility in every room. Internet facility and pure vegetarian restaurant. Just 5 min walk to Mehrangarh fort and same distance to old local market in opposite direction. Rooms with TV and A/C available.

name: Bristows Haveli Homestay
price: 4500RS for an apartment with two rooms
description: An old restored haveli (oldtown villa) with a few rooms. Rooms are small, everything is decorated lovingly, there is a wonderful garden and the family that loves there is very welcoming and helpful. Beautiful place, highly recommended.

name: Chhotaram Prajapat's Homestay
description: Traditional hut rooms with a basic air cooler. ₹1,500 for 2 people, free pickup and return to anywhere in Jodhpur, all meals, water and internet facility included.

name: Devi Bhawan
description: A 90-year-old heritage building with rooms set around lush trees and gardens with fountains and a pool. The rooms are decorated with period furniture and Rajasthani textiles. 1.5 km from the centre of the town.

name: Krishna Prakash Heritage Haveli
description: Old heritage haveli located on the foot of Mehrangarh Fort, with views of all monuments. Will arrange airport/train station pickup.

name: Pal Haveli
description: A short (though steep) walk from Mehrangarh. Will arrange airport/train station pickup. ₹1,300-1,500/1,500-1,800. (singles/doubles)

name: Umaid Bhawan Palace
description: 5* hotel managed by the Taj Hotels and housed in the famous Umaid Bhawan Palace. The view is scenic and it has an underground swimming pool for the guests along with squash and tennis courts.

name: The Ummed Jodhpur Palace Resort
description: Set on more than 11 hectares of gardens, Warm rooms feature Wi-Fi, flat-screen TVs and garden views. Amenities include 2 restaurants (1 outdoor), a beer garden, and a bar with a billiard table and exposed-beam ceilings. There's also an outdoor pool, a gym and a lobby sitting area. Parking and breakfast are available, as is meeting and event space.

name: Bishop Cotton School
description: A heritage building from the British era. It is in the heart of city and pride of Nagpur.

name: Diamond Crossing
description: A unique marvel of engineering that exists in a very few places of the world. The double lines crossing from the north to the south and those from east to west form a square shape and is called the diamond crossing. It is crucial and is used widely.

name: Satpuda Botanical Garden
description: The botanical garden of Nagpur with several rare plant species. The garden is also popular among bird enthusiasts.

name: Lok Bhavan
description: The winter residence of the Governor of Maharashtra.

name: Vidhan Bhavan
description: The seat of the winter sessions of the Maharashtra Legislature. It was built in 1912 to house the government of the Central Provinces of Berar, as Nagpur was its capital. The province was later incorporated into Madhya Pradesh in 1952 after India's independence, and Nagpur remained the capital of the Indian state. However, the Vidarbha region of Madhya Pradesh was later incorporated into Maharashtra in 1960, and Nagpur became the winter capital of the then-new state under the Nagpur Pact to protect the interests and equal development of Vidarbha.

name: Zero Mile Stone
alt: शून्य मैलाचा दगड Śūnya Mailācā Dagaḍ
description: A monument marking the geographical centre of colonial India. It was built by British during the 1907 Great Trigonometrical Survey of India in Nagpur. The Zero Mile Stone consists of a pillar made up of sandstone and another small stone representing the GTS Standard Bench Mark, and four stucco horses that were added later. The height of the top of the pillar is above mean sea level.

name: Nagpur Central Museum
description: One of the oldest museums in India, founded in 1863. Its collection includes artefacts like dinosaurs' fossils, coins, ancient inscriptions, sculptures, arms and tribal artefacts. It has QR codes in display galleries, which provide information about artefacts in Marathi, Hindi and English, as well as 13 other languages.

name: Narrow Gauge Rail Museum
description: A railway museum with old & heritage articles from Indian Railways: old steam engines, coaches, saloons and many more things related to narrow gauge Indian Railway. A very good garden with a toy train.

name: Raman Science Centre
alt: Raman Science Centre and Raman Planetarium Complex
description: An interactive science centre, similar to Mumbai's Nehru Science Centre. Named after Nobel laureate C. V. Raman, the centre was developed to promote a scientific attitude, portray the growth of science and technology and their applications in industry and human welfare, and hold science exhibits.

name: Khindsi Lake
description: Khindsi is a picturesque lake 40 km from Nagpur city and is famous for the natural beauty and water-sports. The lake is in a valley covered by thick forest and is a very popular tourist destination of Central India. There are cottages for accommodation too.

name: Phutala Lake
description: Evening host for food in exotic lake view.

name: Sonegaon Lake

name: Vidarbha Cricket Association Stadium

name: Yashwant Stadium

name: Maharajbagh Zoo

description: Each of 25 rooms is centrally air conditioned & elegantly furnished. Restaurant serving North and South Indian and Chinese cuisines.

name: Ramtek
description: A temple town 50 km from Nagpur. Has wonderful temples on top of Satpuda hills and covered by greenery. Watersports are operated in Khindsi lake with water zorbing, water scooter, paddle boat, speed boat, banana boat and rain dance and cultural tourism park Ramdham is nearby.

name: Goa State Museum
description: Hindu and Jain sculptures, including bronzes, from the 4th to the 8th centuries. The Christian Art Gallery shows different sculptures from the Portuguese period. Also on display a printing press that was brought to Goa by the Portuguese in 1556 AD.

name: Goa Science Centre and Planetarium
description: At a scenic location along Miramar Beach, this is a great place for kids. There's also a movie theatre showing 3D science-related films..

name: Gallery Gitanjali
description: Run by Ajit Sukhija in a building that once was the People's High School at Panjim's Latin quarter of Fontainhas.

alt: opposite the Goa Urban Cooperative Bank

address: Dempo Trade Centre Patto Plaza, Panjim

name: Fundação Cidade de Lisboa
address: a Dias Building, 1st floor Rua de Ormuz, Panjim

name: Casino Caravela
address: Caravela Jetty, Opposite Mandovi Hotel, Fisheries Building, D B Mart, In the starting point for the cruise
description: Casino Caravela, on board a yacht, offers a combination of sightseeing and gaming - American Roulette, Black Jack, Rummy, Stud Poker, Baccarat, Pontoon and Flash. ₹2000 (For entry and buffet.) Includes ₹1000 casino chips that cannot be cashed in.

name: INOX - Old GMC
address: Old GMC Heritage Precinct, D.B. Road, Campal
description: Watch the latest Bollywood flicks at the INOX theatre at Panaji.

name: Mandovi River Sunset cruise
description: Go for a short boat ride on one of the many "Cruise" boats, that sail up and down the river, with loud music, and frantically dancing revellers. Beside the Captain of Ports jetty on the Mandovi river at Panaji. The Santa Monica and Goa Boat Cruise is the oldest and best known of the lot, though the others are as good. Cruises start from around Sunset. There is also a floating restaurant, on the same pier.

name: Miramar Beach
description: Relax under a palm tree on Miramar beach, feel the sea breeze in your hair and watch the surf on the waves. Watch the many iron ore barges cruise lazily down the river towards the Arabian sea, in a typical "Socegad" Goan manner.

name: Dr. Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary
description: On the western tip of the island of Chorao, along River Mandovi and can be easily accessed from Panaji. Take a bus, or drive down the causeway along the river Mandovi towards Old Goa. A little after the turn at Ribandar, take a ferry across the river to reach the Bird Sanctuary. The best time to spot birds is between October and March, when many species of migratory birds visit the sanctuary from as far as Siberia. Don't forget to bring along some mosquito repellent, as the marshy land and mangrove forests have a lot of mosquitoes

name: Broadway Book Centre
description: Broadway Book Centre boasts of the "largest bookshop in Goa" (approx and also some good prices.

description: Focus on newspapers and magazines coming in from the rest of the country and abroad.

name: Reading Habit

name: Avanti Bar & Restaurant
description: Serves excellent vindaloo, sausages and Goan fish curry and rice.

name: Cafe Real Tea Room
description: Serves excellent vegetarian snacks. Piping hot, Bhaaji pao (Curried vegetables with local Goan Bread), Crisp Hot Kandea Bojjea (batter fried Onions), Mirchi Bojjea (Batter fried Green Peppers that are not half as hot as you would have imagined) over a hot cup of tea shouldn't be missed.

name: Fidalgo Hotel
description: 6 restaurants serving different types of food (veg, non-veg, Goan, etc.) Prices are high by local standards, but inexpensive for foreigners. Food is of excellent quality and there is something to be found for everyone! Aloo-stuffed paratha recommended at the Legacy of Bombay restaurant.

name: George
description: Recommended for the Goan specialty of tongue roast.

name: Godinho's and George Bar and Restaurant
description: Serve authentic Vindaloo, Sorpatel, Cafreal and Goan Sea food dishes.

name: Gujarat Lodge
description: Excellent snacks and sweets. Busy in the evening when they have hot samosas (₹5/- each!) and other snacks. Also have great packaged snacks like chevda and banana chips to take home.

name: Horse Shoe
description: Portuguese Goan cuisine. If you are in need of some good western food, this is an excellent choice. Recommended!

name: Kamats
description: Serves good Goan vegetarian dishes. Famous for their vegetarian Thaali (a stainless steel tray with rice, puris, various types of daals and vegetables served in small steel bowls)

name: Shanbag Cafe
description: A clean, simple cafe serving South Indian food, Indian snacks and thalis. Prices are excellent and the food is very tasty. Veg thali highly recommended (₹25/-).

name: Viva Panaji
description: Tucked away in a small side street, Viva Panjim offers a variety of traditional Goan dishes at astonishingly good prices. The proprietor, Linda, makes the rounds to chat and make sure people are happy. The food is delicious, and authentic (read spicy).

name: Down The Road
description: The other landmark is the general post office, 20 meters down to the bridge. The ground floor is a bar with Kala OK. The restaurant is at the 1st floor.The menu is GOA flavor and also Indian and Chinese food. Fish, pork is with highest cooking quality. sitting on the baloney, watching the river and surrounding is all local Panaji people.

name: Rajshahi Restaurant
address: G1 G2 G3 Karmally Glass towers
description: Muglai and Punjabi food.

name: Spicy Bella Bar & Restaurant
address: opp Campal Parade Ground, Bal Bhavan Rd
description: The speciality of this restaurant is Italian Pizzas and Pasta, which you have to try. The ‘Spicy Bella Pizza’ shown at the right is unarguably the best Italian pizza you can get around Panaji. It will keep you wanting for more. The other Italian pizzas are a bit plain, and go for those only if you have an appetite for Italian pizzas specifically. If you love Domino’s and US pizzas, it is likely that you won’t like the usual Italian ones. The menu hosts an exotic list of pasta dishes. Since every pasta dish is totally different, we can’t comment much on their taste in general. The quantity is good enough for 2 people though. And with every pasta or pizza, you get about 4 different spices and pepper sauce. The drinks menu lists about 6-7 mocktails, but if you let them know that you’re all in for mocktails, you will be presented with the bartender’s special menu with super exotic ones and all kinds of combinations such as kiwi juice with blue crush, pineapple juice with coconut cream and so on. We tried some cool ones. In the adjoining photo, the leftmost one is “Mickey donald”, with a dominant pineapple taste and a hint of strawberry and cream. Perfect for pineapple lovers. The one in the middle is ‘Pink Blossom’ from the regular menu. It has a combination of pineapple, orange and litchi. The one that took the longest to make is the one at the right, called ‘Spring Cooler’. It is a unique blend of juices, cream, and crush. Overall, we can say that Spicy Bella has the most exotic list of mocktails on the menu.

name: Ginger Goa
address: Plot No. 37 & 38, SGO Complex, near Passport Office EDC, Pato
description: Budget hotel with spacious rooms and modern facilities. Value for money.

name: Mitaroy Suites Goa
description: A small Heritage Hotel with a couples-only policy. Suites are extremely spacious and some even have balconies. Jack, the manager, was really friendly and helpful. Free Wifi and Free Goan Breakfast.

description: One of the better heritage hotels in Panaji, available only on advance booking.

address: 1/38, Teles House, Luis de Menezes Road
description: This is a small guest house so best to book ahead. Extending your stay here is nearly impossible as they will book your room out from under you. It is clean. No Wi-Fi; water is hot.

name: British Tourist Assistance Office
description: Britain, which has a significant number of tourists visiting the region, also has its Tourist Assistance Office (earlier designated as a consular officer) based here. Germany, Austria (in the port town of Vasco da Gama) and Italy have their honorary consuls.

name: German honorary consulate
address: Cosme Matias Menezes Pvt. Ltd., Rua de Ourem
description: Mr. Dean Menezes serves as Germany's honorary consul within the State of Goa. Only limited services

name: Portuguese Consulate General
description: Goa is home to the Consulate General of Portugal, which is understandable, as Portugal has had close and long historic and colonial ties with Goa. As Portugal never recognized India's takeover of the state, for a long time, it considered Goans eligible for Portuguese passports. While it is no longer as easy as it once was for people of Goan origin, this continues to be available, but difficult and time-consuming to obtain now especially for those born after 1961.

description: Professional cab operator for Pune to outstation trips.

name: Pushkar Lake
description: Pushkar Lake is a beautiful, sanctified spot in the centre of Pushkar. It is said to have been created by Lord Brahma and is therefore a place of pilgrimage for the Hindus. The lake is surrounded by 52 different ghats, or series of steps, which Hindus use to descend to the lake for ritual bathing, especially in the month of Karthik.

name: Aptaeshwar Temple
description: A temple dedicated to Shiva with an underground component.

name: Atmeshwar Temple
description: A beautiful Shiva temple.

name: Brahma Temple
description: One of the very few temples in the world dedicated to Brahma. Read up on Hinduism to learn why this temple is such a rarity! No matter where you stay in Pushkar, you will hear the daily chanting ceremonies or aartis conducted here: One begins two hours before sunrise, one 40 minutes after sunset, and one 5 hours after sunset.

name: Pap Mochini Temple
description: A beautiful temple on a hill dedicated to Gayatri, one of the 2 consorts of Brahma.

name: Rangji Temple
description: A Vishnu temple built in South Indian style that is very different from other temples in North India. Poojas are performed here by Iyengars of Tamil Nadu.

name: Savitri Temple
description: Dedicated to Savitri, the wife of Lord Brahma, this temple is the second-most important temple in Pushkar. It requires a climb of 650 steps to reach it, but the view at the top of Pushkar and the lake is worth the climb. Do it at sunrise!

name: Sri Panchkund Shiva Temple
description: The Shiva temple is said to have been built by Pancha Pandavas.

name: Varaha Temple
description: The oldest temple in Pushkar. Dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Not well maintained, but impressive due to its age and spiritual importance.

name: Man Mahal / Hotel Pushkar Palace
description: This beautiful palace was built as the guest house for Raja Man Singh I and has since been converted into the Hotel Pushkar Palace.

name: Pushkar Yoga Garden
description: Runs 4 classes per day, each 90 minutes in length. Courses deal with all aspects of yoga from stretching, workout, and philosophy. Students can stay with the family that runs the center and take classes every day.

description: This restaurant has a nice garden with a hammock.
