address: At the east end of Ellis Bridge
description: Foundation bastion of the city. Associated with folklore of Baba Maneknath.

name: Magen Abraham Synagogue
description: Only Jewish synagogue in Gujarat. It was built in 1934.

name: Lokmanya Tilak Garden
description: Historical garden established in 1905 houses some monuments. Green relief in concrete jungle.

name: Calico Museum of Textiles
hours: Thu-Tue 10:30AM-12:30PM, 2:30-5:30PM (no entry after 11AM in morning). Entry restricted to 30 visitors – 15 visitors on the basis of first-come-first-served and 15 by group booking
address: Sarabhai Foundation, The Retreat, Airport Rd, Shahibag
description: One of the finest textile museums in the world in one of Gujarat's famous carved wooden havelis. The museum displays a magnificent collection of rare textiles dating back to the 17th century. There is also an excellent reference library on textiles. It's in the Sarabhai Foundation, in Shahibagh the Calico Museum of Textiles, widely regarded as one of the finest textile museums in the world was constructed in 1949. It has a fine collection of textiles, clothes, furniture, temple artefacts and crafts. Also has a collection of marble, sandstone and bronze icons.

name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Memorial
description: It is a memorial and museum dedicated to the National Activist and first Home Minister of independent India, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The Museum is opposite the Circuit House in the Moti Shahi Mahal Complex in Shahibaug.

name: Jama Masjid
address: Jama Masjid, Manek Chowk, Gandhi Road, Khadia
description: It is amongst the most popular tourist sights in the city. Built of yellow sandstone this mosque stands on 260 pillars which support 15 domes at varying elevations. The mosque was built by Ahmad Shah in 1423. It is easily accessible as it stands in the centre of the old city. This imposing structure reflects the Muslim architecture of that period.

name: Jhulta Minara
description: Quite an unusual structure, Jhulta Minara or swaying minarets are a part of the mosque of Siddi Bashir and can be moved back and forth by applying a little force at the topmost arch. One of the minarets was partly demolished by an Englishman in his endeavours to unravel the mystery of the swaying minarets. The mosque was built by master craftsmen and the crucial mechanism that leads to the vibration is still a mystery.

name: Shahpur or Kazi Mohmad Chisti's Masjid
Dada Harir ni Vav
description: A unique 'water building' in Asarwa.

name: Hathisingh Jain Temple
description: An impressive white structure, the Jain temple built of white marble and elaborately carved is dedicated to Dharmanath - the 15th Jina or Jain Apostle. Similar to all Jain temples, this temple to is rich in intricate carvings displaying, among other things, musicians.

name: Heritage Walk
description: 2km long walk across the old city to know about culture, architecture and monuments.

name: Gujari Bazar
description: Located near Ellis Bridge and newly developed space of riverfront. The market is paradise for lovers of antique pieces ranging from old coins, records, furniture to old computers. Once a Sunday market for resale of low cost goods it now round the year market.

name: Manek Chowk
description: Surrounded by historical structures. It is a vegetable market in the morning, a bullion market in the afternoon and the popular street food market at night. Enjoy steaming Masala Dosa and Pau Bhaji. Try a Chocolate Sandwich or Pineapple Sandwich and Kulfi of Asharfi or Prem Mewad as a dessert.

name: Chandravilas Hotel
description: On Gandhi Road, this restaurant is well known for its delicious and iconic Fafda-Jalebi. In January, people flock here to buy Undhiyu.

name: Radhe Khaman
description: Gujarati snack, Khaman and its crushed form Sev-Khamani with Chatni draws people here. Anytime you go, you have to wait in line for few minutes. But it's worth it.

name: Lucky Tea Stall
description: Drink refreshing Masala tea with Maska Bun. Enjoy a painting by renowned artist M. F. Hussain who gave it to owner as a gift of friendship. The stall is located amid graves.

name: House of MG
address: Bhadra Road, Opp. Sidi Saiyad Jali, Lal Darwaja
description: The heritage hotel built in a restored, Baroque-inspired 1924 home. It is linked by courtyards and archways. Breakfast and parking are free. There is an open-air cafe, and a restaurant on a bi-level terrace, an authentic Gujarati restaurant. A lotus-themed health club has an indoor pool with dining space.

name: The Cama, A Sabarmati Riverfront Hotel
description: 2 dining options, an outdoor pool and a liquor store.

name: Amar dham
description: This religious site is known for its architectural grandeur.

name: Comfort Inn Sunset
address: Airport Circle, Ahmedabad Airport Exit Rd, Sardarnagar, Hansol
description: It has a unique architectural design.

name: The Ummed Ahmedabad
description: An upscale, luxury hotel with amenities including: a 24-hour eatery, a cocktail lounge, a refined dinner restaurant, a spa, gym, and an outdoor pool with a sundeck. Free Wi-Fi and Free breakfast/parking are provided.

name: Kankaria Lake
description: A circular lake built in 1451 by Sultan Qutub-ud-Din. In the centre of the lake is an island garden with a summer palace known as Nagina Wadi. It has a beautiful Musical Fountain show, although the music isn't too good the lights and fountain are worth the visit. 'Bal Vatika' - an aquarium, a boat club, a toy train, a natural history museum and a zoo.

name: Kamla Nehru Zoological Garden
description: It is near to Kankaria Lake and one of the best zoos in India.

name: Shah-e-Alam's Roza
description: Mosque and tomb complex associated with Shah-e-Alam

name: Baba Lului's Masjid
address: East end of Sardar Bridge, Jamalpur

name: Dinner Point Restaurant And Banquet
address: Near Diwan Ballubhai School, Kankariya Gate No. 3, Dairy Corner
description: Mostly North Indian food. There are lunch buffet options available.

name: Hotel Royal Landmark
address: Opp. Pushpakunj Society Near Apsara Aradhna Cinema, Kankaria, Maninagar
description: Every room has basic amenities like a TV and air-conditioning. In general the rooms are spacious and clean. However, there is no parking available.

name: Auto World Vintage Car Museum
address: Dastan Estate, Eastern Sardar Patel AUDA Ring Road, Kathwada
description: Shri Pranlal Bhogilal has a converted his private collection of vintage cars into a museum. It has a collection of more than 100 cars including Rolls Royce, Bentley, Maybach, Jaguar, Cadillacs, Austin, Chrysler, Lincoln, Ford and many many more. You can drive some of them for ₹500 for 3.5 km.

name: Bibiji's Masjid at Raipur
description: This century-old mosque is now a national monument.

name: Gauri Cinema
address: Near Soni ni Chali, National Highway - 8, Odhav

name: Fun Blast
address: near Shayona Arise, opposite Shiv Farm Hanspura, Naroda

name: Gandhi Aashram
description: The Sabarmati Aashram was once the house of Mahatma Gandhi and he founded the ashram in 1915. Today, without doubt, it is the biggest visitor attraction in Ahmedabad. It lies on the tranquil stretch of the Sabarmati river and was referred to as the Satyagraha Ashram during the lifetime of the Mahatma. It was from here that the Mahatma began his famous 'Dandi March' in 1930 to protest against the Salt Tax imposed by the British. One can see the three wise monkeys and many more of Gandhiji's teachings at the ashram premises. The ashram today continues the work started by the Mahatma and houses a handicrafts centre, a handmade paper factory and a spinning wheel factory. There are several other attractions.

name: Sabarmati Riverfront
description: Across the city on both the banks of the Sabarmati River, is a refreshing place in the mornings; a very relaxing atmosphere in the evening. A must-visit place. It can be accessed by a narrow road on the right, a few metres ahead from the point where Subhash Bridge ends on the Shahibaug side. Also a road to the left, just a little ahead of Income Tax on Ashram Rd (from RTO side), leads to the Riverfront on the opposite bank to that of the Subhash Bridge one.

name: Amdavad ni Gufa
description: An underground art gallery near Gujarat University in Navrangpura. Designed by the architect Balkrishna Vithaldas Doshi, it exhibits works of the Indian artist Maqbool Fida Hussain. The gallery represents a unique juxtaposition of architecture and art. There are facilities for special painting exhibitions and for projecting films. Gardens and Zen café are above ground. thumbnail|right|300px|Amadavad ni Gufa (Caves of Ahmedabad), Navrangpura

name: Darpana Academy of Performing Arts
description: One of the oldest performing arts academies in the city. Its amphitheatre Natarani has a fabulous performance venue overlooking the Sabarmati river, and is one of the few places to bring internationally acclaimed performing artists to the city.

name: Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Museum
description: It is one of the best arts displaying museum in city. It has a wide collection of Indian miniature paintings, stone sculptures, terracotta, paintings of Tagore, art of Nepal and Tibet, bronzes, textiles, wood work, cloth paintings, metal sculptures, coins. The museum houses priceless collection of books, manuscripts and other reference material from ancient India.The museum is a treasure trove of manuscripts relating to Jainism. In all there are about 45,000 printed books with 75,000 manuscripts including out of which 500 are illustrated ones. These documents from the past cover a wide range of subjects like Vedas, Agamas, Buddhism, Tantras, Jain Darshana, System of Indian Philosophy, Jaina Philoshpy, Grammar and Poetics. The institute has also published seven volumes of catalogues in languages like Hindi, Sanskrit, Old Gujrati, Prakrit and Rajasthani. The institute also conducts periodical workshops on manuscriptology and paleography.

name: Veechar Utensil Museum
address: Opposite A P M C Market Vasna, Vishala
description: The only museum in the country showcasing over 3000 utensils used by the various households in India. The lack of labels or explanation gives it the air of a rusty junkyard. It's part of Vishalla, a restaurant serving ethnic Gujarati food.

name: National Institute of Design
description: India's premier design institute with over 16 disciplines of design.

name: Parimal Garden
address: Chimanlal Girdharlal Road, Panchavati Society, Gulbai Tekra
description: A public park with nice green surroundings. A good place to jog and relax.

name: Sanskar Kendra:Ahmedabad City Museum
description: It is a history, art and cultural museum dedicated to Ahmedabad. It has small separate kite museum. The building was designed by French architect Le Corbusier and was created as a cultural centre with roof top garden.

name: Rauza of Azam Khan-Mauzzam Khan
description: Brick Tomb of generals

name: Shreyas Foundation Museums
description: Four museums are on the campus; Gujarati Culture, dolls, music instruments and arts. It also houses a school and small deer park.

name: Kochrab Ashram
description: It was the first such place founded by Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of the Indian independence movement, in May 1915 where he lived till June 1917. Now a museum.

name: Villa Shodhan
description: Permission required.

name: Kaligam Fort
description: A large abandoned fort dating back to Sultanate era with collapsing brick walls and turrets. Poorly maintained and deserted place.

name: Yog Sadhan Ashram
description: Do Yoga or get cured by Yoga Therapy at Yog Sadhan Ashram, An oldest institute of Yoga Education and Therapeutic Research founded By His Holiness Brahmaleen Swami Shri Manuvaryaji Maharaj.

name: Narendra Modi Stadium
description: Built in 2020 to replace Sardar Patel Stadium, this is by some distance the world's largest cricket ground, with a capacity of 134,000. It hosts Gujerat Titans in IPL.

name: Grand Cinemas
address: Shree Balaji Agora Mall, Sardar Patel Ring Road, Gandhi Nagar, Highway, Village Sugad
description: Dubai - fame Grand Cinemas. Very good quality screens, on northwestern periphery of Ahmedabad in a high - end mall (Agora Mall).

name: City Gold
address: Nr. Abu Coba Cross Roads (Sabarmati Tollnaka), Motera Stadium Road

name: Rajhans Cinema
address: 4th floor, Kalasagar Mall, opp. Saibaba Temple, Sattadhar Cross Roads, Naranpura

name: Law Garden Handicraft Market
description: Considered the main centre of activity in Ahmedabad, one can purchase handcrafts and traditional Gujarati outfits, amongst other things.

name: Reliance Fresh
address: Ashram Road, Hridaya Kunj, Old Wadaj
description: The mini-malls have variety of items that are available in a typical supermarket store. They also sell fresh vegetables, fruits, milk, dairy products, etc. There are 3 stores in Navrangpura, 1 at Mithakali Six Roads, 1 at Ambawadi, 4 on and off C G Road, 2 at Paldi, 1 at Vasna, 1 at Subhash Bridge and 1 at Motera (Visat - Gandhinagar Highway).

name: Shree Balaji Agora Mall
address: 4th Floor, Shree Balaji Mall, Visat to Gandhinagar Highway, Motera to Chandkheda, Ahmedabad.
description: It is a high-end mall having the Dubai-fame [http://www.cinegrand.com Grand Cinemas], the best gaming zone in Ahmedabad, a food court, cuisine theme - based restaurants serving Thai, Italian, Gujarati, etc. and a Sky Cafe. It has a really good antique shop. The retail stores are opening up gradually.

name: Amazo Restaurant, Gelateria, Cafeteria
address: Campus Corner Ground Floor H L College Road Navrangpura
description: Specialised vegetarian Italian and Mexican food.

name: Asharfi
description: These outlets serve desserts only. The Kulfis are excellent.

name: Bhagwati Chat
address: 73, White House, Panchwati Circle, C G Road, Navrangpura, Ahmedabad
description: It serves fast food and snacks. Try Paneer Tikka, Pani Puri, Gulab Jamun, Jalebi, etc.

name: Cafe Upper Crust
description: A popular cafe chain amongst the younger crowd. It serves continental fare including veg/non-vegetarian sizzlers, pastas, sandwiches, etc. The bakery has breads, cakes and desserts that are also worth trying. Look out for their special food festivals. Since 1989.

name: Choice Snack Bar
description: Provides excellent chaats, Chinese foods, fries, pizzas, burgers, etc.

name: Honest
description: A well-known fast-food chain in Ahmedabad that started as road-side joint serving Pav-Bhaji and Pulav in Law Garden area and now a developing restaurant chain.

name: Sankalp
description: One of the famous institutions of Ahmedabad, with an excellent variety of South Indian fare, along with other items. It had once set a Guinness World Record for the "longest dosa (thin-crepe) in the World" (25 feet).

name: Seva Cafe
address: Shopper's Plaza, 4th Floor, Opp. Municipal Market, C G Road
description: Seva Cafe is a gift economy restaurant, serving meals made by volunteers in C G Road, Ahmedabad. These meals made with love our offered as gifts to the guests who are asked to ‘Pay Forward’ this chain of kindness from their heart. The guests and volunteers of Seva Cafe have continued this chain for the last 7 years, offering more than 85,000 meals so far.

name: Vishalla
price: Lunch ₹484, dinner ₹1019, plus GST, children about half-price
address: Opp. APMC Market, Vishalla Circle, Vasna
description: Best dish: thali meals. Average food, but unusual because of its village-like decor and rather strange utensils museum. It has several pre-dinner activities like puppet-show for children, folk music and dance, snake-charmers, etc.

name: Zen
description: An open air café. You must place your food order near the entrance and they will serve it to you wherever you are sitting in the sprawling area. The menu is not very extensive, but has coffee, juices, iced teas, sandwiches and paninis. Come here for the ambience. Let food be just an accompaniment to conversation as the menu is limited, expensive and not worth the spend. Zen Cafe is comfortable and peaceful. The swaying trees and the twittering birds create a rustic ambience to rejuvenate your spirits. Evenings are beautiful as they light up the place, so visit after 7 PM.

name: Hotel Comfort Inn President
address: Off C.G. Road, opp. Municipal Market, Navrangpura
description: Multi-cuisine "Princess" restaurant. C.G. Road is one of the most posh commercial areas in Ahmedabad. Hotel is in the heart of the Ahmedabad city. The hotel's liquor shop carries liquor bottles from wide range of brands of whiskies, wines, and beers against liquor permit issued in the liquor shop to non-residents of Gujarat and foreigners against their recognised photo identity proof with address, e.g. passport, election card, motor driving licence.

name: Hotel Fortune Landmark
description: It is a leading economy hotel of Ahmedabad located in the heart of the city's business centre, around 10 km from the airport. Business facilities, food & beverage options.

name: Hotel Westend
description: In the commercial area of Ahmedabad.

name: Lemon Tree Hotel, Ahmedabad
description: Located in Ahmedabad’s downtown shopping and commercial area of CG Road in Navrangpura, this attractive and airy hotel is walking distance from Hazira LNG, Adani House, Vadilal Industries, Suzlon Energy, HDFC Bank, Standard Chartered Bank, Reliance Capital, Bank of Baroda and more

name: Hotel Inder Residency
address: Opp. Gujarat College, Surendra Mangaldas Road, Ellisbridge
description: 5-star hotel in calm and quiet western suburbs of Ahmedabad, close to main commercial roads: C.G & Ashram road. Easy accessibility to the Railway Station and Airport, and it is close location to main Ahmedabad, and other business areas.

name: Radisson Blu Hotel Ahmedabad
address: Near Panchvati Cross Roads, Off C.G. Road, Ambawadi Ellisbridge

price: Doubles from ₹5,000, room with all meals ₹11,200
address: Between Girish Coldrink & St. Xaviers Corner, Off CG Road, Navrangpura
description: Near Gujarat College. Swimming pool, dining options and banquet facilities.

address: Airport Circle, International Airport Road, Sardarnagar, Hansol
description: 91 rooms and suites, a full-service spa, a fitness center, and multiple dining venues.

name: Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Ahmedabad
description: A business school in Vastrapur.

name: International Society for Krishna Consciousness Temple
description: This Hindu temple depicts Krishna, and his lover, Radha, who is regarded as the personification of love.

name: S. G. Highway
description: The hub of entertainment in Ahmedabad.

description: Known for its architectural complexes.

name: Gujarat Science City
price: ₹50 entry, ₹20-50-100 for 2-4 wheeler-bus parking), Extra for each exhibit/place
description: A large science theme park with plenty of places to experience.

name: Swaminarayan Gurukul
description: It is a residential and day boarding school run by the Swaminarayan faith of Hinduism. The school teaches not only formal education but also provides training in horse-riding, archery, dairy development, Yoga, Ayurveda, etc. Entry by permission only.

name: Vaishnodevi Temple
description: Replica of famous Vaishnodevi temple at SG Highway.

name: Vastrapur Lake
description: An artificial lake, it was beautified by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) after 2002 and has since become a popular spot in the city. Every weekend, a large number of people visit this lake. It offers an open air theatre and children's park. There is a pathway all around the lake which serves many walkers and joggers in the early mornings and in the evenings. The lush green lawns surrounding this lake also serve as a central hub of Ahmedabad, wherein various cultural events take place regularly. At times, the water from Narmada River is allowed to flow into this lake. The lake has pretty gardens with lots of stone work in them.

name: Vikram Sarabhai Space Exhibition
address: Space Applications Centre Jodhpur Tekra, Nr. BRTS Bus Stop
description: Working models, live panels, static displays, the 3D theatre and the interactive multimedia presentations to educate general public about space technology developed by ISRO.

name: Sundarvan
address: Near ISRO, S. M. Road, Jodhpur Tekra
description: A nature education centre with an urban forest with a zoo. Puppet show at 5PM and snake show at 5:30PM on every Sunday.

name: Yoga Vedic Village
address: Yoga Vedic Village, opp. Raj Residency, Nr. Shalin Bunglows,Umiyamatamandir lane, Shilaj
description: An institute and a retreat of yoga education and therapeutic research, one of the best in Ahmedabad.

name: Cinépolis
address: Cinepolis India Pvt. Ltd., 3rd floor, Alpha One Mall, Vastrapur
description: A Mexican cinema chain, one of the better quality screens in Ahmedabad.

name: Mukta A2 Cinema
description: The quality of viewing and the seats, especially the legroom, are among the best in Ahmedabad.

name: PVR Cinemas
address: PVR Cinemas, 2nd floor, Acropolis Mall, Thaltej Cross Roads, S G Highway
description: A premier cinema chain.

name: Sunset Drive - In Cinema
address: Sunset Drive, In Cinema, Drive In Road
description: The largest screen in Asia. You watch films sitting in your car or on the grass or in the balcony seats.

name: Ahmedabad One Mall
description: This mall in Vastrapur consists of the cinema multiplex chain Cinepolis, food joint KFC, a lot of local and international food chains and retail brand stores and showrooms.

name: Dev Arc Mall
address: Located on S G Highway in Satellite area.

name: Iscon Mega Mart
description: On S G Highway connecting Sarkhej to Gandhinagar.

name: Jalaram Tadka Punjabi
description: Serves authentic Punjabi food specialities such as Amritsari Kulcha, Bathure-chhole, stuffed parathas and lassi.

name: Holiday Inn Express
address: Plot 38/1, Prahladnagar Road, Besides Venus Atlantis, Prahlad Nagar

name: Formule1 Hotel
description: The French discount major opened in July 2012.

name: Ginger Hotel
description: Off Drive-in road, close to the SG Road Business district. Expect a no-frills, business class hotel experience, similar to the other Gingers. From ₹1000/night

name: Hotel Country Inn
description: A four-star hotel suited for business travellers. It is in the heart of business and shopping areas, off Drive-In Road.

name: Hotel Ramada
description: This is a four-star hotel, suited for business travellers. It is in Prahladnagar, near the SG Road, which is a business and shopping area

name: The Grand Bhagwati
address: 301, Circle P, Prahaladnagar Garden Road, S.G. Road

name: Hotel Pride
description: This hotel is in the Judge's Bungalows area by Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway.

name: Ista Ahmedabad
description: In the heart of the city adjacent to the Vastrapur Lake.

name: Hyatt Ahmedabad
description: Restaurant, fitness centre, pool, spa.

name: Taj Skyline
address: Sankalp Square III, Sindhu Bhavan, Bodakdev
description: Dining facilities include an all-day diner, pan-Asian speciality restaurant, and a lobby lounge. Pool overlooking Ahmedabad's skyline. Fitness centre.

name: Lal Mahal
description: The palace where Shivaji spent his childhood.

name: Nana Wada
description: Former mansion of Nana Phadnavis.

name: Shaniwar Wada
description: This palace was built by the successors of Shivaji, the Peshwas in 1736. A massive fire destroyed the building in 1827. Most of the palace interiors were destroyed and all that remains is the old fortified wall. The brass studded gates and lotus pools have also withstood the ravages of time. This palace is situated in the heart of the city next to Deccan Gymkhana, Shivajinagar, and Laxmi Road. There is a 'Light & Sound Show' in three languages (Marathi, Hindi and English) every evening at the wada. It details the history of the Maratha empire and the significance of the role the Shaniwar played.

name: Vishrambaug Wada
address: RB Kumthekar Rd, Perugate, Sadashiv Peth
description: The remains of this palace stand in the heart of the old city. It was built during the 18th century by a descendant of Bajirao Peshwa. It is well known for its elaborate wooden façade.

name: Zero Stone
description: Zero-mile stone or simply zero stones are stones marking the exact point from which distances of a city are measured. The Pune zero stone is located on the eastern wall of the General Post Office (GPO). The stone was probably installed in the late 19th century and over the years it was buried under layers of concrete. In 2018 the concrete was removed revealing the entire stone. The stone has the names of places marked on it. Since 2018 several efforts have been made to landscape the area and turn it into an open-air museum focusing on the history of survey of India. But within years several installations including life-size fibre glass statues have been uprooted and damaged.

name: Fergusson College
description: Built in 1885, the college has a beautiful tree-lined campus with smooth rolling hills in the background.

name: Darshan Museum
address: HH Prince Aga Khan Rd, Sangamvadi
description: This museum is a light and sound show that uses 3D holographic technology. It's a 100-minute show that takes you through the saint Sadhu Vaswani's life story via different sets. It uses probably the only implementation in the country to use a technique called Pepper's Ghost to create realistic 3D. The sets are real but the people who enact the scene are projections of light. The museum also houses a huge spectrum of artwork that's used to build the sets. A place for the entire family, the Darshan Museum is a must visit for anyone visiting the city. It is close to the Pune Railway Station at Sadhu Vaswani Chowk.

name: Mahatma Phule Museum
description: You can see various industrial products, agricultural and handicraft articles in this museum, which was established in 1890.

name: Raja Dinkar Kelkar Museum
address: 1377-78, Off. Bajirao Rd, Natu Baug, Shukrawar Peth
description: The museum is housed in a Rajasthani style building situated close to the hustle and bustle of the busy Bajirao Road. The artifacts in the museum were once part of a personal collection. It is now open to the public and houses over 20,000 objects of which roughly 2,500 are displayed. There are 36 sections to the museum and the objects within range from carved palace and temple doors, 2,000-year-old pottery, traditional Indian lamps, and 17th century paintings.

name: Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati Temple
description: This Ganesha temple is visited by over a hundred thousand pilgrims every year. Devotees of the temple include celebrities and chief ministers of Maharashtra who visit during the annual ten-day Ganeshotsav festival. The temple is a beautiful construction and boasts a rich history of over 100 years. Jay and Vijay, the two sentinels made of marble catch the eye of all at the outset. The construction is so simple that all the proceedings in the temple along with the beautiful Ganesha idol can be seen even from outside.

name: Pataleshwar Caves
description: This 8th-century temple is hidden in the heart of the city, nestled between modern high-rise structures and developments. Reminiscent of Ellora, the temple and its massive pillars, a Shiva shrine, and a Nandi bull, have been carved out of a single boulder of massive size. The temple is still used by worshippers today.

name: Bal Gandharva Ranga Mandir
description: Theatre and art gallery. The place is maintained by the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) and has an air-conditioned theatre. Most of the famous Marathi plays are performed here. The theatre is named after the famous Marathi artist Bal Gandharva.

name: Deccan Gymkhana Ground
description: A playground with basketball and volleyball courts and a cricket ground, along with a gymnasium hall. It also has facilities for swimming, table tennis, billiards, cards and 11 tennis courts.

name: Kamala Nehru Park
description: A park with a jogging track, a kids' playground, a fountain and two lawns. A military jet (HAL HF-24 Marut) is also kept in one of the lawns. There are stalls of food item outside this park's main gate.

name: Nehru Stadium
description: A multipurpose stadium, used mainly for cricket matches.

name: Peshwe Park
description: A park managed by the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC). It is an energy park that stresses the importance of renewable energy in present times. Adventure Park is also launched here. The idea behind the park is to remove the fear element in kids from a young age as was first mooted by its designer B. S. Deshmukh.

name: Sarasbaug
description: A major landmark in Pune. The lake in Sarasbaug was built by Peshwa Bajirao II. There's a Ganesha temple in Sarasbaug known as Talyatla Ganapati Temple (तळ्यातला गणपती मंदिर).

name: Goethe-Institut
description: German language school.

name: Chitale Bandhu Mithaiwale
description: Outlets in the city are also a must go for a variety of sweetmeats and snack items. The Gulabjamun with sprinkled sugar which is a dessert dish and the famous Bakarwadi which is a fried chickpea flour preparation, are something worth trying while visiting Pune.

name: Laxminarayan Chiwda
description: They are famous for their Rice flakes Chiwda, Cornflakes Chiwda and Potato Chiwda.

name: Badshahi Lodging and Boarding
description: It's a nearly century-old place and serves very nice and authentic Maharashtrian pure veg thali (Brahmani). Food items to be had when fasting are a speciality here. It's a nice and clean place.

name: Bapat Upahar Gruha
description: Excellent Maharashtrian food.

name: Cafe Good Luck
description: One of the oldest and among the most popular restaurants in Pune. Famous for bread items and Mutton Kheema. It serves Iranian/Punjabi dishes, but is well known for its tea and butter bread. Mostly frequented by collegians, it's a cool place to hang out.

name: Chaitanya Paranthas
description: Known for its stuffed parathas (layered chapatis).

name: Manohar Fast Food
description: Clean authentic home-made Maharashtrian food with some delicious bharit-bhakri (an eggplant dish similar to babaganoush served with jowar or bajra bread) or even kadhi-khichadi (rice-lentil porridge). Finish up with a glass of taak (buttermilk) or solkadhi (kokum + coconut milk).

name: Tilak
description: Best quality tea and vada pav; an any time snack and other mouth lingering varieties at most affordable price. No waiter and no tips. Just a service counter based on token system.

name: Top in Town
description: Amazing non-veg food items. Do not miss fish and Chicken here.

name: Vaishali
description: A popular youth joint serving amazing South Indian dishes. Their sambhar is arguably the best in the city.

name: Vohuman Cafe
description: An awesome Iranian place serving delicious omelettes. Good for breakfast. Try the cheese omelettes and bun maska of this place.

name: Wadeshwar

name: Malaka Spice

name: Oh! Calcutta
description: A fantastic spread of Bengali cuisine.

name: The Orient
description: Serves authentic Chinese food in a laid-back atmosphere with soft music in the background. Quite similar to the Whispering Bamboo in the Taj.

name: Sigree

name: Suyash Lodge

Has a small pool and basic gym, a restaurant and bar and helpful staff. Soul Purpose bar: extremely subdued lighting would make this a good place for an illicit rendezvous. Clientele is a mix of business travellers and dining guests.

name: Hotel Satkar
description: Reasonably priced, clean rooms available with 24-hour hot water, TV in each room and close to the station.

name: Hotel Sagar Plaza
address: 1, Road Next to S.G.S. Mall, Wellesley Rd

name: Hotel Studio Estique
address: Amar Avinash Corporate Plaza, Bund Garden Rd
description: Offers five categories of contemporary design rooms and more than 10 different room sizes, to suit your budget.

name: Sheraton Grand Pune
alt: Bund Garden Hotel - previously Le Meridien
description: Including the popular: Entresol Bar, Roof Top Bar and a number of restaurants.

name: The Pride Hotel
address: 5 University Road, Narveer Tanaji Wadi, Shivajinagar

name: Shreyas Hotel
description: Basic facilities.

name: Alandi
description: The resting place of the 13th century Marathi saint Sant Dnyaneshwar. His devotees believe that he is still alive. A temple complex was built at Dnyaneshwar's samadhi and is visited by pilgrims, especially those of the Varkari sect.

name: Ghorawadi Caves
description: A cave with carvings and statues of Buddhist and Hindu deities.

name: Savitribai Phule Pune University
description: The site of Pune University was the official residence of the Governor of Bombay during the monsoon season. The campus features mansions built in Italian-Gothic style. A 300-m-high tower beckons to all these who come here in the pursuit of higher education. It is one of the oldest universities in India.

name: Indori Fort
description: A fort built by Sarsenapati Khandojirao Yesajirao Dabhade in 1720-21. The fort also has a mint building inside the fort which is in shambles. The entrance gate is in good condition. The fort has 9 bastions which are well connected by a fortification wall. The walls of the fort are high made of basalt rock with brickwork at the top. There is a temple of Kadjai inside the fort.

name: Aga Khan Palace
price: ₹25 for Indians, ₹100 for foreigners. Extra for photos
description: This historical landmark's architecture features Italian arches, salons, suites and spacious lawns. During the 1942 Quit India Movement, the British interned Mahatma Gandhi and his wife Kasturba Gandhi here. The palace belonged to Aga Khan, prince and head of the Khoja sect, who later donated the palace to erect a memorial dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi and his wife. Must see is an exhibition of very rare black-and-white photos and paintings from various epochs in the freedom movement, but descriptions are sparse so it helps if you already have background to the story. Also worth seeing is the Samadhi of Kasturba Gandhi in the backyard.

name: Chapekar Wada
description: The house of the Chapekar brothers, two Indian revolutionaries in the British period, now converted to a museum.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Museum of Indian History
description: The museum contains various exhibits on Indian history. It was founded by French author François Gautier.

name: Pimpri Chinchwad Science Park
price: Adults: ₹50 for museum and ₹30 for shows. Children below 15: ₹30 for museum and ₹20 for shows
description: A science centre housing a museum, an art gallery, an auditorium, an amphitheatre and a planetarium.

name: Japalouppe Equestrian Centre
address: Somatne Ohata, Mumbai Pune highway, talegaon Dabhade
description: Punes Premier Riding school, Japalouppe is spread out over a picturesque 19 acres, with a team of 60 horses catering to a wide skill set of riders, from basic trotting and school work to advanced jumping and dressage.

name: Pune University Heritage Tour
hours: 2nd and 4th Sun of every month starts at 11 am
description: The curated walk takes visitors inside the main building complex, which was built in 1871 and served as the summer residence of the Governor of Bombay. Building was designed by James Trubshaw and was modeled in lines of Prince Albert’s Osborne House on the Isle of Wight, while the bell tower was inspired by Giotto’s Bell Tower in Florence, Italy. The interior consisted of a grand ballroom which has been converted into an auditorium. The dining room today serves as a seminar room. In spite of the adoptive reuse the interior is mostly kept unchanged and still contains the antique furniture and chandeliers. The building also houses a museum with exhibits from history, geology and anthropology. Weapons from the 19th-century Maratha armory are also on display.The most interesting part of the Pune University heritage tour is a 300-foot-long underground tunnel that once connected the kitchen. Note: The notice appears on the Savitribai Phule Pune University website on Friday and there is no need for a prior booking and participants can simply drop in at the venue at 11:00AM. The walks starts at 11:30AM.

name: Annasaheb Magar PCMC Stadium
description: A multipurpose stadium owned and managed by the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC).

name: Maharashtra Cricket Association Stadium
description: It hosts both one-day internationals and test matches with a seating capacity of 37,000 spectators. It serves as the home stadium for the Maharashtra cricket team, as well as the IPL team Pune Warriors.

name: PCMC Hockey Stadium
description: A field hockey stadium.

name: Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park
description: A large tech and business park spread over 2,800 acres, built by the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation. It has offices of over 800 companies, including TCS, Infosys, Cognizant, Wipro, Tech Mahindra, etc.

name: Barberque Nation
description: Offers a vast & delicious variety of concept dining menus. Really worth paying for, especially for the unlimited servings of prawns, crabs, chicken, mutton, fish and also equally delicious Veg food. Rotate skewered dishes yourself with a grill built into the table. Good 8-10 variety of desserts to finish your meal.

name: St Laurn Business Hotel
address: 220, Phase 1, Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park, Hinjawadi

name: Sentosa Resorts and Water Park
description: Also has a multi-cuisine restaurant, open 11AM to midnight daily, that serves North Indian, Continental and other cuisines, has outdoor and indoor seating and has live music and ghazals on weekends. The water park is open daily, 10AM-6PM and costs $6. Sentosa is easily visible from the main highway.

name: Empress Botanical Garden
description: It has a collection of regional plants, including rare trees and flowers.

name: National War Memorial
address: Prince of Wales Dr Rd, Ghorpuri Lines, Dobarwadi, Ghorpadi
description: The National War Memorial is an stone pillar dedicated to post-Independence war heroes. A garden surrounds it and has paved pathways. The memorial was funded entirely by the citizens of Pune, under the sponsorship of the Express Citizens' Forum. The foundation was laid in November 1997 and inaugurated in October 1998.

name: Tribal Cultural Museum
address: Tribal Research & Training Institute, Koregaon Rd
description: A unique museum housing interesting artefacts from the Sahyadri (Western Ghats) and Gondhwa regions of Maharashtra.

name: St. Mary's Church
description: Commonly known as the "mother church of the Deccan" for being the oldest church in the region. It was inspired by the St Martin-in-the-Fields Church in London, and it contains many memorials of the British soldiers who served in various wars and battles.

name: Chintamani Temple
description: A Ganesha temple and one of the 8 Ashtavinayak temples.

name: Shinde Chhatri
description: Shinde Chhatri is a cenotaph dedicated to the 18th century Maratha military leader Mahadji Shinde (also known as Scindia). He was the commander and chief of the Peshwas from 1760 to 1780. The memorial consists of a Shiva temple along with a flat-roofed pavilion adjoining the temple. The pavilion houses a statue of Mahadji Shinde. The exterior walls of the temple and pavilion have intricate ornamentations along with stained glass windows. The complex also houses a domed structure housing the ashes of Mahadji Shinde. A small temple dedicated to Vital Meenakshi stands on the south-western corner of the complex.

name: Hadapsar Gliding Centre
description: Go for a joy ride in a glider and experience flying like a bird. Get an aerial view of Pune at a cost of ₹187. You can also learn to fly gliders at the Gliding Centre, which is India's oldest and to date the most active hub for gliding. Flying activity is conducted from Sunday through Thursday.

name: Kayani Bakery
description: Famous for its Shrewsbury biscuits, Walnut Cake and Sponge Cake, many mouth-watering bakery items here disappear almost instantly over the counter.

name: Garden Vada Pav Centre
description: Serves one of the best vada pav with green chutney. The vada itself is packed with tonnes of herbs and spices, the pav is robust, the mint chutney is delicious, and they even give you scraps and onion which elevates the whole experience to another level.

name: Sarangi

description: Celebrity chef Sanjeev Kapoor dishes up a wide variety of interpretations of Maharashtrian and northern Indian cuisines. Choose between the outside veranda with a bar-b-q buffet, or venture into the stylish modern interior for à la carte. The choc chip kulfi is listed as a must try - this is no exaggeration!

name: Khadakwasla Dam
description: A dam on the Mutha River, which created a reservoir called Khadakwasla Lake, which is the main source of water for Pune. Many people come here on weekends and during the monsoon season. The Peacock Bay hosts a large number of peacocks. It hosts various competitions like the annual national inland championship, open lake swimming competition, etc. Khadakwasla Lake is a venue for water sports in Pune.

name: Saras Baug
address: Saras Baug Road, opposite Sanas Ground
description: A 25-acre park featuring a famous Ganesh temple built in the middle of a lake by Nanasaheb Peshwa in 1784. The "Chowpatty" outside the park is one of Pune's most famous spots for Pav Bhaji and Bhel Puri.

name: Pune-Okayama Friendship Garden
description: One of the largest gardens in Pune, modelled after Korakuen Garden in Okayama as a bridge between the two cities. It is the largest Japanese garden outside Japan, spanning over 10 acres.

name: Rajiv Gandhi Zoological Park
description: A zoo managed by the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC). It is divided into three parts: an animal orphanage, a snake park and a zoo and it also includes the Katraj Lake.

name: Sinhagad
description: It has historical importance dating back to the era of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. The surroundings are beautiful in the rainy season and on clear days you can see a panoramic view of the surrounding countryside.

name: Taljai Hills
description: A hill and a wildlife reserve. The road to this hill passes through the Shivaji Maratha College campus with a picturesque mountain path, with sharp turns. Near the forest entrance is a temple to the hill's namesake Taljai Mata; a Hindu goddess. The reserve attracts migratory birds and is home to peacocks. The location is therefore popular with amateur bird watchers. Vehicles are prohibited in the area.

name: Blades of Glory Cricket Museum
description: A museum with over 51,000 cricket items.

name: Parvati Hill
description: A few temples and a museum are seated on top of this tall hill which offers spectacular vistas of the surrounding area. A steep flight of 108 narrow steps leads to the hill top temple built by Balaji Baji Rao. ‘Nagarkjana’ drum house is the temple of Parvati and Devdeveshwar. This was once the private shrine of the Peshwas. It is also the final resting place of Nana Saheb Peshwa. The Parvati museum houses portraits of Peshwas, old manuscripts, coins, and other artifacts.

name: Zapurza Museum of Art & Culture
description: It has an extensive collection of family heirloom of Maharashtra, coupled with a collection of Indian painters and historic artefacts.

name: Shivsrushti
address: Sr. No. 13, Katraj Bypass Road, Ambegaon Budruk
description: Historical theme park dedicated to the life of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, with exhibits and displays depicting events and aspects of Maratha history.

name: ISKCON Temple
alt: New Vedic Cultural Center (NVCC), Sri Sri Radha Vrindavanchandra Temple
description: The largest temple in Pune dedicated to Radha Krishna. The temple complex has two temples- the main Radha Krishna temple and the Venkateswara (Balaji) temple. The Radhakrishna temple is built in North Indian architectural style using red stone and marble while the Venkateswara temple is built in South Indian architectural style using Kota stone.

name: Digvijay Pratishthan Horse Riding Academy
description: And go out for horse treks with Digvijay Pratishthan.

name: Sumangal Youth Hostel
description: Clean three-star facilities nice lake view.

name: Paradise Homestay
description: Accommodation with private rooms in the Sinhagad Road area.

name: Pashan Lake
description: An artificial lake, once a source of drinking water has become heavily silted and degraded by pollution. Efforts are underway to rectify these issues. This lake remains to be a bird watcher's spot due to the variety of birds found in the area.

name: Vetal Hill
description: The walk up to the Vetal Baba Mandir (temple) provides good views of the city but trees and the radio transmitter building obstruct the best views. The trail goes through scrub and forest maintained by local nature volunteers. There is a car park on Gokhalenagar Rd but if you start lower down from Kanchan Galli you will also pass the small temple Hanuman Mandir. There is also a chance of seeing wild Peacocks in the area.

name: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Museum
description: One of the many museums dedicated to B. R. Ambedkar in India. Contains a library.

name: R K Laxman Museum

description: A museum and archive, containing 35000+ works of cartoonist R K Laxman. The museum also has a light and sound show.

name: Alliance Française de Pune
description: French language school.

name: Lizzes Hairdressers
price: ₹450 for a good men's hair cut (no shampoo)
address: E Square Multiplex, The Gordan House Hotel, S No 132/A, 6th Floor, University Road, Ganeshkhind
description: English understood well.

name: Asha Dining Hall

name: Janaseva
description: Traditional Maharashtrian Thali, very famous and visited by many Maharashtrians visiting Pune.

name: Nisarg Vada Paav
description: The best Vada Paav in Pune, but the place not at all clean.

name: Sharvaree
description: Sharvaree is upstairs and famous for traditional Maharashtrian 'thalipeeth', a savoury multigrain pancake snack. Downstairs is Shabree which is multicuisine but specialises in Maharashtrian thali (₹150). The food is good and the restaurant is very clean and pleasant.

name: Shreyas
description: Serves very good local Marathi cuisine thali (all-you-can-eat set menu) at a reasonable price and a clean dining place. Amras and Ukadiche Modak (steamed sweet coconut-filled rice dumplings) are not to be missed during mango season and Ganesh festival respectively.

name: Le Plasir
address: Shop No.4 B, Lane 6 Intersection, Bhandarkar Road, Deccan Gymkhana
description: A small French bistro, where you can get very delicious pastas and salads. Macroons and eclairs of this place are must to try

name: Shangrila

name: Dorabji

name: Durga

name: Corporate Stay
address: No.9, Sahyadri Farms, Baner Road, Lalit Estate, Baner

name: Aaina Mahal
address: in compound of Pragmahal Palace, Darbargadh Chowk
description: The literal translation of Aaina Mahal is an apt one. A beautiful palace now renovated after the massive earthquake in 2001. It also houses a handicraft museum where crafts from various parts of Kutch have been placed.

name: Bhujiyo Hill
description: A fort made by ancient rulers to protect the city. Now it is open for common public to see. A sure shot favorite if photography is your interest. You can get a nice panoramic view of whole city from here.

name: Chhatardi
description: The cenotaphs of rulers is a picturesque place. Featured in Bollywood movies, the place and garden around it makes a nice time.

name: Hamirsar Lake
description: A 450-year-old artificial lake built during the reign of the Jadeja Dynasty, the lake is quite a site to sit and chill out while roaming around it.

name: Pragmahal Palace
description: The palace of rulers of Kutch region. Maharao Pragmalji initiated the creation of this palace. This Gothic styled structure is a must visit. Opens at 10AM.

name: Kutch Museum
description: The museum is located on the scenic bank of lake Hamirsar and has the largest collection of inscriptions from the period of Western Satrap rule during the early centuries CE. Established in 1887, Kutch Museum is the oldest museum of Gujarat.

name: Shree Swaminayan Temple
description: A magnificent architectural masterpiece built from marble a stunning place to visit. The all white structure of the temple is sure to take breath away.

name: Tapakeshwari
description: A temple near small hills. Climb and see the beauty of the surroundings.

name: Hill Garden
description: A large amusement park with rides and garden. A large whale skeleton is also displayed here. Kids-friendly place.

name: Smritivan Earthquake Memorial and Museum
description: a memorial park dedicated to the victims of 2001 Gujarat earthquake and museum on Bhujiyo Hill. It has seven blocks with displays on seven different themes.

name: Ramkund
description: Ancient square stepwell.

name: Khari river gorge
description: A river gorge best for photography.

name: Sharad Baug Palace
description: A former palace of erstwhile Kutch State rulers, now a museum surrounded by nice gardens.

name: Old Swaminarayan Temple
description: Displays belongings of Swaminarayan.

name: Bharatiya Sanskriti Darshan Folk Art Museum
description: Kutchi culture centre with folk art, folk craft and textile museum.

name: The Rann Utsav
description: The three-day Rann Utsav is held every year during the full moon night in the month of December at Bhuj and goes around the district with a grand finale. The festival is visited and enjoyed by more than 8000 tourists from all over the world to celebrate the mystical magic of Kutch and its diversity.

name: Bhujodi Village
description: This is the handicraft village. People make the crafts and garments at their own home and sell there only. You can even see the process of weaving the garments. A fantastic value for money place to buy the items.

name: Shrujan
description: For good quality embroidery products of Kutch.

name: Gandhi Samadhi [Memorial]
description: The only second place where last remains of Mahatma Gandhi is kept and over that a memorial is built.

name: Jesal-Toral Samadhi
description: At nearby town named Anjar, you can visit this legendary temple famous amongst locals.

name: Kandla Port
description: One can take permit from Port officials to visit one of the biggest port of India.

name: Kutchi Handicrafts and Garments
description: There is a nice bunch of shops where one can buy Handicrafts and garments made specially at nearby villages.

name: Milk Sweets
description: Kutch is famous for its milk. And there are plenty of Milk sweet shops in the city. Khavda sweets is one of them. You can buy delicious sweets for your family.

name: Dabeli
description: This food item is very famous around the area. Have it from any food shop or even small time food corner. Its tasty and worth it.

name: South Indian Food at Chawla Cafe
description: The oldest restaurant in the city. It serves fabulous south Indian dishes and snacks. Must visit for a foodie.

name: Fruit Juice
description: Gujarat being a dry state, you will not find any liquor unless you have got permit. After having permit you can buy liquor from allowed places. Otherwise, fruit juice at roadside joint at Tagore Road, is a must visit.

name: Vijay Vilas Palace
description: It is a summer palace of erstwhile royal family of Kutch. Built in 1929 by Vijayrajji. Made of red sandstone in Rajpur architectural style. Great rooftop balconies giving fantastic view of the sea and surrounding greenery. It has a collections of stuffed animals, furniture and portraits of royals. Bollywood film Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam was filmed here.

name: Mandvi Beach
description: Scenic beach at sunset. Enjoy water sports. Bath in seawater and enjoy snacks sold by vendors. Ride horse or camel. Locker rooms and bath available.

name: Mandvi port
description: Small ships are loaded and unloaded here from this ancient port.

name: Kashi Vishwanath Beach, Salaya
description: An isolated beach with mostly no people or some locals playing cricket.

name: Mandvi Fort
description: Some ruins of the fort survives including gates.

name: Shipbuilding near old port
description: Traditional shipbuilding from wood can be seen along the old port on mouth of Rukmavati river. These 400 years old industry still use traditional methods of building plank by plank. The timber industry of the town depend on this.

name: Sagar Ship Museum
description: Maritime history and miniature ships museum.

name: Old town
description: The streets of the old town is dotted with old Havelis of wealthy merchants of the town of bygone era. The facades of the havelis depict European influences including angels and faces as well as stained glass windows. The market is busting in day and empty at night.

name: Bukhari Pir Dargah
description: Shah Murad Bukhari arrived and ruled Khanate of Bukhara (now in Uzbekistan) but he was spiritually inclined. He came to India during the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb (1662) and lived at Nizamuddin Dargah in Delhi for some time and later reached Kutch where he was welcomed by Rao Tamachi and locals. He lived in Mundra from 1662 to 1670. When he died, a Dariya Pir Dargah (shrine) dedicated to him was built. Aurangzeb built a gate in his honour, which still stands and is known today as the Mughal Gate. The seafarers and merchants used to visit it for blessings before venturing into the sea. The shrine receives a large number of devotees returning from the pilgrimage to Hajipir in March–April.

name: Fortification
description: The walls of the old city fortifications have a religious origin, as they were dragged from the ruins of the ancient city of Bhadravati (now Bhadresar). The walls can be seen along Kevdi river and road north of the town.

name: Hans Tower
description: Gateway to old fortified town is now topped with a clock tower. This is a main entrance to the old town.

name: Navlakho Bungalow
description: A very large and handsome two-storied bungalow built by Laximdas Laddha, son of Laddha Damji who was a manager of the firm of Jairam Shivji, a merchant banker who dominated commerce in East Africa in 18th and 19th century. It can be only seen from outside as inside is locked.

name: Swali Sheri
description: The family of Jairam Shivji came to be known as Swahili due to their business in East Africa where Swahili language is spoken. His family adopted the surname Swali and the street near his house became known as Swali Sheri. There are several old houses along the street.

name: Shantinath Mahadev Temple and Garden
address: near Shantivan Colony, Nana Kapaya village
description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva. Shantivan Colony is a township for employees of Adani Port. The temple is surrounded by a garden.

name: Nilkanth Mahadev temple
description: At Baroi, about a mile from Mundra, enclosed in a small court, is a temple of Nilkanth Mahadev, or the blue-necked Shiva, with, at the right side of the shrine door, an inscription dated 1667 (Samvat 1724). The linga is overshadowed by a large seven-headed brass snake. It is said to have been brought from the Shiva temple of Duda at Bhadresar.

name: Mahadev temple
description: It has memorials to some sailors of town.

name: Mundra Port
description: The largest private port with multiproduct special economic zone owned and operated by Adani Group. Accessible only by special permission and gate pass. Having a car is a must as there is no permission for tourists to get off the car in the port zone.

name: Aradhya Nova Cinemas
description: Watch Bollywood or Gujarati film.

name: Khatri Hasanbhai Allarkhya
description: Buy Bandhani and Ajrakh clothing. Bandhani Saree is a handcrafted tie-and-die sarees.

name: Satkar Lodge
description: Eat Gujarati and Punjabi Thali.

name: Shiv Shakti Bhajiya Centre
description: Eat freshly fried Bhajiya, Pakora, Khaman and Patra; all Gujarati fast food snacks.

name: Referral Hospital and Community Health Centre
Adani Hospitals
description: 100-bed secondary care hospital with an emergency services.

name: Maharaoshri Khengarji Library
description: More than 5000 books in Gujarati, Hindi and English languages with separate children's reading section.

name: Lakhpat Gurdwara Sahib
description: The place was visited by Guru Nanak who founded Shikhism on one of his pilgrimage to Mecca in 16th century.

name: Lakhpat Fort
description: The fort, rebuilt and expanded in 1801 by Fateh Muhammad, is an irregular polygon, defended by round towers and built of hard brown stone. The 7km-long walls are of considerable height but not thick. The walls can be climbed at several places and has post of Border Security Force as it is near Pakistan border. The vast open marshlands of creek can be seen from the walls in the north and Arabian sea from the walls in the west.

name: Pir Ghaus Muhammad Kubo
description: 19th-century tomb dedicated to Sufi saint is made of black stone, situated on a high platform, rising in a conical dome, and octagonal in shape, with four side doors arched and richly carved, and the walls decorated with patterns of flowers and leaves. Inside, the floor is paved with white and black marble, and the grave is covered with a white marble canopy. On the walls are passages from the Quran. It is still unfinished. The water tank opposite the tomb is believed to have healing characteristics for skin diseases.

name: Sayyed Pir Shah Dargah
description: Nine-domed Dargah with intricate carvings.

name: Lakhpat Maqbara
description: Tomb from past era.

name: Akbani Mahal
description: Ruins of the house of Akbani, the wealthy trading family of Lakpat in its glorious days.

name: Custom House
description: This 19th-century administrative building for collecting custom duties from trade was located on crossroads of Bada Bazar and Chowk Bazar. It has meeting rooms for merchants and officials. The high ornate window was for camels who can feed from the windows while goods on their back can be checked by custom officials without unloading them. It is in ruins.

name: Akbari Fort and Museum
description: Emperor Akbar's royal residence, now serves as a museum, which houses an excellent collection of Mughal and Rajput armour, and some fine sculptures.

name: Ana Sagar Lake
description: The dam built by the grand father of Emperor Prithviraj Chouhan in Ajmer. Daulat Bag is an enormous park by the side of Ana Sagar and is a nice place to relax. there are marble monuments by the shore and plenty of ice cream and papad-wallahs selling snacks. There is apparently boat rental, though other than a bumper boats tank.

name: Brahma Temple
description: Must go to Pushkar to visit this amazing Brahma Temple near Pushkar Lake, go shopping in the narrow but ethnic and colourful lanes of the marketplace, eat traditional foods as well as international delicacies in the numerous eateries.

name: Ajmer Sharif Dargah
address: 111 Faiz Manzil, Nathwan Shah, Dargah Sharif, Khadim Mohalla
description: The Dargah is a major pilgrimage centre of Muslim religion and holds a special place in the life of the Sufi saint Khwaja Moin Uddin Chisty(RA). Entry is free, but you should pay the people watching your shoes a couple of bucks. Priests are available to act as guides and to perform ceremonies at the shrine. Men and women must cover their heads, and women must cover their shoulders. The beggars in the Dargah Bazaar can be quite persistent. It is suggested for women not to enter the shrine in western clothes.

name: Happy Valley
description: Only if it is rainy season and you don't have old members in your group.

name: Nareli
address: Sri Dnyanoday Tirtha Area, Gyanoday Nagar
description: A Jain place on the outskirts (Kishangarh bypass). This is a good place to visit, has a very big temple and offer authentic Jain food (You have to check the meal hours in advance, they are strict in serving meals in those hours only).

name: Prithviraj Smarak
description: A park dedicated to Emperor Prithviraj Chouhan of the 11th century.

name: Shah Jahan Mosque
description: This mosque is the most beautiful of all the structures, in the Dargah precinct. It is made of white marble, delicately carved with trellis-work.

name: Ajmer Jain temple
description: This Jain temple built in the 19th century on the way to Ana Sagar is quite beautiful from the outside, it has a gold model of the city of Ayodhya, the birthplace of Hindu lord Ram, but usual temple protocols apply.

name: Taragarh Hill
description: It has a shrine and it is the second highest peak in Rajasthan

name: Mango Masala
description: A diner with separate places and menus for non-vegetarians and vegetarians.

name: Cafe District 01
description: Cafe with different veg & non-veg dishes for travelers.

name: Ambrosia
description: Vegetarian and non-veg cuisine, both traditional and neo-Indian cuisine. Apart from a private AC seating area, there is also a rooftop seating arrangement.

name: Hotel Mansingh Palace
description: A good place to stay. It's a 3-star hotel with decent facilities.

name: The Ambassador Hotel
description: This hotel offers a comfortable stay for travellers. The facilities offered are great and the tariff is economical. It can also be used to host a conferences and meetings.

name: Lohagarh Fort
description: Built in by Jat ruler Maharaja Suraj Mal in the 18th century. It's one of the few forts in India not conquered by the British, despite them laying siege to it for six weeks in 1805. The fort is surrounded by a moat, which has remained intact to this day. The approach is through two gates.

name: Jawahar Burj
description: It was built by Raja Jawahar Singh in 1765 to commemorate his victory over the Mughals at the Battle of Delhi (1764)

name: Keoladeo Bird Sanctuary
description: It is also known as Ghana, is a world famous sanctuary developed by Maharaja of Bharatpur. It is also one of the few Natural UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India. The best time to see the park is in October to February when there is a lot of migratory birds, otherwise it can be relatively bird free. The best times for bird spotting are early evening and morning. Admission is ₹200, an optional driver is ₹100 per hr, and an optional guide is ₹150 per hr. Another way to see the park is to hire a bike at your hotel or entrance (approx ₹40/day).

name: Ganga Maharani Temple
description: Built by Maharaja Balwant Singh in 1845.

name: Jama Masjid
description: The main mosque of Bharatpur. Built by Hindu Jat rulers. Sandstone structure.

name: Laxman Temple
description: 400 years old temple.

name: Buns and Tins
description: Open air restaurant.

name: Laxmi Vilas Palace Hotel
description: A heritage hotel with 30 spacious rooms, modern amenities and facilities.

name: Shagun Guest House
price: Single: ₹80, Double: ₹90; both with shared bathroom
address: Nawab Gali, inside Mathura Gate, Tara Mahendra Colony

name: Swaraj Resorts
description: Pool, wifi, multi-cuisine restaurant, well-stocked bar, and lush green garden.

name: Gajner Palace
description: A jewel in the Thar Desert, the palace is built on the embankment of a lake. Built by H.H. Maharaja Sir Ganga Singhji of Bikaner, this Grand Heritage property is spread over 6000 acres. Gajner Palace was used as a hunting resort by the former Maharajas and visiting British dignitaries during the days of the Raj.

name: Jain Temple Bhandasar
description: An ornate two-storied Jain temple with vibrantly adorned paintings with gold leaf patterns. Marble pillars bearing floral arabesques, multi colored walls and floors appeal to the senses. This temple is visited by many devotees daily and worth the visit.

name: Junagarh Fort
description: The fort was built by Raja Rai Singh, the sixth ruler of Bikaner who reigned from 1571 to 1612. It is a fort of the Bikaner royal family. You will get a chance to know about the history of the Bikaner royal family. Also has a museum which displays weapons and ornaments of the previous era. This is one of the oldest forts and was one of the few forts in India that was never defeated. One of the kings saved all Hindus in India from being converted to Islam by emperor Aurangzeb.

name: Karni Mata Temple
description: Located at Deshnok, 32 kilometres from Bikaner. This is a temple of a local deity, "Karni Mata". It is believed that the "Karni Mata" used to take care of the Rajputana family. This temple has a rat infestation but the locals believe them to be holy. You will likely be told that seeing a certain white rat is very auspicious, but if you press further most locals will tell you there is always one or two visible around the temple. Be careful while walking inside the temple: You might accidentally step on a rat.

name: Laxmi Niwas Palace
description: The Laxmi Niwas Palace is a former residential palace of the king of the former Bikaner state, Maharajah Ganga Singh in Bikaner in the Indian state of Rajasthan. It was designed by the British architect, Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob in the year 1902, completed in year 1926, and it is part of Lalgarh palace. The style of architecture is Indo-Saracenic. It is now a luxury hotel owned by Golden Triangle Fort & Palace P. Ltd.

name: Lalgarh
description: Lalgarh is another fort of the Rajputana family. Some of the Rajputana kings used to stay here. You will see the royal story of the Rajputana family.

name: Rampuriya Haveli
description: Built by Balujee Chalva commissioned by the rich merchant Rampuria family. This represents the opulence and architectural splendor of Bikaner. Flowers, birds and animals carved in red sandstone almost come alive. These priceless homes are more than 400 years old.

name: Shivbari Temple
description: This is a centuries old Shiva temple. It has two huge "Bawris" (water reservoirs). Thousands of people visit this place every year. The Shiv Bari Park partially surrounds this temple.

name: Charkha
description: A souvenir shop run by the local Ngo Hastshilp, a society for handicrafts which is supporting ancient crafts in the villages of Bikaner. It has taken its inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi and is making traditional hand-woven fabric known very famously in India as "Khadi".

name: Chhappan Bhog
description: One of the oldest fast food joints of Bikaner. The Rajkachori of this place is a show stealer, and a must for all those who are in for a chaat-treat. Other Good items on the menu include the Rava Dosa, with amazing fresh coconut chutney. The typical Indian-Chinese Chowmein is also lip-smacking.

name: Sankhla Kesar Kulfi
description: If you have a sweet tooth, particularly a penchant for Indian sweets and are looking for some relief in the rising temperatures of Bikaner, then you need to drop by at Sankhla Kesar Kulfi. The place promises to sell the best Kesar kulfi, and most of the consumers vouch for it; refreshingly cool. .

name: Hotel Sagar
price: Single Room: from ₹1620 to ₹4350. Double Room: from ₹1800 to ₹4350. Breakfast included.
description: It's a high end place in a palace. Huge, kind, attentive staff, they pamper you.

name: Hotel Shri Ram Heritage
price: Double Room: from ₹1000 to ₹3000. Single Room: from ₹800 to ₹1500. Breakfast & Taxes excluded
description: Nicely decorated spacious rooms, with attached baths having hot and cold running water, in a calm residential area. Open Courtyard in front and rear with big open terrace upstairs.

name: The Laxmi Niwas Palace
description: 106 year old palace, which is the former residential palace of the king. 45 standard rooms and 15 suites, all air-conditioned and many of them have direct access to an open terrace. Indoor games like billiards and ping pong, WiFi, conference rooms, a bar and a swimming pool. Rajasthani folk singers/dancers perform at the palace every evening. They have pictures of the royal family with the relevant historical factoids on the hallway walls which can be very informative for those interested, and they also arrange 'Sand dune dinners' with cultural programs at a desert site nearby.

name: Kirti Stambha
description: Kirti Stambha ("Fame Tower") is a 22 m (72 ft) high tower built on a 9.1 m (30 ft) base with 4.6 ft (1.4 m) at the top, is adorned with Jain sculptures on the outside and is older (probably 12th century) and smaller than the Victory Tower. Built by a Bagherwal Jain merchant Jijaji Rathod, it is dedicated to Adinath, the first Jain tirthankar (revered Jain teacher). In the lowest floor of the tower, naked figures of the various tirthankars of the Jain pantheon are seen in special niches formed to house them. A narrow stairway with 54 steps leads through the six stories to the top. The top pavilion that was added in the 15th century has 12 columns.

name: Meera Temple
description: Built by Maharana Kumbha in 1449, this lord Vishnu Temple has beautiful idols in its sanctum, mendap and pillars. In the same premises, there is a small temple of Lord Krishna.

name: Padmini's Palace
description: This palace, a white building, a three storied structure (a 19th century reconstruction of the original), is located in the southern part of the fort. Chhatris (pavilions) crown the palace roofs and a water moat surrounds the palace. This style of palace became the forerunner of other palaces built in the state with the concept of Jal Mahal (palace surrounded by water). It is at this Palace where Alauddin was permitted to glimpse at the mirror image of Rani Padmini, wife of Maharana Rattan Singh. It is widely believed that this glimpse of Padmini's beauty besotted him and convinced him to destroy Chittor in order to possess her. Maharana Rattan Singh was killed and Rani Padmini committed Jauhar. Rani Padmini's beauty is compared to that of Cleopatra and her life story is an eternal legend in the history of Chittor, in particular and of the Mewar state in general.

name: Rana Kumbha's Palace
price: [Admission Fee: ₹2 for Indians, ₹50 for foreign tourists. Camera: ₹50 extra]
description: At the entrance gate near the Vijaya Stamba, Rana Kumbha's palace (in ruins), the oldest monument, is located. The palace included elephant and horse stables and a temple to Lord Shiva. Maharana Udai Singh, the founder of Udaipur, was born here; the popular folk lore linked to his birth is that his maid Panna Dhay saved him by substituting her son in his place as a decoy, which resulted in her son getting killed by Banbir. The prince was spirited away in a fruit basket. The palace is built with plastered stone. The remarkable feature of the palace is its splendid series of canopied balconies. Entry to the palace is through Suraj Pol that leads into a courtyard. Rani Meera, the famous poetess saint, also lived in this palace. This is also the palace where Rani Padmini, consigned herself to the funeral pyre in one of the underground cellars, as an act of jauhar along with many the other women. The Nau Lakha Bandar (literal meaning: nine lakh [900 000] treasury) building, the royal treasury of Chittor was also located close by. Now, across from the palace is a museum and archeological office. The Singa Chowri temple is also nearby.

name: Vijay Stambha
alt: Victory Tower, Vijaya Stambha or Jay Stamba
price: Free Entry for Indians. For foreign tourist charged ₹50
description: The tower is called the symbol of Chittor and a particularly bold expression of triumph, was erected by Rana Khumba between 1458 and 1468 to commemorate his victory over Mahmud Shah I Khalji, the Sultan of Malwa, in 1440 AD.Built over a period of ten years, it raises 37.2 m (122 ft) over a 4.4 m² (47 ft²) base in nine stories accessed through a narrow circular staircase of 157 steps (the interior is also carved) up to the 8th floor, from where there is good view of the plains and the new town of Chittor. The dome, which was a later addition, was damaged by lightning and repaired during the 19th century. The Stamba is now illuminated during the evenings and gives a beautiful view.

name: Fateh Prakash Palace
description: Built by Maharana Fateh Singh, this huge palace is of modern style. This place has been named Fateh Prakesh after Maharana Fateh Singh. There is a big Ganesh idol, a fountain, and different frescoes which are to be seen to be believed. This palace, now a museum, has a rich collection of sculptures from temples and buildings in the Fort.

name: Gaumukh Reservoir
description: A deep tank filled by a spring coming from a 'cow mouth', situated at the edge of the cliff. It is considered to be sacred where you can feed the fishes.

name: Jain Temples
description: There are six Jain temples on the fort of Chittor. The largest and chief among them is the temple of Bhagawan Adinatha with fifty-two devkulikas. The place of this temple is known as ‘Sattavish devri’. It means that at some time in the past, there were twenty-seven temples here. The Digamabar Jain Kirtistambh and seven-storied Kirtistambh are two among them. The seven-storied Kirtistambh was built in the fourteenth century in memories of Bhagawan Adinatha

name: Kalika Mata Temple
description: Across from Padmini’s palace is the Kalika Mata Temple, Chittorgarh Fort. A Sun temple dated to the 8th century dedicated to Surya -the sun-god, was destroyed in the 14th century. It was rebuilt as a Kali temple.

name: Tulja Bhavani Temple
description: on the west side of the fort is the ancient Tulja Bhavani temple built to worship goddess Tulja, considered sacred. The tope khana (cannon foundry) is located next to this temple in a courtyard, where a few old cannons are still seen.

name: Bassi Fort Palace
description: Serves paranthas, vegetarian food & regional dishes.

name: Castle Bijaipur
description: Poolside restaurant serves traditional Rajasthani food.

name: Hotel Meera
description: Serves Indian and Mughal meals.

name: Hotel Padmini
address: River View, Near Sainik School, Bhilwara Road
description: Serves pure vegetarian meals.

name: Pratap Palace
description: Serves continental, Indian & Chinese as well as local dishes (dal-baati-choorma and Lal Mas)

name: Hotel Gaurav Palace
address: Sector1, Gandhi Nagar, near Apsara Talkies

name: Hotel Padmini
description: A good and scenic location alongside the river and with a panoramic view of the fort.

name: Hotel Shree Ji
description: The hotel comprises 31 rooms with attached bathrooms, fully a.c., open balcony. A vegetarian hotel equipped with dining hall.

name: RTDC Hotel Panna
description: The hotel is just like standard hotel. A/c, room heater, room service, restaurant and a helpful staff.

name: Bassi Fort Palace
description: A heritage hotel owned by the Welcome group, it has 16 well appointed rooms and suites. The hotel is also a treasure house of many historical deeds and artifacts.

name: Castle Bijaipur
description: Calm and tranquil. Excellent place to relax and unwind amidst nature.

name: Jaisalmer Fort
description: Also known as the “Sonar Quila” or "Sonal Kella" or "Sonar Kila" as pronounced differently in parts of India. Colourful shades of the setting sun and golden hues of the desert ambience give a fairy tale look to this mega structured fort. The interior of this fort is amazing. It is a 'working fort' meaning that unlike every other fort in India, there are people living and working within its walls. Tourists can also visit many 'havelis' or Grand Houses of rich merchants, which are also having a touch of great classical interior and design.

name: Gadisar Lake
description: This is a rainwater lake which supplies water to the city. It is surrounded by temples and tombs of saints. Boat rides are offered. Nearby is the desert cultural centre and a local museum built out of the collections of a local schoolteacher Mr N.K. Sharma. This centre conducts puppet show in the morning and evening. There are people who will try to sell you bread to feed the huge number of catfish in the lake.

name: Jaisalmer War Museum
description: A museum displaying India's modern military history. There is a hall dedicated to the noted Battle of Longewala fought near Jaisalmer during the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971.

name: Jaisalmer Folklore Museum
description: A museum showcasing Rajasthan's folk heritage, arts and customs. There are two nightly half-hour long traditional puppet shows, starting at 6:30PM and 7:30 respectively, which is the highlight in the museum.

name: Sam Sand Dunes
description: These sand dunes are around 50 km from Jaisalmer city but one has to go there to have this altogether different experience. This is an amazing sight and the sunset view from there is stunning. Also don't miss the camel ride or a camel cart ride over the semi desert. You can stay overnight in one of the tented lodges along the road. There are many to choose from - the lodges stretch for about 10 km.

name: Suryagarh
description: It's "only" a hotel, but you still wonder how they built it in the middle of the desert. Lush gardens, lovely pools and fountains, impressive stone carving techniques. While most cannot afford to stay there, stopping to have tea is an option that allows you to have a look at lesser cost.

name: Sunset point
description: Lovely cenotaphs. Fantastic pictures.

name: Bronze statues
description: Hindu statues in bronze or silver plated Buddha statues. Various collectibles: prayer mills, thangkas, mandalas.

name: Jewel Caravan
description: Large choice of silver jewellery, Tibetan jewellery, precious and semi-precious gemstones. Lovely Kashmiri textiles collection. Singing bowls and statues. Friendly service.

name: Shayama Cashmere Store
description: Mr. Sushil Kumar, the owner, is a very honest and knowledgeable person. In this store, there is a nice collection of cashmere pashmina shawls.

name: Silk & Cashmere
description: Scarves, shawls, stalls, kurtas. Silk & cashmere blends, with or without embroidery.

name: Silver Jewelry
description: Silver Rajasthani jewelry (necklaces, bangles, pendants, earrings, rings). Gemstones (rings and pendants), Tibetan jewelry (turquoise & coral inlaid jewelry).

name: Indian crafts Boutique-Museum
description: Nice informative brochures available about jewelry making and different jewelry styles in India, detailed explanations about textile production. Insight into Indian history and local history as well: Jaisalmer, the silk trade, etc. For those interested in alternative medicine, there is even information about ayurveda, chakras and meditation tools. Nicely presented and fairly well researched.

name: Anchal Sweets
description: Fresh kachori and samosa.

name: Free Tibet Restaurant
address: Fort Rd, Khejer Para, Manak Chowk, Amar Sagar Pol
description: The restaurant has one of the highest rooftops in Jaisalmer. They serve a combination of Tibetan, Chinese, Indian and European cuisine. The thukpa is highly popular. It is more affordable than the other restaurants with good views of the fort.

name: German Bakery
description: Good lemon cake. Decent croissants. Almond cookies. Delicious tea. Great place to have a "western-style" breakfast.

name: Lakeview Lounge Restaurant
description: This restaurant serves excellent food. The Porridge w/ Banana Honey (₹40), Mushroom Cheese Tomato Burger (₹65) and the 'Speghatti Spinesh Tomato Cheese' (₹70) are highly recommended. The service is excellent as well because of the speed and courtesy of their staff. The restaurant has some of the best views in all of Jaisalmer, at the second level of the restaurant. They also have free WiFi at the restaurant and the attached Hotel Surja.

name: Little Italy
description: Real pizza, with actually good mozzarella cheese. Very decent pasta as well. Amazing view on the Fort from the terrace, fun low tables-and-cushions concept inside.

name: Midtown restaurant
description: This restaurant is in front of the Golden fort. The view is amazing and the food is fine with friendly service. The homemade Dutch apple pie is delicious. Pullavs are great.
