The outer wall has niches in the wall containing stucco figurines representing various aspects of Lord Siva. The complex also has a do-chal structure north-west of the main shrine.

name: Joysagar Devi Dol
description: Again, a creation of Ahom King Rudra Singha (reign: 1696 – 1714). This temple stands on the west bank of Joysagara, near the north-west corner. The temple follows the do-chala architecture style with a do-chala mandap.

name: Ghanashyam House
description: It is an early 18th-century brick temple built during the reign of the king Rudra Singha dedicated to the architect Ghanashyam. The temple was constructed by one Ghanasyamuddin Khanikar, later renamed as Ghanashyam. It is believed that Ghanashyam was earlier a Muslim who converted to Hinduism. As a result the temple is a mixture of Hindu and Muslim architectural elements. The brick-built temple has rich terracotta ornamentation. The temple is located inside the Swargadeo Rudrasingha Udyan Complex. For access to the temple, entry tickets and camera charges of the park are to be paid

name: Jagadhatri Doul
description: Jagadhatri Doul was built during the period of Swargadeo Shiva Singha. The brother of Phuleswari Kunwori, Harinath Borpatra Gohain worshipped Jagadhatri Devi. Neraby is a Vishnu Doul constructed by Hari Nath Borpatra Gohain during the time of Swargadeo Shiva Singha (1774-1744)

name: Fakua Dol
description: Fakuwa Doul was constructed by Swargadeo Rudra Singha in remembrance of his mother Queen Joymati Kunwari, between 1703 and 1704 A.D. Although considered a temple, locals believe it to be a maidam, a burial chamber of Ahom royals. It is believed to be a burial chamber of Queen Joymati, the patriotic wife of Swargadeo Gadadhar Singha. The pyramidical structure stands on an octagonal base. Four sets of stairs lead to the top, housing the shrine.

name: Ranganath Dol
description: Built in 1703 by Sukhrungphaa, the 30th Ahom king. The Shiva temple houses a lingam. A do-chala mandapa is attached to the sanctum. A newly built shed is attached to the do-chala mandap.

name: Hara Gouri Dol
description: This is a brick-built temple constructed during the reign of the Ahom king Swargadeo Rajeswar Singha (1751 – 1769 AD). The inner sanctum of the temple follows the do-chala style and is attached with a do-chala pavilion. The temple is profusely ornamented, with the upper part of the outerwall containing floral designs.

name: Talatal Ghar
description: Built by Rajeswara Singha (AD 1751-1769). All the rooms were connected with small passages. Talatal ghar had three storeys underground and four storeys above ground. The remains of this palace is standing tall in Sivasagar town. Though top levels of the palace having wooden works are completely destroyed. All the rooms were connected with small passages. Similarly the underground levels are closed for tourists. Bortop (guns) preserved in Talatal Ghar.

name: Gola Ghar
description: An ammunition storehouse used by the Ahom Kings. It was built during the reign of Chakradhwaj Singha (1663-1669 AD). It represents a rectangular brick hut with a two-layered (do-chala) roof. It has been renovated as a museum gallery. It displays various weapons, arms, armour, process of making gunpowder

name: Rang Ghar
description: A two-storied building, which was the royal sports-pavilion from which the Ahom kings and nobles witnessed games like buffalo fights and other sports at the Rupahi Pathar (pathar meaning field in Assamese) specially during Rangali Bihu festival in the Ahom capital, Rangpur. On the roof of the Rang Ghar is a design of an Ahom royal long boat. The building was constructed during the reign of Swargadeo Pramatta Singha in 1746. It is northeast of the Talatal Ghar, a multi-storied royal complex in Joysagar west of Sivasagar town, on the other side of the Assam Trunk (AT) Road in Sibsagar district in Assam.The Rang Ghar is said to be the oldest amphitheatre in Asia. The base of the monument has a series of arched entrances and atop the roof is a decorative pair of carved stone crocodiles. In many of these, only the brick framework exists with vestiges of sculptural adornments here and there. The Ahoms, who used special thin baked bricks, did not have the use of cement and, therefore, used a paste of rice and eggs as mortar for their construction.

name: Sivasagar Tank
description: The lake dates back to 1734 and was an initiative of Queen Ambika, wife of Ahom King Siva Singha (reign:1714 – 44). On the southern bank of the lake stands the Siva, Devi and Vishnu Dol. Queen Ambika also constructed the temples. Like the other temples of Sivasagar, these are also active temples, but unlike the others, they are visited by a large number of devotees every year.

name: Sivasagar Shiva Dol
description: Standing at 32 m it is the tallest of the temples in the Sivasagar region. The spire of the pancha-rath structure is accompanied by four smaller miniature spires (angashikhara) positioned precisely in the four cardinal directions. The mandap is of char-chala style. A thatched metal shed has been added in front of the mandap of the temple.

name: Sivasagar Vishnu Dol
description: The Devi Dol is located west of the Shiva Dol, and both temples face south. Here the mandap is do-chala and has a thatched metal shed extension. The spire has vertical ridges and has 8 turrets (2 each on 4 sides).

name: Sivasagar Devi Dol
description: This temple lies on the eastern part of the complex and faces west. The spire is built in honey comb style with 8 turrets.

name: Tai Ahom Museum
description: The 1992 museum showcases a fascinating repository providing an insight into the grandeur of the Ahom dynasty. From ornate goblets to ceremonial palanquins to swords, shields, canons from the Ahom royals. Beyond the royal collection, the museum exhibits items of everyday life for Assamese people, including fishing and hunting equipment. The museum also showcases a rich collection of rare manuscripts.

name: Kareng Ghar
description: Considered the finest example of Ahom architecture, it served as the administrative building of the kingdom. It was built of wood up to the reign of Swargadeo Pramatta Singha, 1751 AD. But Swargadeo Rajeswar Singha built the present permanent structure in 1752 AD with seven storied palace made of bricks and boulders.

name: Gola Ghar
description: which probably functioned as a store house.

name: Bishnu Dole, Namti
description: Vishnu Doul, Namti is a brick-built temple constructed by Namatial Bhagati Barbarua in the year 1775 A.D. during the reign of Swargadeo Gourinath Singha (1780 -1794)

name: Charaideo Museum
description: Provides an insight into the rituals of Ahom royal burial. The museum displays items recovered from the excavation of maidams, which include human bones, gold and ivory items.

name: Prashaanti Tourist Lodge
description: The lodge is operated by Department of Tourism and Assam Tourism Development Corporation Limited.

name: Aranya
description: Under Assam Tourism Development Corporation.

name: Borgos Resort
description: It is a lush green resort at the gate of the Kaziranga National Park.

name: IORA, The Retreat
description: Around 2 km from Kaziranga National Park. IORA has 42 rooms including 4 thematic suites, 4 supreme rooms, 23 luxury rooms and 11 deluxe rooms.

name: Landmark Woods
description: A resort near the western range of the park.

name: The Nature-Hunt Eco Camp
description: Relatively new and not commercialized. They provide excellent service as the owners personally take care of the guests. Apart from offering services in Kaziranga they also offer services in other North Eastern states and can arrange stay in all the national parks.

name: Wild Grass
description: They have specialist guides and very beautiful grounds. The resorts offer an old world charm Jungle resort environment, with no distractions of Cable Television. The rooms are large and comfortable, and staff efficient. Make advance reservations during season to avoid disappointment. The resort is a little away from the highway, and easy to miss. A simple phone call, and the lodge's vehicle will come to the highway to receive guests.

name: Wild Mahseer
description: Wild Mahaseer is a colonial plantation bungalow. This property is a historic one characterized by its Victorian architecture and has spacious rooms across four bungalows.

name: Tesco Resort
description: Tesco is 7 km from Kaziranga National Park. Tesco has 25 rooms including 1 suite, 12 Supreme deluxe rooms, and 10 Deluxe rooms.

name: Musa Jungle Retreat
description: There are three cottages of the resort: 1) Striped Panthera 2) Grazing Rhino 3) Bansbari Villa.

name: Nameri Eco Camp
description: The camp could become fully booked on weekends or national holidays well in advance. They also organize jungle walks and rafting tours.

name: Jia Bhorelli wild resort
description: They also organize jungle walks.

name: Auniati Satra
description: It is famous for "Paalnaam" and Apsara dances. It also houses an extensive assortment of ancient artefacts. It includes Assamese old utensils, jewellery and handicrafts.

name: Kamalabari Satra
description: It is a centre of art, culture, literature and classical studies. The finest boats on the island are made here. Its branch

name: Benegenaati Satra
description: It is a storehouse of antiques and an advanced centre of performing arts. The royal robes of the Ahom king, Swargadeo Gadadhar Singha, are preserved here. Also on display is the royal gold umbrella.

name: Garamurh Satra
description: Famous for Rassleela (celebrated in end autumn). The satara has a collection of large cannons (bartop)

name: Samaguri Satra
description: Famous for mask making.

name: Dakhinpat Satra
description: Dakhinpat Satra is located on the southern part of the Majuli island and is on the north bank of the Brahmaputra River. Famous for Raasleela festival.

name: Komal Saul
description: Komal saul is a unique type of rice from Assam that can be eaten without cooking. It is rendered fluffy and edible by being soaked in water for a short time. The rice may be eaten with milk or curd, jaggery, yogurt after being immersed in warm water for just 15-20 minutes.

name: Bora saul
description: Bora saul is a variety of glutinous rice found in Assam. It has an important role in Assamese traditional occasions like Bihu. It is used in Jolpan (snacks) and Pitha (ricecake or pancake). Soaked and ground bora saul is used in preparing Pitha. Boiled bora saul is served as Jolpan with curd or milk, jaggery or sugar.

name: Joha Restaurant
description: Serves authentic Assamese food, including thalis.

name: Circuit House Garamur
description: 8 two-bedded rooms and 2 VIP suites

name: Prashanti Eco Tourism Resort (Assam Tourism Development Corporation)
description: The lodge is operated by Department of Tourism and Assam Tourism Development Corporation Limited.

name: La Maison de Ananda
description: Traditional hut built in 2005 by a French architect that was then donated to the actual owner, Manjit Risang and his family. Not particularly comfortable but it is interesting to see how local people lived in the past (in more remote parts of Majuli many still live in such houses). Next to the hut there is a concrete building with more modern facilities. Other in-line huts were built later to accommodate extra guests. Breakfast is served in the morning and it possible to have dinner with the family that is still cooking in the traditional way. Moderate price for a great and unique experience. The owner is super friendly and knows the area very well, he can give you precious suggestions.

name: Panam Ningthou Sacred Site
alt: Panam Ningthou Laipham (Chakpa Panam Ningthou Meithoupirol Shanglen)
description: This sacred site houses a temple dedicated to God Panam Ningthou (patron deity of Andro town), inside which a holy fireplace is still burning for the last 2000 years since the 1st century AD. It also has art and cultural museums.

name: Mutua Museum
alt: Mutua Bahadur Museum, Andro Cultural Complex
description: It is an artistic, cultural and historical museum cum cultural complex. It houses ancient potteries, antique coins, old manuscripts, paintings, basketries, bell metals, jewelries, wood carvings, replicas of the houses and the doll representations of Meitei ethnicity as well as the 34 recognised tribesmen communities of Manipur.

name: Santhei Natural Park
description: It is a Natural Recreational Park that has an artificial lake and an artificial island, surrounded by an artificial forest along a gentle hill slope. It is a picnic area as well as a film shooting location. Boating facility is also available in the lake.

name: Kakching Garden
description: This is the most popular garden in Manipur. It is famous for having unique topiary plants in the state. It houses many scared sites of Sanamahism as well as Hinduism.

name: Kakching Aerodrome
description: It is a World War II aerodrome used by the British Army, against the Indian National Army. This aerodrome used to serve all the essential things to the British Army during the wartime. It is mainly occupied by the Assam Rifles.

name: Langol Temple
description: This is a temple dedicated to Goddess Langol Lairembi of Sanamahism. The temple premise is generally crowded with the assembly of devotees, including temple dancers and singers. There is a thick woodland and a hill next to the temple complex. Besides religious purposes, people of other religious sects also come to the adjacent woods for outdoor recreation (including backpacking, bushwalking, hiking, trekking) as well as nature photography.

name: The Nest
description: It is a holiday campsite cum resort. It provides most of the vacationers' wants, food, drink, lodging, sports, entertainment, and shopping on its premises. Holidaymakers will find this place in an affordable price.

name: Game Village
description: It is a countryside mega human settlement established by the Government for providing the accommodations for sportspersons during international, national as well as state level grand sports events. During vacancy on sports events, government employees are allowed to stay here as quarters. Tourists are also allowed to stay here.

name: Beit-El Synagogue
description: It is one of the few synagogues in the Lamphelpat area. Here, prayer, study, assembly and reading of the religious scriptures are mainly done.

name: Manipur Zoological Garden
description: A smallish zoo but teeming with wildlife. Spanning 8 hectares, in total there are 55 species of animals and 420 animals overall with 14 species endangered and endemic. The rarest and most enchanting of these is the Sangai, also known as the brow-antlered deer.

name: Ebudhou Thangjing Temple
description: Annually, traditional 'Lai Haraoba' is celebrated in May. During the festival, people from all over the state, assemble to seek the blessings of God 'Ebudhou Thangjing' (Eputhou Thangching). This festival continues for almost a month or more. During the festival, a mega dance and singing program is offered to the God.

name: The Ina Museum
description: A war memorial museum focusing about the Second World War, and is the only WWII museum in the state of Manipur.

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
description: The world's only floating national park.

name: Khana Chaopa Wangpurel Khuman Temple
address: Near Porompat Water Supply Mamang Lampak
description: This is a temple dedicated to Wangbren (Wangpurel or Wangpulel), god of water of Sanamahism.

name: Yumnam Gunindro Art Gallery
description: It is an art gallery displaying visual arts of many artistic disciplines.

name: Yangoi Ningthou Lai Temple
description: It is a temple dedicated to God Yangoi Ningthou of Sanamahism.

name: Sijagurumayum Temple
description: It is a temple dedicated to many gods of Hinduism. Here, many idols of Hindu deities are installed.

name: Satya Sai Baba Temple
description: It is a temple dedicated to Sai Baba of Hinduism.

name: Khongjom War Memorial Complex
description: This is the largest war memorial complex in Manipur. It commemorates the freedom fighters and matyrs of Anglo-Manipuri War that took place in Khongjom, Manipur. It houses the tallest statue of sword in the world.

name: Thoubal Keithel
description: It is one of the largest market complexes in Manipur. Here, one can get everything, starting from local handloom and handicrafts products to local seasonal fruits and vegetables.

name: Sirohi National Park
description: The world's only natural habitat for the Shirui lily (Lilium macklineae), it also hosts tigers, leopards and a variety of rare bird species such as the Blyth's tragopan. Shirui Peak during monsoon season is covered with the blooms of the exotic lily. The best time to see the Shirui lily flower is the third or fourth week of May when the annual Shirui Festival takes place.

name: Chiko Adventures
description: They offer customized camping, trekking, and cycling tour activities and can help you with information and village homestays in the surrounding area. You can also hire camping equipment and bicycles from them. Thecation is in the same building of 25 Degree North Hotel. You can ask the 25 Degree North Hotel and they will direct you to Chiko Adventures.

name: Chico Adventures
description: Offers customised camping, trekking and cycling tour activities, information and village guest accommodation in the surrounding area. It is also possible to hire camping equipment and bicycles from them.

name: 25 Degree North Hotel
description: One of a very few accommodations in Ukhrul that offer free Wi-Fi. It has a restaurant on the second floor, offering common foods such fried rice and noodles and western-style breakfast. The hotel also offers hot water, shower, laundry, and airport transfers.

name: Living Root Bridges
description: The Living Root Bridges created by people of Khasi tribe is one of the most amazing examples of bio engineering. Created over years by carefully guiding the roots of Ficus benghalensis these bridges can last up to 500 years. The most famous Living Root Bridges are in the village of Nongriat and Mawlynnong.

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: An exciting and beautiful for adventure seekers. Most tourists explores the caves bare foot as the floor is damp. Some passageways are narrow and steep so a minimum level of fitness is required to view the cave in its entirety.

name: Avron Restaurant
description: Good vegetarian and non-vegetarian food. Diverse range of India, Chinese and international.

name: Nongriat Guest house
description: The guesthouse is very basic but reasonably priced. Recommended for people who can tolerate little discomfort to enjoy pleasures like taking bath in natural swimming pool and spot beautiful butterflies.

name: Saimika Park
description: Saimika Park is a 65-acre plot of land with a restaurant, 7 guest rooms, two of which are made in traditional design using locally available construction material, a dormitory is available for backpackers. A conference hall is also available. Some of the amenities include a plunging pool, a basketball court, tennis court, fishing pond and trekking guides to take you to visit community forests. There are also indoor board games available.

name: By the way
description: Great place for backpackers. Both rooms and shared bathroom (hot water) are well maintained and clean. The owner is very knowledgeable local who knows the area well. Do not bother trying to make reservation, just show up and he will find you a spot. As of March 2023 they no longer have hostel dorms, but there are probably a couple of rooms to rent.

name: Polo Orchid Resort
description: Rooms with elegant decor and a magnificent view of Nohsngithiang Falls. A jacuzzi and spacious balcony facilities are also provided. On-site, there is an open-air grill restaurant, the Sky Grill, and a multi-cuisine restaurant called Sohra House Bar and Bistro

name: Saikuti Hall
description: This is where most of the concerts and celebrations are held. A unique museum has also been established in the hall where local painters demonstrate their skill and exhibit their works.

name: Fiara Tui
description: This river is 65 km from Champhai (known as "the purest summer water on Earth") has its source in the Tan Tlang Mountain.

name: Hnahlan
description: This is an area which near Champhai with vineyards and a beautiful climate.

name: Lamsial Puk
description: Cave is near Farkawn village.

name: Lianchhiari Tlang
description: This is a rocky cliff ledge near the village of Dungtlang.

name: Mizo Hlakungpui Mual
description: A monument at the southern end of Khawbung village that commemorates the Mizo classical composers.

name: Murlen National Park
description: A home to a wide variety of flora and fauna.

name: Mura Puk
description: This lake is in Zote village. There are 6 caves (pits) at this site.

name: Tan Tlang
description: A legendary mountain (85 km from Champhai) located near Vaphai village.

name: Thasiama Seno Neihna
description: This is a plateau on a rugged hill near Vaphai village.

name: Zokhawthar
description: A trading town on the border with Myanmar.

name: Hotel Holiday Home
description: Pleasant budget hotel. Nice view of the valley from its rooftop.

name: Tourist Lodge
description: Run by State Government. Clean and pleasant place to stay

name: Dimapur Airport
description: IndiGo has Boeing flights to Dimapur from Kolkata and New Delhi. Air India Express has flights to Guwahati. Alliance Air flies to Imphal

name: Dimapur Ao Baptist Church
description: The largest church in Asia.

name: Boxanagar Ruins
description: A Buddhist archaeological site, which first emerged during the Khadga dynasty, a Buddhist dynasty which ruled the eastern Bengal from 625 to 716. Historians believe that the Buddhist culture flourished in Boxanagar between the 6th and the 12th century, a period marked by rich history, learning, and the arts.

name: Kamalasagar
description: An artificial lake popular for picknickers and location of a Navaratri fair.

name: Kasbeswari Kali Temple
description: A temple built atop a hill by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in the late 15th century. The Kamalasagar Lake in front of the temple rightly enhances its beauty.

name: Rowa Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A small sanctuary reflecting the natural vegetation of the region. You will be able to spot several species of birds and primates.

name: Unakoti
description: Historic site containing large and mysterious yet fascinating rock-cut and stone sculptures of Hindu deity Shiva.

name: Swapna Momos
address: Kalibari Road, near Kali Dighir Par, Dharmanagar
description: Small, inexpensive specialist momo shop known for steamed momos, spicy chutney and soup. Mainly an evening stop rather than a full-service restaurant.

name: Restaurant J.C. Plaza
address: DNV Road, near BSNL Office, Dharmanagar
description: Casual family restaurant serving Indian, Chinese-style and local favourites. Fried rice and chicken dishes are among the commonly ordered meals.

name: Ottimo Cucina
address: 1st floor, KTM/Royal Enfield Showroom, College Road, Nayapara, Dharmanagar
description: Modern sit-down restaurant with Indian, Chinese-style and international dishes. A useful option for travellers looking for a more contemporary dining room rather than a simple local eatery.

name: Juri Tourist Lodge
address: Ramkrishna Mission Road, Office Tilla, Algapur, Dharmanagar
description: Government tourism accommodation in Dharmanagar and a useful base for trips around North Tripura. Reserve ahead when possible, particularly during festivals and busy travel periods.

name: Hotel Divine Palace
address: Station Road, opposite LIC Office, New Bazar, Dharmanagar
description: Small centrally located hotel useful for railway travellers and short stopovers. Its Station Road location makes local transport and restaurants easy to reach.

name: Hotel Stay Inn
address: Batarashi Road / Tilthai Road, Rajbari, Dharmanagar
description: Small budget-oriented hotel in the Rajbari area, convenient for travellers using Dharmanagar as a base for regional sightseeing.

name: Neermahal
alt: Bengali: নীরমহল Nīrmahal, Kokborok: Twijilikma Nuyung
description: Literally the "Water Palace", the Neermahal is a royal palace of the former Kingdom of Tripura, in the middle of the Rudrasagar Lake. Built by Maharaja Bir Bikram in 1930, the Neermahal is one of the two water palaces in India, the other being the Jal Mahal of Jaipur, and is significantly larger than the Jaipur one. The palace is divided into two parts: the Andar Mahal at the western side for the royal family, and the open-air theatre at the eastern side for drama, theatre, dance and other cultural events. The palace has 24 rooms in total. The Neermahal has two stairways inside leading down to a ghat on the water of the lake, called the Rajghat, which was used by the maharajas to go to the palace by hand-powered boats. On the ceiling, the palace houses one of the most beautiful terrace gardens of India.

name: Feni River
description: The river forms the international boundary between India and Bangladesh. Public roads and permitted riverside areas provide views across the water toward Ramgarh. Remain outside fenced or restricted border areas and follow instructions from security personnel.

name: Maitri Setu
description: A 1.9-km road bridge connecting Sabroom with Ramgarh in Bangladesh. It was inaugurated in 2021 as part of plans to improve access between northeastern India and the Chattogram region. The bridge and land port are working security and customs installations, not unrestricted sightseeing areas. Do not attempt to enter the bridge without authorization.

name: Sabroom railway station
description: The southern terminus of Tripura's railway system. The small modern station is of interest to railway enthusiasts and marks the end of the broad-gauge line from Agartala. Obtain permission before undertaking elaborate photography or entering non-public railway areas.

name: Kalapania Nature Park
price: A small admission or activity charge may apply
description: A landscaped nature park developed around a large lake between low wooded hills. Attractions have included walking paths, bridges, a nature-interpretation centre, boating and cottages. Maintenance and activity availability can vary, so confirm conditions before making a special journey.

name: Is-Land Eco Park
description: A small landscaped eco-park near the international-border region and the Ludhua tea-growing area. It contains paths, greenery, bridges and places for a quiet family outing. Carry identification because security checks may occur in the wider border zone.

name: Mahamuni Pagoda
description: A Buddhist shrine and monastery serving the Mog community and pilgrims from across Tripura. A major annual fair is usually held around March or April. Dress respectfully, remove shoes where required and ask before photographing worshippers.

name: Srinagar Border Haat
hours: Tue 10AM–3:30PM according to the district administration; confirm before travelling
description: A controlled weekly market on the India–Bangladesh boundary where approved vendors and visitors from nearby communities trade local goods. It is not an ordinary duty-free market open automatically to every tourist. Carry identification and confirm visitor eligibility and opening status with the Sabroom administration before setting out.

name: Dakshinayan Tourist Lodge
description: A Tripura Tourism property operated under lease, offering basic accommodation in Sabroom. Call before arrival to confirm that the numbers remain current, room availability, meals, hot water, air conditioning and accepted payment methods.

name: Tripura Sundari Temple
price: Free; offerings and donations cost extra
hours: Daily; arrive early to avoid the largest queues
description: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas and Tripura's most important pilgrimage sites. Maharaja Dhanya Manikya constructed the present temple in 1501. Its form resembles a traditional Bengal hut and is sometimes compared with the shape of a tortoise, giving rise to the name Koorma Peetha. The approach contains stalls selling flowers, offerings and the local milk sweet known as peda. Dress respectfully and expect extensive queues during Diwali.

name: Kalyan Sagar
description: A sacred lake forming part of the Matabari temple complex. It contains fish and freshwater turtles revered by devotees. Keep plastic and food packaging away from the water, do not fish or enter the lake, and follow local instructions concerning animal feeding.

name: Bhubaneswari Temple
description: A 17th-century temple built by Maharaja Govinda Manikya, probably between 1660 and 1675. Its architecture combines the curved roof form of a Bengal temple with decorative towers and floral motifs. Rabindranath Tagore used the temple and the neighbouring royal setting in Rajarshi and Bisarjan. It is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Old Rajbari Palace
description: Ruins of the former royal complex used by the Manikya rulers when Udaipur was Tripura's capital. Little of the palace remains intact, but the site provides historical context for Bhubaneswari Temple and the works of Rabindranath Tagore. Avoid climbing unstable masonry.

name: Gunabati Group of Temples
description: A compact group of three 17th-century temples. The principal temple is associated with Maharani Gunabati and an inscription dating to 1668. The monuments display the curved-roof temple style characteristic of historic Tripura and are protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Tepania Eco Park
price: Admission and activity charges may apply
hours: Daytime; confirm weekly closing day locally
description: A 155-hectare forest recreation area established in 1995. It contains walking paths, gardens, picnic areas and woodland vegetation. Facilities have included a treehouse, children's areas and tourist log huts, but individual activities may close for maintenance.

name: Atithi Fast Food
description: A straightforward local option for snacks and quick meals in the central commercial area.

name: Sagar Cafeteria
description: A convenient stop for pilgrims and visitors around Matabari. Opening and meal availability may depend on temple crowds and the season.

name: Gouri Hotel and Guest House
description: A local guesthouse and restaurant serving simple meals. Confirm that the published number and dining arrangements remain current before making a special journey.

name: Gomati Yatri Niwas
description: A Tripura Tourism property operated under lease. Its central location is useful for the lakes, markets and transport services. Contact the current operator to confirm room rates, meals, air conditioning, hot water and accepted payment methods.

name: Gunabati Yatri Niwas
description: A Tripura Tourism property convenient for pilgrims and early-morning temple visits. Confirm current availability and facilities directly, particularly during Diwali.

name: Tepania Tourist Log Hut
price: Rates are displayed through Tripura Tourism's booking service
description: Forest accommodation associated with Tepania Eco Park. It offers a quieter setting than central Udaipur but is less convenient without private transport. Confirm booking status, park access, meals and check-in arrangements before travelling.

name: Chinese Fishing Nets
description: Serves as the official icon of Kochi and is a testimony of relations between the Ancient Chinese Empires and the Cochin Kingdom. They were gifted by the Chinese Emperor Kubalagi to the Kochi King in the 14th century. There were more than 100, though only a few remain in working condition.

name: David Hall
description: This 315 year-old Dutch bungalow was the official residence of Dutch Army commanders, the most famous being Hendrik Adriaan van Rheede tot Draakestein, who authored Horticus Malabaricus. The complex belongs to the Netherlands Govt. agency CNO which has been renovated to open a large art gallery, a traditional Dutch performing arts centre and a large studio for young painters. The building is a classic specimen of colonial Dutch architecture with elaborate Dutch gardens. Check at the reception to know the schedule of cultural performances.

name: Dutch Palace
description: Constructed by the Portuguese in 1568 as a gift to the Maharaja of Cochin, Veera Kerala Varma, after he granted permission to construct Fort Immanuel. During the Dutch siege of Cochin, many parts of the original palace were destroyed. However, the Dutch Governor repaired the palace and renamed it as Dutch Palace. Coronations of Cochin Maharajas are held here. A large throne and coronation costumes are on display, and there is an extensive collection of royal chariots, swords and other artefacts. The most interesting part is the mural room, which has the entire Ramayana and Mahabharata depicted in a single mural.

name: Greenix Tourist Theater
description: A good cultural theatre with a gallery, food court and mini museum.

name: International Pepper Exchange
description: Kochi's answer to New York's Wall Street, but instead of money, it's all about pepper trading. This is the world's only pepper exchange. Nowadays, trading all happens online, so there is not much to see any more except the historical place.

name: Kumbalangi Integrated Tourism Village
description: India's first eco-tourist village, this award-winning initiative allows tourists to explore and enjoy the authentic rural culture with the cooperation of natives without disturbing their natural lifestyle. Tourists to this island village have chances to explore rural work styles, a specialised local paddy cultivation, canoeing in a country boat in a maze of mangrove forests or enjoying fishing or partying in rural style with locals. In order to maintain best eco-protection practices, several restrictions are placed on the use of plastics, smoking or even carrying soft drinks.

name: Peirce Leslie Bungalow
description: The only surviving bungalow built in authentic Portuguese style, it was the home and office of a famous English merchant family - the Leslies. It has been restored into a boutique hotel. The hotel management allows tourists to explore the grand exteriors and public interior spaces.

name: Princess Street
description: The most famous street of Fort Kochi, which gives you a slice of authentic colonial European architecture. The only street that never faced any raid or demolitions in the past, Princess street is a perfect destination for an evening walk with numerous western-style cafes, souvenir shops, art galleries and heritage complexes.

name: VOC Gate
description: The only remains of the office of the Dutch East India Company is this large wooden gate with a monogram VOC (Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie), the emblem of Dutch East India Company.

name: Willingdon Island
description: A large man-made island made from sand dredged from the backwaters to deepen the Kochi Port. Named after Long Willingdon, the then-Viceroy of India, it houses the Kochi Port, the Indian Southern Naval Command Headquarters and many five-star hotels.

name: Dutch Cemetery
description: Established in 1724, it is the oldest European cemetery in India. It houses 104 tombs. It is normally locked.

name: Bastion Bungalow
description: Typical Indo-Dutch architecture, this bungalow was built on the site of the erstwhile Stromsburg Fort, which was demolished during the Arab raids. It serves as the District Heritage Museum.

name: Indian Naval Maritime Museum
description: Built by the Indian Navy, the museum has many life-size exhibits, a huge display of naval arms and ammunition, replicas of large naval ships and personalities. One section inside a military bunker unravels India's shipbuilding prowess, which took its culture to the shores of Java, Sumatra and Bali between 4 BC and 11 AD. The section outdoors takes you through the Indian Navy's moments post 1947. These include the commissions of various types of ships, submarines or aircraft carriers, as well as superficial details of Junaghad operation, Goa liberation, Indo-Pak conflicts of 1965 and 1971 and strategic manoeuvres during the Kargil war. When you visit, bear in mind that India is one of the top ten naval powers in the world.

name: Indo-Portuguese Museum
description: It highlights the start of European colonisation of the Orient in the 16th century. The museum showcases the growth and decline of Portuguese life in Kochi with a focus on the growth of the Latin Church. There are also excavated ruins of the former fort wall in the basement of the museum.

name: Kashi Art Gallery
address: Burgar St, Fort Nagar, Fort Kochi
description: is both an art gallery and a cafe that serves light breakfasts and lunches. The gallery exhibits work by popular contemporary Indian artists.

name: Cochin Port Maritime Heritage Museum
description: The museum is housed in the residence of the chief engineer during the construction of Willingdon Island. It was converted into a museum in May 2014. The museum has a rare collection of photographs depicting the evolution of the port city of Cochin.

name: Jew Street and Paradesi Synagogue
hours: Synagogue Sun-Fri 10AM-5PM, Fri afternoon and Sat only open to Jews
description: The synagogue was constructed in 1568 after allowing Jewish refugees from Jerusalem to settle here during the Crusades, making this the Commonwealth's oldest synagogue. This is one of the very few functioning synagogues in India, and the structure is unique due to the influence of native Hindu-Christian architecture, as well as being the only synagogue having two bimahs. Many Jews lived in the area until the creation of Israel; today, there is only a handful. Jew Street is a heritage zone with several antique/handicraft shops.

name: Holy Cross (Coonan Kurisu) Church
description: Historic church where native Christians had once received the Bishop of Persia and declared their affinities to the Orthodox Eastern Church. Here, Malayali Christians in the 17th century revolted against Portuguese Jesuit missionaries' attempts to convert them to the Latin church. This was the first recorded revolt against Europeans in India, forcing the Pope to recognise native Christians and establish a new church, the Syro-Malabar Church.

name: St. Francis Church
description: Constructed by the Portuguese in 1503, and the burial place of Vasco da Gama (his remains were later transferred to Lisbon). His tombstone can be seen inside the church. The church has a large cemetery which serves as the resting grounds of many Portuguese army officials and soldiers. The church is the only Catholic Church not demolished by the Dutch, which was handed over to the British to re-establish an Anglican church. A large war memorial is at the back and honours the unknown soldiers who died in World War I.

name: Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica
description: The first European church built in Asia, by the Portuguese in 1502, also the first Cathedral of Asia and the seat of the second Catholic Diocese in India. The British modified the structure and added oil paintings. Today, it serves as the primary seat of the Latin church of Kerala. Pope John Paul II declared it a basilica in 1984. It houses several historical paintings, decorations and artefacts.

name: Chembittapally Mosque
description: Famous for its large super-imposing structure having large shining copper domes (thus the name, which means Mosque having Copper Roofs). The compound has 3 gates; one in west which opens way to Panayapilly, second in south which opens way to Goldenmukku and Kochangadi, and the main gate in the eastern side of compound, which opens way to Angadi, which in turn leads the way to Jew Street and Mattancherry Bazaar towards the north and to Chullickal towards south.

name: Dharmanath Desar Jain Mandir
description: Popularly known as the Gujarati Mandir, it is one of the oldest Jain temples in India, established by the Gujarati community who settled here more than 300 years ago. This is a major Theerth (pilgrimage) for Jains and all major North Indian festivals are celebrated grandly. Pigeon feeding during noon is one of the main rituals here.

name: Thirumala Devaswom Temple
description: Built by the Gowda Sarawatha Brahmins with Lord Venkateswara as the main deity. It is famous for housing the second-largest brass bell in Asia. The North Gopuram is fully roofed with copper.

name: Fort Kochi Beach
description: A historical beach where 1st Portuguese-Dutch war broke out in the 17th century. Once a very large beach, it has reduced to a quarter in size after the 2004 tsunami. A beautiful, small walkway is ideal for evening strolls. One can find remnants of the Old Portuguese Immanuel Fort, along with parts of the Dutch Stormberg Fort, with some cannons still kept intact. An obsolete boiler that was once used for powering cranes of old port and a very large anchor of an old Portuguese ship are displayed on the walkway. Works for creating a new artificial beach are undergoing near this old beach with the help of the Tsunami development funds.

name: Mattancherry Old Spice Market
description: One of the oldest spice markets in the country. There are nearly half dozen small markets, mostly run by Gujarati and Konkanis where you can slice of Indian market flavours.

name: Cochin Crafts Antique Shop
description: Good collection of crafts and antique shops.

name: Crafters Exports
description: This shop has certified large collection of artifacts and heritage pieces. It's a very popular option.

name: Isidore Art Palace
description: Will reliably ship stuff outside India. Bargain hard.

name: Yousuf Art Gallery
description: Showcases art work from many different local artists. Prices are reasonable, and they very often have exhibitions showing some amazing art work from the region. They feature art works and exhibitions by professional artists as well as talented emerging artists from South India.

name: Sree Krishna Cafe
description: Gujarati restaurant famous for its cutlets and battoora, and vegetarian curries.

name: Fort House Restaurant and Hotel
description: At the waterfront, offering good Kerala food and great views.

name: Shala
description: Started by the same people who run the Kashi Art Cafe, Shala serves delicious Keralan food. The menu which changes daily. The owner, Anoop, hires local housewives to cook their local specialties. The restaurant is in a beautiful and tastefully restored historical building.

name: Thai BBQ House
address: Kunnumpuram Road, Njaliparambu Junction, Fort Kochi
description: Thai cuisine, with grilled squid tempuras and coconut prawns.

name: Upstairs Italian
description: Run by an Italian family, classic traditional Italian cuisines.

name: Lily Grace Seafood Restaurant
address: Post box 22, River Rd., Fort Kochi
description: Freshly caught seafood from Kerala.

name: XL Fishnet Bar
description: The bar fills up each day with tourists looking for a beer in Fort Cochin. There is nothing cosy about the place and the staff are quite lazy. It can be a nice spot to meet other travellers, since everyone has one thing in common: drinking beer. There is a busy restaurant downstairs that also serves beer (more pricey) and may be preferred by solo women.

name: The Hosteller
description: Hostel with options of dorms and pvt rooms. A place for backpackers and budget travellers.

name: Casa Linda Ballard
description: A well-maintained hotel in typical European style.

name: Hotel Fort Avenue
description: A well-maintained hotel.

name: Hotel White Rose
description: A newer hotel, which is clean and good-looking. Ideal for families

name: Tag und Nacht
description: Very clean and beautifully decorated rooms with comfortable beds. The owners, Antonio & Kristina, are friendly and helpful. Free WiFi, assistance with arranging trips inside and outside of town. Fabulous breakfasts.

name: Vintage Inn
address: Rids Dale Branch Road, Njaliparambu Jn.,
description: Clean, comfortable ensuite rooms, fan or A/C, free WiFi in the lobby, 5 min walk from historic centre.

name: Cherai Beach Resort
description: This is the most upmarket place with rooms starting at ₹2500. The place is a set of bungalows set around inlets from the lagoon. There are quite a few insects around (a man comes around to fumigate the rooms at sunset). The place tries to be an upmarket resort but the rooms are a little too basic for that. The management of the place is also very poor.

name: Ballard Bungalow
description: A heritage colonial bungalow, which still maintains the colonial charms and recreates an atmosphere of the British Raj.

name: Gama Heritage Residency
description: A typical Portuguese bungalow, which housed the Portuguese army until its defeat by Dutch forces. Today it is a stylish heritage hotel, famous for its hospitality.

name: Brunton Boatyard
description: A heritage bungalow, once built as Dutch Governor's Palace, later owned by the Brunton brothers boatbuilders. Today is a premium property of CGH group. It has huge Dutch styled gardens, Kerala-Dutch style interiors, large cannons and good restaurants.

name: Casino Hotel
description: The first property of CGH established in 1957, it's an iconic hotel famous for its seafood restaurants and themed room, all overlooking Cochin Harbour.

name: Killians Boutique Hotel
description: A very well maintained and modern hotel in the heart of Fort Cochin (water treatment plants, attuned to the German Standards).

name: Koder House
description: Once home to an affluent Jewish couple, today this is a large Jewish theme hotel. It has a good restaurant which serves authentic Kosher certified food and a very large indoor pool.

name: Old Lighthouse Bristow Hotel
description: This heritage property was once the residence of Sir Robert Bristow - the architect and father of modern Kochi Port. It has opulent interiors in a traditional English style and a good antique collection, along with large pools, a garden and host of other facilities.

name: Ramada Resort Kochi
description: The resort is famous for a vast maze network of pools that merges into backwaters overlooked by the balconies of well appointed cottage suites. The resort is equally famous for its pool parties, dance floors, lounge bars and sprawling gardens.

name: Taj Malabar Resort & Spa
description: On the tip of Willingdon Island. Its heritage wing was built in 1935 to accommodate the visiting Princess of Wales (Elizabeth II), and later to accommodate senior officials of the Royal Navy. It is full of Victorian design & decor and was a Crown Property until its handover to the Taj Group in 1954. The tower wing is more modern. The Infinity Pool is one of the oldest swimming pools famous for its beauty.

name: Trident Cochin
description: Near to Ernakulam Port Wharf, this premium property has 69 luxury rooms and 10 premium suites along with several world cuisines restaurants and a world-class spa.

name: Daniels Homestay
description: In one of the silent by-lanes of Fort Kochi very close to the Santa Cruz Basilica. Friendly, clean and comfortable.

name: Dream Catcher Home Stay
description: Home-cooked food, clean rooms, but host quite unpleasant. Free pick-ups from bus and railway station.

name: Green House Home Stay
price: High season doubles are around ₹1,000 non A/C or ₹1,500 A/C, ₹300-600 during the low season, extra charge for A/C rooms
description: Friendly home stay in a good location close to Princess St. TV and a fridge are provided in the communal living room as well Internet.

name: Leelu Home
address: Cheerans Ebenezer, behind Fort Kochi Post Office, Quirose St
description: A renovated Victorian building in the heart of Fort Kochi. Cooking classes are conducted in the kitchen daily from 11AM-1PM and from 6PM-8PM.

name: Maison Casero Home Stay
address: Near Santa Cruz Basilica Church, Fosse Road, Kottavalappu, Fort Cochin
description: The owner Jaison and his family are very friendly and helpful.

name: Padikkal Residency
description: Free Wi-Fi, private rooms with ensuite bathroom. Common balcony. Traditional style homestay with helpful staff. Approved by the Department of Tourism Development. Close to the main Fort Kochi area, but in a quiet enough location to be away from the hustle and bustle of the main tourist traps.

name: Prem's Homestay
description: Clean, homey atmosphere, welcoming hosts. Home-cooked food on order. Close to major tourist attractions. Will organise trips inside and out of town if you wish.

name: Rak Villa
description: Rak Villa is a four-bedroom villa mostly suitable for family. Alcohol is prohibited here. Most preferable for Arabians.

name: San Mike Tours Homestay
price: ₹500 per person or less if there is more than one of you
address: No. 1/957, Directly opposite Santa Cruz Basilica
description: Friendly homestay run by two brothers Victor and Martin. They can organise anything from a ₹500 backwater cruise in Allepey to a day riding an old Enfield motorcycle down the Malabar coast.

name: Cochin Port Hospital
description: General medicine and has a large in-patient ward. Near the Kochi Port area, it's regularly used by sailors. All certifications required for mariners and sailors are available from this hospital.

name: Gautham hospital
address: at Panayapilly, near Fort Kochi and Mattanchery
description: A major multi-speciality hospital in West Kochi. 24-hr casualty, accident and trauma unit, ambulance services and an ICU and other state of the art medical care.

name: Kochi Tourist Police Station
description: This is the country's only tourist police station. Assistance for tourists including visa and immigration information can be provided. There is a small police museum here. Check for the difference of police uniform here. The Tourist Police wear a blue shirt and khaki pants.

name: Church of Our Lady of Hope
description: Located at the southern tip of the Vipin Island, the church dates back to 1605. The church follows a distinct Mannerist and Indo-Portuguese architectural style. Statue of Ecce Homo: The church houses a famous 500-year-old rosewood statue of Jesus wearing the crown of thorns (Ecce Homo).

name: Vypin Lighthouse
description: The tallest lighthouse (46 metres / 151 ft) in Kerala. The original structure dates back to 1839. The present structure dates back to 1979.

name: Azheekkal Sree Varaha Temple
description: The temple is dedicated to Varaha, the third incarnation of Vishnu. The temple belongs to the Gowda Saraswat Brahmin community. The present structure if the temple dates back to 1880s. The temple houses all the seven deities of the Gowda Saraswat Brahmins and hence is referred to as the complete temple.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Snows
description: The church dates back to 1503. The original structure was heavily renovated with majestic Gothic arches in 1931 and rebuilt again in 2006.

name: Pallipuram Fort
description: The oldest existing European fortification in India. Built by the Portuguese in 1503, it was later handed over to the Travancore Army to become a major army base till 1903, when it was converted into a heritage museum. It has a small museum and good views of the lagoon on one side and the sea on the other.

name: Cherai Beach
description: Gold beaches with big sand grains, coconut palm corridors, backwaters and historical monuments. Cherai Beach surpasses all with its swimming facilities and coconut groves. Occasional sights of dolphins are also an added attraction. This is one of the safest beaches for swimming, watersports and beach games. A very large, beautiful backwater is 250 m from the beach and is famous for its scenic beauty and boating. The best way to reach Cherai is a ferry from Fort Kochi to Vypin Island and then a local bus (₹12) to Cherai Junction. From there, take an auto-rickshaw (₹20) to the beach. An alternative is taking the auto-rickshaw from the ferry for about ₹100. There are also buses from Ernakulam to Cherai Junction.

name: National Shrine Basilica of Our Lady of Ransom
alt: Malayalam: വല്ലാര്‍പാടം പള്ളി, Portuguese: Basilica de Nossa Senhora do Resgate
description: A minor basilica and a major Christian pilgrimage centre. The picture of the Virgin Mary and Infant Jesus, installed at the top of the main altar of the Vallarpadam Church, was brought by Portuguese merchants under the leadership of Vasco da Gama in 1524. In 1676 the old church, founded by the Portuguese missionaries, was destroyed by a heavy flood, and the picture was found floating in the backwaters. Nobody except Paliyath Raman Valiyachan, the prime minister of Maharaja of Cochin, could recover it. The present church at Vallarpadamis is built on land donated by him.

name: Matsyafed Milky-way Aqua-Tourist Village
description: A unique concept where a large shrimp farm of the state-run cooperative Matsyafed is converted into an aqua-tourist village with options to fish for fresh prawns, crabs and shrimp for a nominal fee, canoeing within a mangrove forest, sun-bathing, swimming at a private beach nearby and enjoying sunset picnic cruise. Breakfast and lunch are included in entry cost and have a wide range of fish delicacies and pickles.

name: Bolgatty Palace
description: A premium heritage property of KTDC, where English Royals celebrated their life during British Raj days. The Palace complex was built in 1630s by Dutch owners and soon became the residence of the British Resident Commissioners for Cochin and Travancore. The resort is famous for its honeymoon cottages, large Dutch style gardens, horse tracks and golf course. A marina and accompanying marina suites are nearby near to the ex-Residence.

name: Durbar Hall Ground
description: The venue for many fairs during festivals and regular evening concerts and other programmes.

name: Kerala Folklore Museum
description: A theatre with regular evening performances, a state-of-the-art museum and cultural gallery.

name: Pareekshith Thampuran Durbar Hall Art Gallery
description: Contains oil paintings, old coins, sculptures, Mughal paintings plus models of temples and traditional Kerala buildings. It was the official Durbar Hall of Kochi Maharajas, now converted into a large fine arts gallery. It is named after last Maharaja of Kochi, who was an oil painter. A small studio nearby promotes young artists.

name: Malayattoor Mount
description: A major Christian pilgrimage centre believed to be the place where St Thomas performed his first miracle in AD 52. Today, it is famous for its annual Holy week-Easter pilgrimage.

name: St. Antony's Shrine
description: At this shrine that belongs to Archdiocese of Verapoly people of different faith and culture flock together day and night seeking blessings.

name: St. George's Syro-Malabar Forane Church
description: A popular church, also amongst non-Christians. Famous for its poison cure treatments.

name: St. Mary's Syro-Malabar Cathedral Basilica
description: The cathedral is dedicated to "Our Lady of Ports". The cathedral was built in the early twentieth century under the direction of Mar Louis Pazheparambil. It is also a prominent Marian pilgrim centre in India.

name: Kanjiramattom Mosque
address: Kanjiramattom Thalappara Rd, Millungal Junction, Kanjiramattom
description: Major Muslim pilgrimage centre and venue of the Kudikkuthu Festival. Famous for the annual Urs festival. Imams of this mosque are famous for being leading scholars who were advisors to Kochi Rajas. This mosque is an example of antique beauty of mazhars and dargahs. This was recognised by Kochi Maharajas as official along with temples. The annual Chandanakudam in January attracts many pilgrims. During the festival, pilgrims carry pots smeared with sandalwood paste in a procession to the mosque, with caparisoned elephants and percussion musics – both found in temples – form essential parts of the Chandanakudam festival.

name: Ernakulam Shiva Temple
description: Has three temples within its complex.

name: Gurdwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha
description: It is the lone Sikh Gurudwara of Kerala, established by the Punjabi community of Kochi in 1955. Special rites and Guru ka Langar rituals are held every Saturday and Sunday.

name: Managalavanam
description: A thick 80-acre mangrove forest in the heart of Kochi and declared a flora sanctuary. More than 30 unique flora are found here and it is also a major bird sanctuary, where migratory birds feed and rest when they escape the cold northern winters.

name: Marine Drive Walkway
description: A two-km-long promenade and no car is allowed to ply there. The backwaters are on one side and a busy shopping district is on the other side of the walk. The walkway starts from , goes through two scenic bridges and ends at Rajendra Maidan. The total distance is less than a kilometre. Stroll along this calm stretch without motorised traffic and enjoy an ice cream or fruit juice. A few malls stand along the way. Chill off the heat while you walk with a Sharjah shake or ice-cream, or one of the local delicacies. There is a children's park in the middle and two hanging bridges.

name: Changampuzha Park
description: A spacious place established in 1977, ideal for picnics and group discussions.

name: Subhash Bose Park
description: One of the largest parks in Kochi.

name: Kerala Fine-Arts complex
description: This is one of the oldest centres, with regular cultural performances. Many require prior booking, as they are organised by prestigious societies and groups. There are some performances that have free entry, and the monthly cultural programs of Bank Employees Union is one such.

name: See India Foundation
description: Kalathil Parambil Crossroad, nr Valanjambalam Temple, Chitoor Rd. An evening Kathakali theater, where daily performances take place from 6PM-8PM. This is the oldest and first evening Kathakali theater in India. The show is preceded by a detailed discourse of Kathakali history and philosophy, elaborate make-up performances and a demonstration of Kathakali techniques.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru International Stadium
description: Good open multipurpose stadium where locals play regularly, free of cost. Badminton and tennis courts next to this ground can be used on payment of fees at sports office of St. Albert's College which owns them.

name: Rajiv Gandhi Indoor Stadium
description: It has badminton, tennis, squash, volleyball and basketball courts. Rooms for chess, caroms, table-tennis and board games are also available. For an entrance fee payable at the indoor sports office, you can play here or join regular users. There is a state-of-art fitness complex and billiards-snooker pool inside this stadium. An Olympic-sized swimming pool is available outside. Large football and cricket pitches are available free-of-charge. Locals play regularly here and you can join them.

name: Wonderla
description: second largest theme park in South India. Spread over 50 acres of land with more than 50 Rides and various shows, it has well maintained gardens and five restaurants as well as small cafes

name: Silverstorm Water Park
description: A good family theme park with 29 water and dry rides, a very large park and a Chinese village

name: Boating on the Kochi backwaters
description: Get the real feel of the Vembanad Lake through boating. There are many cruises offered by many private players as well as the Kerala State Inland Shipping Corp. Sunset cruises are popular. Many guesthouses offer the trip and in the centre you can arrange it by yourself as well. Speedboats also ply on the backwaters. Some premium hotels in Willingdon Island and Fort Kochi offer motorised watersports for its guests. Daily backwater tours can be organised directly through the state tourism office at Ernakulam Park Jetty. They cost ₹650 per person and must be booked at least the day before. The tour includes a stop at local small industries and food sites.

name: Kerala Kathakali Centre
description: Offers short-term courses in Kathakali, Kalaripayattu and percussion instruments for visitors. Ideal for learning a bit about the essence of Kerala's, although it is not so authentic being aimed mostly at tourists.

name: RLV College of Dance and Music
description: Established in the 1920s by the Maharaja of Kochi in Tripunithara as a remembrance to his late wife and daughter, this is one of the most popular music and dance colleges in the state. There are many short-term courses, making it ideal for interested visitors.

name: Sree Sankara School of Dance and Music
description: Popular school for learning classical Indian art forms, offering certificates and diplomas.

name: ENS Kalari
description: One of the most popular Kalari centres in the state. Part of Kerala Kalaripattyattu Association, this institute is guided by trainers who are versed in ayurveda, mathematics and physical education.

name: Art of Living-Ernakulam Chapter
description: Part of the international yoga and spiritual centre of Sri Sri Ravi Shankar.

name: Broadway Market
description: One of the Kochi's oldest shopping corners where you can buy anything from safety pins to motor scooters (light motorcycles). A spice market operates inside, offering the best of Kerala's spices, saffron and various oils. There is also a cloth market, a jewellery market, a fancy items market, a vegetable/fruit market and an electronic/watch market.

name: Cauvery
description: A government emporium well known for quality handicrafts at reasonable price.

name: Kalanikethan
description: A newly opened shop in Kochi, a place for women's wear.

name: Kalyan Silks
description: One of the largest silk saree showrooms and a good place to get many kinds of Indian and western clothing, including popular western brands, at very reasonable rates. Silk Sarees are its trademark and most of them are well priced.

name: Kasavukada
address: South End of Foreshore Rd near Church Landing
description: A good place to buy a wide range of ethnic Kerala dress like Mundu, Kasavu Mundu Neyriyattu and ethnic men's Jubas

name: Seematti
description: One of the posher silk and dress fashion centres and a trend setter in creating unique designs and special materials for its Sarees. Its owner - Beena Kannan - is a leading fashion designer and new designs come every six months. Most of its sarees are out-of-traditional kind, making its unique. It is comparatively more costly than other brands. The men's area is not so elaborate and has only few collections.

name: Village Shop
address: Behind Sony Center, Ravipuram, MG Road
description: Village Shop is a Home Furnishing store in Kochi. They sell hand-loomed soft furnishings.

name: Jayalakshmi Silk
description: The oldest and most popular destination for bridal collections and popular throughout Kerala. It also houses a very large men's collection with many traditional and modern outfits. It is suitable for a wide range of budgets.

name: American Express Foreign Exchange Services Pvt Ltd
Thomas Cook (India) Ltd
address: Palai Towers, 1st Floor, Right Wing, M G Rd

name: Blossom Book Fair
description: Good place to get brand new and second hand books at discounted rates.

name: Crossword
description: Stationery and bookstore, providing various fiction and non-fiction books and music CDs, branded pens like Cross, Sheaffer and Parker and other stationery.

name: DeeCee
description: A very large multi-lingual bookstore, famous for wide range of English fiction books.

name: Kurien's Tower
description: Has many good book stores within it. Includes DC Books.

name: Pai&Co
description: The first bookstore of the city, its very popular for all kinds of reading materials.

name: The Penguin Store
description: a desirable place to buy all sorts of books.

name: Alapatt Gold
description: One of the oldest with an extensive gold collection, ranging from traditional to modern.

name: H. Venkatesha Naik Jewellery
description: Rajaji Road, Near Kavitha Junction. Offers modern designs and lightweight collections. It also has an extensive diamond gallery and trendy collection of watches.

name: Josco Jewellers
description: A Good 916 gold and diamond jewellery.

name: Kirtilals
description: Opposite Maharaja's College Ground, MG Rd. A grand exclusive diamond gallery, featuring more than 2,000 diamond collections and platinum jewel designs.

name: Malabar Gold
description: Jewel Junction, opposite Grand Hotel, MG Road. An extensive gold, platinum and diamond collection. It has one of the largest watch gallery selling latest international premium brands like Rado, Tissot and others.

name: Oberon Mall
address: near Padivattom Signal Junction, NH Bypass Road
description: was one of the earliest large scale multi-format shopping malls here. A typical mall with wide range of branded stores, large hypermarket, anchor store of Reliance Trends (multi-brand apparels), book/stationery store, spa, beauty saloon, large food court and four-screen cinemas.

name: Centre Square
description: was the latest mall opened in Kochi and has a food court and an 11 screen multiplex called Cinepolis.

name: Bay Pride Mall
description: A small-sized family mall, one of the earliest in Kochi, in heart of city with a few brand stores, a small food court, a fitness centre, a gift shop and a music store. Also connects directly to Marine Drive.

name: Alphonsa Cosmetics Collections
description: Convent Junction. A good collection of all international and national cosmetics brands.

name: Goodwill Collections
description: TKM Park, Convent Junction. One of the largest cosmetic store with collections of jewellery and bags.

name: Le Mars
description: A popular multi-brand women's store.

name: Currents
description: Apple's premium reseller

name: Imagine
description: The first Apple premium reseller in Kerala

name: Lulu Connect
description: Gaming consoles, tablets, smartphones and other appliances.

name: QRS
description: A store for electronic appliances.

name: Reliance Digital
description: A showroom for all sorts of electronic gadgets.

name: The Grand Pavilion
address: Grand Hotel, Jewel Junction, MG Rd
description: Popular especially during evenings for its seafood, particularly karimeen pollichathu (smoked pearlspot fish) and Alleppey fish curry.

name: Ojeen
address: By-lane after SBT towards Broadway, Marine Dr
description: Variety of snacks from the Malabar region, juices and milkshakes. Ojeen is probably the only place in Kochi for the delectable, meat-rich Malabar snacks.

name: Arya Nivas
description: A chain of vegetarian restaurants run by Tamilians, famous for typical south Indian foods.

name: Hotel Thali
description: Very good Kerala-style cuisine.

name: Hotel Unnikrishnan
description: Famous for Kerala-style fish fries and set meals.

name: Indraprastha Gujarati Food Court
description: Famous for its unlimited North Indian thalis and various sweets. A full plate thali with five dishes, Roti and rice costs ₹50.

name: Krishna Kripa Seafood Restaurant
description: Good Kerala-style food, low prices and a great location.

name: Mughal Restaurant
description: Has a good range of north Indian foods and a good juice bar.

name: Banana Leaf
description: Good traditional Kerala food with non-veg and veg options.

name: Delhi Durbar
description: A good, small North Indian restaurant.

name: Kadaloram
description: Good typical Kerala buffet at about ₹300 per head.

name: Khyber Pass
address: First floor, Bimbis Restaurants, Jos Junction, MG Rd
description: A North Indian/Afghan food outlet with a wide range of tikkas and kebabs.

name: Mirch Masalas
description: Vegetarian Punjabi restaurant with good ambience.

name: Raju dhaba
description: Authentic north Indian dhaba food.

name: Sharma's Restaurant
description: Good North Indian food at low prices.

name: BTH Kempa
address: BTH Hotel, BTH Junction, Durbar Hall Rd
description: A classic hotel which dates back at least 100 years. Its restaurant, Kempa, is popular among high-end vegetarian travellers. Serves North Indian, South Indian and Kannadiga-Udupi dishes.

name: Chillis Andhra
description: Very tasty, as well as fiery food, particularly the chicken options. Few vegetarian options.

name: Hotel Dwaraka
description: It was the first star hotel in Kochi and it remains a popular option for Indian vegetarian food.

name: Ila
description: Tasty Travancore food, with both Southern Travancore veg options and Central Travancore Syrian Christian non veg specialities.

name: Sreekrishna Inn
description: This restaurant is famous for its classic look and theme, and offers a large range of Indian vegetarian dishes. The dosas are most famous, along with its elaborate thalis.

name: S36
description: Traditional North Indian cuisine, particularly Mughal specialty foods.

name: Tandoor
description: Tasty North Indian, particularly Punjabi, food. The Kadai chicken and ginger chicken is truly world class, and no other place in Kochi can offer their unique taste. The peas masala is also really superb. Their trademarks are romali roti and stuffed bread options. A full Kadai chicken serves at least 4-5 people. Caution, it is very spicy.

name: Royal Food Court
description: Good food with Arabic-Lebanese delicacies around the clock.

name: Street Menu
description: Offers a lot of grilled options at low prices.

name: Chiyang Restaurant
description: One of the oldest Chinese restaurants.

name: 14Avenue Restaurant
address: 14 Cross Rd, Main Avenue, Panampilly Nagar
description: Italian and continental cuisines, including lasagna, pies, pastas and steaks.

name: South Star
description: Well maintained, nice interiors. Food styles from North Indian, South Indian, Chinese and Arabic and a wide range of Biriyanis.

name: Arctic Circle
description: Steak, more than 14 sizzlers, such as an American styled sizzler with Texas mashed potatoes with mushroom sauce. 20 European dishes, along with a few continental salads.

name: Ayela & Keshai
description: A very good seafood restaurant with four theme courts, Kochi, Thai, Vietnamese and Japanese. It has a fresh seafood selection court, with the fish cooked in front of the guests. A multi-cuisine restaurant also operates at the site.

name: Conucopia
description: A cricket theme restaurant, operating inside Bat&Ball Inn, this restaurant is famous for its wide selection of Continental, Greek, Mediterranean cuisines.

name: Golden Dragon
address: Mercy Estate, Atlantis Junction, Ravipuram side of MG Rd
description: A pure Chinese restaurant without any Indianisation. Serves alcohol.

name: Hon. East India Company
address: Hotel Travancore Palace, Warriam Rd, Durbar Hall Rd
description: A historical themed restaurant operating within the four star Travancore Palace Hotel. Famous for its classic paintings and heritage photo galleries as well as its food. The evening buffet is one of the largest in town, offering the best of English, Kerala and North Indian cuisine.

name: Lokah World Cuisines
description: Offers nine international cuisines from an American Wild West theme to Vietnamese sea-food, Italian pastas and Arabic grills. This restaurant has a family hall, a smoking lounge, a street food area and French cafe along with bakery. Free wifi for guests.

name: Itty's Place
description: Itty's place is an eco-friendly restaurant made completely with bamboo, coir and wood having 3 sit-down options. Favourite Italy offers traditional Italian pizzas, pastas and subs.

name: Ming's Wok
description: Authentic Chinese cuisine prepared by professional chefs, using quality ingredients.

name: Spice Route
address: Level 4, Oberon Mall, NH Bypass Rd, Palarivattom
description: Themed around historical spice route with focus on traditional Persian foods.

name: Somewhere Else
description: It has a cafe and restaurant. The cafe serves a wide range of coffees and mocktails, whereas the restaurant has sizzlers, steaks, grilled wraps, burgers and desserts. Also offers some good biriyanis and Indianised European options. Free wifi for guests.

name: 24 Carat
description: A popular upscale multi-cuisine restaurant, themed around weddings, it is ideal for candle-light romantic dinners and high power lunches.

name: Central Park Bar
description: A posh, well-maintained bar having a designer lounge.

name: Glow&Corktales
description: Atlantis Junction-MG Rd. Dance floor and large lounge bar. It has night parties from Thursday to Sunday with various themes and age groups.

name: Oberoi Bar Beer and Wine
address: MG Rd, Padma Junction, North Kaloor, Kacheripady
description: A good small bar dominated by men.

name: Opium the Club
description: Palarivattom Jn., A posh upscale dance floor and large discotheque, it has various events from Tuesday to Sunday, each in various themes. (Closed on dry days)

name: Polakkulattu Sliverspoon Bar
description: A good, well maintained bar with branches in Palarivattom near Metlife, and in SA Rd at Janatha Junction.

name: Silca Bar
address: Hotel Mercy, Ravipuram area, MG Rd
description: A lovely, upscale bar lounge popular with businessmen and upscale visitors. Famous for its signature dishes and cocktails.

name: Velocity
description: A stylish bar with a wide range of liquors and beer.

name: Amaara Maradu
description: A unique heritage hangout set in a 200-year-old Mangayil house. Serves authentic Kerala coffee and popular varieties of dosas. Regular cultural performances, cooking class, ethnic handicrafts class are some of the popular activities there. The cafe also houses a large library for reading as well as venue of regular book exhibitions.

name: Barista
description: The place to cool down with coffee after a walk at Marine Drive. Not cheap though.

name: BTH Coffee Shop
description: A moderate priced coffee shop, famous for its traditional Kerala snacks and savouries along with dosas and idilies.

name: Cafe Cochin Lavazza
description: The only direct Lavazza coffee outlet in South India.

name: Cafe Coffee Day
description: A popular national chain, which is a standard coffee hangout with western style eateries and a wide range of coffee.

name: Cafe Persia
description: A unique Arabic themed cafe, famous for Sheeshas/Hookah smoking and an excellent range of Arabic coffee and tea, along with snacks.

name: Kashi Art Café
description: Serves great iced coffee, fresh lunches, and a variety of sandwiches and tasty cakes.

name: Teapot
description: A unique cafe which serves a variety of teas, particularly 6 unique Indian flavours. It also has good traditional English snacks.

name: YMCA Youth Centre
price: A/c starts from ₹800 and non A/c starts from ₹375
description: indoor sports, parking facility with a reasonable restaurant.

name: Hotel Sreekrishna Inn
address: Near ESI Hospital, North Railway Station
description: Mr. MG.Menon, manager: 9349267906

name: C.R.H. Dormitory A/c
address: Banerji Road, Near North Railway Station

name: Grand Residency
address: St. Benedict Road, North Railway Station

address: North side of the North Railway Station, Near ESI Hospital

address: Opp. Town Hall, North Railway Station
