description: Established in the 1930s by Dr. E. Stanley Jones, this serene estate houses a chapel, a guesthouse, and a library. The Sunday service (in English and Hindi) is open to all. The ashram’s simple stone architecture blends with the forest.

name: St. John’s Church
description: A beautiful stone church with stained‑glass windows, set amidst tall pines. The quiet churchyard is a place for meditation.

name: Subhash Dhara
description: A natural spring emerging from the hillside, named after Subhash Chandra Bose. The water is crystal clear and considered sacred. A small temple sits beside the spring.

name: Lakeside temples
description: A cluster of tiny shrines dedicated to Shiva, Hanuman, and local deities at the edge of Purna Tal. Offerings of flowers and bells ring gently in the breeze.

name: Kayaking & boating
description: Kayaks and pedal boats are available for rent at the main jetty (approx ₹150–300/hr). Paddle to the quieter corners of Purna Tal, especially at sunrise when the mist rises.

name: Forest walks & trekking
description: A well‑known trail leads from the ashram through oak forest to a viewpoint offering a panoramic glimpse of the Himalayan peaks (on clear days). Another trail circumnavigates all seven lakes (approx 5 km, 2–3 hr). Maps are available at the forest checkpost.

name: Butterfly spotting
description: With over 100 recorded species, Sattal is a butterflying paradise. Post‑monsoon (September–October) is peak butterfly activity. The forest edges and stream beds are excellent spots.

name: Angling
description: With a permit from the Forest Department (available at the Bhimtal office), catch‑and‑release fishing for mahseer is possible in certain stretches. The season is March–June and October–November.

name: Birding trails
description: Sattal is one of India’s premier birding destinations. Walk the forest paths at dawn to spot red‑billed blue magpie, orange‑flanked bush robin, black‑headed jay, and migrant flycatchers. The mission estate and the ridge above Purna Tal are prime zones. Local guides (available at the forest checkpost) charge ₹500–1,000 for a morning walk.

name: Sattal Butterfly Museum
description: A small, private collection showcasing the region’s astonishing butterfly diversity. Over 50 species are displayed; the curator can guide you to nearby hotspots. Entry ₹30.

name: Bagnath Temple
description: Ancient temple dedicated to Shiva. The temple, built in 1450, has various statues dating from the 7th-16th centuries.

name: Dhaulinag Temple
description: A divine place, located on the top of Vijaypur Mountain, 5 km from Bigul.

name: Watch the sunset
description: The elevation, isolation and lush greenery of Bigul make it great spot to watch the sun go down.

name: Dandeshwar Shiv Temple Complex
description: Situated slightly upstream from the Jageshwar temple complex, the Dandeshwar temple complex is in a dilapidated condition. The stone lingam is a natural rock, and, unlike the lingams of the Jageshwar complex, is not carved.

name: Jageshwar Mahadev
description: Tarun Jageshwar is one of the principal temples situated in the temple premises. The temple has two dwarapalas (door guardians) in the form of the armed Nandi and Skandi.

name: Pushti Devi
description: It is the temple of Goddess Devi. The temple enshrines the full murti of Goddesses. This temple is situated in the Jageshwar main premises.

name: Sri Briddha
description: This temple is situated three km north to Jageshwar.This temple is situated at the top of the hill and comes after an uphill trek. It is contemporary to Jageshwar group of temples.

name: Sri Mahamritunjaya Mahadev
description: The Mahamrityunjay temple is the largest and oldest temple in the Jageshwar temple complex.

name: Vinayak Kshetra
description: This place is 200 mts from Artola village from where temples of Jageshwar starts. From this place Vinayak Kshetra or sacred area begins. This place lies between Jhanker Saim temple, Vrudhh jageshwar and Koteshwar temples.

name: Archaeological Museum
description: The Archeological Museum run by Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), houses idols and statuettes removed from Jageshwar shrine dating 9th to 13th century AD

name: Golu Devata
description: Golu Devata or Lord Golu (Hindi: गॊलू दॆवता) is the legendary mythological and historical God of the Kumaun region of Uttarakhand state of India and is their deity. The Golu Devta Chitai, temple is about 4 km from the main gate of Binsar wildlife sanctuary & about 10 km. from Almora.

name: Janardan Resort Kausani
description: The resort has 10 rooms with 24x7 hot & cold water, attached toilets, room service on call, balcony restaurant & LCD TV. Panchshuli Himalayan Ranges are visible from balconies & room windows. The in-house restaurant, Janardan Rasoi, serves Chinese, Continental and Indian food, both veg and non-veg. The food is simple and tasty with a Kumaoni touch and costs ₹200 for 2 people.

name: Hansling Parwat
description: Approached via the Gori River valley north of Munsyari

name: Johar
description: The gateway to Milam and Milam Galacier.

name: Khaliyatop
description: Alpine meadow 4,000 m above sea level

name: Nanda Devi Temple
description: A refreshing 3km trek; one can enjoy horse riding on this trek

name: Panchachuli
description: A series of high mountains that can only be visited with planning, support and technical climbing skills

name: Thamri Kund
description: A picturesque natural lake surrounded by broad-leafed forest, and a natural habitat of Musk Deer

name: Maheshwari Kund
description: A beautiful pond above the Maheshwari Hills. Can be reached by trekking 1.5 km from Munsyari.

name: Bhalu dam
description: A small artificial lake 2.5 km from the Chaubatia Garden.

name: Chaubatia Garden
description: Laden with fruit orchards especially apples are the perfect natural interlude. 10 km from Ranikhet town famous for fruit belt and the Fruit Research Centre.

name: Dwarahat
description: 38 km from Ranikhet, once been the principal seat of the Katyuri Rajas. Dwarahat is full of ancient sculptures.

name: Kalika golf links
description: 6 km on the road to Almora via Ghingharikhal. Famous mountain golf links maintained by the army. Also a Kali temple nearby.

name: Sitalakhet
description: Sitalakhet, 36 km (via Kathpuriya) from Ranikhet, is a sleepy hamlet with fantastic snow views (on clear days). Tarikhet 8 km. Sauni 13km. Khairna 22 km. The Binsar Mahadev temple just past Sauni is worth a visit.

name: Chevron Rosement
description: This is a 100-year-old British summer house.

name: Dunagiri Retreat
description: The retreat overlooks deep rural valleys and the Himalayas. Accommodations are comprised of two restored guesthouses within expansive gardens.

name: Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam
description: Has two guest houses, one at Chaubatiya with nice views, and the other at Chiliyanaula, a small town about 4 km from Ranikhet.

name: West View
description: Amidst all the natural beautyon a plateau overlooking the west valley, surrounded by pine and fir forests, covering an area of 6 acres.

name: Windsor Lodge
description: This is a WelcomHeritage Hotel that was built as a hunting lodge in 1909.

name: Corbett Treat Resort
description: Cafe HoHo is the subsidiary of Corbett Treat Resort. Their speciality is local Kumaoni and traditional Indian food.

name: Jim's Jungle Retreat
description: Provides accommodation in 18 lodges and cottages with attached bathrooms, running hot and cold water. Also provides outdoor activities, jungle safaris, bonfires, bird watching, jungle tail, etc.

name: Nadiya Parao Resort
description: 4-star resort amidst the jungle 5 minutes’ drive from the Jhirna & Bijrani Safari Zones has 53 rooms and cottages.

name: Namah Resorts
description: Surrounded by lush greenery, on the bank of the River Kosi at Corbett National Park, close to the wildlife sanctuary.

name: Tiger Kingdom Resort
description: Beautiful balance of luxury and exclusivity amidst the pristine natural background of the Jim Corbett National Park.

name: Aranya the Kanan Resort
description: An eco-friendly resort in Corbett city. Equipped with air-conditioning and heating.

name: Aahana Resorts in Corbett National Park
description: Aahana Resorts offers spa, pool, restaurants, activity areas, meeting room, and safari facilities, free WiFi Internet (Lobby), outdoor pool, parking, bar, gymnasium/health club.

name: Camp tour of Corbett National Park
description: Entry to Dhikala tourism zone, Jeep safari, viewing wildlife, especially the tiger, elephant ride, fish-eating crocodile

name: Archaeological Museum
description: The museum's main attractions are a collections of sculptures during the medieval kingdom period as well as fossils and stone tools from a much earlier era in the ancient site of Dhol Baha, northwest of Hoshiarpur.

name: Takhni-Rehmapur Wildlife Sanctuary
description: You will come across nilgai, wild boars, peacocks, deer and leopards at this sanctuary.

name: Swaran Theatre
description: One of the oldest cinema complexes in town. Classier but pricier than the cinemas in the malls.

name: Miraj Cinemas
address: J's Eminent Mall, The Mall Rd, Manavta Nagar
description: A large cinema with good acoustics. The popcorn and snacks are quite costly.

name: Hotel Maharaja Palace
address: Sutehri Rd, Central Town, Manavta Nagar
description: Free WiFi and parking. Rooms are air-conditioned.

name: Devi Talab Mandir
description: A replica of Amritsar Golden Temple.

name: Nikku Park
description: Nice park for strolling.

name: Nakodar
description: The town was founded by the Hindu Kamboh. The Kamboh settlements lay to the west of present town and the sites are still marked by extensive ruins and two old tombs, now called the Black and Red Domes, from the colour of the material. The large and handsome tombs dating at least from the times of Jahangir, the fourth Moghul Emperor (1569 – 1627). One of them is said to be the burial place of the adviser of Emperor Shah Jahan, but it is not known who is buried in the other tomb.

name: Pushpa Gujral Science City
description: Almost all students in Punjab are taken on school trips to visit Science City.

name: Wonderland
description: One the best place for enjoyment for one day outing for the entire family with thrilling rides, water games and many more.

name: Bombay Jewellers
description: Gold and diamond jewellery.

name: Tanishq & World of Titan
description: Jewellery and watches. Sub-brand of Tata Group.

name: Viva Collage Shopping Mall
description: Jalandhar's largest shopping mall, featuring a five-screen multiplex.

name: The Great Kabab Factory
description: A wide selection of vegetarian and non-vegetarian kababs and curries

name: Headquarters
description: Mixed cuisine

name: Heat 7
description: Fast food restaurant. Indian, Punjabi, Chinese and other dishes

name: Lovely Sweets
description: Candy store

name: Pahwa Kulfi House
description: [https://www.facebook.com/pages/Pahwa-Kulfi-House-Model-Town-Market-Jalandhar/178470325639283]

name: South Indian Dosa
description: Mixed cuisine

name: Volga Restaurant
description: Mixed dosa and paneer dosa. The aloo tike is better from the street vendor just outside the restaurant.

name: Billa Kulfi corner
description: This is one of the famous kulfi corners known for kulfi and faluda rabri and affordable prices. "Milk badam" and "kesar milk" are also delicious there. Other locations: Adarsh Chopati & Model town

name: Haveli
description: One of the best places to eat typical Punjabi food. It hosts variety of snack stalls as well.

name: Rangla Punjab
description: Traditional Punjabi cuisine. The Punjabi village setting makes it one of the favorite places of everyone who visits this city. It models village houses, wells etc. It offers buffet in a typical Punjabi village home setting. The hospitality offered here reflects the open and loving hearts of Punjabi people. One can get tired of eating but the food will not stop coming. It also hosts a number of shops where you can buy the Punjabi jutis (slippers), clothes, bangles, etc. On weekends, cultural performances by singers and dancing groups is offered. Definitely a "must" visit place.

name: Vijay Dhaba
description: Traditional Punjabi food. It's one of the famous dhabas known for fresh food (like home-cooked) and affordable prices. "Shahi Paneer" and "Kheer" is definitely a must try.

name: Prithvi's Planet
description: A family recreation (1 fast food, 1 restaurant, pool table and six lane bowling alley) Mixed cuisines

name: Sagar Ratna
description: Very popular. South Indian food in a great ambiance but not many options

name: Grand Lily Resorts
description: A traditional hotel surrounded by well kept gardens. It's equipped with a fitness centre, a spa and a swimming pool. The huge banquet hall is often used as a reception venue for larger wedding parties.

name: Radisson Jalandhar
description: The only five-star hotel in the city

name: Sekhon Grand
description: Multi-cuisine restaur

name: Kathgarh Temple
description: An ancient temple 25 km away.

name: Masrur Rock Cut Temple
description: A complex of 25 temples carved out of one rock

name: Nagni Mata Mandir
description: temple and monastery.

name: Nurpur Fort
description: is old fort built by Tomar Rajputs, was destroyed in earth quake, only ruins remain... this fort has granite idol of Lord Krishna which Mirabai used to worship, it was brought from Chittorgarh in 17 century by Raja Jagat Singh

name: Hotel Shagun
description: Clean budget accommodation.

name: Raja Sansi International Airport
alt: Sri Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport
description: A modern airport in the heart of Punjab. It is approximately 70 kilometres from Qadian, and most flights are usually from and to Delhi although the airport also has traffic from international destinations, such as Doha (Qatar), Sharjah (UAE), Birmingham and London (UK).

name: Darul Masih
description: The residence of the founder of Ahmadiyya, which comprises of the rooms with historical significance, such as the room where he was born, all in the original structure of the time.

name: Mubarak Mosque
description: The first Ahmadi mosque in history who's foundation, is believed to, have been laid after divine guidance. The mosque also has other several parts such as Bait-ul Fikr, Bait-ud-Dua as well as Gol Kamra each with their significance.

name: Aqsa Mosque
description: Built by the father of the founder of Ahmadiyya, Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Murtaza in 1876, and expanded multiple times to increase its capacity, now at 15,000, a mosque where the tradition of Jalsa Salana originates.

name: White Minaret
description: Known as the Minaret of the Messiah, the White Minaret is believed to signify the second coming of the Messiah in the Ahmadiyya Muslim community, as per a prophecy. It is located inside of Aqsa Mosque.

name: Noor Mosque
description: The mosque founded by the first caliph of Ahmadiyya Muslim community in Islam, where the second caliph was elected and where Jalsa Qadian have been held.

name: An-Noor Exhibition
description: Located inside of Kothi Darus Salam after, the abode of the first caliph of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community, after being renovated and turned into the an-Noor exhibition centre

name: The Holy Qur'an Exhibition
description: Exhibition centered around the holy book of Islam.

name: Makhzan-e-Tasaweer Exhibition
description: A gallery of the archives of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community.

name: Nooruddin Library
description: a signifiant central library of the Ahmadiyya movement in Qadian with historical importance.

name: The Heavenly Gardens
description: Located in the Qadian Park with historical monuments to see and discover, such as Makaan Hazrat Amma Jaan. It is also the burial site of Hazrat Mirza Ghulam Ahmad, the founder of the Ahmadiyya Community and his companions and other spiritual beings, established after receiving revelations of his demise.

name: Aabai Qabristan
description: Visit the ancestrial graveyard of Qadian, where the family members of the Promised Messiah are buried

name: Dar-ul-Ziafat
address: Langar Khana Rd, Ahmadiyya Mohalla, Qadian
description: Cares for visitors and seekers after truth, both Ahmadis and non-Ahmadis, who come to Qadian, where adequate arrangements are made for board and lodging. Also has a Langar Khana where food is provided to guests.

name: Qila Mubarak
description: Constructed by Raja Dab during the period 90-110 AD.

name: Gurudwara Hazi Ratan
description: Grain Market, Bhatinda

name: Pizzano
description: Food Zone

name: Shahidi Park
description: Literally meaning the "park of the martyrs", on 25 June 1989 26 RSS volunteers were gunned down by terrorists. A memorial was built and committee was set up at the park and on the first Sunday after 25 June each year, the committee pays tribute to the victims of the attack.

name: Shagun Dhaba
description: Hearty Punjabi food. They serve a free glass of buttermilk with every meal.

name: Pizza Philia Samana
description: A popular joint where in addition to pizza serves burgers, pasta and nachos.

name: Hotel Adarsh Palace

description: Restored in 2016.

description: Purported to be the place where the only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate was originally buried.

name: Balu

description: The resting place of the 16th century Islamic saint.

name: Kalayat Ancient Bricks Temple Complex
description: A temple complex built in the 8th century and now partially in ruins. It has the oldest surviving temples made from brick north of Delhi. Based on the Gurjara-Pratijara architectural style, they creatively make use of floral motifs.

name: Chacha Nehru Children Park
description: Named after India's first prime minister, the lush green park has a dinosaur-themed playground, keeping kids entertained for hours. There is also a 1 km walking and jogging path for fitness lovers.

name: Vegetarian Village Restaurant
address: 2nd Floor, Padma City Mall, Karnal Rd
description: Modern Indian family dining.

name: Lakhanpal Hotel & Restaurant
description: Tidy rooms

description: Mughal style garden with seven terraces. A museum is also located here.

name: Atal Park
description: Well maintained park with gardens and fountains. Travelers and local populace enjoy this park for picnics and leisurely strolls.

name: Cantonment Church Tower
description: The Cantonment Church Tower is a church tower in Karnal city of Haryana, India. It stands near National Highway 1 of India. It has been declared as a historical monument by Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage. It was the tower of St. James' Church, Karnal, dedicated to St. James, one of disciples of Jesus Christ. The tower is 35m tall, and is surmounted by an ornamental cross.

name: Dargah Nuri
address: Karnal-Kunjpura road, Village of Newal (10km NE of Karnal)
description: There is a Dargah Nuri at village Newal on Karnal-Kunjpura road. This Dargah was built in memory of Hazrat Sufi Shah Alama Nur Mohd of Delhi, and is managed by Managing Committee, village Newal.

name: Kalander Shah's Tomb

description: A park

name: Tikkar Taal
description: A popular destination, they are also home to the region's first adventure park. The park, which lies on the bank of the smaller of the 2 Tikkar lakes, was set up by Haryana Tourism in 2004, with the intention of promoting adventure tourism in the lower Himalayan region. It offers a range of activities from low ropes, commando nets, Burma bridge, rappelling & rock-climbing. It also has a tree house, fountains and a cafeteria.

name: Cactus Garden
price: A ticket is required for entry
description: This is the largest succulent botanical garden of Asia. Situated in the heart of the city of Panchkula, it covers a total area of 7 acres. The Cactus Garden is known for its rare & endangered species of Indian succulents. You can spot nearly 3500 different kinds of species over there. Chandigarh Cactus Garden was set up in the year 1987. This unique garden consists of three green houses. It has been drawing more and more crowds every year, consisting not just of tourists, but botanists also.

name: WelcomHotel Bella Vista
description: Offers a spectacular view of the lofty Shivaliks.

name: Bhiwani Zoo
description: A small zoo with around 10 types of animals, including hippos, gharials, and peafowl. Takes 30 minutes to one hour to see them all.

name: Star Monument

name: Rewari Railway Heritage Museum
description: This museum holds the oldest surviving steam locomotives, including the Fairy Queen. There are exhibits of toy and model trains, railway equipment used in the 19th century, a 3D virtual reality coach simulator and short documentary films showing the railway history of India.

name: Golden Huts
description: 96 room resort. It has conference facilities, a swimming pool, party lawns, a billiards room, a restaurant and a coffee shop,.

name: Hotal Raj

The temple is open to all. The site is bustling with devotees mostly on Thursdays. Buses and taxis regularly ply to and from Bhuna.

description: Eco-friendly, all-vegetarian, five-star hotel, second largest Country Inn & Suites in the world.

description: Refreshing interiors and landscaped gardens. Centrally air conditioned hotel offering 55 rooms and suites with a large banquet and meeting center, business center, multi-cuisine coffee shop, fitness center and swimming pool.

name: Gautam Buddha University

name: Surajpur Wetland and Bird Sanctuary
description: A protected nature reserve, home to over 180 species of birds. Best for bird watching and eco-tourism.

name: Buddh International Circuit
description: India’s first Formula One race track, hosting motorsports events, karting, and driving experiences. Since 2023, it has been the home of the MotoGP Grand Prix of India.

The Grand Venice Mall
description: An Italian-themed shopping mall. The mall has 258 stores representing Indian and international chains and brands. It is decorated with replicas of Roman statues and Venetian buildings and has two canals with gondola rides for visitors.

name: Digamber Jain Mandir
description: Consecrated in 1806, it is the oldest Jain temple in Hastinapur dedicated to Shri Shantinatha, the 16th Jain Tirthankara.

name: Hastinapur Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A protected area in the Gangetic plains that covers 2,073 km². Mammal species recorded include swamp deer, smooth-coated otter, Ganges river dolphin, gharial, Indian leopard, chital, sambar deer, nilgai. 117 bird species have been recorded.

name: Jambudweep
description: A Digambara Jain temple built in 1972. Jambudweep is a depiction of Jain cosmology.

name: Shri Ashtapad Teerth
description: A 46-metre-high (151 ft) structure dedicated to first tirthankara Rishabhnath.

name: Kailash Parvat
description: A 40-metre-high (131 ft) structure that is home to several Jain temples, including Yatri Niwas and Bhojanshala.

name: Pandeshwar Temple
description: This temple is dedicated to Shiva. It is believed to be the place where Kauravas and Pandavas received their education in Vedas and Puranas. A temple of the Hindu goddess Kali and many Hindu ashramas are also present on a hillock between the ruins. Legend has it that in the Mahabharata period, Pandu's eldest son Yudhishthira had established the shivalinga at the Pandeshwar Mahadev temple before the war of Mahabharata and prayed to Shiva for a blessing of winning the war.

name: Karna Temple
description: The Karna Temple is located on an old ravine along the bank of the Ganges. The Shivling inside the Karna Temple is believed to have been established by Karna, one of the prominent figures in the Mahabharata.

name: Rao Raj Vilas
description: A heritage resort formed by restoring a section of Mr. Ajit Singh's ancestral property. The Kuchesar Fort was brought into the Singh family’s possession in the eighteenth century when the Mughal King Najib-ud-Daula bestowed the Jat family with the title of Rao Bhahadur and the Jagir of Kuchesar that comprised of 365 villages - one for each day of the year. Thereafter, structures were added to the fort which reveals different architectural influences. The family resides in a part that houses the erstwhile reception and dining halls built in the colonial style. The section that has been made into the hotel bears influence of Mughal architecture. Its rooms enclose a square courtyard and have balconies with arches and lattice edges that are quintessentially Mughal in style. The resort offers 10 rooms, divided into 2 King Suites, 3 Queen Suites and 5 Prince Suites. Recreational facilities include a swimming pool, badminton court, table tennis room, billiards room, participation in evening prayers at temples, picnics in sugarcane fields and mango groves, boating in the Ganges, etc.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Graces
description: Basilica of Our Lady of Graces, also known as Churches among the Churches, is dedicated to Virgin Mary. The Church was built by Begum Samru, a Nautch girl of 14 who married a European mercenary soldier Walter Reinhardt Sombre. Samru converted to Roman Catholicism in 1781 and adopted the name Joanna Nobilis. She is regarded as the only Catholic ruler in India, and ruled the Principality of Sardhana in 18th and 19th century. The church is the largest in North India.

name: Mustafa Castle
description: An edifice built by Nawab Mohammad Ishak Khan in memory of his father Nawab Mustafa Khan Shefta, a poet and critic.

name: St. John's Church
description: The oldest garrison church in Northern India, built from 1819 to 1822. Its cemetery contains graves of David Ochterlony and Rollo Gillespie.

name: Subhash Chandra Dwar
description: The gateway between and the city's market, built between 1913 and 1914. The clock imported from Germany to to be at the Allahabad High Court in Prayagraj, and was installed in the gate at Meerut in 1914.

name: Gol Market
description: You can visit this market and taste some amazing pastries. Burgers are the best thing to have there.

name: Surajkund
description: Cricket equipment is made here that is exported to whole world. One can get best price here.

name: Jalikothi

description: Boutique hotel with a restaurant.

name: Noida Film City
description: A hub for films and television in India. It has been the location for many Bollywood and Indian films.

name: Kiran Nadar Museum of Art
description: Established in January 2010, it is India's first private museum of art exhibiting modern and contemporary artworks.

name: Stupa 18 Gallery
description: An art gallery where you can see and buy art pieces by various new as well as established talented artists. Open to public, this gallery has interesting exhibitions every month.

name: Rashtriya Dalit Prerna Sthal and Green Garden
description: The green expanse along the banks of river Yamuna includes a mini-museum called the Rashtriya Dalit Smarak (National Dalit Memorial). It includes the idols consecrated for the people who devoted their life for humanity, equality and social justice, including Buddha, Kabir, Birsa Munda, Jyotirao Phule, B.R. Ambedkar, Periyar etc.

name: Shivalik Park
description: The garden that hosts the annual Noida Flower Show.

name: Okhla Bird Sanctuary
description: A haven for over 300 bird species, especially waterbirds.

description: There are three sections within the modern theme park complex: a water park, an amusement park and a go-karting track.

description: The mall has around 330 stores spread over 7 floors consisting of both international and local brands.

description: One of the largest malls in India. Big Cinemas cineplex, slick (and pricy) Spoon food court on the 3rd floor, Big Bazaar department store, somewhat forlorn amusement part outside.

name: Modi Mall

name: Noida Haat
description: A cultural centre with food plaza and crafts bazaar. It is inspired by the Dilli Haat in New Delhi.

name: The Yellow Chilli
address: 1 A/31 H Block. Commercial Market, Sector 63
description: One of celebrity chef Sanjiv Kapoor's restaurants. The food is varied and is inspired by dishes from all over India though there is an emphasis on Punjabi and Mughlai cuisine.

name: Punjabi by Nature
description: P-19, Sector 18 (Atta Market). The local outlet of the exuberantly hip Punjabi chain, serving up tandoori lobster and vodka golgappas next to crazy decor that's half dhaba, half crystal chandeliers and indoor waterfalls. While there's a premium to pay for the surroundings, the food is solid and the makki ki roti with sarson ka saag is worth the price tag. ₹500, more if you sample the booze or seafood.

name: Mamouchee
description: offers quite good range of cocktails. On the food side , good Lebanese options

name: Quantum
description: arguably one of the best nightclubs in Delhi-NCR.

name: Nirulas
description: Oldest hotel of Noida. Possibly 3-star. Good fast food joint, pastry shop, bakery, tea/coffee lounge, bar.

name: Mosaic Hotel
description: A hip, trendy hotel. Rooms are modern and comfortable, service is friendly and efficient, but wireless Internet is expensive and patchy. Has a bar called Flluid and a restaurant called Latitude.

name: Radisson Blu Hotel Noida
description: Noida's first branded hotel.

name: Nau Gaja Peer Shrine
description: Nau Gaja Peer roughly translates to the "Nine Gaja Saint" (Gaj is a traditional unit of length in India equivalent to about 0.91 metres or 3 feet). This makes the legendary saint the shrine is dedicated to more than 8 metres or 27 feet. The shrine also houses a Hindu Shiva temple. As such, it is a pilgrimage site visited by both Muslims and Hindus.

name: Ibn Sina Academy of Medieval Medicine and Sciences
description: Museum on Indian heritage and Library on History of Medieval Medicine

name: Amir Nisha Market
description: Amir Nishan Market is a residential and commercial area in Aligarh. it's a top place for cheap but high-quality traditional Indian clothes for women. It's closed on Friday.

name: Aligarh old city market
description: Quite clumsy and lack parking space but you can find practically anything of daily use and industrial purpose in this market.

name: Locks
description: Aligarh is famous for its lock industry and one can spend some time buying and searching some new and attractive lock models in the local city market.

name: Centre Point
description: Centre Point is a shopping center in Aligarh, it's a large area and not just a big mall, there are outlets of most luxury fashion brands. You can buy clothing, electronics, sweets, fast food & gold. There are also luxury salons, temples, mobile repair shops, and medical stores. It's the most posh area of Aligarh.

name: Ananad Bhavan
description: Near the old bus stand.

name: Ruby Palace
description: Near the old bus stand.

name: Nandagram Temple
description: The spacious temple of Nanda, built by the Hat ruler Roop Singh. The other temples here are dedicated to Narasingha, Gopinath, Nritya Gopal, Girdhari, Nand Nandan, and Yashoda Nandan, which is halfway up the hill. There are two black marble Deities of Krishna and Balarama in this temple. They are both in three-fold bending forms, holding flutes. On Their left and right are two tall deities of Yashoda and Nanda Maharaja. Next to the deity of Mother Yashoda is a deity of Srimati Radharani, a small deity of Rohini (the mother of Lord Balarama) and Revati, Balarama's wife. Next to Nanda Maharaja are two of Krishna's friends, Sudama (maybe Sridama) and Madhumangala. The Deities in this temple were originally installed by Vajranabha. It is believed that the Deities in this temple were found by Sanatana Gosvami in a cave on the hill.

name: Radha Rani Temple
description: The temple is dedicated to Radha, Krishna's consort. It is stretched on the top of Bhanugarh hills, which is about in height. It attracts huge crowd of devotees and tourists visiting temple from around the world for its most popular festivals: Radhashtami and Lathmar Holi.

name: Etawah Safari Park
description: One of the main attraction of the city, with a breeding centre for the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo leo). Here, you walk through the cage paths where the lions and other animals are moving freely in the jungle.

name: National Chambal Sanctuary
description: Home to various endangered species like the gharial, Gangetic dolphin, red-crowned roof turtle and various species of birds.

address: Purabia Tola Char, Pacca Talab, Chauraja

address: Hotel Chanakya Agra Rd, Pakka Talab

name: Saifai Clock Tower
description: A unique and different type of clock tower, not like the classic ones. Also part of Kisaan Bazaar, it is a party hub and landmark.

name: Saifai International Cricket Stadium
description: An International Cricket Stadium, situated inside Major Dhyan Chand Sports College campus. Contact or connections with special person may be required to get inside the stadium when no event is going on.

name: Dakshinmukhi Hanuman Ji's Statue
description: One of the biggest Hanuman statues in India.

name: Sarsai Nawar Wetland
price: ₹40 for foreigners, ₹5 for other adults, ₹2 for children under 12 years; still cameras are allowed for ₹25.
description: Bird sanctuary, notable for the presence of the Sarus Crane. Beware of monkeys stealing food in the main office of the park.

name: Joney's place
description: Perfect for early breakfast, when you want to wake up early to visit the Hajari Mahadev Temple at 6AM. ₹10 Toast, ₹10 coffee, ₹15 cornflakes.

name: Kaushal Halwai
description: Roof top restaurant with view of the Bird Sanctuary. Beer available. ₹70 for a vegetable curry.

name: Bihariji
description: The best-known temple in Vrindavan, home to a Krishna idol known as Thakur-ji. The idol's eyes are said to be so powerful that it is kept hidden from view behind a curtain, which is opened and closed every few minutes.

name: Jaigurudeo Temple
description: It resembles the Tajmahal, built with white marble. It is a unique temple in that you are prohibited from donating if you are a non-vegetarian.

name: Krishna Balaram Mandir
description: Better known as the ISKCON Temple. A major draw for Hare Krishna (ISKCON) pilgrims to India, and uniquely among Vrindavan's temples well equipped to deal with foreign visitors. Free breakfast and lunch are available. Great restaurant. Comfortable guesthouse on the Temple grounds.

name: Prem Mandir
description: The temple was constructed in 2012. There are fantastic light shows and designs. The light show closes at 7:30PM in the winter days, and at 8PM in the summer.

name: Radhavallabh Mandir
description: A very well-known ancient temple of Vrindavan, founded by Shri Hith Harivansh Mahaprabhu, Sri Radhavallabh Lal's idol resemble Sri Radha and Sri Krishna to be embodied in it together: "One soul and two bodies".

name: Rangji Mandir
description: The single largest temple in Vrindavan, built in 1851 in a South Indian style, complete with intricate seven-story gopuram (gateway) at the entrance. Inside is a 50-ft high wooden chariot, taken out yearly for festivals, and in the inner courtyard is the 50-ft high gold-plated pillar known as Dhwaja Stambha.

name: Nidhi Van
description: Krishna rested with His beloved Sri Radha. The shrine inside has a bed, which is decorated with flowers by the priest every evening. No one is allowed to stay inside after dusk because according to popular belief the Lord visits the spot with Sri Radha. The samadhi (memorial) of Svami Hari Das is also within this complex. All the groves of Vrindavan are notorious for monkeys that have a special fascination for cameras and spectacles. The Yamuna river flows through Vrindavan and Mathura. It is one of the most sacred rivers in India as it is so intimately connected with Krishna's pastimes.

name: Bharati Foods
address: Near Ramjibai Satsang Bhavan, Vidhyapeeth Chauraha
description: This is the Most Genuine restaurant in Vrindavan, they serve North Indian, South Indian, Chinese foods and also Indian Sweet Dishes at reasonable prices. Seating facilities are good.

name: Govindas Restaurant
address: On the backside of Krishna-Balaram Mandir
description: Excellent vegetarian food. Air conditioned. Serves Indian, Italian, Chinese, South Indian cuisines.

name: MVT Restaurant
description: Best place to get Western food that is cooked by Westerners. A lot of fresh organic salads, pasta, great pizza, lasagna and Baskin Robins ice cream.

name: 56 Delight's Restaurant
description: all-day dining: buffet, à la carte meals and regional specialties.

name: Bharti Guest House
description: Very close to Bankey Bihari Temple (2-min walk), quite economical, A/C Double Room ₹800, Non AC Rooms also available, situated in the heart of the city (ideal location if you wish to visit lot of famous temples).

name: Hotel Basera
address: Raman Reti Marg, Opposite Phogla Ashram, Vrindavan
description: Clean rooms, convenient location, 24-hour power back-up, TV, air-con, parking, veg restaurant , banquet room.

name: Hotel The Shubham
description: Vidyapeeth Crossing. City hotel with air-conditioning, CTV, room service, 24-hr hot and cold running water. A/C doubles from ₹1000. Also includes Swastik Restaurant, a strictly vegetarian restaurant without onion and garlic that serves Indian, Indian Chinese and Continental cuisine.

name: Yamuna Dham
description: Very Economical, A/C double room ₹900, clean rooms, close to Isckon and Bankey Bihari Temple.

name: Hotel Krishnam
description: 40 AC rooms, restaurant, conference hall. Provides 24 hours Power back up, tea/coffee makers in rooms, electronic safe, free Wi-Fi, LED TV with satellite connection, in-house parking.

name: Buland Darwaza
description: This grand gate was built to commemorate the military triumphs of Mughal emperor Akbar in Gujarat.

name: Jama Masjid
description: One of the largest mosque complexes in India. The architecture blends Indian with Persian influences.

name: Tomb of Salim Chishti
description: Salim Chishti was a Sufi saint, dearly respected by Emperor Akbar. In fact, the emperor held Salim in such great esteem that he named his son Salim (who would later be known as the Mughal emperor Jahangir) in honour of the saint. The mausoleum built for Salim Chishti in 1580 and 1581 is considered to be one of the greatest examples of Mughal architecture.

name: Anup Talao
description: The red sandstone architectural symmetry of the walls and bridges that crisscross the artificial lake or pool is beautiful but the water nowadays is polluted and dirty.

name: Birbal Bhawan
description: Birbal was a Hindu courtier of Akbar, who ended up becoming one of Akbar's closest and most trusted military advisors. The stone carvings and interior of the palace where Birbal lived are magnificent.

name: Diwan-i-Khas
description: Striking architecturally, a central pillar dominates the hall which is thought to represent religious syncretism that Akbar sought. An audience platform where the emperor sat crowns the pillar with bridges leading to the four corners of the room leading to open galleries around the upper floor.

name: Ibadat Khana
description: A hall where Emperor Akbar invited religious scholars of a variety of religions to discuss and debate.

name: Panch Mahal
description: Literally translating to "Five Palace", the five-storey building stands out from the rest of the complex with its almost Buddhist pagoda-like influences in its architectural design.

name: Hiran Minar
description: A high, circular tower covered in spikes that look like elephant tusks. Akbar is said to have built it in remembrance of his beloved elephant, Hiran.

name: Naubat Khana
description: It is here where the musicians of the court would play songs to announce the arrival or departure of the emperor, and for various other ceremonies.

name: Samosa Mahal
description: The funny name of the palace (samosa referring to the pyramidal shaped dumplings in Indian cuisine) is because it does, in fact, resemble a samosa! It is clean and well maintained, though be wary of the guides in the palace, who can be pushy and touty.

name: Jodha Restaurant
description: North Indian vegetarian and vegan food in a casual setting.

name: Sher-e-Punjab
description: Punjabi and other North Indian food with non-vegetarian and vegetarian options. The meals are hearty and feel satisfying after a long day of sightseeing.

name: Hotel Vrindavan
description: Hotel with basic amenities.

name: Panchala Museum
description: The collection of the museum includes prehistorical stone sculptures, goddess heads of Mauryan era, and a chariot of Gupta period. The numismatic section displays 500 coins belonging to periods earlier than that of Guptas. Most of the artifacts are from the archaeological site of Ahichatra (or Ahi-Kshetra)

name: Alakhnath Temple
description: The main centre of Naga Sanyasins belonging to the Shiva order of Anand Akhara.

name: Tapeshwar Nath Temple
description: This is the oldest temple in town.

description: It has huge wedding gardens, restaurant & swimming pool along with all the facilities of star hotel.

name: Rangoli Lodge
description: Good, clean and nice place to stay with homely atmosphere. It was the first hotel in Unnao opened 2001. Rooms are air-cooled/air-conditioned with attached and non-attached toilets wall to wall carpet & TV. It has a capacity of 40 beds (16 rooms and a dormitory) provided with power back up generator & inverter. The price varies room to room, starting from ₹60 and closes to air-conditioned ₹800. Home made delicious lazeez veg. food made by housewives is provided in tiffins for breakfast, lunch & dinner ordered in specific time. A travel desk is always ready at your service on demand.

name: Lakh Bahosi Sanctuary
description: A bird sanctuary spread over two shallow lakes.

name: Government Archaeology Museum
description: The museum has artefacts depicting the rules and common folk spanning the numerous dynasties that rules Kannauj over the millennia.

name: Dadri Mela (fair)
description: Dadri Mela is the second largest cattle fair of India. The fair starts on the full moon of the month of Kartik (October–November) with a holy dip in the Ganges River. This fair is held annually in the honour of Dadar Muni, the disciple of Maharishi Bhrigu. This fair is celebrated for more than one month and is organised in two phases. The first phase starts before 10 days of Kartik Poornima (full moon) in which traders bring some excellent hybrids of cattle from across India for sale/purchase. On or after Kartik Poornima, various cultural programs are organised and one can find shops of different items at one stop during the next fortnight.

name: Chunar Fort
description: Established by Maharaja Vikrmaditya the King of Ujjain to commemorate the stay of his brother Raja Bhartihari who had taken his Samadhi when he was alive and still that Samadhi Sthal is worshipped. As per Alha Khand in 1029 AD. King Sahadeo made this fort as his capital and established the statue of Naina Yogini in a cave of Vindhya hill and put the name as Nainagarh. King Sahadeo built a stone umbrella based on 52 pillars in the memory of the victory on 52 other kings, inside the fort which has been preserved.

name: Mausoleum of Iftikhar Khan
description: Iftikhar Khan was an official in the court of Jahangir. The tomb dates back to 1605. It is a Mughal-styled domed structure flanked by four chatris, The tomb stands at the centre of a walled complex planned in char bagh style. The entrance is through a massive gateway from the west. North of the tomb complex lies an

name: Dargah of Kasim Shah Sulemani
description: Kasim Shah Sulemani was a Sufi saint from Peshawar who visited the Purvanchal region during the reign of Jahangir. Jahangir, who was a disbeliever of saints, had him imprisoned at Chunar Fort. Despite his imprisonment, he was seen offering prayers in the neighborhood. Jahangir saw the miracle and immediately released him and became his follower. He died in 1606 had was led to rest on the banks of the Ganges. The complex also houses the grave of his son Wasil Shaw. The tomb complex is approached through a magnificent gateway on the south. The gateway is made of chunar stone and has intricate ornamentations. Today tomb complex overlooks the mighty Ganges and is approached by a magnificent Chunar stone gateway. Apart from the octagonal tomb of Kasim Shah Sulemani the complex houses several graves and tombs including the tomb of his son Wasil Shaw. It is an active dargah attracting people of all faiths. Every year, a fair is held at Chunar Dargah Sharif after Holi. It is believed that wishes made here come true. No wonder it attracts people, irrespective of faith, from far and wide.

name: British Cemetery
description: The cemetery is located on the banks of the Ganges and falls on the left side of the road leading to Chunar Fort. There are several graves of British and European origin.

name: Vir Bahadur Singh Planetarium
description: A good place to spark children's interest in astronomy and physics. The planetarium runs 45-minute long shows at 1pm, 3pm and 5pm daily.

name: Gorakhpur Zoo
address: Buddha Vihar Rd, Rail Vihar Colony Phase 3rd, Phase 3rd
description: The second largest zoo in the state with several big cats, deer, monkeys, bears, reptiles, birds and fish in the aquarium section.

name: Gita Vatika
description: Beautiful temple of Lord Krishna and Radha

name: Gorakhnath Math
description: A temple named after Yogi Gorakhnath.

name: St. John's Church
description: 200-year old church with rich history.

name: Lord Buddha Museum
description: Nice and quiet place to visit.

name: Railway Museum
description: There are the lots of collections related to Indian railway and Gorakhpur railway station.. The Rail museum is also a very good picnic place.

name: Taramandal
description: You can go Taramandal for boating

name: Neer Nikunj Water Park
price: ₹650 pp from Monday to Saturday and ₹750 pp on Sunday
description: The only water park in Gorakhpur, it has a number of water slides, pools, wave pools and a few non-water related amusement rides like a merry-go-round and Ferris wheel.

name: Terracota items
description: Terracotta trinkets (decorative things made of muddy soil) are made here.

name: SRS City Mall
description: This mall has a movie theatre with 3 screens.

name: Baldev Plaza
description: The oldest shopping mall in town. It has several shops, especially for jewellery and gifts.

name: Golghar
description: Sells personal items

name: Gita Press
description: The world's largest publisher of Hindu religious texts is based in Gorakhpur.

name: Orion Mall
description: Shopping mall with clothing and footwear stores, a game zone arcade, food court and cinema.

name: Bobi's Restaurant
description: Affordable restaurant serving a variety of cuisines. In-house bakery for cakes and pastries.

name: 10 Park Street, Cafe & Kitchen
description: serving Indian, Oriental and Continental cuisines.

name: Choudhry Hotel
description: Good and clean Indian food. Agreeable service with reasonable rates. Can get everything from typical Punjabi dishes to South Indian with variety of sweets.

name: Hotel Ganesh
description: Good and clean Indian food. South Indian dishes like Dosa, Masal Dosa, and Idly Sambar are available here at reasonable rate.

name: Tandoor Food - Take away
description: Most famous food joint in the city specializing in Mughlai non-vegetarian foods like authentic biryani, kababs, tandoori chicken. The prices are reasonable and the quality is great. Open for dinner only. A busy place.

name: Mahraja restaurant
description: Good non-veg food in city, delicious taste of Lucknowi food.

name: Hotel Awadh
description: In centre of the city.

name: Hotel Bobina
description: The oldest hotel in town. It also has a swimming pool.

name: Hotel Kabeer
description: Modest place to sleep and food quality is good.

name: Hotel Clarks Grand
description: Upscale hotel.

name: Hotel Park Regency
description: All rooms are air-conditioned and have Wi-Fi.

name: Shivoy Hotel
description: Free WiFi and free breakfast. Has a restaurant which serves both Indian and Chinese.

name: Jaunpur Fort
description: The name Sahi Quila literally translates into royal fort. The fort dates back to the 14th century and was constructed by Ibrahim Naib Barbak, a chieftain of Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Over the years the fort has gone through various modifications and extensions. The fort stands on an artificial mound on the north bank of Gomti. It is irregular quadrangular in shape. The fort is surrounded by two sets of walls topped with battlements and reinforced with bastions, The entrance is through the east and the interiors are reached after passing through two gateways. Nothing much is left in the interiors apart from a mosque and a hammam.

name: Mosque
description: The mosque dates back to 1376 and was built by Feroz Shah Tughlaq's brother Barbaq Shah. The mosque has three arches on the eastern side and is topped with three domes. There are pillared extensions on the north and south sides. Slender minaretes add to the elegance of the small mosque. The mosque also has a slender minaret in front of it.

name: Hammam
description: The Turkish Hammam is located next to the mosque. The hammam is located next to the mosque and is built in Turkish style. The hammam consists of a series of domes complete with turrets allowing light to pass in. The interiors are accessible and consist of a series of rooms connected with a maze of passageways. The rooms consist of water tubs connected with a series of water channels supplying hot and cold water.

name: Shahi Bridge
description: A picturesque 16th century bridge across the Gombti which was constructed during Mughal times. One of the finest example of the engineering in the medieval period of India.The old bridge over the Gomti River in Jaunpur dates from 1564, the era of the Mughal emperor Akbar.

name: Atala mosque
description: The mosque was constructed in 1408 by Ibrahim Shah Sharki. The foundation stone of the mosque was laid by Feorze Shah Tughlaque in 1393. It towers to a height of 100 ft and have three towering gateways. The mosque has intricate stone works.

name: Jaunpur Jami Masjid
description: Built by Hussain Shah Sharqi, the 15th century is one of the largest in India. Situated inside a walled complex it has domed gates on the eastern, northern and southern sides. The mosque lies on the western side and consists of a dome flanked on both sides by vaulted roofs.

name: Char Angul Mosque
description: This small mosque is a hidden gem. It is located deep inside the Mufti Mohalla locality of Jaunpur and is difficult to find. Unlike the other Jaunpur mosques it doesn't have a towering gateway but still has its share of elegance.

name: Lal Darwaza Masjid
description: This Mosque was built in 1447 (as per inscription of this mosque), during the reign of Sultan Mahmud Sharqi, by Queen Bibi Rajyi, dedicated to Maulana Sayyid Ali Dawood Kutubbudin, a celebrated saint (Maulana) of Jaunpu. This mosque is also located inside a large walled complex with the mosque at the western end. There are gates on the other three sides.

name: Jhinjhari Masjid
description: A small and elegant mosque with a towering arched gateway complete with intricate calligraphy from the Koran along with floral and geometric design. It was constructed by Ibrahim Shah Sharki.

name: Tomb of Shah Feroz
description: Feroz Shah (not to be confused with Feroz Shah Tughlaq) was a commander of Babur. The tomb consists of a single domed structure.

name: Tomb of Sher Zaman Khan
description: The tomb houses the mortal remains of Sher Zaman Khan, a Farukabadi Nawab. It is a spectacular structure crowned with a massive dome. Sadiy, it lies in neglect.

name: Tomb of Qaliach Khan
description: Qaliach Khan was the governor of Jaunpur during Akbar's reign. His tomb consists of a single dome flanked with chhatris on both sides.

name: Sheetla Chukia
description: Temple of Sheetla Devi

name: Matha Kuar Shrine
description: Matha Kuar Shrine is the place of Buddha's last sermon. After having a meal of pork (some say mushroom) in a nearby place (present-day Fazilnagar) Buddha fell severely ill. The meal was provided by a blacksmith named Chunda and is considered as Buddha's last meal. Despite his illness, he travelled to Kushinagar to deliver his last sermon. After the sermon, he told his disciples to prepare his deathbed in the nearby sal forest. Over the years and centuries, several kings and nobles have paid tribute to Buddha by creating several structures. Today it is a protected site under the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). It follows a typical plan of a Buddhist Vihar complete with a central courtyard surrounded by cells or small rooms. On the western end of the vihar is a small white temple like structure complete with a porch supported by pillars. It houses a 3-metre-tall statue of Buddha in bhumisparsha (earth touching). The monolithic statue was made of Gaya blue stone and was excavated during the archaeological dig of 1876. The statue was restored and placed in its original location and was enshrined in the small temple like structure in 1927. (Photography is allowed but for the Buddha statue only mobile photography is allowed).

name: Mahaparinirvana Temple
price: Free. Cameras not allowed. Mobile Photography allowed
description: This site marks the exact location of Buddha's death. A 1965 built temple stands above the ancient ruins, The temple consists of a shrine and stupa was built to commemorate the 2,500th anniversary of the death of Buddha. The shrine houses a 6.1-metre-long Buddha statue in reclining posture, with the head towards the north. It is made out of a single stone and rests on a stone couch. The statue was discovered in 1877 in a heavily damaged state and fragmented parts. The fragments were joined to create the statue. The temple stands on the ruins of a Buddhist vihar. The ruins were part of century-old structures constructed by various kings as a tribute to the Buddha. These structures have been excavated by various archaeological digs. The earliest part of the excavated ruins dates back to the time of Asoka with subsequent additions by the Kushans (50 -241 CE) and Guptas (320 – 647 CE). Today the Mahaparinirbab site is the main attraction for pilgrims and tourists. Throughout the day thousand of pilgrims visit the site with huge yellow coloured sheets which are placed over the reclining statue of Buddha.

name: Ramabhar Stupa
description: This is the site of the cremation of Buddha. After his death, his mortal remains were cremated about a km east of his death place. Later a giant stupa was built at the location which was unearthed during an archaeological dig in 1910. The central stupa is surrounded by smaller votive stupas and several vihar like structures. Devotees frequent the place and do the parikrama of the stupa and perform various other rituals.

name: Relic Distribution Site
description: After the cremation, the mortal remains of Buddha were kept as relics and distributed among eight kings of north India. There are no historical remains at the site but it is believed that the distribution happened at this very place. Today a small shrine housing a statue of Buddha marks the site. It is located off the main road and barely visited by pilgrims and tourist.

name: Museum
description: The site museum displays artifacts collected from the different archaeological sites of Kushinagar. Over 1,300 artifacts are on display, including those made of stone, terracotta and bronze items along with coins and other artifacts.

name: Yama Cafe
description: The owner, Mr. Roy, is an old-timer at Kushinagar and can advise on many things there.

name: Tibetan Monastery
description: both donation and by payment available

name: Japanese-Sri Lankan Temple
description: Probably one of the first modern temples, established in 1984. Guest house stay by donation. The temple gate opens between 7am to 5pm, so you can visit and ask if there are any empty rooms available. The main hall is designed and built by Japanese and transferred to Sri Lankan management.

name: Pathik Niwas
description: Uttar Pradesh tourism.

name: Lotus Nikko Hotel
description: This is a well-managed hotel with comfortable rooms.

name: Aashbujha Temple
description: See the scenic beauty of The Vindhyas from this temple.

name: Budhenaath Temple
description: See the old stone carving at Pakka Ghat and Budhenaath Temple

name: The Clock Tower
description: It is one of its own kind.The stone carving of the tower will make mesmerize you. The clock is very old and is one of the sisters in Big Ben family.

name: Vindham, Sirsi and other water falls
description: There are various water falls surrounding the city.Vindham, Sirsi, Sidhnath ki dari being most famous in them

name: Explore the ghats
description: Mirzapur is situated at the bank of Ganges. You can enjoy a serene evening at one of the Ganges Gahts. The ghats in Mirzapur are relatively calm and quiet compare to Ganges Ghats of Varanasi and Allahabad. Visit Pakka Ghat to watch some rare and beautiful stone carving. It is situated in middle of the city and you can get Handrikshaw from any of the place in city. Try some boating in the serene Ganges.

name: Hotel The Galaxy
description: member of FHRAI and HRANI is fully air-conditioned hotel situated at 1.5 km from Railway Station. You might be charged around ₹10-₹15 by handrikshawpuller or auto rikshaw to reach here. Airport (Babatpur, Varanasi) is 60 km and taxis are easily available. Hotel also has a pick up facility on demand.

name: Hotel Jahanvi
description: It is the hotel of Indian Tourism Department. Situated at 4 km from Railway Station. Direct autorikshaw or handrikshaws are available from railway station.

name: Ramnagar Fort
description: The fort of the King of Kashi, built in 1750 in the Mughal style, is now a museum with a collection of ancient weapons and other artefacts. It was built by Raja Balwant Singh of Banaras of red sandstone and has a unique blend of Mughal and Rajput architecture. It has grand courtyards, intricate carvings and beautiful gardens. Inside the palace, there is a costume museum, famous for showcasing the royal collection of costumes and textiles including traditional Varanasi sarees, weapons and many other antiques.

name: Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Park
description: Contains a statue of Deen Dayal Upadhyaya.

name: Varanasi Beach
description: A river beach with remote views of Ganga aartis.

name: Son View Point
description: A lookout and a picnic area. Great views of the Son Valley.

name: Salkhan Fossils Park
description: The 25 hectare park contains fossils of stromatolites, algae and ancient trees that are around 1.4 billion years old, dating to the Proterozoic period. For science lovers, it is a wonderful place but the park is not well maintained by the locals. Signs, guides and basic amenities are limited. The tourism potential of the site is untapped, making it for now, off the beaten track.

name: Veer Lorik Stone
description: The split stone structure has its origin in a folklore love story. The hero Veer Lorik demonstrates his love for Manjari by cutting the stone with his sword in a single swipe.

name: Vijaygarh Fort
description: The fort is believed to have existed in the mythological times of the Mahabharata. In the 11th century, it was upgraded by Maharaja Vijay Pal. Inside the fort there are stone gravings and a number of statues. Four lakes surround the fort, adding it to its visual appeal.

name: Maurya Vegetables Market
description: Fresh rural produce.

name: Khalsa Hotel Restaurant
description: Lunch, dinner and a variety of sweets.

name: New Hotel Savera
description: Has an in-house restaurant serving pizza and tandoori options. All rooms have running hot and cold water.

name: Ram Ghat
description: Ramghat is the main feature of Chitrakoot and resembles a minature Varanasi with river boats and pilgrims. It is located on the banks of the quiet river Mandakini. It is an important pilgrim spot and there are many ashrams where holy men in saffron dresses meditate and offer the solace of their wisdom to the large number of pilgrims who congregate there.

name: Gupt Godavari
description: Gupt Godavari is a natural wonder consisting of two caves. There is a pond known as 'Sitakund' in one of these caves which is perpetually fed by a small stream of water. It is believed that Ram and his brother Lakshman held court in the cave with a stream of water running along its base and two natural throne-like rocks. It really is quiet nice, be prepared to walk through knee deep water on uneven ground. Entrance is ten rupees but beware, the ticket office may fry to sell you multiple tickets and the cave is full of shameless priests who will demand donations, offerings, larger donations, and are not above grabbing tourists! Assume you will lose at least 50 rupees.

name: Hanuman Dhara
description: Hanuman Dhara is a spring located on a steep hillside in Chitrakoot. On foot one has to climb a steep flight of 650 steps to reach this place. There is a big statue of Lord Hanuman, on which the water of this spring tumbles over. It is believed that, Hanuman Dhara was created by Ram to assuage Hanuman when he returned after setting Lanka on fire. Another 180 steps from here will get you to the Sita Rasoi. You may avoid the 650 steps by taking the newly launched (as of 2021) cable car ride by DRIL for ₹130 for a 2-way ticket.

name: Janaki Kund
description: Janaki Kund is situated 2 km south of Chitrakoot in Satna District, on the banks of the Mandakini River. Literally ‘Janaki Kund’ means the ‘Pool of Sita’. According to a legend, it was the favorite bathing spot of Sita, during the years of exile with her husband Lord Ram. It is said that Sita's footprints are imprinted on the rocks here. It is a quiet place which is blessed by Sita and people consider it auspicious to bathe here.

name: Kamtanath Mandir
description: Some people said that during exile of lord Ram. Rama prayed to Kamtanath (Deity of local villagers) to fight with devils. After darshan in temple one must do parikrama of 5.5 km around the Kamadgiri hill.

name: Lakshaman Pahari
description: Some people believed that during exile younger brother of Ram stayed on the Lakshaman Hill. Lakshman hill is situated on half way of Parikrama path of Kamdgiri.

name: Sati Anusuiya
description: Sati Anasuya Temple is located at Sati Anasuya in Chitrakoot District of Uttar Pradesh. It enshrines the idol of Sati Anasuya, the wife of saint Atri, with her three babies who are said to be the incarnations of Brahma, Vishnu and Maheswar.The 24 different forms of god appeared on the earth can be found here in the form of idols. The Mandakini River flows nearby. The ancient ashram of Rishi Atri is above the temple.

name: Sfatik Shila
description: Sphatik Shila is situated in a densely forested area to the south of Chitrakoot in Satna District. This picturesque spot is famous for its two massive rocks which are believed to have the footprints of Lord Ram. It is located within a short distance beyond Janaki kund, on the banks of the Mandakini River. According to legend it was here that Sita was pecked at by Jayant, son of Lord Indra, in the form of a crow.

name: Sita Rasoi
description: This is believed that this place was the kitchen of Lord Ram’s wife Sita. Sita Rasoi is situated on the peak of the Hanuman Dhara Hill.

name: Shivani Shakti Peeth
hours: 7.30 AM - 11 AM and 1 PM to 7.30 PM
description: One of the 51 Shaktipeeth in India. Inside the Temple, there is an idol of Lord Shiva known as Chanda. Festivals like Ramnavami, Makar Sankranthi and Deepavali are celebrated here. According to Hindu Mythology it is the holy place where Right breast of maa Durga felt down. Maa is worshiped here with the name Maa Shivani/ Gayatri and her concert, Bhaitavs is worshiped with the name Chanda.

name: Mata Shri Jai Devi Anand Ram Jaipuriya Smriti Bhawan
Pitri Smriti
price: around 500RP for a simple room with attached bathroom.
description: One of the few hotels on the Ghat accepting foreign tourists,clean, Great views from the large patio.

name: MPT official tourist bungalow
description: The official Tourist bungalow in Chitrakoot (dham), well maintained with friendly English speaking staff, a refreshing garden (and an electric shoe polisher!) it's definitely recommended. The cheap dormitories tend to book out completely. Accepting foreign tourists, beware "official" guides loitering inside.

name: Mata Shri Jaidevi Anandram Jaipuriya Smriti Bhawan
Mahavir Swami Wildlife Sanctuary
description: The sanctuary has a variety of fauna including many kinds of deer, monkeys and leopards.

name: Deogarh
description: A group of 31 Jain temples, built between the 8th century and the 17th century. The most famous of the temples is the Shantinath temple, which was built before 862. The Jain temples have a large number of panels depicting scenes from Jain mythology and votive tablets. The pillars are carved with a thousand Jain figures. Worship at some of the Jain temples is still held regularly.

name: Kakramath
description: A Shiva temple made from granite and built in a Khajuraho-like architectural style.

name: Kirat Sagar
description: An artificial lake made by the Chandela kings in the 11th century.

name: Chaurasi Gumbad
description: A square-shaped landmark comprising of nine domes and 84 arches. Built in an Indo-Islamic architectural style, it is believed to house a tomb of one of the Sultans of the Lodi dynasty, who ruled parts of Northern India from the 15th to 16th centuries.

name: Ocean World Water Park
description: A water park full of swimming pools and slides.

name: Om Bazar
description: Orai's first shopping mall.

name: OYO 47405 Comfort Inn
description: Clean, air-conditioned rooms with complimentary breakfast.

name: Bhitiharwa Ashram
description: The torch of freedom movement started here by Mahatma Gandhi in 1924. The Satyagrah Andolan started from here as well.

name: Valmiki National Park
description: A dense forest and a holiday spot in the periphery. According to mythology it was the residence of Sita, wife of lord Rama, with Luv and Kush, her sons, for years in the Valmiki ashram. Now it is a sanctuary with wide range of animals and goons with pistols.

name: Hotel Amrapali
description: A no-star hotel, luxury suites.

name: Hotel Kishan
description: A small 0-star hotel, small rooms.

name: Fun and Adventure Water Park
description: A water-based amusement park.

name: Moti Jheel
description: An oxbow lake.

name: Gandhi Sangrahalaya
description: A museum dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha movement, with wide collection of relics and photographs. The tall monumental column nearby was designed by Nandalal Bose, an artist from Santiniketan. The column is at the site where Gandhi was presented in court.

name: Tandoori
address: 20m down a small non-market alley off to the left of the main road as you walk towards the border.

name: Golghar
description: Captain John Garstin built a Golghar for the storage of food for the British army with storing capacity of 140,000 tons in 1786.

name: Mahatma Gandhi Setu
description: The bridge over the river Ganges connecting Patna and Hajipur.

name: Kumhrar
description: Explore the ancient ruins of Pataliputra. Of the 80 pillars (Fa Hien, in 5th century CE, found the pillars shining as bright as glass) excavated at the site; only one remains.

name: Bihar Museum
description: Opened in 2015, the museum shows you the history of Bihar. It has several galleries, including the regional gallery, the contemporary gallery, the historical art galleries and the gallery on Bihari diaspora. The museum is open from 10:00 to 19:00 except Monday. However, the history part is closed after 17:00 hours and only the Children's Gallery is open from 17:00 to 19:00. Ticket costs for Indians are as follows: Adults - ₹100, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹50, Students - ₹50, while for foreigners is: Adults - ₹500, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹250, Camera - ₹100

name: Deep Narayan Singh Museum
description: Small local history museum, named after independence hero and first minister of Bihar, Deep Narayan Singh, who was born in Hajipur.

name: Gandhi Sangrahalaya
description: A public museum showcasing the life and principles of Mahatma Gandhi. It contains an exhibition containing photos, paintings, sculptures, manuscripts and quotations; all the major events in his life are told here. There is also a section containing photographs of his childhood through the various phases of Gandhi's life, including being taken to the crematorium. The building also houses a library which has a rich collection of books, magazine, literature and audio-video material related to Gandhi's life.

name: Indira Gandhi Planetarium
description: Among the largest and best planetariums in Asia, it attracts a large number of both domestic and foreign tourists. The planetarium has regular film shows on subjects related to astronomy and also holds exhibitions.

name: Patna Museum
price: Entry for foreigners ₹250, Indians, ₹10 additional ₹250 to see Holy Relic Casket.
description: It has more than 50,000 rare art objects, with many related to India in the ancient, middle ages and the British colonial era. Don't forget to see the Holy Relic Casket with the sacred ashes of Lord Buddha, and the beautiful statue Yakshani.

name: Shrikrishna Science Centre
price: ₹30 for general entry, tickets for particular shows cost extra
address: West Gandhi Maidan, Raja Ji Salai, Dujra Diara
description: The main science museum in the city with over 50 exhibits on physics and mathematics, with an emphasis towards optical illusions. Targeted towards kid aged 10 and over but adults will also have an enjoyable time the first time around.

name: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Science City
Rajendra Smriti Sangrahalaya
description: A museum dedicated to Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India.

name: Bharatiya Nritya Kala Mandir
description: A crafts museum and a multi-purpose cultural centre. The building contains dance and drama studios, a gallery space, and an art museum.

name: Kali Temple-Darbhanga House
description: One of the oldest temple of Goddess Kali.

name: Pathar ki Masjid
description: Built by Pervez, the elder brother of Shah Jahan and the first Mughal prince who made Bihar his residence.

name: Padri Ki Haveli
description: Oldest church in Bihar. When Roman Catholics first arrived in Bihar, they built a small church in 1713.

name: Takht Sri Patna Sahib
description: The birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.

name: Maner-Sufi Saint Shrine
description: You can buy famous Maner Ka Ladoo(Sweets). Maner Sweets is one of the popular shops that specializes in these. However, avoid going there in the late evening or night.

name: Sonepur Cattle Fair
description: Largest cattle and animal fair in Asia. It is held in November in Sonepur which across the Ganges from Patna.

name: Buddha Smriti Park
description: A large park constructed in former jail ground is an oasis from noise and bustle of the city. Quiet meditative place and air conditioned libraries are the real relief even for a waiting time for the train. The large stupa is where ashes of Buddha originally from Vaishali are kept. There is a laser show in the evenings, which is related to the history of Bihar from the Ramayana to present.

name: Funtasia Water Park
description: Contains attractions like waterslides, wave pool, swimming pools, multi-cuisine restaurant, coffee shops, souvenir shops and a banquet hall.

name: Gandhi Maidan
description: Gandhi Maidan is the heart of this city today.

name: Sanjay Gandhi Jaivik Udyan
alt: Sanjay Gandhi Biological Park, Patna Zoo
description: One of the most popular picnic spots in Patna. It consists of a zoo and a botanical garden.

name: Shaheed Veer Kunwar Singh Azadi Park
Patna Golf Club
description: With some very tough holes, this well-maintained course situated downtown will prove interesting to amateur and pros alike. The Patna Golf Club is set in beautiful surroundings.

name: Bandhan Boutique
address: G-9, Pushpanjali Complex, Opp. S.K. Puri Check Post, Boring Road

name: Pind Balluchi
address: Revolving Floor, Biscomaun Bhawan, Gandhi Maidan
description: Pind Balluchi is a well-known chain of restaurants with franchises in various cities, now including Patna.

Elegant rooms feature wood floors, flat-screen TVs and sitting areas, as well as desks, washers, and balconies or terraces. Suites add dining tables and separate sitting areas. A 24-hour buffet restaurant serves international cuisine. There's also a stylish lounge with a bar and a snack menu, as well as a banquet hall and a fitness room.

name: Rohtasgarh Fort
description: The massive fort of Rohtasgarh stands on top of the Kaimur Hill and is about 45 km south east of Sasaram. The fort is constructed on a plateau at a height of 1600 ft above sea level. The fort gets its name from the mythological character Rohiteshwa, the son of King Harischandra, but there are no historical evidences regarding supporting this fact. The exact origin and history of the fort is not known but the earliest structure of the fort dates back to the time of king Sashanka of seventh century AD. It was also captured by Prithviraj Chauhan but the Rohtasgarh Fort came into prominence after it was captured by Sher Shah, from a local Hindu king, in 1539. In 1558, Raja Man Singh, Akbar's general and governor of Bengal and Bihar, took charge of the fort. Raja Man Singh made considerable addition to the fort including the famous Hati Pol or Elephant Gate. In the later years the fort sheltered rebels, dacoits and even Maoist guerillas In 2010s the Rothasgarh Fort has been cleared of Maoist rebels. Today the ruins of the fort are spread over a large area. There are four gateways and several structures inside the walled complex. the palace complex is the most well preserved and most visited area of the fort and is directly accessible by car. There are several trekking routes in the fort and one can chose a different combination of gates and routes. The Elephant Gate lies on the southern part of the palace complex. The sand stone gate way, with white marble ornamentation, was constructed by Man Singh and is flanked with sculpture of elephants. It leads to the diwani aam or public court. At the centre of the complex lies the Raja and Rani Mahal, which was connected by a causeway. there are several structures in the palace complex with ornate oriel windows and cupolas. Outside the palace complex stands the Jami Masjid, which was constructed by Sher Shah. Apart from these there is a Ganesh Temple. The Masjid and the Ganesh temples is located just south of the palace complex. About 4 km east of the palace complex lies the Rohtasgarh lies the Rothasgarh Devi Temple along with a Shiva Temple. The Rohtasgarh Devi Temple is a domed structure while the Shiva temple has a towering structure and is located atop a small hill. The Shiva temple is approached by a long flight of stairs.

name: Shergarh Fort
description: Located on the Kaimur Range and east of the Durgabati River the Shergarh Fort is lying unattended for more than 400 years. It is located 32 km south west of Sasaram. It is a natural hill fort sited amidst gorgeous scenery. The top of the hill, now a mass of ruins commands a magnificent view of the distant range of hills and the valley of Durgawati. Although named after Sher Shah it is quite likely the fort was constructed at an earlier date by a local Hindu king and was later taken over by Sher Shah. Much smaller in size than the Rohtasgarh Fort, the fortification of Shergarh is visible from a distance. The nearest motorable point is Badalgarh, From Badalgarh one has to walk for about 1.5 km to the reach the stairways leading to the fort. The fort stands on a plateau, which has two different elevation. The depression between the two levels served as a natural reservoir, which was feed by rain water. The lower side of the plateau lies on the north and probably had no structure; now it is covered with thick jungle. The southern and the higher side contains several palatial buildings, which were probably erected by Sher Shah. The palatial building contains an intricate network of underground passages, rooms and even a well. Shergarh lacks basic tourist infrastructure, which includes approach roads and absence of local guides make exploration difficult..

name: Mahabodhi Temple
description: The site where Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment. This complex is large and contains a number of major attractions within it. One common way of visiting the statue is to "walk in the steps" of the Buddha. It is said that, after attaining enlightenment, the Buddha spent seven weeks in what is now Mahabodhi temple meditating on the nature of what he had discovered. There are several spots in the temple that relate to this tradition. Since the bombing incident in 2013, the temple has been under enhanced security. No laptop, mobile phone, or camera are allowed into the temple ground. The temple is open from 6AM to 9PM. There is no dress code, though visitors are expected to act in a way that respects the sacred nature of the site and expresses courtesy to others. See: Buddhism

description: Opened in 2015, the museum shows you the history of Bihar. It has several galleries, including the regional gallery, the contemporary gallery, the historical art galleries and the gallery on Bihari diaspora. The museum is open from 10:00 to 19:00 except Monday. However, the history part is closed after 17:00 hours and only the Children's Gallery is open from 17:00 to 19:00. Ticket costs for Indians are as follows: Adults - ₹100, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹50, Students - ₹50, while for foreigners is: Adults - ₹500, Children (up to 12 years) - ₹250, Camera - ₹100

It contains an exhibition containing photos, paintings, sculptures, manuscripts and quotations; all the major events in his life are told here. There is also a section containing photographs of his childhood through the various phases of Gandhi's life, including being taken to the crematorium. The building also houses a library which has a rich collection of books, magazine, literature and audio-video material related to Gandhi's life.

There is a laser show in the evenings, which is related to the history of Bihar from the Ramayana to present.

Elegant rooms feature wood floors, flat-screen TVs and sitting areas, as well as desks, washers, and balconies or terraces. Suites add dining tables and separate sitting areas. A 24-hour buffet restaurant serves international cuisine. There's also a stylish lounge with a bar and a snack menu, as well as a banquet hall and a fitness room.

name: Rajnagar Palace Complex
description: The primary reason to visit Rajnagar is to witness the hauntingly beautiful ruins of the once-grand palace. The sprawling estate, though partially lost to the 1934 earthquake, still displays ornate façades, frand gateways, Mughal-Rajput hybrid domes, beautifully carved Hindu temples, and long corridors and courtyards. Unlike many other palace complexes in India, this one remains uncommercialised, open to wanderers, photographers, and heritage enthusiasts who want to explore unfiltered history.

name: Eco Park

name: Snow Yard
price: Expect spending hefty on professional photography
