It is a popular attraction among photographers as the calcium-carbonate-rich slurry has built up into white "mountains", which evoke the glacial fields of Switzerland more than the Thar Desert Rajasthan is known for. Several Bollywood movies are shot here for a snowy backdrop without the exorbitant costs for exotic places.

name: Nagaur Fort
description: Nagaur Fort is one of the finest examples of Rajput-Mughal architecture. Built in the early 12th century and repeatedly altered over subsequent centuries, it witnessed many battles. 90 fountains run in the gardens and buildings. The fort's buildings and spaces, both external and internal, serve as venue, stage and home to a Sufi Music Festival.

name: Khimsar Fort
description: A 500-year-old fort in the middle of the Thar Desert; turned into a hotel furnished with modern facilities. Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb used to stay here; Khinvsar town has 25 small temples; black deer roaming in herds are a tourist attraction.

name: Meera Bai Temple

name: Ladnu

name: Banasthali Vidyapith University

Rajasthani, Indian & continental cuisines are prepared with great care to make you visit a rich experience in Indian Royal Gastronomy. Special meal preferences for children and people with dietary restrictions are supervised by the lady of the house. Facilities include a swimming pool, doctor on call, travel, transport, excursions, massages, cultural programs, puppet shows, yoga, internet, cooking lessons, Jeep safari, boat rides, horse riding and in-house laundry.

description: Best place for coffee or lassi.

name: MGB Hotel in Alwar
description: The hotel has 35 furnished rooms, including 5 suites. Also has an outdoor swimming pool.

name: Bara Baoli
description: (1732 AD) Hindu-style five-storey stepwell is believed to connect to the Palace by a secret tunnel. A popular site for the visitor, Bara Baori has arched windows, traditional paintings and courtyards. Many excellent carvings of birds and animals adorn the structure. It is also a place of some religious importance.

name: Bhadrawati Palace
description: Built in the 11th century. This palace was converted to a hotel, it retains its splendour and is an important site to visit.

name: Chand Baori
description: Situated in Abhaneri, Chand Baori was constructed in the 10th century. It is a huge 100-ft-deep well that consists of steps on three sides.

name: Keoladeo National Park
description: (100km) Formerly known as Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary in Bharatpur.

name: Mehendipur Balaji Temple
description: This temple dedicated to Hanumanji and attracts many pilgrims daily.

name: Neelkanth
description: Located in Aravali hills at Dausa (also located in the Jaipur Division, is a temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. Panch Mahadev is one of the oldest temples enshrined with a large stone Linga.

name: Ranthambore National Park
description: One of the best places in India to see tigers in the wild.

name: Sariska Reserve and National Park
description: One of the most famous national parks in India and designated as a tiger reserve.

name: Khetri Fort
description: One of the most haunted places in India.

name: Pahari
description: A small place for trekking also have a temple on top.

name: Panchwati udhyan
description: Houses animals (mainly deer) made of concrete, popular among local families .It is based on the mythological story Ramayna.

name: Shiv Ganga
description: BITS Campus

name: Surajgarh Fort
description: It also has a good resort for stay.

name: Choti Ganga
description: It is a good place for quick bites like sandwiches, samosas, different types of maggi. They also offer fruit juices and tea. It is famous among the students for being the only few places that sell "sutta"(cigarette).

name: All the "redi"s in the BITS campus
Arjun family guesthouse
price: ₹150 in the off season, ₹300 in peak, all including food
description: They organise a ₹500 per person (ideally minimum two) overnight camel trek. No room charge if you do, but you can leave your bags in a room overnight if he's not booked out. Lovely host. He's not that pushy, even if he does meet you at the bus stop. Be a little wary of the food - once contained off milk.

name: Badal House Khuri
description: Rustic, peaceful accommodation. The owner, Mr. Badal, will take you on a desert safari riding the camels and night camping.

name: Bangar Museum
description: A small museum with a good collection of stone artifacts acquired from different places of Rajasthan. It exhibits ancient, historical and artistic items such as costumes, coins, and arms.

name: Virendra Singh Shaktawat
description: Arranges horseback safaris from Udaipur to Ranakpur, around the Aravalli Mountains and through the Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary. Contact also for jeep safaris, night drives and nature hikes around Ranakpur.

name: Hotel Maharani Bagh
description: Spacious, clean rooms set among a mango grove. Doubles are around ₹5000 per night. Room service is slow, especially in the morning.

name: Shivika Lake hotel
description: Shivika Lake Hotel is set in an idyllic setting with hills around. Shivika Lake Hotel has in total 13 rooms and 5 tented accommodation. All rooms are tastefully and traditionally furnished with local material, colour & design, rooms give a camp atmosphere with modern amenities. You can also trek or have a safari from there.

name: Bheemgad
description: Bheemgarh (Kakoni) is situated about 85 Km. from Baran district Headquarters in the Chhipabarod Tehsil. It is surrounded by the Mukundra mountain ranges and on the bank of Parwan river. It is said that the temples at Kakoni are built in 8th century. These are the remains of the 'Vaishnav', 'Shiv' and 'Jain' temples. About 60% statues of the Kakoni temples are kept in the Museums at Kota and Jhalawar districts. Archaeological department has announced the place as secure since 1970.

name: Dalhanpur - on the bank of River Chhapi
Jain Temple
description: Mahaveer Jain Temple situated in near to city centre. It has a big standing sculpture (granite stone ) of Lord Mahaveer. Bhagwan Mahaveer is worshipped as the 24th Thirthnakar in Jain religion. Once you get in the temple you can find a peace and inner joy. Don't violate Jain regulations inside the temple. This temple is maintained by Agrawal Jain Samaj Aklera.

name: Kamkheda Balaji
description: A small village famous for a very big temple of Lord Hanuman and is a very sacred place for Hindu and The President of this temple is Gajanand Ji Mangal (Ugani Wale, Aklera) and devotees come not only from Rajasthan but also from Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, New Delhi. It is believed that those who visit the temple in the months of Vaishakh, the Lord Hanuman will bestow his blessings on the devotee as well as fulfil his wishes. The village got electricity and road facilities in 1977 by the efforts of the former member of legislative assembly, the Late Shri Vitthal Prasad Sharma (1920-1982). That's why people of Aklera and Kamkheda gratefully installed a milestone in the honour of him. The easiest way to reach there is by road through Aklera for the devotees from Rajasthan and from Binaganj in M.P., for devotees from M.P. and U.P.

name: Shiv Mandir
description: One of the oldest Lord Shiv Temple of city. It has an ancient and big Shiv Linga.

name: Rani Ki Ji Baori (Queen's Step Well)
description: The most famous step well in Bundi, it was built in 1699 by the spurned queen. It is 46 metres deep and includes 200 steps.

name: Dabhai Kund
description: The largest in Bundi. Though slightly overgrown, it is well worth a visit for the spectacular carvings on the numerous steps leading down to the water level.

name: Nagar Saga Kund
description: Constructed between 1871 and 1875, these are 2 step wells that have been extensively refurbished.

name: Taragarh Fort
description: Built in the 16th century, this is one of the most famous forts in Rajasthan due to its intricate structures and a highly-regarded painting gallery.

name: Garh (Bundi) Palace and Chitrashala - Ummed Mahal
description: These adjacent structures are must-sees and include some of the most amazing paintings in India. It is a steep climb to get up to the palace, which needed protection from attacking elephants.

name: Sukh Mahal
address: On the southern tip of Lake Jait Sagal
description: A smaller palace built on a dam wall; Rudyard Kipling stayed here.

name: Chaurasi Khambon ki Chhatri
description: Constructed in the late 17th century by the maharaja as a memorial.

name: Lake Jait Sagar
description: Once famous for louts flowers, this lake is adjacent to a small garden and Shikar Burj, an area used by kings for hunting.

name: Lake Nawal Sagar
description: A large square-shaped artificial lake containing many small islands. A temple dedicated to Varuna, the vedic god of water, is half-submerged in the middle of the lake. The lake feeds the numerous step wells in the old city by creating an artificial water table.

name: Lake Kanak Sagar
description: An extremely beautiful lake and town.

name: Ramgarh Vishdhari Sanctuary
description: A 307 km² park. Animals that live in the park include leopard, sambhar, wild boar, chinkara, sloth bear, Indian wolf, hyena, jackal, and Fox. The best time to visit is between September and May. Safaris can be booked at several hotels, including Vrindawati, which is operated by the government.

name: Shree Krishna Art Jewelry
description: A store where you can find local treasures such as antiques, artwork, old coins, etc.

name: Yug Art
description: Yug is a fine painter who captures the beauty of Rajasthan. Styles range from portraits to landscapes to comics.

name: Bundi Cafe & Crafts
description: Best place to buy Bundi School Paintings.

name: Kipling Cafe
description: Fruit ingredients are grown next to the restaurant.

name: Lakha
description: A tiny place where you sit on cushions and the owner cooks you an amazing meal.

name: Namaste Cafe
address: Fort & Palace Road, Nahar ka chohta
description: Soul food. Really nice ambience and service.

name: Tom and Jerry
description: Western food, popular with tourists.

name: Haveli Braj Bhushanjee
description: Traditionally decorated Darikhana is being used as dining hall. One can enjoy best local vegetarian meals in traditional atmosphere. You can also have your meals on the terrace with magical view of illuminated palace and town.

name: Sathi Lassi
description: Good, thick lassis.

name: Bundi Haveli
description: The rooms are comfortable.

name: Daulat Niwas
description: Built in the early 1700s. The cheapest place to stay in Bundi - but only a few rooms are available.

name: Dev Niwas (God's Residence)
description: Built by Deva Dhabai in 1684. Very luxurious for a budget hotel.

name: Hadee Rani Guest House
description: Opened in 2006, the establishment is run by a friendly family. The food is good; so are the rooms.

name: Haveli Braj Bhushanjee
description: Haveli Braj Bhushanjee was built 200 years before and belongs to Bohara Braj Bhushanjee family, which gave Bundi as many as four Prime Ministers all in the 19th century. Haveli Braj Bhushanjee offers traditional architecture by way of tibaries and courtyards which are painted in Bundi School Paintings, consisting of Raganies, court scene, hunting scenes. Extensive painted courtyards are worth visiting. Each and every surface of this haveli are nicely decorated with old photographs and antique collection. The Haveli offers 24 well appointed AC rooms with all modern amenities. All the rooms have been renovated in such a way that the atmosphere of the old architecture is not disturbed. The rooms have been traditionally decorated and few rooms have some of the finest Bundi School Painting (murals) one can see in this region.

name: Kasera Heritage View
description: A beautiful haveli run by a family.

name: Mangalam Guest House and Indian Restaurant
description: A nice homestay with good food in a well-kept haveli.

name: R. N. Haveli Guest House
description: All-women run establishment. Good home style food (ask for the dal dhokla), decent rooms and a nice atmosphere.

name: Rajmahal Guest House
address: Suraj Ji Ka Bad, Balchand Para
description: Clean, friendly budget hotel run and owned by two young brothers.

name: Tarah Homestay and Guest House
description: Nice cosy rooms overlooking the palace. Home atmosphere with tasty cooking. Rooftop has great views. Manager's name is Jitu.

name: Vrindawati
description: A 7-room basic hotel operated by the Rajasthani government.

name: Hadoti Palace
description: Very spacious rooms, swimming pool, on a noisy street.

name: Ishwari Niwas Heritage Resort
description: A 100-year-old haveli previously inhabited by Maharao Raja Ishwari Singh, the ruler of Bundi. Rooms are decorated with paintings in the Bundi art style.

name: Ummaid Bagh Resort
description: A camping site owned by the ruler of Bundi in the 18th century, it now provides accommodation in luxury tents.

name: Gagron Fort
alt: गागरोन का क़िला Gāgron Kā Qilā
description: One of six hill forts in Rajasthan that have been inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. However, the hill itself is surrounded by water, being constructed on the confluence of the Ahu and Kali Sindh rivers. That's why it's often called jaldurg (जलदुर्ग), meaning "water fort". Unlike other hill forts, Gagron is off the beaten track.

name: Shantinath Jain Temple
description: 11th century temple

name: The Government museum
description: Displaying paintings, statues and manuscripts.

name: Kolvi Buddhist caves
description: An ancient religious complex consisting of around 50 caves.

name: Sun Temple
description: An intact 11th century temple intricately made from red stone consisting of over a hundred pillars and several beautifully carved sculptures. Its architectural style is reminiscent of the temples at Khajuraho and the more notable sun temple in Konark.

name: Juna Mahal
description: A former royal residence on the foothill. Accessed by narrow crowded road up the hill. Early Rajput fort palace built from 13th to 19th century by different rulers. It has seven floors decorated with local green stone called pareva, murals, frescoes, mirror and glass inlays. The palace is fortified and represent the evolution of architecture, art and construction from 13th to 19th century. Poorly maintained but worth a visit. Buy tickets at Udai Bilas Palace and then go here.

name: Badal Mahal
description: A pleasure palace built on the bank of Gaip Sagar Lake. Now converted into small museum of royal items and stone sculptures.

name: Naulakha Bawdi
description: An old stepwell built in 1586 by Premal Devi, wife of Maharawal Asakaran of Dungarpur State. Surrounded by forest area.

name: Nanabhai Park
description: A small park on the bank of Gaip Sagar Lake for good view of the lake

name: War Museum
description: A small museum on army above a gate

name: Shrinathji Temple
description: Old Vaishnava temple with large statue of Shrinathji.

name: Udai Bilas Palace
description: An 20th century Indo-Sarasenic architecture palace. Residence of Dungar State royals. Open for guests and visitors.

name: Dungarpur Mews Car Museum
description: A collection of vintage cars and other artifacts by the royals of Dungarpur

name: Bird Sactuary Park and Flower Garden
Fatehgadi
description: Located on the hillock near the city. Gives fantastic view of the city and Gaip Sagar Lake

name: Navgrah Madhav Park
description: Small city garden

name: Shaheed Smarak Park
description: Small city park

name: Sagar Hotel and Restaurant
description: Multi-cuisine restaurant

name: Mammadev Temple
description: The temple and the kund were again built by Rana Kumbha in the year 1460. The temple stands exactly below the fort and once had four large slabs with several inscriptions on them. The writings gave the history of Mewar from the time of Guhil, the founder of Mewar dynasty, till Rana Kumbha, a great builder of forts and temples. The slabs are now preserved in the museum at Udaipur. The temple houses an image of Kuber (God of Wealth) and also has two chhatris (cenotaphs) in memory of Rana Kumbha and the famous warrior Prithviraj Chauhan. Very near the temple is a large kund or reservoir close to which is the chhatri cenotaph) of Prithviraj - the knight-errant of Mewar.

name: Vedi Temple
description: A sacrificial temple, this was also built by Rana Kumbha and is a three storeyed Jain temple. The structure was later renovated by Maharana Fateh Singh and is also the only remnant to have survived of all the ancient sacrificial places of India.

name: Aodhi Hotel
description: A sanctuary-resort.

name: Dera Kumbhalgarh Tent House
description: Marvellous tent hotel on a hillock.

name: Karni Palace Hotel
description: This is a reasonable budget choice that does not seem to have yet hit the guide books. It is clean, close to the bus stop to Udaipur and has a restaurant.

name: Kumbhalgarh Fort Hotel
description: A luxury hotel combined with the most modern and ‘state of the art' facilities and amenities offer the most comfortable stay.

name: Ratnadeep Hotel
description: The mid-range Kumbhal Castle, and finally, two low-end but perfectly adequate regular hotels at Kelwara village, 6 km from the fort. Do not confuse it with the New Ratan Deep (note change in name), face each other across the only street in Kelwara.

name: Tiger Valley Resort
description: Consists of twelve spacious and well-appointed rooms which provide comfortable living.

name: Sadbhav Dining Hall
description: Unlimited Thali ₹INR 70. Good food.

name: Daya Bhawan Dharamshala
description: Daya Bhawan is strictly a budget accommodation for pilgrims. Toilets are common outside the room for most of the rooms. It has 32 rooms.

name: Dehliwali Dharamshala
description: Delhiwala Dharamshala is strictly a budget accommodation for pilgrims. It has 91 rooms.

name: Garden View Hotel
description: Garden View Hotel of Nathdwara offers Contemporary luxuries in peaceful surrounding and within proximity to the world famous Shrinathji Temple in Nathdwara with modern amenities.

name: Shreeji Resort
description: Shree Ji Resort offers you the best of traditional Indian Hospitality with modern comforts in Nathdwara. A well appointed and spacious seventeen room resort located on national highway number eight, just about one kilometer from world famous Lord Krishana temple.

name: Nikunj River Resort
description: The resort offers accommodation in well appointed cottages provided with modern amenities and beautiful view of the natural surrounding.

name: Arasuri Ambaji Shaktipith Temple
description: The temple has no statue in the sanctum but a geometric shape matrix called yantra which is venerated. The shikhara of the temple is adorned with gold. The temple is visited by millions every year, especially on full moon days. The major festivals include full moon days of Kartika and Bhadrapada months in Hindu calendar. In Bhadrapada month, thousands of pilgrims visit the temple travelling by foot from far away places. These long streams of padayatri pilgrims come with shrine on wheels, long flags and banners, musical instruments and loudspeakers playing songs. Camps serves these pilgrims with food, drinks and medicines across the travel routes.

name: Ambaji temple on Gabbar hill
description: An eternal flame in a small shrine on top of the Gabbar hill is visited by pilgrims. The place is considered as the original place where the heart of goddess Amba fell, according to mythical story about the origin of the 51 Shaktipeeths. The hilltop can be reached by a ropeway or climbing about thousand steps.

name: Kumbharia Jain temples
description: A cluster of five Jain temples built during the rule of Chaulukya dynasty between 11th and 12th centuries. Similar in plan but varying in decorations and construction. The Neminath temple is a central major temple with colossal statues. Reached via shared jeeps or private vehicles from Ambaji. Has boarding and lodging facilities for Jain pilgrims only.

name: Kamakshi Temple
description: South Indian style temple dedicated to Kamakshi Devi along with 51 other shrines dedicated to goddesses. Built in 2008.

name: Koteshwar Mahadev temple
description: An old temple dedicated to Shiva. There is a perennial natural water stream and a tank nearby where pilgrims bath.

name: Kailash Tekri
description: A small Shiva temple is located on hilltop of Kailash Hill. Beautiful place for watching sunset.

name: Mangalya Van
description: Forest garden developed by state government. Good for family picnic.

name: Ambaji ropeway
description: Go on the Gabbar hill by ropeway. Visit the sacred shrine and have a view of the town and the valley from the top. The Aravalli hill range is visible.

name: Marble statue shops at Koteshwar
description: Plenty of shops selling marble statues, especially Hindu gods and goddesses and decorative pieces, on the way to Koteshwar temple. The town is surrounded by several marble quarries and the artisans can be seen chiselling statues and pieces at many places.

name: Street vendors across town
description: The town is surrounded by forest so forest produce such as honey and wax can be purchased from street vendors. The Kesuda flowers are sold in its blooming season in March. Kesuda flowers are boiled in water to produce coloured water which is used in Holi festival and in bathing for its medicinal properties.

name: Kumbhariyaji Jain Bhojanshala
price: ₹50 for breakfast, ₹75 for lunch, ₹20 for tea, ₹60 for dinner
hours: Sunrise to 9AM for breakfast, noon to 2PM for lunch, from 5PM to sunset for dinner
description: For Jain pilgrims only. Jain diet rules are strictly followed. Collect passes from office.

name: Ambaji Bhojanalay
description: Serves Gujarati dishes at an affordable cost. The food is provided by the temple trust.

name: Soda-shops near Ambaji temple
description: Try lemon soda or pudina soda. Cool refreshing drinks with carbonated water and salted spices to beat the summer heat.

name: Hotel Ambaji International
description: Has a friendly and knowledgeable staff and the rooms are quiet and serene.

name: Kumbhariyaji Jain Dharmashala
price: ₹950 for 2-bed room, ₹1200 for 4-bed room, ₹150 for extra bed
description: For Jain pilgrims only. Contact office for booking.

name: Ambaji Trust Hospital
description: Basic medical facilities.

name: General Hospital
description: Government cottage hospital.

name: Kazi ni Vavdi
description: It is a well with inscriptions on the side walls, one in Arabic and the other in Devnagri, bearing respectively the dates 1417 (820 Hijri year) and 1522 (Samvat 1578). The second inscription shows that the well was built in 1522 by Shamsher-ul-Mulk, who is stated by tradition to have been a son of Sultan Ahmed Shah.

name: Sapteshwar Mahadev temple
description: Located at the confluence of Sabarmati and Debhol rivers, this is a place of natural beauty. The kund and a temple housing seven linga of Shiva is ancient and associated with lores of Saptarishis.

name: Mini Pavagadh
description: A 300-year-old temple dedicated to Mahakali is popular in pilgrims. Fairs are organised on Janmashtami and Mahashivaratri.

name: Roda Group of Temples
description: Seven Hindu temples built during Gurjara-Pratihara or Rashtrakuta period (8th-9th century). Considered as the fountainhead of all classical temples of Gujarat.

name: Tomb of Sikandarshah
description: A mausoleum built by Gujarat Sultan Mahmud Begada in honour of his soldier Sikandar Shah in c. 1480.

name: Mahakali temple
description: Constructed by king of erstwhile Idar state in 15th century for the fulfillment of wish of child.

name: Tropic of Cancer Science Park
description: science museum right where the Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat. Exhibits on geography, geocoordinates, seasons and related phenomena.

name: Tirupati Rishivan Adventure Park
description: Water park and adventure park with many rides. Meera Hotel Resort with lodging and stay facilities. Outside food allowed.

name: Ramaleshvar Lake
description: This lake is said to have been built by Rao Ranmal, with its western bank covered with picturesque domed cupolas, chhatris, raised over the ashes of the forefathers of the leading Idar families.

name: Idar Fort
description: The town was surrounded by a brick wall in the past which had three gateways named Mira Darwaja, Dhuleta Darwaja, marked with many red hands each recording a victim to the rite of sati. Inside of the wall, a road, running round the town, leads to the Gantino Darwajo, a rock-cut passage giving access to the main route to Rajasthan in past. Only a portion of the fortification is present now.

name: Clock Tower
description: The starting of old town.

name: Sheela Udyan
description: A rock garden.

name: Rani Talav
description: a lake, half a mile to the north-east of Idar, has an area of ninety-four acres and a greatest depth of seventeen feet. Its supply lasts throughout the year but is used for irrigation. The east side of the lake is banked with masonry steps. It is said, but this is doubtful, to have been dug and built about 380 years ago by the wife of Rao Bhau, chief of Idar.

name: Pavapuri Jain temple
description: built in the centre of the lake which can be reached by a bridge. The main temple is around 72 feet high, 72 feet long and is built on 72 pillars. The height of central idol of Mahavira is 72 cm which is surrounded by 72 carved figurines.

name: Shrimad Rajchandra Vihar
description: a Jain temple complex on eastern hillock dedicated to Shrimad Rajchandra.

name: Juna Bhavnath Temple, Mau
description: This 1300-year-old temple has a reservoir, kund, named Bhrigukund which believed to cure leprosy if bathed in its water. There is a temple dedicated to Shiva and temple dedicated to the son of Bhrigu, Avan Rishi. The place is situated on the banks of Hathmati river dam. The fair is organised on the last Monday of Shraavana month of Hindu calendar and on Mahashivratri which is visited by large number of people.

name: Hotel Rajdeep
price: 2 double beds room ₹2500, 1 double bed room ₹1500
description: AC rooms and restaurant.

name: Thol Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Small and beautiful bird sanctuary. This 7-km² artificially created fresh water has several islands. Surrounded by marshes, it attracts migratory birds in winter including pintails, flamingos, cranes, pelicans, mallards, geese and many more. 150 species of birds are seen here. It was established as irrigation tank in 1912. Call Assistant Conservator of Forests, Sanand for details.

name: Brahma Vav
description: Based on ornamentation of the miniature shrines in the stepwell, it is dated to 14th century. It has 27 niches without any idols now. It is now in despair due to lack of maintenance.

name: Brahma Temple
description: One of the rare Brahma temples of India. It was built in third quarter of the 11th century.

name: Ambika Mataji temple
description: Situated in north-east of the town, the Ambika temple was built in the early 11th century and has been renovated many times since.

name: Bhrigurishi Ashram and Bhrigunath Mahadev temple
description: It is associated with folklores and Puranic stories.

name: Kshirjamba Mahalaxmi temple
description: According to religious texts, Kshirja was the family goddess of people created during the yajna of Brahma. The temple is on a hillock accessible by vehicle as well as steps. Gives a good view of the Harnav river.

name: Pankhanath Mahadev temple
description: A west-facing plain simple temple which is restored several times. In the back-niche of the temple, there is a figure of Nataraja (Shivatandav) with eight hands which helps in deciding the dating of the temple. There is also one more Shiva figure in other form. The temple belongs to c. 11th century, built during reign of Bhima I of Chaulukya dynasty, contemporary of Sun Temple, Modhera. In the sanctum, there is a small protuberance instead of an elaborate lingam which is considered swayambhu (self-existent) by the devotees.

name: Mahavir Swami Jain temple
description: 500-year-old temple which is under reconstruction now.

name: Polo Group of Monuments and the Vijaynagar Forest
description: There are several ruined ancient Hindu and Jain temples which are more than 500 years old.

name: Sardar Chowk market
description: There are several shops and carts selling items of daily needs, fruits, vegetables and groceries.

name: Krishna Sweet Mart
description: Local popular sweet shop.

name: Raghu Chhaya Palace
description: Punjabi dishes.

name: Blue Moon
description: For Punjabi and Gujarati dishes.

name: Royal Darbar
description: Dalbati - Rajasthani dish.

name: Amul Parlour
description: Dairy parlour serving various milk products.

name: Mahudi Jain Temple
description: It was established by Jain monk, Buddhisagar Suri in 1917 CE. There is an inscription in the Brahmi script of it. The 22-inch marble idol of Padmaprabh is a central deity. A separate shrine is dedicated to protector deity, Ghantakarna Mahavir. Guru Mandir is a shrine dedicated to Buddhisagar Suri. Devotees offer sukhadi, a sweet to Ghantakarna Mahavir. After offering, it is consumed by devotees within the temple complex.

name: Kotyrak Khadayata temple
description: is dedicated to Krishna and is kuldevta of Khadayata community.

name: Padma Pyramid Centre
description: is another Jain temple nearby in shape of pyramid.

name: Boter Kothani Vav
description: A stepwell built in 1674 CE during the reign of Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. It has unique twin wells. It is now polluted and in poor condition. The oldest surviving monument of the city.

name: Rajmahal
address: Near Old Bus Stand, Rajmahal Road
description: Built in 1904 by Sayajirao Gaekwad III of Baroda State, it was used as the government office and later as the court until 2017. It has three floors and 130 rooms.

name: Swami Vivekanand Lake
description: Redeveloped in 2019, the lake has a children's playground, yoga centre, food court, jogging tracks and boating facilities.

name: Arvind Baug
description: A garden.

name: Biladi Baug
description: A garden with children play area. It has another small stepwell known as Badiyashi Vav built by Shah Virchand Jadavji.

name: Simandhar Jain temple
description: Built in 1971, a large Jain temple dedicated Simandhar Swami, a Jain Tirthankara. A fine example of Maru-Gurjara temple.

name: Dudhsagar Dairy
description: A postmodernist building designed by Achyut Kanvinde. You can watch dairy processing here. Requires prior permission for visit.

name: Manoranjan Parshwanath Jain temple
description: A more than hundred years old Jain twin temples. The central deity Parshwanth was consecrated in Samvat 1920 and is among 108 major Parshwanath temples. The other central deity is Sumatinath. This beautiful two storeyed temple has glass studded roofs and pillars. There are five footprint shrines on the roof accessible only by special permission. No photography without permission.

name: Toranwali Mataji temple
description: The town deity of Mehsana. According to the legend, the temple marks the foundation of the town.

name: Jain Dadawadi
description: Consecrated in Samvat 1956, the hall has a shrine containing footprints of Jain Tirthankara Adinath. The footprints of Jain Muni Ravisagar was consecrated in Samvat 1979 while the idols of Ravisagar and Sukhsagar were installed in Samvat 1991. Later a separate shrine dedicated to Buddhisagar was built outside the hall in Veer Samvat 2495. All these are respected Jain monks so the shrines are visited by their followers. The complex is under reconstruction as of 2026.

name: T. J. Highschool
description: Founded in 1889. Old school building.

name: Nagalpur Lake
description: A lake garden.

name: MMC Plaza
description: Roadside community space where events are organised on Sundays

name: Lakhwad Garden
description: a large urban park.

name: Sai Talav
description: Lakefront garden.

name: Shakti Kund, Akhaj
description: Built in the third quarter of the 10th century during Chaulukya rule. The stepwell has many figures of goddesses and gods in its niches. Must be part of large temple complex in past like Modhera Sun Temple. A small museum nearby holds parts of the former temple.

name: Jasmalnathji Mahadev Temple
description: 12th century temple.

name: Fun Blast
price: ₹20 entry, extra for each game, minimum ₹500 card
description: Enjoy at game and adventure zone for kids and adults. Indoor games, arcade, bowling, trampoline, zipline and many more. A multicuisine restaurant Multi Menu is also there.

name: Swimming Pool at Atal Sports Centre
description: Enjoy an hour of swimming pool in summer heat. Confirm timing.

name: Sardar Patel Stadium
description: Enjoy a cricket match at local stadium during tournament seasons.

name: Wide Angle Cinema
description: Watch Bollywood or Gujarati film. Online Ticket booking available.

name: Mukta A2 Cinemas
description: Enjoy a movie with popcorn

name: Shanku's Water Park and Resort
description: Get cool in summer in water park. It has many water rides.

name: Shanku's Natural Health Centre
description: A wellness centre which offers traditional naturopathy, meditation, massage and yoga therapies. Organic food and balanced diet are available. 3-10 days packages.

name: Bliss Aqua World Resort
price: M-Sa ₹650, Su ₹800, food and costumes extra
description: Enjoy a day at the water park.

name: Tirupati Natural and Water Park
price: Entry ₹60, ₹40 for group of 40 people (Zula Vihar ₹20, Hightech Riders ₹20 Extra)
description: Spread over an area of 50 acres. Rides, boating, gardens, water park and picnic spots. Barren land was cultivated and converted into this park by locals. Guest house with 15 cottages. Restaurant.

name: Nimba Nature Cure
description: A wellness centre offering therapies ranging from physiotherapy, yoga, naturopathy and Ayurveda. Rejuvenate your health.

name: D Mart
description: A shopping mall. Free parking. Can fulfill most needs of the tourist.

name: Sahyog Sweets and Namkeen
description: Try Penda, Mohanthal or Devda, the sweets; or Bhakharwadi, a savoury snack. Fast food, groceries and milk products are available. This is a cooperative run by Dudhsagar dairy staff.

name: Nilkanth Restaurant
description: Multi-cuisine restaurant.

name: Domino's Pizza
description: Try local flavoured pizza.

name: Meera Ice Cream
description: Hand churned "sancha" styled ice cream shop. Best known for fruit based ice creams such as chilly guava and jamun. Wanna try something unusual? ask for ginger honey ice cream! Provides travel packs for long distance takeaway.

name: Madhvi Dairy
description: Drink lassi and milkshakes.

name: Hotel Sahara Bridge
address: Apollo Enclave, Opp. Simandhar Jain temple
description: Upscale hotel. Western toilets, AC rooms, multi-cuisine restaurant, laundry, room service.

name: Hotel Tulsi and Restaurant
address: Opp. Nagalpur Bus Stand, Nr. Nagalpur College
description: Simple rooms, multi-cuisine restaurant (₹500 for two), AC options, room service, budget option.

name: Malgudi Food Inn
description: Great food at multi-cuisine restaurant. AC, room service, laundry.

name: Head Post Office
address: Visnagar Link Rd, Behind GEB, Balark Park Society, Ramdevnagar

name: Blue Dart Express
address: 41, Sardar Patel Vyapar Sankul, Opp. Nalanda School, Urban Bank Road, Malgodown
description: Courier service.

name: Government district library
description: Open Wi-Fi by GTPL.

name: Lions Hospital
description: Medical facilities including for emergencies.

name: Civil Hospital
description: All basic medical facilities operated by Government.

name: Sun Temple
price: ₹25 for Indians, $5/₹300 for Foreigners, ₹30 for parking
description: Built around 11-12th century, the temple complex was commissioned by Chaulukya king Bhima I. The beautifully carved sandstone temple complex has three parts; a reservoir Surya Kund, the assembly hall Sabha Mandapa and the shrine proper Gudha Mandapa. It is located on the bank of Pushpavati river. There is a small museum as well. Public Toilets are behind the museum.

name: Vav of Modhera
description: 11th century stepwell with moderate carvings. Unusual mandapa shrine in the middle pavilion tower. Usually premises is locked.

name: Dharmeshwari Stepwell
description: Belongs to 16-17th century, it has a shrine at the first pavilion of the stepwell instead of usual at the end.

name: Modheshwari Mata Temple
description: Modheshwari is a clan deity of several families belonging to the village. A very large and beautiful temple.

name: Narmada Canal Syphon on Pushapavati river
description: See how canal crosses a river by going under it! Understand the engineering and mechanics of the system.

name: Hawa Mahal
description: A lakeside pavilion on high plinth probably made from parts of earlier structure belonging to Solanki period. It is erected in six pilaster and 12 columns of sandstone with some decorations on pillar capitals and on plinths. A jali windows are there in rear wall.

name: Khokhla Wetland
description: A large embankment forms this wetland where migratory and local birds flock in winter. A good seasonal birdwatching spot.

name: The Modhera Dance Festival
description: The three-day Modhera Dance Festival is held every year during the third weekend of January after the conclusion of Uttarayan festival. The dance festival is frequently visited by art and dance connoisseurs from around the world. Classical and folk dancers and musicians from different states of India exhibit their talent and flair while culture enthusiasts become part of the festival to witness this splendid event.

name: Toran Restaurant
description: Serves snacks, drinks and dishes. Operated by the government contractor.

name: Eulogia Restro Cafe
description: Beverages, fast foods, snacks and meals.

name: Modheshwari Mata Temple canteen
description: Serves tea, coffee and drinks along with light snacks.

name: Sub Post Office
description: Special cancellation mark of Sun temple.

name: T Point: Ticket Counter
description: ID Proofs are compulsory.

name: Zero Point:
description: a border location along the India-Pakistan border. From Zero Point, one can observe the land of Pakistan from fencing

name: Tourist Help Desk
description: You can get tourist map, other programme schedules and answers to your questions.

name: Parking
description: There ample space for parking cars, private vehicles and buses.

name: Ajay Prahari
description: A key feature of Nadabet, showcasing the history and role of the BSF. The 'Ajay Prahari' monument honours soldiers who sacrificed their lives for the nation.

name: BSF Stambh
description: A 30-feet high T-Junction Pillar adorned with murals.

name: Sarhad Gatha
description: The museum space has six galleries, offering insights into the geographic and demographic aspects of Nadabet and the challenges of border terrain.

name: AV Experience Zone
description: high-tech interactive installations, including virtual patrolling and simulators, providing an immersive experience of border life.

name: Bharat Ke Veer
description: Documentary on soldiers.

name: Adventure Park
description: Activities like zip-lining, shooting, and paintball are available for visitors, along with displays of military equipment like missiles, tanks, and aircraft.

name: Evening Parade at Parade Arena
description: The retreat ceremony, similar to the Wagah Border ceremony, is a major draw, featuring the ceremonial lowering of the flag by BSF soldiers.

name: Auditorium
description: Attend the events and performances organised on major festive days. Check their calendar.

name: Toran Lounges
description: For government officers and dignitaries.

name: Mithi Vav
description: 18th-century stepwell which is four-storey deep. Now neglected but still an attraction, it was probably built from material from previous monuments. It has fine carvings of Ganesha, Bhairava, Apsaras etc.

name: Pataleshwar Mahadev Temple
description: According to local legend, the Chaulukya king Siddhraj Jaisimha was born in Palanpur so his mother Mayanalla Devi had ordered to build a stepwell. During the construction a Shivalinga was found so a temple was built instead of the stepwell. It is believed that it was a habitat of the serpents.

name: Joravar Palace
description: Old palace of Nawab. There are beautiful paintings in the courtroom and the stair has fine sandalwood decoration. Photography with permission.

name: George V Club
description: A private sports club now. Nawab Sher Mohammed Khan built it to commemorate coronation of British King George V in 1913.

name: Pallavia Parshwanath Jain Temple
description: Beautifully carved marble Jain temple.

name: Jahanara Baug
description: Beautiful large garden built by Nawab Taley Muhammed Khan dedicated to his Australian wife Begum Jahanara aka Joan Falkiner.

name: Old City
description: Explore the traditional haveli mansions with carved wooden facades and brackets in gated communities called pols in Moti Bazar, Nani Bazar, Jhaveriwad, Teen Batti, Paththar Sadak and Khoda Limda areas.

name: Diamond Market
description: There are around 50 diamond wholesalers along this road. Any shop will show you how they cut and polish diamonds in their workshop. Palanpuri Jains are well known for their hold on diamond business around the world. You may find them in Belgium too!

name: Palanpur Museum
description: Explore the artifacts and history of Palanpur. 2 hr.

name: Shahi Roza
description: Several stone-carved royal cenotaphs. Poorly maintained.

name: Kirtistambh
description: The four-storied memorial pillar was built in 1936 for Nawab Sher Muhammed Khan by Nawab Taley Mohammed Khan. The marble plaques on the surface are inscribed with the history of Nawabs and information about Palanpur. It is located on the traffic island.

name: Mira Gate
description: In 1750, Nawab Bahadur Khan built a brick and mortar city-walls of Palanpur. It was 3 miles round, 17 to 20 feet high and 6 feet broad with seven bastioned gateways, and, at the corners, round towers armed with guns. The gateways of the city-walls were Delhi Darwaja, Gathaman Darwaja, Malan Darwaja, Mira Darwaja, Virbai Darwaja, Salempura Darwaja, Sadarpur Darwaja or Shimla Darwaja. Only Mira Darwaja survives today.

name: Gayatri Mandir
description: A large new Hindu temple.

name: Mansarovar Lake
description: Early Jhalori ruler Malik Mujahid Khan built this lake dedicated to his queen Manbai Jadeja in 1628.

name: Check Photo collection of A. L. Syed (1904-1991)
description: He was an official photographer of Nawabs of Palanpur. Contact his son Azmat Syed.

name: Sur Mandir Carnival Cinemas
description: Watch Gujarati or Bollywood films. Snacks and beverages are available too.

name: Street Food at Guru Nanak Chowk
description: The street food vendors serve variety of food in the evening to late night here.

name: Janta Kachori House
description: Oldest and best known shop for eating Kachori.

name: Jayanti Fafda House
description: For lip-smacking fafda-jalebi.

name: Hotel Guptaji
description: Affordable and tasty Punjabi meals.

name: Hotel Welcome Guest House
address: Bus Station Road, Nr. Railway Station
description: Free Wi-Fi.

name: Circuit House
description: For government employees.

name: Rani ki Vav
price: ₹40 for Indians, ₹600 for foreigners, Free below age 13, Parking: ₹10 for 2-wheelers, ₹20 for 4-wheelers
description: A stepwell, inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List, that was built in the 11th century.

name: Sahastralinga Tank
description: The reservoir was built in 1084 by Solanki ruler Siddharaj Jaysinh on the erstwhile bank of the Sarasvati River. The lake had 1,008 Shiva shrines on its embankment. Spread over 17 acres, it has ruins of an 84-pillared Shiva temple and three-ringed sluice gates. Only 20% of the lake is excavated. It had a natural filtration system.

name: Kalika Mata temple
description: This temple of Kali, built by Siddharaj Jaysinh, is over 1,000 years old. Kali is a clan deity of the Solankis. She guards the town.

name: Patan Patola Heritage
description: To learn about Patola sari and its heritage. Operated by Salvi weaver family.

name: Patan Museum
price: ₹5 for Indians, ₹1 for school/college students, ₹50 for foreigners, ₹100 photography, ₹500 for videography
hours: 10AM-5PM, Wed and 2nd and 4th Sat closed, Government Holidays closed
description: Established in 2010, the museum has large number of marble and sandstone sculptures dating back to the ancient and medieval times.

name: Fort and Gates
description: The town is surrounded by fort walls and gates still largely intact. The old town situated in the fort has bustling bazaar. The havelis with wooden carved facades and brackets are located here. In the narrow pol streets, people are found making rope or bidi (traditional cigarette). Bagwada, Chhidiya, Mira, Aghara, Kothakooe, Phatipaal (Fatipal), Ghoonghdi, Kanasda (also known as Kalika), Khansarovar, Motishah, Bhathi, Lal are twelve medieval gates of the town. These gates are State Protected Monuments. Ganesh Bari is a small gate in the town. Some Patola and mashru weavers live here. Many old Jain temples are located here.

name: Panchasara Parshwanath Jain temple
description: The town has more than 100 Jain temples. Panchasara temple is chief among them. It is one of the largest and most profusely carved temple.

name: Hemachandracharya Jain Gnan Mandir library
description: Holds ancient Hindu and Jain texts including palm-leaf manuscripts. It has small museum displaying old artifacts, coins, palm-leaf manuscripts and tools used for writing it.

name: Tankwada
description: Mashru is a fabric woven from silk and cotton. Visit to find Mashru weavers.

name: Trikam Barot ni Vav
description: Another small stepwell

name: Anand Sarovar
description: Public park

name: Khan Sarovar
description: Historical square shaped lake. Sluice gates are state protected monument. Now a public park.

name: Shaikh Farid Tomb
description: Sheikh Farid's mosque and mausoleum is an early Islamic construction of Gujarat, built even earlier than monuments in Ahmedabad. It has a beautifully carved ceiling. It is falsely identified as Behram Khan's Maqbara.

name: Ruins and Megh Maya Temple
description: Located on a hillock, there is a temple of legendary Megh Maya associated with folklore of Sahastralinga Tank. There are some old ruins behind the temple.

name: Regional Science Museum
price: ₹20 (₹50 on weekend and holidays), ₹50 for 5D theatre (₹100 on weekend and holidays), Monday closed, Parking: ₹10 for 2-wheelers, ₹20 for 4-wheelers

name: Patola Sari
description: A double ikat woven sari. A small scarf cost about ₹5000.

name: Hotel Garden
description: Serves good Gujarati Thali and Punjabi dishes.

name: Gangotri Hotel
description: Only basic accommodation facilities.

name: Hotel Surya Palace
price: ₹250-700 for single, ₹350-1000 for double, ₹500-800 for triple bed, ₹75 for extra bed
description: Located outside the town

name: Rudra Mahalaya temple
description: Ruined temple was dedicated to Rudra, a form of the Hindu deity Shiva. It was built by the Chaulukya (Solanki) rulers of Gujarat and took nearly 175 years and three generation of rulers from Mulraj to Siddhraj Jaysimha to complete. It is estimated that it had a three-storey shikhara, 12 entrances and 1,600 pillars. It was surrounded by more shrines and had ornamental gateways (torana). Later it was destroyed in the 12th and 15th centuries by Ulugh Khan and Ahmad Shah and a part of it was converted in a mosque. Now a row of surrounding shrines, two porticos and torana is all that surviving. The idols of deities and parts of the temple are scattered around. As it is now a contested site, it is closed to public, but a security guard may allow you to have a look.

name: Shristhal Sangrahalay
description: Opened in 2017, it has three galleries presenting religious and ritual significance as well as history and society of the region.

name: Bohra havelis
description: Mansions in European influenced architecture are largely belonging to Dawoodi Bohra trading community and spread over 18 mohallas or neighbourhoods in Najampura and Hassanpura. They are known for their wooden architecture and interior decorations. They are painted in pastel colours. Nearly 500 of these mansions are empty as their owners have migrated.

name: Bindu Sarovar
description: A small artificial tank considered pious by Hindus. According to Hindu theology, there are five sacred lakes; collectively called Panch-Sarovar; Mansarovar, Bindu Sarovar, Narayan Sarovar, Pampa Sarovar and Pushkar Sarovar. It is the only place where Matrushraddh, Shraddh ritual for mothers, is performed thus thousands of people visit it annually to perform the rituals for their dead mothers, in Kartika month of Hindu calendar.

name: Arvadeshwar Shiva temple
description: An ancient place associated with Natha Sampradaya.

name: Siddheshwar Mahadev temple and Moksha Peepal tree
description: The Saraswati river is nearby and the riverfront has been developed for rituals.

name: Lalumal Lassiwala
description: Drink Lassi, a cool refreshing milk based drink.

name: Ajitanatha Jain temple
description: The large 12th-century Jain temple built by Chaulukya ruler Kumarapala in late Maru-Gurjara architecture style.

name: 14 Digambara temples in the foothills
description: The oldest temple in foothill compound dedicated to Sambhavanatha was built in Maru-Gurjara architecture in 11th century.

name: Taran-Dharan Mata shrines
description: The shrines of Taran Mata and Dharan Mata is situated near a natural stream. The idol of Taran Mata is dated to 8th-9th century based on its style.

name: Buddhist Stupa remains.
description: Brick structures and other archaeological remains were found near the seasonal stream.

name: Jogida ni Gufa
description: Buddhist sculptures and rock shelters atop the hill. Need some trekking to reach there.

name: Tirthankar Van
description: Good for family picnic.

name: Nilkanth Vav Jal Mandir
description: A small square stepwell built in 1830.

name: Rock climbing at Frog Rock
description: Rock climbing should be performed only with help of suitable equipment and team as this is very isolated place.

name: Fortification remains
description: Located in southwest of hill, this fortification remains are probably from 3rd or 4th century BCE. There are probable place of historical Anarta/Anandpura. One has to trek difficult forest to reach there. Help from experienced local trekker is a must.

name: Ajitnath Jain Dharmashala
description: For Jain pilgrims only.

name: Digambar Jain Dharmashala
description: For Jain pilgrims only.

name: Tapovan Jain Dharmashala
description: For Jain pilgrims only.

name: Kirti Torana
description: Two ornamental gateways, east one is better preserved. Built in Maru-Gurjara style (Solanki) architecture, these gateways are 40 feet tall. Built of red-yellow sandstone, they have battle and hunting scenes. They are probably part of a larger temple complex which no longer exists. They might have been erected to commemorate a battle victory.

name: Hatkeshwar Mahadev temple
description: A 15th-century temple of Shiva revered by Nagar Brahmin community. The exterior of the temple is adorned with scenes from Hindu epics Ramayana and Mahabharata as well as dancing Apsaras and musicians.

name: Tana Riri shrines
description: The memorial shrines of Tana and Riri, legendary musician sisters of the Mughal era. A classical music festival is organised here very year.

name: Ambaji Temple behind GMERS Hospital
description: Few ancient temple parts and idols can be seen here.

name: Hathiwalu Derasar
description: A Jain temple.

name: Chauta Adinath Derasar
description: A Jain temple. Jains consider Vadnagar the ancient foothill of Shatrunjaya hill in Palitana. The temple has a memorial foothill.

name: Jhanjhanio Kuvo
description: Ancient circular well connected with local folklore. Must have been larger water structure of the past. The diameter is 3.3 m and constructed from stone. In the inner walls of the well, there are panels with carving of swans, flowers and honeycomb. The exterior wall has a niche with Ganesha.

name: Sharmistha lake
description: A lake with public amenities and ghats. The lake forms the northern boundary of the fort town and shapes northern fort wall in curve while the rest of the fort is rectangular. Kapila river originating from Banganga feeds the water to the lake via canal.

name: Lakeview
description: Scenic lakeview and walkways developed for public.

name: Pancham Mehta ni Vav
description: Ancient seven-storey deep stepwell with 11 kutas built in 16th century. 67 m-long and 5.5-m wide.

name: Gauri Kund
description: Ancient square stepped tank built in stone. The walls are decorated with 54 sculptures. The steps have inscriptions derived from Hindu religious works. It is visited by locals in post-death rituals.

name: Lateri Vav
description: Old stepwell developed as a tourist spot.

name: Saptarshi no Aro
description: Remnants of the ancient lake.

name: Buddhist monastery ruins
description: Dating from 2nd to 7th century.

name: Archaeological Experiential Museum
alt: Anant Anadi Vadnagar Puratatva Anubhav Sangrahalay
description: covers 2500 years history of continuous human habitation of the town as well as its cultural history. It displays more than 5000 artefacts and nearby excavated archeological site is open to the visitors.

name: Rajgadhi Timbo
description: An ancient Jain temple excavated from a mound.

name: Hotel Toran
description: State government run hotel.

name: Vasant Prabha Hospital
description: All basic medical facilities are available.

name: GMERS Medical College and Hospital
description: Emergency, OPD and IPD medical facilities.

name: Khalikpur Hillock
description: A small hillock reachable by vehicle near town to enjoy the scenic views of the town

name: Odhari Lake
description: A sprawling park surrounding a serene lake. It has a children's play area.

name: Mazum Reservoir Viewpoint
description: A large reservoir is best viewed at the dawn.

name: Devraj Dham
description: A temple dedicated to Devanand Pandit located on a small hillock with scenic views of the town.

name: Aquaworld Water Park
description: Enjoy the rides in summer to cool yourself.

name: Amul Dairy
description: Asia's largest dairy.

name: Watch a film
description: There are many cinemas in the city.

name: Amul
description: Dairy products

name: Jumma Masjid
description: A 15th-century mosque with adorned walls and pillars

name: Khan Masjid
description: Built in 1453 on an immense scale near a large lake, this rare brick-and-limestone mosque features massive domes, grand arches, and ornate carved jalis (stone screens). Alif Khan was a general of Gujarat Sultanate under Sultan Mahmud Begada. There is a tomb of Alif Khan nearby.

name: Tanka Masjid
description: A 14th-century stone mosque which is an example of early Indo-Islamic architecture. It features stone as well as wooden colonnades. Permission required to enter.

name: Hazrat Khan’s Roza
description: Locally significant tomb complex.

name: Khan Talav
description: A large octagonal lake next to the Alif Khan Mosque. Picturesque views. Check its sluice gates which bring in the waters.

name: Malav Talao
description: Constructed in the late 11th century by Queen Minaldevi (mother of Jayasimha Siddharaja), this historic stepped tank remains a central landmark. The central platform can be reached by a bridge.

name: Swaminarayan Temple
description: Established in 1827 by Lord Swaminarayan, this grand temple complex of Murali Manohar Dev serves as a key spiritual hub for the regional Swaminarayan tradition.

name: Chandreshwar Mahadev Temple
description: It was built in 1751 by Antaji Rao, an officer of the Gaikwad’s of Baroda State. The temple houses a crystal type lingam. The lamp tower in front of the temple is unique. A small stepwell nearby.

name: Atal Sarovar
description: A lake with walkways and public park.

name: Kalikund Parshwanath Jain Temple
description: A large Jain temple complex

name: Jindatt Suri Dadawadi
description: A Jain temple complex dedicated to Jain monks.

name: Shetrunjay Temple (Mini-Palitana)
description: A miniature replica of Palitana hill temples

name: Shantivan Indrashil Tirth
description: A sprawling Hindu temple complex with large landscaped gardens and beautiful architecture

name: Hilal Khan Ghazi Mosque
description: Built by Hilal Khan Gazi, a general during the Tughlaq dynasty, in 1332-33. A great example of a medieval mosque.

name: Vautha Fair
description: A large annual fair. Held around November, for five days ending on the full moon day of Kartik month in Hindu calendar. Located on the confluence of seven sacred rivers (primarily Sabarmati and Vatrak) where pilgrims take holy dip. The largest livestock trading fair where thousands of donkeys and camels, brightly coloured and decorated, are traded by nomad tribes. Tents are erected across three miles of area offering foods, handicrafts, toys, entertainments and household items.

name: Mini Kachori and Samosa Centre
address: Shop No. 8, Shetrunjay Complex, Kalikund Road
description: A 35-year-old shop. Unique golgappa-sized Kachoris. For Samosas, go early between 10AM-2PM as they are sold fast!

name: Dahi Handi
description: A multicuisine restaurant with Punjabi and Kathiawadi Gujarati meals.

name: Mehta Lassi Centre
description: Since 1965, this shop has been selling lassi (a yogurt-based drink) in various flavours such as rose, saffron, as cardamom.

name: Jain Dharmashala
description: for Jain pilgrims

name: Jindatt Suri Dadawadi Dharmashala
description: for Jain pilgrims

name: Hotel Urban Nest
address: FF, Dev Ganesh Complex, Dholka-Bagodara Road
description: Deluxe, Premium and Family Rooms. Breakfast provided. Special Jacuzzi Rooms are there too.

name: 360 Degree Ville
description: A large resort with villas for stay, adventure games, swimming pool. All meals are included as per request.

name: Gulf of Khambhat viewpoint
description: Visit this only after checking the tidal information for the seashore, as the gulf has pretty much silted up.

name: Jami Mosque
description: The 14th-century mosque is built with peculiar archaeological designs and structures borrowed from the Jain temples built at that time. It is one of the earliest mosques built in Gujarat. There is a tomb of Umar bin Ahmad al-Kazaruni within the complex.

name: Stambheshwar Mahadev Temple,
description: which submerges on a high tide day.

name: Neja Palm Avenue
description: for a picturesque view of palm trees adorning the road.

name: Ghushmeshwar Mahadev Temple
description: comprises shrines of all deities and a Nataraj artifact made out of stone.

name: Madala Lake and Stepwell
description: A historical stepwell is located on an island in the lake. The lake is surrounded by a walkway and has children's play area.

name: Khambhat Fort
description: an old palatial house built from wood and having beautiful colored glass panelled windows. Not open to public but can be seen from closed gate.

name: Lunej #1 Oil Rig and ONGC Museum
description: A small museum on the site of India's first oil rig from which history of petroleum started.

name: Teen Darwaja
description: the historic gate built in 1891 by the Nawab of erstwhile Cambay State

name: Ratilal Chunilal Halwasanwala
description: a sweet shop since 1905, best known for its Halwasan and Sutarfeni.

name: Fort of Pavagadh and the ruined Hindu and Jain Temples on the top of the Pavagadh Hill
Pavagadh ropeway
description: Go on the Pavagadh hill by ropeway to visit Kalika Mata Temple.

name: Lothal Archaeological Site
description: The site is well-planned and divided into distinct zones: the Acropolis (Upper Town), Raised on a high platform to protect against floods, housing civic rulers with paved baths and underground drains; the Lower Town, divided into commercial and residential quarters, featuring bead-making workshops, coppersmith shops, and standard brick residences; the Dockyard, a massive rectangular basin lined with baked bricks, engineered with inlet channels and sluice gates to manage tidal flows; the Warehouse, a large structure situated near the acropolis used for inspect and store cargo.

name: Lothal Museum
description: Located adjacent to the ruins, this ASI-maintained museum houses around 800 artifacts recovered from the site. Key exhibits include Indus seals with animal motifs and Harappan script, micro-beads, copper tools, and terracotta figurines, painted pottery depicting scenes, a scale model reconstruction of the ancient port city.

name: National Maritime Heritage Complex
description: An ambitious world-class heritage complex being developed adjacent to the site to highlight India's maritime history. Phase I is under construction.

name: Shivghat Waterfall
description: A small waterfall that comes to life during the monsoon season.

name: Shrimad Rajchandra Ashram
description: A religious adobe spread over an area of 223 acres. Founded by followers of Shrimad Rajchandra, a Jain philosopher and poet.

name: Echo Point
description: Away from the town but gives superb view of the Saputara valley.

name: Saputara Lake
description: A main attraction in Saputara can be viewed from the Ropeway which offers a 10 minute ride to Sunrise Point.

name: Saputara Museum
description: A small museum that has collections of tribal artifacts of the Dang area. It also gives information on topography and anthropology of the Dangs. The displays include stuffed birds, tribal ornaments, jewelry and musical instruments but don't be disappointed by presentation. Established in 1970.

name: Sunrise Point
description: It is a point which offers the best view of Saputara and adjoining Malegoan could be reached after a walk of 1.5 km in the direction of Waghai. The naming restricts the tourist traffic to this best place as tourists believe that the point should only be visited at sun rise, however, one may visit it at any time of the day to catch a panoramic view. The Tata Consultancy Services has suggested renaming this point as Valley View Point to enhance tourist traffic.

name: Nageshwar Mahadev
address: on southern bank of the lake.
description: A holy temple dedicated to Lord Shiva worshiped by locals.

name: Lake Garden
description: This is an area along the Saputara Lake with various gardens and is a popular picnic site. It also has children's play area.

name: Saputara Adventure Park
description: A recreational park offering many different activities such as paragliding, zorbing, rock climbing, horseback riding and jungle safari.

name: By the Lake
description: The lake surrounded by greenery makes it pleasurable to sail in the lake. Hire boats from the boat-house. For half an hour, a pedal boat is charged at ₹20/person while a rowboat ₹5/person. Maharashtra state border is just 1.5 km away on walk where you can drink beer legally.

name: Saputara Ropeway
description: This cableway is suspended above the lake which connects Vaity Hotel to Sunset Point situated across the valley. Jeeps takes tourists to the boarding point located 2km from main roundabout only between 5:30-6:00 PM. It takes 15 minutes to cross which gives you fantastic view of Saputara town and valley below. Warning: The cable car only operates when there are at least 12 passengers which could take entire day's wait in off seasons.

name: Artist Village
address: On main road to Nashik from Saputara
description: The place display handicraft of local tribals. You can buy pieces of jewelry, vases, pottery, paintings, key chains and pen stands made of bamboo and local materials. The artist may answer your questions and even teach some craft to your children if they are interested.

name: Honey Bee Centre
description: If you ever wonder how bees make honey, visit here. You will learn as well as you can buy pure honey which is bit expensive.

name: Government Purna Dormitory
description: Very basic lodge. It does not provides sheets or towels.

name: Toran Hill Resort
description: Government Tourism Corporation hotel.

name: Gokul
description: best budget hotel on road up from bus stand. Facilities include shower, western toilet, TV (₹50 extra). Room can house up to five people.

name: Lake View
description: It is situated in attractive building and has palm-tree garden. It provides squat toilets, hot water bath and cable TV.

name: Gujarat Tourism Office
description: Will give good orientation of the district and town.

name: Gira Falls
description: 52 km from Saputara.

name: Hatgadh Fort
description: An ancient historical fort.

name: Vansda National Park
description: Originally, a private forest of maharaja of Vansada, the park now covers on area of 24 sq km. Despite its small size the park harbours tiger, leopard, pangolin, rusty-spotted cat, python, giant squirrel, fourhorned antelope etc. Prior permission from the Chief Wildlife Warden, of Gandhinagar or DFO, Ahwa is required before visiting the park.

name: Mahal
description: The Mahal region situated 60 km away from Saputara is dominated by the Purna Sanctuary. The longish drive passes through the most beautiful parts of Dangs with high wooded slopes of bamboo.

name: Parnera Hill
description: It is a hill with a small old fort and a temple. Mainly considered as northern most hill of western ghat.

name: Raja Rani Wada Pav
description: Very famous for the Wada Pav.

name: Daman Ganga Dam
description: A dam on the Daman Ganga River, the lifeline of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

name: Fortune Park Galaxy
description: Only branded chain hotel serving the tourists of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Part of ITC group of hotels. Also on premises is Restaurant Orchid, which serves elaborate buffet breakfast, lunch & dinner & multi-cuisine menu with numerous dishes to choose from.

name: Dwarkadhish Temple
description: The over 2000-year-old, 5-storied Hindu temple is the main sight of the holy town. The temple is dedicated to the god Krishna, who is also believed to have been King of Dwarka for 100 years.

name: Bet Dwarka
description: This is supposed to be the place where Krishna lived, met his friend Sudama and blessed him, and there is a Peetha (Seat) where Krishna is said to have met Sudama. The temple also has the main Dwarkadish deity which was believed to have been made by Krishna's chief Queen Rukmini and in which Meera bai is said to have merged and disappeared from the material world. There are boats available from Okha Jetty from where people are ferried to the island which is approximately 30 km from Dwarka.

name: Rukmini Mandir
description: This temple is 8 km from Dwarka. This is in the outskirts of the city and this is a lonely temple and there is an interesting story of Rukmini being cursed by sage Durvasa because of which the temple is outside the city and its because of this curse only that the water in Dwarka city is salty.

name: Shivrajpur Beach
description: Shivrajpur Beach is another notable beach located near Dwarka. It has been awarded the prestigious Blue Flag beach certification for its cleanliness and eco-friendly initiatives. The beach is known for its crystal-clear waters and pristine surroundings, making it a popular destination for both locals and tourists.

name: Amrutras
description: Known for its vegetarian Gujarati thalis. While they serve non-Gujarati food too, it is not particularly tasty.

name: Dwarkadhish Lords Eco Inn
description: The only hotel in Dwarka facing the sea.

name: Mani Mandir
description: The former residence of the queen and later converted into the Willingdon Secretariat in 1936. After independence of India, it served as the local government office. It is a fine example of Indo-Saracenic architecture which fuses Rajput, European Gothic and Islamic architectural elements. It has fine carvings on walls, ceilings, exteriors, windows and doors. The courtyards are open for public but to visit inside requires permission.

name: Nehru Gate
description: The city gate was inaugurated in 1925 by Sir George Lloyd, the then Governor of Bombay. It was then known as Lloyd Gate. Subsequently post independence, it was renamed as Nehru Gate. The structure has also Indo-Saracenic architecture. The gate was partly destroyed in the earthquake of 2001 and later restored in 2007 by the municipality.

name: Nazarbagh Palace
description: The new two-storey palace has beautiful Art Deco architecture and Art Nouveau interiors.

name: Green Chowk
description: The town square and the main market of Morbi. You may see several shops of watchmakers who are at work here. It is approached by series of three gates.

name: Green Tower
description: Green Tower is built in European architecture and is topped with a three-floored cast iron frame structure with a dome.

name: Pada Pul
description: The old bridge known as Pada Pul because the large bulls are erected on the entry to the bridge. It is a 700-m long masonry arch bridge. The arches are built with white stones while the piers and closed spandrel walls are built with dark stones. It has wrought iron rails. The bridge was damaged during the 1979 dam failure. A new bridge is built parallel to it.

name: Machchhu Mata Temple
description: A temple on river bank dedicated river deity.

name: Rafaleshwar Mahadev Temple
description: A large Hindu temple topped with Rajput architecture elements in its design.

name: Darbargadh Palace
description: The old palace of erstwhile royals of the Morbi State.

name: Mahaprabhuji Bethak
description: An religious place of Hindu Vaishnava Pushtimarg tradition.

name: Post Office
description: An Art Deco building is worth a look too.

name: Palitana Jain temples on Mount Shatrunjaya hill
price: Photography ₹40. Seek permission to photograph inside temples
description: Palitana has over 850 temples atop sacred Mount Satrunjaya (the “hill that conquers enemies”), which makes it most of any temple city. Many of these temples date to 15-16th centuries while some of them date to even earlier periods. The top is reached by climbing (or by being carried up) 3,572 steps—a stiff 2-hour ascent. Amid the massive warren of white marble shrines and temples, you’ll encounter many devotees dressed in white, some wearing gauze masks to filter innocent microbes from the air that they breathe. Some of the devotees attain ecstatic heights, practicing their faith with devotional singing, clapping, and humming. Others create devotional patterns on the ground using rice and nuts, or are seen gently waving fly-whisks over the idols as a gesture of respect.

name: Shri Vishal Jain Museum
address: Opposite Kesariyaji Jain Dharmshala, Taleti Road, Taleti
description: Exhibits ancient manuscripts, idols, history of Jainism, life of Jain Tirthankara Mahavira, models of incidents and legends from Jain universal history. Some information is in English.

name: Jain Cosmic View Show at Jambudweep Temple
description: The temple has a large model of Jain cosmic world. Large number of explanatory notes in Gujarati is there with art explaining Jain view of the world. A show is held in evening explaining views like the earth is no round and the Apollo mission to Moon was hoax.

name: Vijay Vilas Palace
description: It was a country retreat of the ruler of erstwhile Palitana state. Now it is a heritage hotel with view of the hills. Has six rooms.

name: Somnath Jyotirlinga Temple
description: It is one of the 12 Jyotirlinga temples dedicated to Lord Shiva. Three aartis (ritual) performed daily; at 7AM, at noon and at 7PM.

name: Fern Residency
description: Clean, good service, great restaurant, travel desk offers tours with car and driver, nice view from elevator bank of endless sea of palm trees, walk to Somnath Temple in about 25 min., Somnath rail station in about 10 min.

name: Somnath Bus Stand (ST Depot)
address: Somnath Mandir Road, Prabhas Patan, Somnath
description: State-run GSRTC (ST) buses connecting Somnath to Veraval, Junagadh, Rajkot, and other towns in Saurashtra.

name: Veraval ST Bus Depot
description: Larger depot than Somnath's; more frequent long-distance and intercity services.

name: Somnath Terminus (SMNH)
description: Currently under construction/closed (temporarily closed since September 2022) — do not direct pilgrims here until reopened. Rail enquiries nationally: 139.

name: Veraval Junction (VRL)
description: Main functioning railway station serving Somnath/Veraval, with 5 platforms and around 14 originating/terminating trains. Also accessible via Diu Airport, ~73 km away. National rail enquiry helpline: 139.

name: Somnath Travels
address: Somnath Mandir Rd, beside Hotel Somnath Atithigruh, Somnath

name: Somnath Yatra
address: Shop No 105, Maa Complex, Somnath Bhidia Road, opp. Dev In Hotel, GIDC Area, Prabhas Patan, Somnath
description: WhatsApp available at +91 92283 17067.

name: Korigad
alt: also called Koraigad, Koarigad or Kumwarigad)
description: A fort that is about 20 km away from Lonavla in Pune district, Maharashtra, India. Its date of construction is not known but likely predates 1500. It is about 929 m above sea level. The closest village is Peth Shahpur.This fort was incorporated into his kingdom by Shivaji along with the forts of Lohagad, Visapur, Tung and Tikona in 1657. On March 11, 1818, Col. Prother tried to take over this fort but even after a prolonged siege could not make any headway. Finally on 14 March, by igniting the stored ammunition by means of a loose cannon ball he succeeded and this fort went to the British.Now because of the Mulshi dam, a lake has formed close to the base of the hill on which Korigad stands. There are two lakes on the top of the fort. A temple to its patron goddess Koraidevi also exists along with several smaller temples to dedicated to Vishnu and Shiva. The former has been renovated and has a 3-foot-high Deepmala(tower of lamps).The interesting part of the fort is that its wall is completely intact and one can walk along its entire perimeter (about 2 km). Its massive gate is also intact. Several ruins of older structures within the fort still exist. It has six cannons - the largest of which called the Laxmi Toph. It is near the Korai devi temple.

name: Shivneri Fort
description: The birthplace of Shivaji (1630–1680).

name: Lavasa Lake
description: An inlet of the Mutha River, and the central waterbody of the city.

name: Mayureshwar Temple
description: Dassera, the festival in which a Palakhi of lord Ganesha travels through the boundaries of the entire Morgaon village, is a great tourist attraction. In every house of this village people prepare "Bhuinale" and "Hingan" which are some sort of firecrackers originally meant for Dassera event & not for sale.

name: Mayureshwar Wildlife Sanctuary
description: It is not only popular for its birds and wildlife population, but also for its natural environment. One can see the Indian gazelle (chinkara), as well as birds, striped hyena, grey wolf (Canis lupus) and fox (Vulpes bengalesis). Tourists are allowed to drive their vehicles inside the sanctuary as well as to walk.

name: Camp Temgarh
description: An off beat resort

name: Lake Side Verandah
description: A bungalow that has been converted to a resort.

name: Ekayana Resort
description: Resort with a swimming pool and lounge, cottages and villas.

name: Avanti Kalagram
description: It offers container rooms, along with adventure activities. It also has a private waterfall during the monsoon season.

name: Purandar Fort
description: It is one of the most country's important forts of 13th century, and its historically important as the site of a fierce battle that ensued after Mirzaraje Jaisingh and Diler Khan (Generals of Aurangzeb, Mughal Emperor) besieged the fort, Murar Baji Prabhu lost his life while defending the fort. Just after this incident, Shivaji Maharaj signed a treaty with the Mughals and released 23 forts to them. The fort perched on top of a mountain mass at height of 1398 metres from sea level. From the lower base, the fort stands towering at height of 700 metres. The Fort has two main parts: Purandar - the main fort and Vajragad - the auxiliary fort to the east of Purandar, also known by the name Rudramal in ancient times. Pundar fort has a terrace called Machi where there are a few residential-like structures apart from the temple of Purandareshwar from which the fort gets its name. The winding road takes one to the hillock perched on top of Machi. This part is called Balekilla.

name: Panshet Dam
description: It was opened in 1959 by Jawaharlal Nehru, then Prime Minister of India. It was built after the catastrophic flood of 1943

name: Panshet Water Park
description: At a nearby dam, the tourism department has setup a water sports park.

name: Varasgaon Dam
description: It is a popular picnic spot and location for water sports. It supplies water to city of Pune.

name: Samadhi of Sambhaji
description: The shrine dedicated to Sambhaji, the second Maratha emperor. He was tortured and executed in Tulapur after he was captured by Mughal forces. Both Sambhaji and his aide Kavi Kalash were cremated here.

name: Samadhi of Sambhaji
description: The shrine dedicated to Sambhaji, the second Maratha emperor. He was tortured and executed in Tulapur after he was captured by Mughal forces. There's a shrine for his aide Kavi Kalash here nearby as well.

name: Malanggad
description: A moderate trek is required to reach this notable shrine and fort built on a hill.

name: Gajanan Maharaj Temple
description: Kanhor is among the well-known religious places located in a serene & scenic place. The temple is situated just outside of Badlapur village on a small hillock surrounded by fields and greenery all around. The enchanting natural beauty around the temple is another attraction for the devotees who visit the temple.

name: Khandoba Temple
description: The temple of Lord Khandoba is located in Moolgaon, a small village, around 4 Miles (6 km) from Badlapur Railway station. From the temple, you can see the panoramic view of Badlapur, Kulgaon and Vangani. The best time to visit this place is around September to November.

name: Kondeshwar
description: Kondeshwar has a beautiful waterfall along with a pond. There is a temple of Lord Shiva and hence the name Kondeshwar. Kondeshwar is remotely located away from the noise and urban pollution, with the nearest village located about 20/25 minutes by walk. Though Kondeshwar is a very beautiful place to be during a monsoon period, there have been many accidents and fatalities due to unsafe swimming practices by people who have very less knowledge of the crevices under the water. Many people have died due to the turbulence of the waterfall and they were taken inside the crevices from where it is very difficult to come out due to the heavy force of water.

name: Kondeshwar Shiv Temple
description: This is a very old temple.

name: Kondeshwar Shiv Mandir
description: Very old temple in a beautiful place.

name: Bhoj Resort
price: For stay including Swimming, Breakfast, Lunch, Tea, Dinner, Tea: ₹400-₹500 per person per day
description: Facilities include Sauna, Steam bath, Rain Dance, Swimming Pool and camping environment tent facility

name: Farmer's Den
description: A riverside resort for the day and overnight picnics, multi-cuisine, ample space and greenery, cable TV, and Barbecue nights.

name: Durgadi Fort
address: Kalyan-Ahmednagar Hwy, Annabhau Sathe Nagar, Tilak Nagar
