description: Swimming pool, free parking, power back-up.

name: Digha State General Hospital
description: The only hospital in coastal Purba Medinipur.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: A , built in the 13th century in the honour of the sun-god Surya, is in ruins. The entire temple was designed in the shape of a colossal chariot with 24 wheels about 3 m high and pulled by seven horses, carrying the sun god, Surya, across the heavens. Surya has been a popular deity in India since the Vedic period.

name: Chandrabhaga Beach
description: Chandrabhaga is rich in its marine resources. A light house, close by Chandrabhaga is an added histrionic to the splendour of the place. A climb to its top truly takes you to a world of utopia. A natural deer park is recent additions to the riches of Chandrabhaga. There is an ancient Matha believed to be the Ashram of Chandrabhaga's father and two small temples. The sight has aesthetic and importance.

name: Kuruma
description: A popular Buddhist site. The site was built between 9th–10th centuries CE. The monastery, now abandoned, containing an excavated statue of Buddha seated cross legged with right hand in Bhumisparsa mudra while the left hand placed over his left knee. The image also wears a beautiful crown and a beautifully carved necklace.

name: Ramachandi Temple
description: Ramachandi is popularly believed the presiding deity of Konark. From the architectural point of view, the temple of Ramachandi is not important but from the religious point of view, it is one of the famous Shakti Pithas. The beach is often crowded by local students as a romantic escapade or families picnicking at the weekend. The main temple along with its Mukhasala had been built on one platform 3'2" (96.5 cm) high. On the three sides of the temple walls, i.e., south, west and north, there were three figures of Sun god as side Gods. Now one can see these side gods in north and southern side, whereas the figures on the western side have been displaced and are said to have been preserved in the National Museum at New Delhi. This image is said to have some sculptural specialisation and is regarded to be one of the beautiful images of the Sun god. Though smaller in size, the side-gods of this temple are of similar type in all respect with the side-gods in the Sun temple. The side images of the northern side are in somewhat good condition while the image in the southern side has no head and broken hands.

name: Light & Sound Show
description: A light & sound show is held at the Konark Sun Temple complex the temple acts as a projector. The entire history of the temple, including parts of the Kalinga history, is brought to life through light and sound effect. Photography is not allowed during the show.

name: Pipili
description: It has a very wide and distinctive selection of handicrafts. It is a small village. On the main road at Pipili there are many shops selling Applique work products, tourist visiting Puri buy these products from Pipili.

name: Labanya Lodge
description: This place is good for families and backpackers alike. There are tidy rooms with bathrooms and rooms without (the cheapest). Set in an area of comparatively uninspiring hotels, the lodge is an exceedingly short stroll from Konark Sun Temple (turn left) and a very long march from Chandrabhaga Beach (turn right — the only time you'll actually need an auto in Konark). Weak signal Wi-Fi available only in the area near reception and the adjacent veranda. All bathrooms are mosquito-ridden, so opt for a room without. Service no better or worse than what you'd expect in the north of India. This is the best you can expect in such a small town.

name: Yatrinivas
description: Only air-conditioned rooms.

name: Kakatpur Mangala Temple
description: A small temple on the Puri-Astaranga road on the bank of river Prachi. This temple is famous for Goddess Mangala. The Kakatpur Mangala Temple has a close relation with Jagannath Temple of Puri during the Navakalebara (Renovation of the Deities) festival. The most popular festival of Goddess Mangala is 'Jhamu Yatra'. It occurs on the first Tuesday of the sacred month Vaisakh (April 14 to May 15) every year.

name: Jagannath Temple, Baripada
description: The famous Jagannath Temple Rathyatra in Baripada is considered to be second best after that of Puri.

name: Mayurbhanj Palace
description: Palaces of the Maharaja of Mayurbhanj District. One of the Palaces has been converted in to a Govt. College.

name: Jwalamukhi Temple
description: The Jwalamukhi Temple displaying splendid colourful glass work.

name: Kichakeswari Temple, Baripada
description: Towering gateway

name: Heritage Rail Museum
description: Opened in 2021 the 54,000-square-foot museum exhibits the restored narrow-gauge steam and diesel engines and old coaches of the Mayurbhanj State Railway.

name: Haripur Gada
description: Remains of an ancient fort, which once served as the capital of the Bhanja dynasty of the Mayurbhanj estate. The ruins consisted of three temples, excavated ruins and fortification walls.

name: Rasik Raya Temple
description: Rasik Raya Temple is the most prominent structure of the entire Haripur Garh. The temple was built by Baidyanath Bhanja in the early part of the 17th century. The brick temple follows a typical Bengali-style aat-chala plan and stands at the eastern end of an elevated platform. The platform is approachable from the western end by a semi-circular flight of stairs. The temple probably had an extended structure in the front portion, but it has collapsed leving behind only traces of the structure. The temple has a triple-arched entrance and once the front face had elaborate terracotta ornamentation. Over the centuries, the terracotta ornamentation has faded away and only small traces of it can be seen after careful observation.

name: Rani Hansapur
description: This is a partially excavated site, whose layout revels a large a grand multi-room courtyard layout, featuring dedicated residential chambers, a Nrutyashala (dance and performance hall), and a private tank used exclusively by the royal. Sadly, nothing much remains of the grand structures. The layout of the rooms and the halls can only be traced out.

name: Radhamohan Temple
description: North west of the ruins of Queen’s Palace lies the ruins of the Radhamohan Temple. It is approached by a faintly marked trail meandering past scrubs and bushes. The ruined structure is housed inside a walled complex with the entry gate on the eastern side. The temple is the result of Vaishnava influence and incorporates elements of Bengal architecture from the Gouda region. The ruined structure stands on an elevated platform with a flight of stairs on the eastern side. Only a portion of a few side walls remains of the temple.

name: Jaganath Temple
description: The Jaganath Temple is located on the south-eastern corner of the Haripur Garph Complex. The temple follows a unique two-domed structure, with an influence from Gouda region of Bengal. According to legend, the temple has a connection to Gajapati Prataprudradeva, the historic Emperor of the Suryavamshi Gajapati Empire of Puri. According to legend, the temple was established in his honor.

name: Belgadia Palace
description: The Belgadia Palace is a majestic 18th-century Victorian-era royal residence of the Bhnaja Deo family now converted into a luxary hotel

name: Divya Palace
description: A basic hotel with good location. Walking distance from bus terminus

name: Kapilasa Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Elephants, leopards, deer and hyenas are some of the animals that reside in these deciduous forests. Boating activities available.

name: Durga Temple
description: old town temple

name: Jhadeswar Temple
description: Ancient Shiva Temple.

name: Hotel Orchard
address: Sambalpur - Sundargarh - Rourkela Hwy, Chowki Para

name: Baldevjew Temple
description: The largest temple.

name: Maa Tarinee Temple
description: You may go by bus or by reservation. The bus fare is ₹20 from Anandpur and ₹110 from Bhubaneswar.

name: Murga Mahadev
description: Dedicated to Lord Shiva.

name: Badaghagara
description: waterfall

name: Sanaghagara
description: A small but very beautiful waterfall.

name: Bhimkund
description: This is a beautiful waterfall on river Baitarani. Shaped like a tub (that is why named "kund", Oriya for tub), legend is that in during Mahabhatrath this was used by Bhima.

name: Gundicha Ghagi
description: A beautiful waterfall near Ghatagaon Maa Tarini Temple. A total of 13 km. 8 km is good road + 5 km zigzag road. Go safely.

name: Subarnameru Temple
description: A Shiva temple.

name: Karlapat Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A 175 km2 sanctuary lying within a forest ecoregion. Home to wildlife species like tiger, leopard, sambar, nilgai, deer, birds and reptiles.

name: Manikeshwari Temple
description: A temple, where animal sacrifice is offered at Dussehra festival.

name: Phurlijharan
description: 16 m high perennial waterfall

name: Chatar jatra
description: A traditional festival celebrated by the people of Kalahandi District, involving Maa Manikeswari goddess

name: Bhairabasingpur
description: is a village that was an important spot for Jainism. The village includes historical images of Jaina tirthankars, which are spiritual figures in Jainism. There is a shrine for Rishabhanath, and an additional shrine for Shiva, there, as well.

name: Hanging Bridge
description: A suspension bridge over the Nagavali River, with scenic views of the river and the surrounding hills.

name: Jagannath Temple
description: A beautiful temple with Ratha Yatra organised every year.

name: Mayal Lyang Homestay
description: The hosts, Gyatso and his wife, are very nice people and have great tales to tell about the Lepchas and Dzongu in general. The village is set amongst dense vegetation, on the side of a hill, with the Rongyung Chu River flowing at the hill's base. This place is far from the tourist hustle bustle and most peaceful. Visit here if you like to stray from the beaten path. The whole area is picturesque and unspoiled.

name: Gurudongmar Lake
description: The lake is situated at an altitude of 17,000 ft. The weather is extremely cold, with a strong freezing wind in the afternoon.

name: Chopta Valley
description: Chopta Valley is situated at an altitude of 14,000 ft. The temperature is below 10 degrees through the whole year and below freezing point in winter and at night. If you want to visit Chopta valley you have to stay overnight at Lachen. The drive from Lachen to Thangu is 30 kilometres with a difference in altitude of about 4 500 feet. The green vegetation of the lower altitudes changes to an Alpine and finally to a Tibetan plateau type terrain. Indian citizens are allowed to proceed to Gurudongmar Lake, but foreigners may visit Chopta Valley only.

name: Women's Handicraft Center
description: Here you can buy traditional carpets, blankets, handbags and shawls made from yak and sheep wool.

name: Cooch Behar Palace
price: ₹20 if ticket purchased online or else ₹25
description: The main attraction of Cooch Behar and the "Buckingham of West Bengal". The palace shows the acceptance of European idealism of the Koch kings and the fact that they had embraced European culture without renouncing their Indian heritage. The palace houses over 50 rooms including bedrooms, dressing rooms, billiard room, kitchen, dining hall, dancing hall, library, Tosha khana and the ladies gallery. Tickets can be booked at [https://asi.paygov.org.in/ Archaeological Survey of India]. No food items are allowed inside the palace premises. There are provisions for clean drinking water for visitors. Photography is not allowed inside the museum.

name: Rail Museum
description: A minuscule version of the National Rail Museum in New Delhi. The museum is based on the theme "Role of Railways in Development of Dooars region". The building resembles the architecture of Madan Mohan Temple. It has a gallery showing the technological and socio-cultural perspective of rail travel in India. It displays old exhibits dating back to the 1890s of the Cooch Behar State Railways. Photography is not allowed inside the museum.

name: Sagardighi
description: Large rectangular pond surrounded by government offices and seasonally populated by migratory birds. The walkway around it is favourable for morning and evening walks.

name: European Cemetery
description: The graveyard of the Cooch Bihar Northern Evangelical Lutheran Church (NELC), initially set up for European residents and Christian missionaries of the area during British India.

name: Sal Bagan
description: A park full of Sal trees. Great place for walking and relaxing. Has a view of the airport and a railway line.

name: Cooch Behar Church
description: Cooch Behar's only church and convent, with a school for the blind.

name: Baradebi Bari
description: One of the few temples in West Bengal constructed in European architecture instead of the usual Bengal architecture. It is a Durga temple and it hosts a big fair during Durga Puja.

name: Madan Mohan Temple
description: A holy Hindu temple which hosts the Ras Purnima event. A Ras Chakra is also built each year.

name: Madhupur Satra
description: Built by Nara Narayan of Cooch Behar in honour of the Assamese preacher Sankardeva. It has a very peaceful environment. Great place to look at Assamese culture.

name: Bhavani Cinema Hall
description: Good place for movies in a busy street. Mostly Bengali movies are aired.

name: Jaya Cinemas
description: One of the best places to watch movies in the town. Refreshment facilities are available too. English and Hindi movies are mostly aired here.

name: New Cinema Hall
description: Great place to watch movies with friends and family. Mostly Bengali and occasionally Hindi movies are aired.

name: SVF Cinemas
description: A multiplex in the town airing Hindi and Bengali movies. Refreshment facilities are also available.

name: Narendra Narayan Park
description: A great park to go to with family and kids. It has a child-playing area and features a toy train. It has lush green gardens and also has some animals in an enclosure. There are 2 water bodies in the park hosting water sports like boating and bubble swimming.

name: Laxmi Narayan Bastralaya
description: A century-old store with a wide range of collection of garments. Known for women's garments.

name: Reliance Trends
description: You can get modern or authentic Indian outfits in this well-developed store.

name: Samabayika General Store
description: Great shop stocked with all kind of snacks and other necessities.

name: Reliance Smart
address: Nripendra Narayan Road, opposite ACDC CLUB, Gowala Patti
description: A one-stop destination for all groceries.

name: PRM Market City
description: Largest shopping mall in the town. Includes many clothing stores, food courts and a movie theatre.

name: City Mall
address: East Khagrabari, New Cooch Behar Road
description: Located in the outskirts of the town. Has a play area, movie theatre, food courts and clothing stores.

name: Bara Bazaar
address: Biswasingha Road and Rup Narayan Road
description: The biggest street market in the town. Includes clothing stores, cosmetic stores, food courts, street food vendors, hotels, jewellery stores, restaurants and many more.

name: Cooch Behar Bazaar
description: One out of the two main street markets. You can find everything like vegetable stores, fish and meat stores, hardware stores, ATMs etc

name: Baburhat Bazaar
description: Known for its quality vegetables and wide variety of fish.

name: HDFC Bank
address: Opposite Rash Mela Ground,Silver Jubilee Road
description: The only foreign exchange in the town.

name: Mitali Restaurant
description: Great Indian food. Famous for its Mughlai Parantha

name: Samrat Sweets
description: One of the best sweet shops in the town. Usually crowded. Known for its samosa.

name: Food Trucks area
description: A crowded place full of food trucks offering many types of food in the evening.

name: Golpo
description: Huge range of quality food. You can get almost anything you want. Ranging from burgers to full meals; from authentic food to international meals; from drinks to bakery

name: Mio Amore
description: Reasonably priced bakery. Great food and is known for its fresh breads, wraps, hot dogs, and cakes.

name: The Aromas of Punjab
description: Great Punjabi food and also offers other Indian delicacies

name: KFC
description: Restaurant chain known for its buckets of fried chicken, wings & sides.

name: Domino's Pizza
description: A restaurant chain offering a wide range of pizzas & a variety of other dishes & sides.

name: Restaurant Monarch
description: Part of Hotel Yubraj, Great restaurant and great food

name: Restaurant Tara
description: Part of Hotel Ellora. Great food and services. It is a bit pricey.

name: Royal Palace Restaurant
description: Great food. It can handle a large number of guests

name: The Table Talk Cafe & Bistro
description: A well-designed café and a bistro known to be cosy. Great for a quick coffee break.

name: The Hot Box
description: Laid-back, neon-lit hookah lounge dishing up unpretentious snacks, plus mocktails.

name: Hotel BD
description: One of the best affordable hotels in the town. Located within the town centre, it has a view of the busy roads and markets

name: Hotel Maharani Palace
description: It has a bar and a restaurant. Provides a great view of the Cooch Behar Palace.

name: Hotel Subharup
description: A pocket friendly stay within 300 meters walking distance from the Cooch Behar Palace.

name: Hotel Mayur
description: An affordable hotel with a great fast-food restaurant in its ground floor

name: Hotel Green View
description: A value for money hotel with good sized rooms.

name: Hotel Royal Palace
description: A great hotel with a multi-cuisine restaurant and on-demand Wi-Fi.

name: Hotel Ellora
description: One of the best reasonably priced hotels.

name: Hotel Yubraj
description: 2-star hotel, with multi-cuisine restaurant

name: Kotwali Police Station
description: The police station serving the town.

name: Government Veterinary Hospital
description: Emergency veterinarian service.

name: Maharaja Jitendra Narayan Medical College & Hospital
description: Government hospital in Cooch Behar, West Bengal

name: Dr. P K Saha Hospital Pvt. Ltd.
description: 120+ bedded multi-speciality hospital.

name: Purple Lotus Clinic
description: One of the best clinics in the town. Hygiene is properly maintained with a well-trained staff.

name: Subham Hospital & Diagnostic Centre (P) Ltd.
description: Hospital in Cooch Behar, equipped with modern medical facilities

name: Jalpaiguri Rajbari
description: Palace of the Raikat family of the Baiknthapur Estate. Although the original palace was built in 1770, the modern palace was built in the early 20th century by Raja Jayantadev Raikat. This palace is particularly famous for its portico at the entrance. The garden consists of various species of trees, shrubs and flowers.

name: Karala riverside
description: Karala, a small river, flows through the middle of the town, bisecting it into two halves.

name: Jubilee Park
alt: Along the spurs of the Teesta River
description: Jubilee Park is situated on the bank of River Teesta. There is a garden with different flowering plants. There is a wooden statue of an elephant. The park also offers beautiful views during sunrise and sunset.

name: Town Club Ground
address: Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Road, Opposite Art Gallery
description: Watch football matches and other sporting events.

name: Eco City
description: Resort is covered with a tea garden. All rooms have AC, 24-hr room service, doctor on call, laundry, 24-hr light

name: Teesta Sundori Tourism Property
description: Run by West Bengal Tourism.

name: Nya Sylee Bungalow
description: Package includes dinner, breakfast, lunch, tea garden tour and tea factory tour.

name: Sylee Bungalow
description: Package includes dinner, breakfast, lunch, tea garden tour and tea factory tour.

name: Lepcha Museum
description: A museum with a small collection of belongings of the native Lepcha tribe.

name: Mangal Dham
description: A tribute to Guru Mangaldasji, whose samadhi lies in the ground floor of the dham.

name: Lepcha Bong Gumpa
description: Contains a museum.

name: Buddha Pada
description: An institute built in the Japanese minimalist style. Conducts workshops and classes in meditation, classical Indian dance, cinema, and other wisdom-based art forms. Accommodation available. Cafe and dining hall.

name: Triveni Camping
description: A confluence of two rivers, the river Rangeet with its deep green and crystal clear water, meets with the forceful mountain stream Teesta at a point called Teesta Triveni.

name: Art Cafe
address: Sharma Building, Rishi Road, Chotta Bhalukhop
description: A very hip cafe. Large outdoor seating area. View over mountains. Excellent coffee and cakes. Pizza and pasta. Fast and friendly service.

name: Roxberry The Street Outlet
description: Chic cafe, serving espresso-based coffees, pizza, pasta, burgers, and sandwiches. Professional and quick service.

name: Tara Cafe
address: shop no. 8, Big Will Mart D.B.Giri Road
description: Bright and airy cafe. Serves standard espresso-based coffees, pizza and pasta. Friendly service.

name: Melting Point
description: Branch of the Melting Point Pelling, West Sikkim.

name: Homestay Trinity
description: Spacious and clean. Well-equipped audiophile room with good collection of jazz music. Reading room. Meals prepared with home-grown organic vegetables.

name: Holumba Guest House
description: Reasonable rates. Botanical garden with exotic orchids. Guest cottages. Local tours arranged.

name: Kalimpong Village Retreat
description: Situated on a 6-acre (2½ ha) farm. Surrounded by forests and lush terraced paddy fields. Views over the Relli river and the hills of Lava. A popular birding destination.

name: Morgan House
description: A state-run tourist lodge in a 1930s mansion. Reservations can be made in Kolkata. Taxi fare from the market to Morgan House is ₹40 one way.

name: Soods Garden Retreat
description: 8½ miles (14 km) out of town

name: Tenam Garden
address: Dr. Grahams Homes, near Ronaldshay Park, 734301
description: A family-run homestay that welcomes pets, with an on-site restaurant serving organic food. Located in a quiet neighbourhood 3 km outside of town, surrounded by lush greenery.

name: DHR Archive
description: Located in a small room in Kurseong station, the DHR archive house several exhibits including artefacts and old photographs. A cabinet at the centre of the room displays old newspaper articles on DHR. Note that the archive mostly remains locked during office hours. A request to the station master normally opens up the archive.

name: Makaibari
description: Makaibari is one of the famous Darjeeling tea estates. Guided tours are given through the factory every day for free. The best time to see the tea production process is before 10AM and in the summer period (March till November). Tea can be bought after the tour in a small shop. Makaibari also runs a homestay and there are possibilities for volunteer work.

name: Netaji Museum and Centre for Studies in Himalayan Languages Society & Culture
Margaret's Deck
description: Margaret's Hope exclusive tea lounge falls under the Goodricke Teapot chain of tea lounges. It is situated on an extended platform offering 270 degree views of the Goodricke's Margaret Hope Tea Estate. Although there are no views of Mt. Kanchenjungha, the deck offers a great sunset. It serves some of the most exotic teas including Muscatel. It also serves snacks, but momo is not on menu.

name: Amarjeet Hotel
price: Rooms from ₹2500-3700 + 12% tax, up to ₹4800-6400 + tax including all meals. ₹600-1800 for an extra person

name: Cochrane Place
price: Room prices off/peak ₹4,000/4,500 (s) 4,500/5,000 (d) to ₹10,000 (4-person family suite) all including breakfast. Lunch or dinner ₹900
address: 132, Pankhabari Road, Kurseong, West Bengal, India
description: Former residence of British Magistrate John Percy Cochrane, the Cochrane Place Hotel is a modern day hotel with a touch of the Raj. Located just south of Kurseong on the Pankhabari Road the hotel is surrounded by rolling tea gardens. Cochrane Place is a boutique hotel specializing in tea. The Chai Country, the hotel's exclusive tea room serves excellent tea. It also serves excellent food combining continental and local cuisines.

name: Roudra Chhaya Tourism Property
description: A decent, if old-fashioned, state-run lodge with nice views of the mountains. TV and extra blankets are provided, but showers are cold. Breakfast is included in the rate. The restaurant also serves a fine dinner for around ₹300 each. Be early as lunch time can be crowded.

name: Taj Chia Kutir Resort & Spa, Darjeeling
Malda District Museum
description: The Museum dates back to 1937 and is under the West Bengal Directorate of Archaeology. The museum was started as a place of exhibits of artifacts found in the Malda district. The museum houses beautiful stone and bronze specimens dating back around 750 AD to 1200 AD. The exhibits include ancient coins, stone inscriptions, copper plate inscriptions, manuscripts, arms and weaponry of the medieval period. There are also ancient statues of Hindu gods and goddesses dating back to the 4th and 5th centuries.

name: Nimasarai Minar
description: Nimasarai Minar is a collapsed tower with projected spikes. Namasarai literally means halfway inn. It lies halfway between Gour and Pandua in Malda. The probably the place housed an inn in ancient town but no trace of it can be seen today. Only the collapsed portion of the tower stands. Although nothing much is known about the purpose of the tower but historians believe it was constructed as an indication tower for travellers. It was believed that lanterns were put up on top of the tower to guide travellers to the sarai. The projected spikes were probably used for hanging the served heads of executed criminals. The 500-year-old tower is said to be a replica of the Hiran Minar in Fatehpur Sikri. The tower stands on an octagonal base. The upper part of the slightly tapering tower has collapsed long ago. The structure is about 18 feet high and consists of two stories. The stories are marked with projected cornice.

name: Subhankar Sishu Udyan
description: There is a restaurant inside. You can also take a boat riding.

name: Manaskamana Mandir
description: Visit this pious Hindu Kali temple.

name: Ramkrishna Mission Ashram
description: You can visit the place during the evening, experience the chanting and the prayer.

name: Amarapali Tourism Property
description: Run by West Bengal Tourism.

name: Hotel New Heaven
alt: In front of State Bus Stand (NBSTC)

name: District Library
description: Read newspapers and local classifieds for free. The library is open from noon-7PM.

name: Raiganj Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Several types of migratory birds arrive here each year from South Asia and coastal regions. They start arriving in June. The migratory species includes open-bill storks, egrets, night herons and cormorants. The resident birds are kites, flycatchers, owls, kingfishers, woodpeckers, drongoes, etc. Ornithologically, Raiganj Wildlife Sanctuary is a very important heronry.

name: Bahin Rajbari
description: One of the significant historical buildings of Uttar Dinajpur, on the banks of the Nagar River and near the border of Bihar. Zamindar Ishwar Chandra Chowdhury built the palace out of bricks. It has large rooms and a veranda.

name: Mohanta Masjid
description: A Mughal-style mosque built in 1425 and owned by the Mohanta family.

name: Pirpukurer Dargah
description: A dargah of Syed Burhan, built around 1758. Syed Burhan was a leader of the Fakir-Sannyasin rebellion of the late 18th century. The dargah is named after the pond in front of it, where a fair is held on the occasion of Poylā Boishākh (14-15 April).

name: St. Joseph's Cathedral
description: The cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Raiganj and one of the few churches in sub-Himalayan North Bengal. The cathedral features glass and ceiling paintings, prominent pillars on both sides modelled on Greek columns, carved doors and a high altar with a hexagonal dome on top.

name: Uttar Dinajpur District Museum
alt: উত্তর দিনাজপুর জেলা সংগ্রহালয় Uttor Dinājpur Jelā Songrohāloy
description: The museum has a collection of pottery works, terracotta sculptures and Surjapuri (a Bengali/Maithili dialect) manuscripts.

description: Pure vegetarian AC restaurant

description: With restaurant and bar

name: Neora Valley National Park
description: With an area of , Neora Valley is a rich biological zone in Eastern India. It is the land of the red panda in the pristine undisturbed natural habitat with rugged inaccessible hilly terrain and rich diverse flora and fauna.

name: Nihar Bindu
description: Bengali food both veg and non-veg and excellent hospitality.

description: Many antique collections including coins, inscriptions, sculptures, terracotta, ornamental stones, etc. of ancient ages are preserved here.

name: Bangarh
description: An archaeological site with structures from the Maurya Empire to the Pala Empire.

name: Bolla Kali Temple
description: Kali Puja is being observed here every Friday following the Rash Purnima. A fair is organised for three days.

name: Dargah of Shah Ata
description: A brick-built structure built as early as the 14th century. It is a square, roofless mausoleum enclosing the grave of Molla Ataruddin, also known as Shah Ata. Its lower portion is made of stone.

name: Kaldighi Park
description: A large number of migratory birds flock to this place during winter.

name: Sarengbari
description: A small forest with an exquisite picnic spot. There's a small hut with drinking water facilities. Permission is required from Hili Block Development Officer (BDO) to visit the area.

name: Cossimbazar Palace of the Roys
description: The former royal palace of the Cossimbazar royal family, turned into a heritage property.

name: Old Cossimbazar Palace
description: ThisThe place is known as Boro Rajbari and belongs to the Nandi family. It is totally in ruins, and the interiors are not accessible.

name: Old English Cemetery
description: The Old English Cemetery contains several tombs and graves, including the tomb of Mary Hastings, wife of Warren Hastings and that of her infant daughter. There are several other graves in the cemetery, but most of them are unmarked.

name: Dutch Cemetery
description: The Dutch Cemetery of Cossimbazar dates back to the early 18th century. The oldest grave is of Daniel Van der Muyl, who died in 1721. The cemetery has 47 tombs, most of them obelisks. The cemetery houses a white temple-like tomb housing the mortal remains of a Dutch East India Company official, Tammerus Canter Visscher. Incidentally, there is a similar grave in Chinsurah.

name: Residency Cemetery
description: A heritage Christian cemetery protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Many important British residents and military personnel lived in Berhampore were buried in this cemetery.

name: St. Mary Armenian Church
description: It was constructed in 1758 by Khoja Petros Arathoon. The church closed down after its last sermon in 1860, but was reopened in 2005. Although not a functioning church, it is well maintained and is housed in a large compound complete with a landscaped garden. It is a small church and there are several graves inside the church.

name: Byaspur Shiva Temple
description: A Shiva temple with terracotta works. It was built in 1811 by Pandit Ramkeshava Devasharman, and is said to have been inspired by the temple in Baranagar (near Azimganj) built by Rani Bhabani.

name: Murshidabad Maharaja Krishnanath University
description: A public state university in Berhampore with Oxford-inspired architecture. It was established in 1853 as a liberal arts college by Maharani Swarnamoyee Devi. She named it after the demise of her her husband Krishnath Roy, who dreamt of establishing an academic institution. Author Brajendranath Seal developed the college infrastructure further.

name: Saidabad Rajbari
description: Built by Maharaja Nandakumar Roy's son-in-law, the palace was later converted into a museum and district library.

name: Laldighi Park
description: A great place to (re)discover love.

name: Rabindra Sadan
description: Watch theatre.

name: Ritwik Sadan
description: Watch documentary films.

name: Barrack Square
description: The central ground of Berhampore, as part of the fortified British cantonment. It is surrounded by various bungalows and barracks, all of which are now used as government offices.

name: Bohor Tourism Property
description: Run by West Bengal Tourism.

name: Cossimbazar Palace of the Roys
description: The property is managed by the royal family under the banner of Roopkatha Hotels and Resorts. It houses 14 air-conditioned double bed rooms and two suites. The hotel has a restaurant serving Bengali cuisine. There is a heritage tour of the hotel, which is free for hotel guests and outsiders have to pay ₹ 30 per head for the tour.

name: Hotel Lake View
description: Rooftop pool, lounge, cafe, restaurant, ceremony hall.

name: Palpara Temple
description: A char-chala temple with terracotta reliefs.

name: Kalyani Picnic Garden
description: You can enjoy a day long picnic here. It is at the western end of Congress road that leads straight from Kalyani main station. Good for group picnics. Carry utensils and cook food here, but keep clean and don't litter.

name: Kalyani Mela
description: An event worth visiting.

name: Sati mayer mela
description: A religious gathering.

name: Indian Council of Agricultural Research, Kalyani
Aquatic Palace
address: Kalyani Highway, near JIS College of Engineering
description: Where you can have a toast of cool or hot drinks in the ambiance of aquatic peace and beauty...

name: Anurag Guest House
description: Nice Decent place to receive your guests, AC, Non-Ac rooms Available

name: Kathgola Palace
description: Once the residence of the Dugar family, now a museum showcasing chandeliers, mirrors, furniture and other artefacts. It was built by Dhanpat Singh Dugar and Lakshmipat Singh Dugar in 1873, along with the spacious garden. A French architect later renovated a part of this palace, which also involved a Bengali architect. The Kathgola complex also houses a Jain temple, a small zoo, and a statue by the famous sculptor Michelangelo.

name: Adinath Jain Mandir
description: Though some of its early glory has been lost, the temple remains a major tourist attraction, chiefly because of the beautiful temple with an admirable work of stucco. The walls of this temple are also intricately designed. A typically Jain style of ornamentation lends a unique beauty to this Jain temple.

name: House of Jagat Seth
description: The Jagat Seths were a business family and were involved in the business of banking and money lending. The last Jagat Seth was Fateh Chand in 1911 and the title was no longer inherited. Their house has been restored and converted into a museum. The complex also houses a Jain Temple dedicated to the 23rd Jain Tirthankar Parshanath.

name: Jafarganj Cemetery
description: About half a mile from the Hazarduari Palace is Jafarganj Cemetery. The Cemetery contains the tombs of the Nawab's Nazim, from Mir Jafar to Humayun Jah. Mir Jafar's father Syud Ahmed Nazafi, Alivardi Khan's sister, Shahkhanum, Mir Jafar's widows, Munni Begam and Babbu Begam, Mohamed Ali Khan, the brother and Ismail Ali Khan and Asraf Ali Khan, the sons-in-law of Mir Jafar, lie buried here. This cemetery was built by Mir Jafar, over an area of 3.51 acres and houses about 1100 graves.

name: Nashipur Palace
description: The palace was built by King Kirtichand Bahadur in 1865. Within the palace compound are temples: the Ramachandra temple and the Lakshmi-Narayana temple. Closely situated is the Ashram of Mohandas and Jafraganj Deorhi. The two cannons present here are said to be gifted to Mir Jafar by Clive.

name: Nimak Haram Deorhi
description: Nimak Haram Deorhi is the gateway to Mir Jafar's palace. The palace lo longer exist but the entrance gate still stands.

name: Tomb of Azimunnisa Begum
description: Azimunnisa Begum, was the daughter of Murshid Quli Khan. According to legend she was diagnosed with an incurable disease. To get cured she was advised to eat the liver of infants. She got addicted to it and continued the practice. Ultimately it came to the attention of her father and he had her buried alive. There are several versions of the story. She was buried under a mosque and only a small portion of the mosque wall stands to this day..

name: Ghurni
description: The Bangalore-based Deccan Herald has written, "“We have clay dolls, toys and even clay sculptures in different parts of India. But there has been nothing to match the clay doll artisans of Krishnanagar in the Nadia district of West Bengal. The creations of these artists are displayed in most of the handicraft museums of the world. In India, we have a large display of these dolls in the Shankar's Dolls Museum in New Delhi. One look at the clay dolls and we are amazed at the reality with which the artist has displayed the character of the model." Exhibitions of Krishnagar dolls have been held in London, Paris and Boston. Doll makers market their products personally to the local people as well as to the outside visitors. Sales are also made through Krishnanagar Mritsilpa Co-operative Society, Nadia District Service cum Marketing Co-operative Industrial Union Ltd., and West Bengal Handicraft Development Corporation Ltd.

name: Krishnanagar Roman Catholic Church
description: It stands out for its distinctive architecture. There are 27 oil paintings describing the life of Jesus Christ. There also is a Protestant church in the same compound.

name: Rajbari
description: The Rajbari has a beautiful Durga temple in the courtyard. Jhulan Mela is celebrated in July-August, Baro Dol is held 12 days after Dol Purnima in March-April.

name: Clay Model of Krishnanagar
description: Leading manufacturer of clay model based in Krishnanagar

name: Ghurni studios
description: Doll makers market their products personally to tourists.

name: Studio di Scultura
description: Bronze sculpture installed - 7' 6" standing statue of Mahatma Gandhi in Leicestor, UK; 5' sitting statue of Mahatma Gandhi in Munich; 3' 6" bust of Rabindranath Tagore in Shanghai; 3' bust of Jagadish Chandra Bose in Teheran; 6' statue of Rani Rashmoni in Kolkata (Esplanae); 9' statue of Swami Vivekananda in Dakshineswar and many others.

name: Adhar Chandra Das & Sons
description: Claims to be inventor of Swarbhaja and Swarpuriya. Shop founded in 1902. This shop was famous for the shooting of the movie Sabar Upore, starring Uttamkumar and Suchitra Sen. Many other sweetmeat novelties available.

name: Mumpi Hotel & Lodge
address: Krishnanagar Bus Stand, Lal Mohan Ghosh Road

name: Goshala
description: A cowshed which takes care of more than 200 cows and bulls. A veterinary doctor performs timely health checks. Goshala also sells health products derived from the cow such as ghee, yoghurt, go-ark (distilled cow urine) and others.

name: Srila Prabhupada’s Pushpa Samadhi Mandir
hours: Open for general guests from 7:30AM to 1PM and 3:30PM to 8:30AM
description: The magnificent memorial shrine of Srila Prabhupada is the largest of its kind in India. The tall majestic marble dome dominates the skyline and shines beautifully in the golden rays of the sun at sunrise and sunset. The garland which adorned him while placing him in Samadhi has been brought and laid down in the Pushpa Samadhi Mandir. A larger than life size brass murti of Srila Prabhupada has been installed and worshipped here. The Samadhi Mandir’s gardens are very beautiful and extensive. They never fail to attract the attention of all guests. Upstairs, inside the Samadhi, a large diorama display depicts Srila Prabhupada’s life and struggles to establish ISKCON and its preaching mission. Outside, the walls are decorated with terra-cotta displays of Krishna’s pastimes from the Srimad-Bhagavatam. A large auditorium is in the basement with facility for stage lighting. It is equipped with a sound system and seminars, festivals, ISKCON film shows and cultural programs take place here.

name: Mangal Arati
description: Attend the early morning Mangal Arati held in the Sri Radha Madhav Temple. Summer and winter timings may differ by a couple of minutes, however, the reception near the main gate and inside the guest houses within the ISKCON campus will be able to provide a prayer timings pamphlet. It is a blissful gathering of devotees and visitors, and early morning prayer to the deities.

name: Mayapur Tourism Center
description: A building with shops selling handicrafts and religious items on the ground floor.

name: Prasadam
description: There is one restaurant in this town, operated by ISKCON for the glory of Krishna, of course. The breakfast consists of puri and alu sabji along with sweets. Lunch is splendid and so is dinner, but as the menu varies, you have to go to find out what's being served.

name: Poramatala
description: Poramatala is one of the sacred religious centers in Nabadwip. A colossal banyan tree covers this place like an umbrella. The idol of goddess Porama is located in the cavity of the banyan tree.

name: Maa Porama Temple
description: This is the centered temple in Poramatala. Goddess Porama is actually the deity of Maa Kali (some scholars also refer to Maa Saraswati, so her name is also known as "Maa Nil Saraswati".).

name: Bhabatarini Mata Temple
description: Bhabatarini Mata Temple is located on the left side of Maa Porama Mandir. The architecture of the temple is Char-Chala on a Bengali Dalan type architecture with Pankha style artistry. The Presiding deity of the temple is Maa Bhabatarini Kali Mata with a unique style. It was established in 1825 by Raja Girish Chandra. In 1667, Raja Raghab established a big Ganesh idol. Almost 100 years after his death, when Ganges eroded in the flood, the idol of Ganesha was also affected. Then the king Dordonda Pratap Krishnachandra rescued the idol from there. But when the idol was moved, many people touched it and scholars advised him to keep the idol under the ground for 12 years. After 12 years, in the time of Raja Girish Chandra while lifting the idol from the ground, the trunk of Ganesha broke. Then, by the order of the king, an unknown artist made a statue of Girishchandra Maharaj's adored goddess Anandamayi from the idol of Ganesha and named the goddess Bhavatarini Mata.

name: Bhabataran Shiv Temple
description: Bhabataran Shiv temple is situated on the right side of Maa Porama temple. This temple is a rare octagonal peak temple in architecture. This was also established by Raja Raghab for the first time. But with the erosion of the Ganges in 1760 AD, the idol along with this temple was submerged in the Ganges. About 65 years later, in 1825, King Girish Chandra restored the idol of Shiva at Poramatala.

name: Mahaprabhu Birthplace Temple
description: It is the birth place of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, located in the north side of Nabadwip. It is a Naba-Ratna type temple architecture. There is also a hut made of straw in the temple, where an idol of Sachi Mata is placed and Sachi Mata holds Nimai (Chaitanya Mahaprabhu) in her lap. And in the Naba-Ratna temple, Gour-Nitai placed in the middle, Jagannath Mishra and Sachi Mata in the left side, Radha-Krishna in the right side.

name: 60ft. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu
description: In the Narahari Dham Asram, a beautiful 60 ft tall Chaitanya Mahaprabhu statue situated. It is the highest Mahaprabhu statue in the world. There is a museum which beautifully describes the life of Mahaprabhu and also the life of Krishna. Pancha tattva (Five aspects of God), 64 Mahanta, Scholars of Nabadwip, birth of Krishna, lifting the Govardana hill by Krishna, Krishna's eternal bed, Raslila of Kriahna, Astasakhi and many more details of their life beautifully exhibit here.

name: Dhameswar Mahaprabhu Temple
description: Sri Dhameswar Mahaprabhu Temple is very special for the deity of Lord Sri Gauranga Mahaprabhu. The wooden deity of the temple was made in 1534 AD. The beautiful deity of the temple is made of Neem wood. It is the original deity of Mahaprabhu that Visnupriya, wife of Lord Mahaprabhu worshiped.

name: Nityananda Milan Mandir
description: Nityananda Milan Mandir, popularly known as Nitai-er bari (Bengali: নিতাইয়ের বাড়ি), is famous temple of Nitai, the companion of Mahaprabhu.

name: Manipur Rajbari
description: Anu Mahaprabhu is a unique idol made of jackfruit wood. Although each wooden idol of Nabadwip is made of neem wood, it is specifically made of jackfruit tree. In 1798 Manipur Raja Bhagya Chandra settled for going pilgrimage with intention mainly for installation of deity Lord Mahaprabhu in Nabadwip. The Manipuri style is clearly found in the face of the idol of lord Mahaprabhu.

name: Sri Sri Sribas Angan
description: In Sribas Angan there are 37 wooden idols of Chaitanya companion alone with Pancha Tattba. In the middle, there is a beautiful wooden idol of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu with Lakshmipriya and Bishnupriya.

name: Jagai Madhai Uddhar Temple
description: It is a famous temple highlighting the incident of Jagai and Madhai. It represented the fact of Jagai-Madhai, the two brothers of Brahmin family who turned into disrespectful individuals due to bad association. By the grace of Mahaprabhu and Nityananda, these two souls were revived from their sinful life. There are 29 beautiful wooden idols alone with the idol of Jagai-Madhai, Gour-Nitai. Those idols are mainly made of Neem wood.

name: Sonar Gouranga Temple
description: Sonar Gouranga temple is a famous temple in Nabadwip, situated besides Sribas Angan and lies opposite Sri Samaj Bari Ashram. The temple is famous for the Golden idol of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, the great social reformer and saint of Nabadwip.

name: Dwadash Shiva Temple
description: Dwadas Shiva temple is an old shiv temple of Nabadwip built in 1835. The architecture of this temple is 8-Chala peak temple. The presiding deity of this temple is Lord Shiva. The temple contains a beautiful art work of floral designs. A large number of pilgrims come here, especially during Mahashivratri.

name: Buroshib Temple
description: Buroshib Temple is a Naba-Ranta temple in architecture. The Buro Shib is almost 350-400 years old.

name: Purbasthali Oxbow Lake
description: Famous for thousands of migratory birds coming here from far-off places, including Siberia, in winters. People from far-off places come here for birding.

name: Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math
address: Manipur ghat Rd, Nabadwip, West Bengal 741302
description: There is lot of deers, visitor can buy some food for deers to feed from the entry gate of this temple and can feed those deer by your hand.

name: Bimala Mistanna Bhandar
description: Famous for Misti Doi, Singara, Kochuri and all the sweets and confectionery.

name: Nabadwip Boro Bazar
description: This is the main market of Nabadwip. Almost everything is available here.

name: Nabadwip Stadium
description: Matches, exhibitions and varied events.

name: Ananda Kanan
description: Take a walk.

name: Sujata Guest House
address: Station road, near Nabadwip Dham Vidyapith School

name: Churni River
description: A boat cruise in Churni during moonlight is a treat. The place is ideal for a day picnic.

name: Bethuadahari railway station
description: Take Lalgola-Sealdah Passengers or Hazarduari Express from Kolkata station, or the Bhagirathi Express from Sealdah and get off at Bethuadahari railway station. Express trains stop at Bethuadahari.

name: Kheraul Mosque
description: Ruins of a mosque built by Rafat Khan in 1495, during the reign of sultan Alauddin Hussain Shah.

name: Nimtita Rajbari
description: Built in 1866 and later popularised by Satyajit Ray's film Jalsaghar, the neoclassical palace represents the heydays of the zamindar era, now in shambles.

name: Raktamrittika Mahavihara
description: Ruins of a Buddhist university.

name: Bandel Church
alt: Bandel Basilica, Basilica of the Holy Rosary
description: One of the oldest churches in West Bengal, standing as a memorial to the Portuguese settlement in Bengal. It is dedicated to Our Lady of the Rosary. The present church and monastery are said to be built in 1660 by Gomez de Soto, having the keystone of the old church bearing the date 1599 over the eastern gate of the Monastery. In front of the church stands a ship's mast, which was presented by the captain of a vessel which had encountered a storm in the Bay of Bengal and was allegedly saved by the grace of the Virgin Mary. There is the statue of "One Lady of Happy Voyage" in the middle of the church. The church has three altars, a small organ and several tombstones.

name: Debanandapur
description: The birthplace of Bengali novelist Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay (1874–1938). He had written several novels and short stories, and most of them were translated into other languages and even brought to silver screens. There also is a library named Sarat Smriti Pathagar, which includes a museum room containing the things used by the famous writer.

name: Lahiri Baba Ashram
hours: 10AM–noon and 4–6PM. 📵 Shoes, cameras and mobile phones not allowed inside building
description: The temple is known for its architecture and environment, and was built in 2003 on the philosophy of Yogiraj Shyamacharan Lahiri. It is open to all visitors regardless of creed and caste. The temple has blended the Rajasthani and South Indian temple architectures. The gopuram at the entrance is magnificent. There are numerous temples other than the main temple in the ashram area. Not only that, there are separate prayer rooms for Christians and Muslims. The campus is full of ancient mango trees and flower gardens on both sides.

name: Sayed Jamaluddin Mosque
description: A medieval mosque in Saptagram, built in 1529, and it happens to be the only medieval remains of the flourishing port. The mosque was built by Syed Jamaluddin, son of Sayyid Fakhruddin of Amul. It is a brick-built structure complete with intricate terracotta ornamentation. As Islam provides the use of animal and human figures, the ornamentation is restricted to floral and geometric patterns. The roof of the mosque has long collapsed, and nothing much can be ascertained about the original structure. The mosque has four minarets on the four corners, and the interior contains two stone pillars.

name: Bandel Bazar
description: One of the biggest and most important markets in the Hooghly district. It's the hub of agricultural imports and exports. Vegetables, fruits (especially mango and watermelon) and rice are exported from the market.

name: New Haji Biryani House
description: An iconic biryani house in Bandel More. The restaurant is not very big and has few seats. Chicken biryani is ₹110, and mutton biryani is ₹130. Aloo biryani is also available.

name: Gandhi Memorial Museum
description: One of the many museums in India that preserve and display materials associated with Mahatma Gandhi. This one particularly focuses on Bengal and Odisha.

name: Government House
description: The former riverside suburban residence of the Governor-General of India and later the Viceroy of India. It was built in 1823 by then-Governor-General Lord Hastings. Its front lawn contains a marble fountain, which was brought from the Taj Mahal by Lord Hastings.

name: Lady Canning's Grave
description: Wife of viceroy Lord Canning, Charlotte Canning was a painter and a naturalist. She spent her time in Barrackpore indulging in her passions. She remains fresh in the Bengali mind with a popular sweetmeat leḍikeni named after her. After she died in 1861, Lady Canning was buried at her favourite spot. There is a statue of Lord Canning nearby. The former Danish colony of Serampore is visible from the opposite side.

name: Netaji Open University
description: Originally a residence of Rastraguru Surendranath Banerjee, who used to live here for a considerable period of time.

name: Annapurna Temple
description: A Hindu navaratna (nine-pinnacled) heritage temple with a striking resemblance to the Dakshineswar Kali Temple. It was built in 1875 by Jagadamba Devi, the youngest daughter of Rani Rashmoni. Inside the temple complex is a Natmandir, six Shiva temples and two Nahabatkhanas.

name: St. Bartholomew's Cathedral
description: Built in 1831. One of the best in terms of architecture amongst the churches built during the British period.

name: Dada Boudi Biriyani
description: A much hyped Biriyani joint costing ₹160-₹200 a plate (Chicken/Mutton), located just outside Sukanta Sadan. Try a special dish called "Liver Fry" from Dada-Boudi. Be prepared to wait in the queue.

name: Mangaldhara Tourism Property
description: Run by West Bengal Tourism. It features a 24-hour generator facility, air-conditioned rooms with attached bathrooms, car parking, colour television, hot water, laundry, restaurant, room and Wi-Fi services.

name: Roychowdhury Zaminder House
description: This is the ancestral house of former Army General Shankar Roychowdhury. There are Natmandir, old temples in the premises.

name: Upendra Nath Basu Memorial Water Well
description: This looks more like a tower than a tube well (Bengali: নলকূপ; nalkūp). It is in dilapidated condition. A marble plaque on the structure mentions that it was built by Swarnatalata Basu in 1932 in memory of her husband Upendra Nath Basu (1873–1892). (Note: The dates in the plaque were according to the Bengali calendar).

name: Golpatar Jungle
description: Walking trails under the canopy of Golpata trees. The trails lead to the river where there are views of Bangladesh. It is recommended to bring a photo ID as you may be requested to present it before being allowed to enter.

name: Nripendra Atithisala
description: Guest house run by Taki Municipality. There is a garden area outside with a play area for children.

name: Suhasini Guest House
description: Private and dorm rooms in a guest house across the street from the river. Rooms have air conditioning and there is parking and a restaurant.

name: Chandrakona Jorbangla Temple
description: A 17th-century stone-built temple.

name: Mohobani
description: Birthplace of Khudiram Bose.

name: New Digha Beach
description: One of the most popular beaches in West Bengal, and the best place for a safe dip. The beach here is flat and it gets overcrowded, especially during the cooler winter break. Beer is generally served at the beach by the enterprising locals who would accept payment later by coming with you to your hotel. Beware, they may ask a high price for beer. Other activities in the beach include horse riding, sunbathing, volleyball, cricket, football etc.

name: Old Digha Beach
description: The original beach, popular among older generations. However, Old Digha is not safe and conducive for bathing. It is not as wide as it used to be due to heavy soil erosion. Big stones and concrete steps are used to hold together the beach.

name: Mohana Beach
description: A less-visited beach at the estuary of the Champa River. There's a fish market at the beach.

name: Talasari Beach
description: There is a river by the beach. It gets submerged with high tide. The river gets dried up twice a day. Again it gets filled with water once there is high tide. Once you cross the river using ferry boats you will reach the beach. The beach is quiet and the sea is calm. You can easily take a bath in the sea. You can move around the beach and listen to the breeze. You may also take a boat ride if necessary.

name: Shri Jagannath Temple
description: The newly-built temple in New Digha, built in 2022-2025 to rival the Jagannath Dham in Puri. Like the Puri temple, this temple is also built in the Kalinga architecture, with a blend of the Nagara architecture.

name: Masir Bari
description: The Digha counterpart of Puri's Gundicha Temple, used in Digha Ratha Yatra (Chariot Festival).

name: Digha Science Centre & National Science Camp
description: A microcosm of the Science City of Kolkata, with interactive exhibits, science camps and a planetarium.

name: Marine Aquarium and Regional Centre
description: This is possibly the most well-equipped marine aquarium in India, but the collection of specimens is poor. Some common local fish are kept in this huge aquarium.

name: Biswa Bangla Park
description: A park developed in 2015 with the iconic "Biswa Bangla" (World Bengal) globe. The globe depicted the location of West Bengal in the world with the Bengali letter "ব" (from "বঙ্গ" or "বাংলা", meaning "Bengal"). Sadly, the globe was removed after the 2026 state election for political reasons, as Biswa Bangla has become a symbol of the 2011–2026 Trinamool Congress (TMC) regime. Nonetheless, the park still remains as one of the few green spaces in Old Digha.

name: Dheusagar
description: A large seaside space with activities like boating and bungee jumping.

name: Kajal Dighi
description: A pond with toy train (miniature railway) rides.

name: Digha Mohana Fish Market
description: Buy fresh fish here.

name: Digha Youth Hostel
price: Doubles with attached baths are ₹225 per day
description: Bookings can be done at the Directorate of Youth Services, 32/1, B.B.D. Bagh (South), Kolkata.

name: Hotel Kamala Residency
price: Double non A/C rooms ₹900. Double A/C room ₹1,500 and triple with A/C ₹1,800
description: Breakfast included. Restaurant in hotel.

name: Hotel Rajmahal
description: A less expensive yet quality hotel with restaurant near to sea beach.

name: Hotel Suman's
description: A very homely accommodation at New Digha, close to sea beach. Tariff from ₹200. Walking distance from Railway Station and Bus Stand.

name: Minakshi and Taranga
description: A/C double bed rooms.

name: Ownland Hotel & Resort
description: Spa, fitness centre, swimming pool, pool & table tennis, banquet hall, aquarium, Babylon (roof top), disco lounge: Impulse, multi-cuisine restaurant

name: Sandpiper Guest House
description: Eight rooms, all having uninterrupted sea views and each capable of sleeping 4 adults. En suite bathrooms, marble flooring, multi-cuisine restaurant, secure car parking. ₹7000 upwards.

name: Tanrango Lahori
description: Transport available from station.

name: Panthasala
description: Run by the Odisha Tourism Development Corporation.

name: Hotel Santiniketan Digha
price: ₹1,000 standard non-A/C rooms ₹1,700 for triple A/C deluxe room

name: Hotel Sea Coast
description: Conference room, centralised A/C, bar & multi-cuisine restaurant, sea facing rooms & family rooms also available.

name: Hotel Sea Hawk
price: From ₹2500 for a ground-floor sea-facing double up to ₹6,500 for an A/C double bed
description: One of the few places in town that doesn't hike up their prices as demand increases. Food is moderately good and room services standard.

name: Hotel Seagull
price: ₹2,300 for non sea facing A/C rooms
description: Excellent views, good service, ask for a room in the new building. Rooms available from ₹2,300 for non-sea facing rooms up to ₹15,800 for royal suite.

name: Hotel Utopia Digha
price: From ₹800 standard rooms ₹1,500 for an A/C double bed
description: With sea and forest views. TV, air-con, and free wi-fi in the rooms. Free parking.

name: Dighali - I Tourism Property I
description: Run by West Bengal Tourism.

name: Dighali - II Tourism Property
description: Run by West Bengal Tourism.

name: The Palm Resort
price: Double deluxe INR 1800 to deluxe executive INR 4500
description: Swimming pool, free parking, power back-up.

name: Digha State General Hospital
description: The only hospital in coastal Purba Medinipur.

name: Haldia Dock Complex
description: Commissioned in 1977, the Haldia Dock Complex acts as an alternative to the Port of Kolkata. The port is used mainly for cargo ships.

name: The Golden Harvest
address: City Centre, Debhog, The Golden Retreat
description: Northwest frontier cuisine

name: Hotel Dreamland
description: Bar with music. Good place with soothing ambience.

name: Royal Harbour
description: Good crowd in the bar with high class officers and businessmen frequenting the place. There is a protocol and dress code for this place so no non-sense is allowed here.

name: The Golden Retreat
description: Set on 10 acres of tranquil land, amidst lush green surroundings, is a retreat with centrally air-conditioned superior deluxe rooms and suites. The Victorian architecture, spacious interiors, enchanting artefacts and tasteful furnishings spell discreet elegance, creating an atmosphere so relaxing that you can sink into it.

name: The Royal Harbour
description: This is a luxury lodge, hotel, and restaurant with centrally air-conditioned superior deluxe rooms and suites.

name: Mohana
description: Located on an island in the Haldi river at Nayachar (Meendwip), connected with Haldia by ferry service. Natural beauty of the place attracts tourists.

name: Junglemahal Zoological Park
description: The zoo houses deer, snakes, peacocks, bears, crocodiles, black rabbits and various types of monkeys.

name: Sabitri Mandir
description: 350 year old temple.

name: Jhargram Palace
description: Was once owned by the Raja of Jhargram is now run jointly by West Bengal Tourism and the royal family. It has 10 rooms plus 3 dormitories on the ground floor. The Malladev family which owns the building lives on the floor above and they aren’t the last word in luxury.

name: BNR Garden
description: A park and a picnic spot, frequented by people of all ages. It offers toy train rides within the park.

name: Gole Bazaar Durga Temple
description: The temple was established in the early 20th century by some Bengali people working on the railways. It is famous for its Durga Puja and is very popular. It also serves as a seat of culture for the city.

name: Hijli Eco Park
description: It’s a famous picnic spot in winter. There is a small deer park inside.

name: Kalaikunda Air Force Station
description: Built by the British for the Royal Indian Air Force during World War II. It was used to conduct raids against advancing Japanese in Burma and also for operations to transport aid to parts of China. Access to the Air Force Station is restricted to defence personnel and is out of bounds for tourists without special permits.

name: Khargeshwar Temple
description: This is one of the oldest temples in the city, a Shiva temple, from which derives the name of Kharagpur.

name: Salua Air Force Station
description: An airbase used by the 317th Airlift Squadron of the US Air Force during World War II.

name: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur
description: The first Indian Institute of Technology, established in 1951. The IIT attracts visitors throughout the year (especially in the spring academic semester from January to April) on account on the Spring Fest, Kshitij and other departmental and interdepartmental fests and events.

name: Hijli Shaheed Bhavan
description: IIT Kharagpur was originally a detention camp during the British Raj to imprison Indian independence activists. The building was later renamed Shaheed Bhavan (and colloquially referred to as the "Old Building" in the institute), and was built on the Neo-Byzantine style of architecture. In 1990, the building was converted into a museum called the Nehru Museum of Science and Technology. The museum has many indoor exhibits, which include technical models collected from various institutes and organisations across India. The park outside the museum contains 14 open-air demonstrations and outdoor exhibits. The outdoor exhibits include a Hawker Hunter Mk 56 and a steam locomotive. The museum has an archive room showcasing documents relating to the history of IIT Kharagpur and Southwest Bengal.

name: Gole Bazaar
description: A reliable but highly congested shopping destination.

address: OT Road, near Allahabad bank, Inda

address: No shooting Area, Kharagpur Local, Salua

description: Has a minibar and parking.

name: Hotel Park
description: Restaurant, credit cards accepted, TV in rooms.

name: Anicut Dam
description: Not to be confused with the one near Tiruchirappalli.

name: Gopegarh Heritage and Nature Eco-Tourism Centre
description: A good picnic spot

name: Jagannath Temple
description: The temple was built in 1851, possibly at the request of a descendant of the Ganga dynasty of Odisha.

name: Jora Masjid
description: Notable for Annual Urs festival.

name: St. John's Church
description: One of the rare churches in Southwest Bengal.

name: Fort ruins of Rani Shiromani
description: The fort's interior was divided into two parts, the andarmahal (অন্দরমহল) for the royal family and the sadarmahal (সদরমহল) for others. The temples of Dandeshwar, Jogmaya and Mahamaya, the ruling deities of Karnagarh, are south of the fort. Unfortunately, hardly anything, other than memory, remains here. A big fair is held on Poush Sankranti (Makar Sankranti). The Karnagarh family had two other forts nearby – at Abasgarh and Jamdargarh.

name: Khirai
description: A secluded village, often called the "Valley of Flowers" of West Bengal. During the months of January-March, the fields are full of flower species like marigolds, chrysanthemums, tuberose and gladiolus. The remote view of a train passing through the colourful valley can remind one of Bengali classics like Pather Panchali, despite not being shot here.

name: Bargabhima Temple
description: Believed to be more than a thousand years old, it was sculpted by Lord Viswakarma. The temple holds an old icon of the Goddess ‘Tara’, another face of Goddess Kali. According to mythology, Devi Bargabhima was creator of Tamralipta, once a great port of ancient India. This temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas. Puranas say that the small finger of left feet of Parvati fell here when Lord Vishnu cut her sacred body into several pieces to make Lord Shiva quiet.

name: Matangani Sahid Smarak
description: During the Quit India movement of 1942, Matangini Hazra became a martyr at Tamluk. Later, Mahatma Gandhi appreciated her bravery and titled her as ‘Birangana’. This monument is a homage to her by prime minister Indira Gandhi.

name: Tamluk Rajbari
description: It was built in 5th century BC, and engulfs rich traditions and history.

name: Archaeological Museum, Tamluk
description: Contains artefacts of copper, inscribed copper templates and a copper plate of Greek inscriptions.

name: Nava Kailash
description: The temple complex of Nava Kailash consists of 108 Shiva Temples built in aat - chala style. The temple are arranged in two concentric circles. The outer circles consists of 74 temples while the inner circle consists of 34 temples. The outer temples have alternate black and white shiva lingas while the all the inner temples have white shiva linga. At the very centre of the complex is a large well and the space between the circles is laid out with manicured lawns complete with flower beds and other trees. The complex was built in 1809 by the Bardhaman Maharaja Tej Chand Bahadur.

name: Jalesvar Temple
description: The Nava Kailash complex is flanked on either side by two pancha ratna (five-pinnacled) temples. The Jalesvar Temple lies on the west.

name: Ratneshwar Temple
description: The Nava Kailash complex is flanked on either side by two pancha ratna (five-pinnacled) temples. The Ratneshwar Temple lies on the east.

name: Pratapeswar Temple
description: Kalna is known for its terracotta temples and the Pratapeswar Temple definitely stands out among the numerous temples of Kalna. Located at the left of the entrance of the Rajbari Complex this small deul styled temple, whose outer walls are covered with intricate terracotta works. The 1849 built temple stands on a high podium. The Pratapeswar Temple is built in rekh deul style, with curvelinear sikhara and single arched entrance. All the four sides of the temple has rich terracotta ornamentation depicting images of gods and goddesses to scenes from the great epics. It also contains panels depicting war scenes and also scenes from day to day life. On the left of the Pratapeswar stands a small cannon and on the right is a Ras Mancha.

name: Ras Mancha
description: Just north of the Pratapeswar Temple is the Ras Mancha. The octagonal structure has triple arched entrance on all three sides and at the centre is a hexagonal pavilion crowned with a dome.

name: Lalji Mandir
description: Built in 1739, the Lalji Temple is the oldest temple in the Rajbari Complex. It was built by Braja Kishori Devi, the wife of Maharaja Jagat Ram. It houses the idol of Radha – Krishna. Lalji Mandir is a 25-pinacled temple. The Lalji Temple once had elaborate terracotta panels but only a handful have survived. The temple also has traces of elaborate limestone stucco ornamentation. Just in front of the Lalji Temple is a Char – Chala (four sloped roofs) mandap, which served as a gathering platform for devotees visiting the temple. Lalji Mandir is housed in a complex inside the Rajbari Complex. The complex also houses several other structure including the Giri Govardhan Temple with a mountain-like roof.

name: Rupeshwar Shiva Mondir
description: Rupeshwar Shiva Mondir, a flat roof structure with a triple arched entrance. The temple had beautiful stucco work most of it no longer exist.

name: Pancharatna Temple
description: A collection of five hat - chala temples standing on a single raised platform. The temples are not identical. They not only differ in size but also in proportion.

name: Krishna Chandra Temple
description: This like the Lalji Temple is a temple complex situated within the Rajbari Complex. The Krishna Chandra Temple is a 25-pinnacled temple. The Krishna Chandaraji Temple was built 1751–55 and has a three-arched entrance on all sides. It also has a rich terracotta ornamentation in its front facade, depicting scenes from mythologies, epics and even day to day life. The temple also has its share of stucco work. The Krishna Chandra Temple Complex also houses other temples and several other structures, including Vijay Vaidyanathan Temple (a massive at-chala temple), Badrinarayan Temple, Radhavallabh Temple and Ramsita Temple.

name: Mahaprabhu Mandir
description: This temple is dedicated to Sree Chaitanya and his friend and disciple Nityananda. Both the idols are made of neem tree.

name: Shyam Sundar Mandir
description: This is a temple dedicated to Nutyananda, friend and disciple of Sree Chaitanya. The shrine also contains a foot print of Sree Chaitanya.

name: Ananta Vasudev Mandir
description: Ananta Vasudev Temple lies just north of the Siddheshwari Kali Temple and on the other side of the road. It is a huge aat chala temple, which was once covered with intricate terracotta. The temple was constructed by Trilokchand Rai, nephew of Chitrasen Rai, and was originally known as Baikunthanath’s Temple. The temple houses a four feet black stone idol of Vasudev and hence the name Ananta Vasudev. It was once covered with intricate terracotta. Sadly that has been lost due to unscientific restoration work.

name: Baidyapur Jora Deul
description: A pair of temples built in 1550 by Subhananda Pal. The two brick-built temples, with square bases probably had domed top in their original shape. Their façads are of carved bricks. The main temple faces east and the small north and they are interconnected with a passage. The larger temple has an inscription over its domway. It is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

name: Gopalji temple
description: This is the third 25-pinnacled temple of Ambika Kalna. The temple is approached by a dochala porch with a triple arched entrance. Built in 1766 the temple has intricate terracotta panels of the front surface and luckily most of it has survived.

name: Jagannath Temple
description: The twin temples of Jagannath Bari in Ambika Kalna are located on the banks of the Hooghly River. Built in 1753 by two queens of King Chitrasen –Chandakumari Devi and Indukumari Devi , these two temples are in a dilapidated condition. Although in crumbling conditions the terracotta works in both the aat chala temple have survived and can still be seen. Three is also a smaller aat chala structure near the temple.

name: Siddheswari Kali Temple
description: Siddheswari Kali Temple houses the deity of Ambika Siddheswari, after whom Ambika Kalna got its name. The idol is an incarnation of Kali and is said to have been made out of single branch of a neem tree. An inscription on Siddheshwari Kali Temple mention that the temple was constructed by Chitrasen Rai, the then King of Bardhaman in 1740. But historian opine that the temple was originally constructed in 1663 and it was renovated by the Bardhman King in 1740. Siddheswari Kali Temple follows the Jore Bangla Temple of architecture. It has a triple arched entrance and is approached by a long flight of steps. Siddheswari Kali Temple is part of a temple complex which also houses 3 aat chala Shiva temples.

name: Datankathi Tala Mosjid
description: Nothing much remains of the Datankathi Tala Masjid. Acoording to the foundation plaque the mosque was constructed in 896 hijri, which corresponds to 1490. A few arches and pillars is all that remains of the over 500-year-old structure. None of the floral and geometric terracotta designs have survived. A coat of newly added blue paint have robbed the ancient mosque of its antiquity.

name: Hotel Priyadarshini
description: Situated near the bus stand, this is a standard hotel. Tasty Bengali food is served.

name: Ramkrishna Lodge
description: This lodge is beside the 108 Shiva temple complex. If you want to stay near the main attractions, this is a good place. The lodge provides clean rooms and shared washrooms. Food is not available, but with prior order they can arrange home delivery.

name: Bishnu Temple
description: This stone temple is built over a platform with a Bengal hut-shaped roof and arched entrance. The temple dates to about the 14th century CE. A stone, called "Narayan shila", is worshipped here as the deity of the temple. Earlier, a 12 armed Lokeswar Vishnu idol was being worshipped as deity, which has been stolen long before. The temple is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

name: Ghaghar Burhi Temple
description: A small shrine dedicated to Goddess Kali, it is the oldest temple of Asansol.

name: IISCO Steel Plant
description: Operated by Steel Authority of India (SAIL), the IISCO Steel Plant is one of the major steel plants in West Bengal.

name: Manoj Talkies
description: You can watch all newly released movies here. Good cinema hall; one of the biggest with a seating capacity of almost 1800.

name: Nehru Park
description: A beautiful park on the banks of the Damodar River. A cast iron statue of Nehru, casted by IISCO, is in the park. There is an eatery in the park. There's a big pond inside the park with boating facilities. You can get great views of the Biharinath Hill from the park.

name: Panifala
description: A picnic spot with a lake for boating and beautiful garden of flowers.

name: Satabdi Park
description: There are facilities for paddle boating and a few rides for children. Nice place to spend the evening.

name: Galaxy Mall
description: One of the malls in Asansol, giving you access to almost all leading brands. Eylex Multiplex in Galaxy Mall is Asansol's first multiplex with a comfortable movie experience.

name: Arpan
price: Adjacent to Chitra Cinema. It has a bar.

name: Gangar Hotel
description: Dhaba type. No pretensions of luxury. Delicious Bengali food - dal-aloobhaja must try; fish range from rui and chital maachh to ilish and varieties of chhoto maachh; those who like can also order mangsho or dimer dalna.

The hills are crowned with green and dark green during the rainy season, slightly grey during winter and dotted with fiery red during autumn. The fiery red colour comes from the fully blossomed palas tree.

name: Manbhum Holiday Home
description: Set amidst the natural environs of rural Bengal, this hut has 2 rooms (3 beds each) with attached bath dining room and kitchen facility.

description: A Jain prilgrimage centre.

hours: Ferry service:Usually every 4 hours in winter

name: Kangsabati Dam
description: The height of the dam is 38 metres with a lake of 86 sq km. A drive over the dam is recommended. The length of the motorable road over the dam is 14 km. One needs to collect passes to enter this road. Passes are issued free of cost near the dam from 10AM to 4PM.

name: Pareshnath Temple
description: A small shrine containing an ancient stone statue of the 23rd Jain Tirthankara Parshanath. It was found during the excavation of the dam. The shrine also contains a shiva linga and another ancient statue.
